llm_summary: Liver transplantation programs around the world use different systems to decide who receives donated livers, and these systems vary significantly by region, which can affect patient outcomes and fairness. Researchers from multiple countries examined how liver allocation works across Europe, Scandinavia, Asia, Australia, Canada, the United States, and Central and South America to understand these regional differences. The study found that different regions handle exceptions to standard allocation rules in different ways, particularly for patients with liver cancer, and that countries also vary in how they use living donors and organs from people who have recently died. This comprehensive comparison of global liver allocation practices serves as a reference guide to help countries improve their own organ distribution policies and make decisions about which patients should receive priority for transplants. The findings from this international team of liver transplant experts can help foster conversations between countries about how to create fairer and more effective organ allocation systems worldwide.

title: Safety of immunotherapy after liver transplantation-A multicenter study of a prospective standardized clinical practice protocol.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved cancer prognosis significantly, but their use has been avoided in liver transplant recipients (LTr) due to poorly characterized rejection risk. Data surrounding rejection risk are extremely suboptimal, with highly variable immunosuppression approaches and follow-up, and do not account for the learning curve in managing immunosuppression in the setting of ICI. A standardized institutional clinical practice protocol was developed in 2021 for immunosuppression management to facilitate ICI therapy with prospective close follow-up for immunosuppression levels and allograft function. Of 20 LTr, 12 (60%) were male, 18 (90%) were Caucasian, with a mean age of 54.0 (SD 11.2) years. However, 13/20 had 2 or more failed cancer therapies before ICI. Hepatocellular carcinoma ​(HCC) (N=7), lung (N=3), and melanoma (N=3) were the most frequent. Time from first ICI treatment to death was <30 days (N=5), 30-59 days (N=4), 60-89 days (N=1), and >90 days (N=6). Most deaths were cancer-related, reflecting the late stage of disease. ICI toxicity occurred in 3 LTr; pneumonitis (N=1, 5%), myocarditis (N=1, 5%), and acute cellular rejection (N=1, 5%). Four patients remain alive 178-341 days with stable allograft function and slow reduction in immunosuppression. Three out of 4 patients have a partial cancer response, and 1 with slowed progression of disease. ICI treatment in the immunosuppressed LTr is feasible with careful immunosuppression management and follow-up. Demonstrating a low rejection risk should allow for earlier utilization of these agents to improve cancer prognosis. Optimizing rejection risk with cancer response requires ongoing study.Copyright © 2025 American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a type of cancer drug called immune checkpoint inhibitors, which help the body fight cancer by boosting the immune system, could be safely used in people who have received liver transplants and later developed cancer. The team created a detailed plan for managing the anti-rejection medications these transplant patients take while also giving them the new cancer drugs, and they carefully monitored twenty patients who received both treatments together. Out of the twenty patients studied, only one person experienced rejection of their transplanted liver, while three others had other serious side effects like lung inflammation and heart inflammation, showing that the combination treatment was relatively safe. Four patients remained alive with their transplanted livers working well after six months or longer, and three of these four saw their cancers shrink or stop growing, suggesting the cancer drugs could help transplant patients with advanced cancer. The researchers concluded that using these powerful cancer-fighting drugs in transplant patients is possible with careful monitoring, and they called for more research to better understand how to balance preventing organ rejection while still allowing the cancer drugs to work effectively.

title: Prostate T2-weighted spin-echo MRI with and without glucagon: a paired scan quality assessment.
abstract: To evaluate the effectiveness of subcutaneous glucagon in reducing motion artifact during prostate MRI through intraindividual comparison.At our institution patients undergoing a clinical prostate MRI exam receive 1 mg of subcutaneous glucagon before scanning. From February 15, 2024 to February 11, 2025 33 such patients were recruited to undergo an additional, research exam without glucagon. All exams were acquired at 3T. An axial T2-weighted spin-echo series (T2-WI) was acquired within both exams. Evaluation of the T2-WI series was done by three experienced radiologists using the criteria of diagnostic quality (0-3 scale), PI-QUALv2 (0-3 sum), motion artifact (significant, visible, none), and reviewer preference (five-point relative scale). Due to differences in prescribed coverage, the scan times for the two T2-WI sequences were in general different for each subject. Results were stratified using the acquisition time ratio (Trel) between the glucagon vs. non-glucagon scans. Wilcoxon tests assessed score differences.Across all 33 subjects, no significant differences were found between glucagon and non-glucagon scans. However, the observed negative correlation between glucagon preference and Trel (p = 0.026) led to stratification into low-Trel (N = 16) and high-Trel (N = 17) groups. In the low-Trel group the glucagon scans provided significantly improved diagnostic quality (p = 0.048), PI-QUALv2 sum (p = 0.049), motion scores (p = 0.047), and reader preference (p = 0.042).Subcutaneous glucagon provides improved image quality in prostate T2-WI MRI when scan duration remains within 1.25× of that of a non-glucagon T2-WI series. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a medication called glucagon, given as a shot under the skin, could reduce unwanted movement during prostate MRI scans, which is a type of detailed imaging test that takes pictures inside the body. The study included thirty-three patients who each had two separate MRI scans of their prostate at the same facility, with one scan given glucagon beforehand and the other scan without it, and three experienced doctors reviewed the quality of the images from both scans. When looking at all the patients together, the researchers found no significant difference between the scans with and without glucagon, but they noticed that the benefit of glucagon seemed to depend on how long each scan took. When they separated the patients into groups based on scan length, they discovered that glucagon noticeably improved image quality, reduced motion artifacts or blurriness, and was preferred by the doctors when the glucagon scan took no more than one and a quarter times longer than the non-glucagon scan. This finding suggests that glucagon injections can help improve prostate MRI image quality, but the benefit decreases when scans take longer, which is useful information for hospitals deciding whether to use this medication during routine prostate.

llm_summary: Background:  Chronic kidney disease, which is a long-term condition where the kidneys gradually lose their ability to filter waste from the blood, affects millions of older adults and often leads to complications that impact their daily functioning and quality of life. Systemic inflammation, meaning widespread swelling and immune system activation throughout the body, is increasingly recognized as an important factor that may interfere with how well older patients with kidney disease can recover their physical abilities and independence during hospital stays.

title: Non-Invasive Assessment of Continuous Real-Time Workplace Stress Among Surgeons and Surgical Trainees: A Scoping Review.
abstract: To describe how physiological parameters were used to characterize continuous, real-time workplace stress among surgeons and surgical trainees, and to identify the advantages and disadvantages of using wearable devices.We conducted a scoping review to examine how wearable devices were used to objectively measure surgeons' and trainees' physiological stress in the workplace. Peer-reviewed English articles published up to September 2023 in Medline (Ovid), Cochrane Library (Wiley), Embase (Elsevier), and PsycINFO (Ebsco) databases using wearable devices used to measure continuous, real-time physiological parameters representing workplace stress among surgeons and surgical trainees were included in the review.We included studies that assessed physiological stress in the workplace (e.g., operating room and other clinical environments).Surgeons and surgical trainees.A review of 61 articles that met inclusion criteria revealed that the most commonly used wearable devices were Polar 13 (21.3%), Medilog: 6 (9.8%), Holter ECG device: 7 (11.5%), and WHOOP! : 6 (9.8%). Physiological parameters used to measure continuous, real-time workplace stress were heart rate, heart rate variability, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and electrodermal activity. Physiological parameters indicated that surgeons were more stressed in the operating room than in other clinical environments. Intraoperative surgeons' stress increased with performing critical steps of the operation, teaching a trainee, the number of intraoperative events, e.g., bleeding, and decreased with years of experience. There was a negative relationship between stress and the surgeon's intraoperative performance. The advantages of using wearable devices' physiologic parameters were objectivity, longitudinal measurement, and minimally obtrusive. The disadvantages were short battery life, inadequate data capture, artifacts, and data loss.Wearable devices can measure a range of physiological parameters that represent workplace stress continuously among surgeons and surgical trainees.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined how wearable devices, which are small electronic sensors worn on the body, can measure stress levels in surgeons and surgical trainees by tracking physical signs like heart rate and breathing patterns. The study reviewed 61 published research articles that used devices such as heart rate monitors and activity trackers to continuously measure stress in real time while doctors worked in operating rooms and other clinical settings. The findings showed that surgeons experienced the most stress during surgery, especially when performing difficult steps of an operation or teaching a trainee, and that stress levels decreased as surgeons gained more experience over their careers. The research revealed that wearable devices can objectively track stress in an ongoing way without being too intrusive, though they have drawbacks like short battery life and sometimes losing or misrecording data. These results suggest that wearable technology could be a useful tool for understanding and managing workplace stress among surgeons, though more research is needed to improve the devices and determine the best ways to use this information in practice.

title: Sex-specific associations between frailty and long-term outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction: a national population-based study.
abstract: Frailty and female sex are both recognised independent predictors of adverse outcomes after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). While females presenting with AMI are known to have a higher burden of frailty than males, it is unknown whether this fully explains sex-based disparities in outcomes, or if the prognostic impact of frailty itself differs between the sexes.We conducted a retrospective national cohort study using data from the Myocardial Ischaemia National Audit Project (MINAP), linked to hospital admission and mortality registries in England and Wales between 2005 and 2019. Frailty was assessed using the Secondary Care Administrative Records Frailty (SCARF) index and categorised as fit, mild, moderate, or severe. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used with a primary outcome of all-cause mortality at 1-year.Of 931,133 patients with AMI, 317,967 (34.1%) were female. Frailty was more prevalent in females than in males (severe frailty: 53,065 [16.7%] vs. 64,018 [10.4%]). Males received more intensive therapeutic care across all frailty levels. After multivariable adjustment, the relationship between severe frailty and 1-year all-cause mortality was 26% greater in males than in females (relative hazard ratio [rHR]: 1.26, 95% CI 1.19-1.32, P-interaction <0.001). This corresponded to an adjusted absolute risk difference of 1.19% (95% CI 0.58%-1.79%).In this national AMI cohort, while frailty was more prevalent in females, its association with 1-year mortality was significantly greater in males. This sex-specific effect of frailty challenges current risk-assessment paradigms and underscores the need for sex-informed care pathways.National Institute for Health and Care Research and British Heart Foundation Centre of Research Excellence, Leicester.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether frailty, a condition where people become physically weak and vulnerable, affects men and women differently after a heart attack, since both frailty and being female are known to increase the risk of serious complications. The study looked at data from over 930,000 heart attack patients in England and Wales between 2005 and 2019, using hospital records to measure frailty levels and track patients for one year after their heart attack. The results showed that while women had higher rates of frailty than men, the impact of severe frailty on death risk was actually 26 percent greater in men than in women during the first year after a heart attack. This surprising finding suggests that doctors may need to rethink how they assess risk and create treatment plans for heart attack patients, taking into account that frailty affects men and women differently rather than assuming the same risk applies to both sexes. The study highlights the importance of developing personalized care approaches based on sex and frailty status to better predict outcomes and improve survival rates for all heart attack patients.

title: Magnetoencephalography in Epilepsy: Role and Principles.
abstract: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) is a clinical neurophysiological diagnostic test that is noninvasive, passive, simple, and painless for the patient, and which provides precise localization of epileptic activity. Like electroencephalography (EEG), MEG is a direct measure of neuronal activity with very high temporal resolution, enabling the study of propagation but with a much higher spatial resolution than EEG. For guidance of stereo-electroencephalography electrode implantation, MEG has become an indispensable precursor, which is then incorporated with all of the other localizing data into the planning of surgical or ablative procedures.Copyright © 2025 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Magnetoencephalography, or MEG, is a brain imaging test that doctors use to find where seizures start in patients with epilepsy by measuring the magnetic signals produced by brain cells. This test is noninvasive, meaning it does not require any needles or surgery, and it is completely painless and safe for patients to undergo. MEG works similarly to another brain test called electroencephalography or EEG, but MEG can pinpoint the exact location of seizure activity much more precisely because it has better spatial resolution, which means it can see smaller areas of the brain in greater detail. Doctors have found that MEG is essential for planning brain surgery or other treatments in epilepsy patients, especially when they need to place special electrodes inside the brain to gather more information before performing surgery. By combining MEG results with other types of brain imaging and testing information, doctors can make better decisions about which surgical or ablation procedures, which use heat or cold to destroy problem tissue, will work best for each individual patient.

title: Database of CLCN5 Pathogenic Variants Causing Dent Disease.
abstract: Dent disease type 1 is an X-linked proximal tubulopathy caused by pathogenic variants in CLCN5, which encodes the chloride/proton exchanger, ClC-5. Loss of ClC-5 function disrupts receptor-mediated endocytosis, resulting in low-molecular-weight proteinuria, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, nephrolithiasis, and progressive kidney failure. Although many CLCN5 variants have been reported, existing resources remain incomplete, inconsistent, or based on different reference sequences (RefSeqs), thereby hindering variant comparison and clinical interpretation. A comprehensive and uniformly annotated catalog is needed to improve diagnostic accuracy and estimates of Dent disease type 1 prevalence.Potentially pathogenic CLCN5 variants were compiled from firsthand Dent disease type 1 case reports, variant databases, Dent disease type 1-related online resources, and unpublished patients. Variants representing experimental constructs or benign or likely benign changes were excluded. All variants were standardized using The Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) nomenclature and mapped to RefSeqs NM_001127898.4 and NM_000084.5 using Mutalyzer. Pathogenicity was assessed and cross-validated with the literature and public databases.We identified 524 unique pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, exceeding all existing databases. Variant types included missense (31%), InDel insertions and deletions (37%), nonsense (14%), splicing defects (13%), and large deletions (5%). Most variants (74%) were reported only once. Exon 10 (NM_001127898.4) showed the highest density of pathogenic variants, driven by missense and in-frame insertions and deletions (InDel). Structural mapping revealed functional restrained regions in Helix H and O-Q helices. Source-variant counts indicated a minimum of 880 affected families, suggesting approximately 3520 globally.This uniformly annotated catalog-the most comprehensive to date-enhances interpretation of CLCN5 variants, refines Dent disease type 1 burden estimates, and identifies key functional regions relevant for therapeutic development.© 2026 International Society of Nephrology. llm_summary: Dent disease type 1 is a rare inherited kidney disorder caused by mutations in a gene called CLCN5, which normally helps kidney cells filter waste and reabsorb important proteins from urine. Researchers compiled information about 524 different genetic mutations known to cause this disease by searching medical literature, genetic databases, and patient records, then organized all this information using a standard naming system so doctors could easily compare and understand the mutations. The study found that most mutations were unique to individual families, with certain parts of the gene being more prone to damage than others, and identified at least 880 families worldwide affected by this condition. This comprehensive catalog will help doctors more accurately diagnose Dent disease type 1 in patients and better understand how common the disease really is globally. The research also pinpoints specific regions of the gene that are critical for normal function, which could guide scientists in developing new treatments for this serious kidney condition.

title: Impact of area deprivation index on outcomes and health care utilization following shoulder arthroplasty: a systematic review.
abstract: Socioeconomic factors play a critical role in shaping health care outcomes, yet their impact on surgical recovery and post-operative quality of life is often underexplored. The Area Deprivation Index (ADI) is a validated metric used to quantify socioeconomic disadvantage, providing insight into disparities in health care access and outcomes. Despite its relevance, the extent of ADI score reporting in the context of shoulder arthroplasty (SA) remains unclear. This systematic review assesses the extent to which ADI has been incorporated into SA studies and examines its association with post-operative outcomes and health care utilization.A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant search of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase was conducted using the keywords "area deprivation index," "shoulder arthroplasty," and "outcomes." Eligible studies, published in English within the past 10 years, included randomized controlled trials and cohort studies reporting ADI or related socioeconomic metrics in SA populations, focusing on post-operative outcomes, complications, health care utilization, and readmissions. We excluded studies that did not involve SA or failed to report ADI. In addition, case reports, reviews, editorials, conference abstracts, and non-English publications were excluded.Eight studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 264,287 patients. Socioeconomic disadvantage, as measured by the ADI, was associated with lower pre-operative and post-operative functional scores, with 2 studies reporting significantly worse ASES scores in the most disadvantaged groups (P < .01). Readmission rates showed mixed findings; one study found higher odds of readmission in the most disadvantaged group (odds ratio = 1.56, P = .001), while others reported no significant association. Two studies identified a modest but significant increase in post-operative complications among disadvantaged patients (odds ratio range: 1.1-1.13, P < .005). Heterogeneity in ADI stratification and outcome reporting limited quantitative synthesis.Socioeconomic disadvantage, as measured by the ADI, is associated with worse functional outcomes following shoulder arthroplasty. Patients from the most disadvantaged neighborhoods had lower pre-operative and post-operative patient-reported outcome measures, while findings on readmissions and complications were not consistent amongst studies. Integrating ADI into clinical decision-making may help identify at-risk patients and reduce disparities in SA outcomes.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether neighborhood poverty and disadvantage affect how well people recover after shoulder replacement surgery, since wealthier and poorer communities often have different access to healthcare. The team searched medical databases for studies published in the last ten years that tracked shoulder surgery patients and measured their socioeconomic status, which is a way of describing someone's income level and neighborhood resources. They found eight studies involving over 264,000 patients, and the results showed that people from the poorest neighborhoods had worse recovery scores before and after surgery, though findings about hospital readmissions and complications were mixed across different studies. The research suggests that doctors should pay attention to a patient's neighborhood and economic situation when planning shoulder surgery, because this information could help identify patients who might struggle with recovery and need extra support. Future studies need to use more consistent methods for measuring socioeconomic disadvantage so researchers can better understand and reduce these unfair differences in surgical outcomes.

title: Osteoblastoma of the Middle Phalanx of the Hand Initially Diagnosed as Melorheostosis.
abstract: Osteoblastoma of the hand is a rare tumor that is difficult to diagnose. We present a right-handed, 5-year-old boy who presented with pain and edema about the middle phalanx of the right long finger. He was initially diagnosed with melorheostosis and treated with observation then curettage and bone grafting. The patient experienced recurrence with pathology consistent with osteoblastoma, with this being the first report of osteoblastoma of the middle phalanx of the hand. He ultimately was treated with long finger ray amputation. Ray amputation of the long finger was a successful treatment in this patient.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Osteoblastoma, which is a type of noncancerous bone tumor, is extremely rare when it occurs in the hand and can be very difficult for doctors to identify correctly. A five-year-old boy came to the hospital with pain and swelling in the middle bone of his right index finger, and doctors initially thought he had a different bone condition called melorheostosis, so they first tried watching and waiting and then performed surgery to scrape out the affected area and fill it with bone graft material. After the boy's symptoms returned, doctors performed more testing and discovered that he actually had osteoblastoma, making this the first documented case of this tumor appearing in the middle finger bone of the hand. The medical team decided that the best treatment was to remove the entire finger through a procedure called ray amputation, which means taking out the finger along with its connecting bones in the hand. This case shows that ray amputation can be an effective solution for treating osteoblastoma in the hand when other treatments do not work.

title: Advancing Peripheral Nerve Regeneration (Nerve SPACE 2025).
abstract: Peripheral nerve injuries remain a major clinical challenge due to slow axonal regeneration, rapid Wallerian degeneration (WD), and degeneration of target organs prior to reinnervation.Strategies to enhance regeneration can be broadly divided into three categories: preventing or delaying WD, speeding up axonal regeneration, and improving the molecular environment at the injury site. Approaches to delay WD include polyethylene glycol-mediated axonal fusion, which may restore early axonal continuity and conduction, and inhibition of sterile alpha and TIR motif-containing 1, the central executioner of WD, with small-molecule inhibitors now in clinical trials. Methods to accelerate axon regrowth include brief intraoperative electrical stimulation, which activates regeneration-associated gene programs and improves motor and sensory recovery in both preclinical and early clinical studies, and pharmacologic augmentation with 4-aminopyridine, which enhances conduction across demyelinated fibers and promotes remyelination.Optimizing the local microenvironment through cellular and molecular adjuncts, including mesenchymal stem cells, Schwann cells, exosomes, surgical angiogenesis, and local delivery of neuroregenerative drugs such as FK506, has also shown promise in experimental models. Across all approaches, progress is hindered by heterogeneous outcome measures, a lack of standardized protocols, and barriers to multicenter collaboration.Coordinated efforts among academia, industry, and regulatory agencies are needed to standardize methodologies, develop objective outcome measures, and enable well-structured multicenter clinical trials to achieve meaningful clinical translation. Ultimately, meaningful functional recovery will depend on integrating complementary approaches and bridging gaps in mechanistic understanding, delivery systems, and trial design, creating the synergy needed to translate promising therapies from bench to bedside.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Peripheral nerve injuries, which occur when nerves in the arms, legs, and other parts of the body are damaged, are difficult to treat because nerves heal slowly and the muscles and skin they control can deteriorate before healing is complete. Researchers reviewed three main strategies to improve nerve healing: preventing the breakdown of damaged nerve fibers, speeding up the growth of new nerve connections, and creating a better chemical environment around the injury site. The most promising approaches include using electrical stimulation during surgery to activate healing genes, applying a special substance called polyethylene glycol to reconnect severed nerve fibers, and using stem cells or other biological materials to support nerve regrowth. However, the field faces major obstacles because different studies use different methods to measure success, there are no standard procedures that all doctors follow, and hospitals struggle to work together on large research projects. To move these treatments from laboratory discoveries into actual patient care, doctors, companies, and government agencies need to work together to create consistent testing methods, develop better ways to measure results, and run large organized clinical trials that prove these therapies truly help patients recover function.

title: Characterization of adrenal masses in young adults at a tertiary care academic medical center.
abstract: Evidence on the etiology and function of adrenal masses in younger adults is scarce.This work aimed to characterize the clinical, imaging, and biochemical presentation of adrenal masses in 18- to 40-year-olds.A retrospective cohort study was conducted January 2016 to December 2021 at a tertiary academic medical center. Participants included young adults (age 18-40 years) with adrenal masses identified through radiologic registry. Exclusion criteria included preexisting adrenal masses before 2016, hyperplasia, or masses smaller than 1 cm. Outcomes included adrenal mass diagnosis, as determined by reference standard of histopathology, radiologic surveillance, and biochemical evaluation.A total of 255 patients (women 142 [56%]; White 156 [61%]; median age 35 years [interquartile range 30-39 years]) were included. Comorbidities included genetic predisposition syndromes (16, 6.3%), preexisting malignancy (70, 27%), obesity (100, 48%), hypertension (89, 35%), and diabetes (25, 10%). The majority of adrenal masses were incidentally found (184, 72%) and median size was 1.9 cm (IQR 1.4-2.7 cm) on detection. Among adrenal masses in young adults, prevalence of malignancy and pheochromocytoma was 16% and 4%, respectively; among adrenal incidentalomas, 5% were malignant. Factors associated with malignancy or pheochromocytoma in multivariable analysis included nonincidental mechanism of discovery (odds ratio [OR] 15.5; 95% CI, 7.2-35.7; P < .001), and larger size (OR 1.5; 95% CI, 1.2-2.0; P < .001). Hormonal evaluation was performed in only 57 (22%) patients and was positive for hormone hypersecretion in 16 (28%) of tested individuals.We demonstrated a high prevalence of malignancy and pheochromocytoma in our cohort of young adults with adrenal masses. Completion of appropriate hormonal work-up was infrequent, potentially missing patients with functioning adrenal adenomas.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined adrenal masses, which are growths on the small glands that sit on top of the kidneys, in young adults between ages eighteen and forty because little information exists about these growths in younger people. The study looked back at medical records from two thousand sixteen to two thousand twenty-one for two hundred fifty-five young adults who had adrenal masses found through imaging scans, checking their medical histories, imaging results, and hormone levels to determine what type of growth each person had. The researchers discovered that sixteen percent of the adrenal masses were cancerous and four percent were a specific type of tumor called pheochromocytoma, with cancer being less common when masses were found by accident rather than during investigation for other reasons. The study found that hormonal testing, which checks whether these growths are producing excess hormones, was only done in about one out of five patients, meaning doctors may have missed some patients with functioning tumors that produce harmful hormones. These findings suggest that young adults with adrenal masses need more thorough hormone testing and careful monitoring, especially when masses are discovered through symptoms rather than by chance.

title: Donor-derived Cell-free DNA for Detection of Rejection After Pancreas Transplantation.
abstract: Donor-derived cell-free DNA (dd-cfDNA) has emerged as a promising noninvasive biomarker for detecting allograft rejection in solid organ transplantation. However, its diagnostic utility in pancreas transplantation, including in multiorgan recipients, remains underexplored.We conducted a retrospective analysis of 42 pancreas transplant recipients (38 simultaneous pancreas-kidney, 4 pancreas transplant alone) who underwent for-cause organ biopsy and dd-cfDNA testing between April 2020 and December 2024. dd-cfDNA was measured using the Prospera assay, with a threshold of ≥1% considered high risk and <1% low-risk. Biopsy results were correlated with dd-cfDNA to assess test performance.A total of 50 dd-cfDNA tests and 45 organ biopsies were analyzed. Among simultaneous pancreas-kidney recipients, dd-cfDNA demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.7%, specificity of 52.2%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 54.2%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 85.7% for rejection. In pancreas transplant alone recipients, all high-risk dd-cfDNA results corresponded to biopsy-proven rejection, yielding 100% sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV. When combining both cohorts, dd-cfDNA testing achieved an overall sensitivity of 88.2%, specificity of 57.7%, PPV of 57.7%, and NPV of 88.2%. Additionally, dd-cfDNA kinetics suggested its potential utility as a surveillance tool posttreatment, potentially reducing the need for closure biopsies.dd-cfDNA is a valuable noninvasive adjunct for monitoring of rejection in pancreas transplant recipients. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a simple blood test measuring donor-derived cell-free DNA, which are tiny fragments of genetic material from a transplanted organ that leak into the bloodstream, could help detect rejection in pancreas transplant patients without needing invasive biopsies. The study looked back at 42 pancreas transplant recipients who had both the blood test and tissue biopsies performed between 2020 and 2024 to see how well the blood test could predict rejection. The blood test showed strong results, correctly identifying rejection in about 88 percent of cases overall, with particularly excellent performance in patients who received only a pancreas transplant rather than multiple organs. These findings suggest that donor-derived cell-free DNA could become a valuable tool for monitoring transplant patients and potentially reduce the need for painful biopsy procedures to check for rejection. The researchers emphasized that while these results are promising, larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings and determine the best way to use this blood test in everyday transplant care.

title: Comparison of coronary computed tomography angiography to invasive coronary angiography for coronary allograft vasculopathy surveillance in patients with orthotopic heart transplant.
abstract: Invasive coronary angiography (ICA) is considered the gold standard for diagnosing coronary allograft vasculopathy (CAV) in post orthotopic heart transplant (OHT) patients. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) has been used as an alternative modality, but outcome studies comparing CCTA to ICA are limited.We studied consecutive OHT patients who underwent CCTA (n = 38) from January 2010 to January 2024 and compared them to an age- and sex-matched cohort who underwent ICA (n = 76). The outcomes of interest were clinical events (death, myocardial infarction, heart failure, and stroke) and testing-related adverse events or complications at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included test characteristics of CCTA in patients who also underwent ICA within 90 days (paired subgroup, n = 20).Baseline characteristics were similar between CCTA and ICA groups. CAV presence was similar between groups (CCTA: 8/38 [21%], ICA: 20/76 [26%], p = 0.54). There were 4 adverse events in the ICA group (coronary spasm [n = 1], access-site bleeding [n = 2], and radial artery spasm [n = 1]) and none in the CCTA group. Clinical events occurred in 16% (6/38) of the CCTA group vs 7% (5/76) of the ICA group (OR 2.74, 95% CI, 0.77-10.13, p = 0.12). In the paired subgroup, CCTA demonstrated adequate diagnostic capabilities for the detection of CAV (accuracy 95%, sensitivity 75%, specificity 100%, positive predictive value 100%, negative predictive value 94%).CCTA showed strong agreement with ICA for CAV detection and severity assessment. CCTA may emerge as a safer, noninvasive alternative to ICA for CAV assessment.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a newer imaging test called coronary computed tomography angiography, which uses special X-ray scans to look at heart blood vessels, could safely replace the traditional invasive procedure called coronary angiography, which involves inserting a tube into blood vessels to check for damage in transplanted hearts. The study compared 38 heart transplant patients who received the newer scan to 76 similar patients who received the traditional procedure, tracking whether either group experienced serious health problems or complications from the test itself over one year. The newer scan detected heart vessel damage at similar rates as the traditional procedure, found no complications in patients who received it compared to four complications in the traditional procedure group, and showed strong accuracy when both tests were performed on the same patients within three months. These results suggest that the newer scanning method could become a safer option for monitoring transplanted hearts since it avoids the risks of inserting tubes into blood vessels while still detecting problems just as well. Future research should continue comparing these two approaches in larger groups of patients to confirm whether hospitals can routinely use the newer scan instead of the traditional invasive procedure for checking transplanted heart health.

Doctors must decide whether to perform this balancing surgery on the unaffected breast immediately during the same operation or wait until a later date, and this choice can affect both the surgical outcomes and the patient's recovery experience.

title: Primary peripheral nerve repair: A systematic review of sutures, fibrin glue, and biologic-augmented approaches.
abstract: Fibrin glue neurorrhaphy (FGN) has demonstrated functional improvements for traumatic peripheral nerve injuries (PNI) in preclinical studies; however, evidence regarding its clinical effectiveness in humans remains limited. Recent advances in regenerative medicine, particularly involving biologics such as platelet-rich plasma (PRP), represent an innovative therapeutic strategy that leverages its neuroprotective, anti-inflammatory, and immunomodulatory effects as well as trophic support for tissue regeneration. To assess the safety and effectiveness of these approaches, we conducted a systematic review comparing FGN and microsuture neurorrhaphy (MN), used either individually or in combination with biologics, for primary peripheral nerve repair.Systematic literature searches were conducted across multiple databases from 1990 to 2025 in accordance with PRISMA guidelines, and the protocol was registered with PROSPERO. The primary outcome of interest was motor and sensory functional recovery and safety. Other outcomes included neurophysiological examinations, pain or discomfort and operating time. The Revised Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool for Randomized Trials(RoB2) and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale(NOS) were used to assess the risk of bias.A total of 164 patients from six studies were included. The mean patient age was 31.43 years, and 61.6% were female. Compared with MN, FGN achieved comparable motor and sensory recovery while offering shorter operative times and simpler technical execution. When combined with PRP, faster functional recovery was observed, and no major complications were reported.FGN may represent a sutureless alternative to MN with comparable functional outcomes in selected patients for primary peripheral nerve repair. The adjunctive use of PRP may facilitate nerve regeneration and improve functional recovery without introducing major safety concerns. However, given the heterogeneity of nerve types and the high risk of bias among included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and require confirmation in adequately powered future studies.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Nerve injuries from accidents and trauma can cause lasting damage, and doctors need better ways to repair them beyond traditional stitching methods. Researchers reviewed six studies involving 164 patients to compare three repair approaches: traditional microsutures (tiny stitches), fibrin glue (a biological adhesive), and these methods combined with platelet-rich plasma (a concentration of healing cells from a patient's own blood). The results showed that fibrin glue worked just as well as traditional stitches for restoring movement and feeling, while taking less time in surgery and being simpler to perform. When doctors added platelet-rich plasma to either repair method, patients recovered their nerve function faster without experiencing serious complications. However, the researchers warned that the studies they reviewed had significant limitations and inconsistent results, so more rigorous testing is needed before these approaches become standard practice in hospitals.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Endoscopic Adenoma and Cancer Detection.
abstract: Colorectal cancer incidence and mortality have declined over time, due in part to high-quality screening and surveillance colonoscopy. Nevertheless, postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer (PCCRC) occurs in up to 7% of cases and is inversely related to examination quality. Artificial intelligence-assisted colonoscopy aims to improve performance metrics and, ultimately, patient outcomes. Multiple randomized trials show that computer-aided polyp detection (CADe) increases adenoma detection, predominantly for diminutive lesions (≤5 mm). Computer-aided polyp characterization (CADx) enables real-time optical diagnosis, potentially shifting management of diminutive polyps by supporting resect-and-discard and diagnose-and-leave in situ strategies. Computer-aided quality assessment (CAQ) systems monitor key metrics-including cecal intubation rate, withdrawal time, speed, and mucosal exposure. Whether CADe alone leads to a reduction in PCCRC or cancer-related mortality remains to be determined; in the near term, a combined approach using CADe, CADx, and CAQ is most likely to deliver the greatest improvements in patient outcomes.Thieme. llm_summary: Colorectal cancer deaths have been dropping thanks to better screening methods, but some cancers still develop after a colonoscopy procedure, which happens in up to 7 percent of cases and is linked to how well the doctor performs the exam. Researchers studied how artificial intelligence can help doctors during colonoscopies by using computer programs to detect polyps (small growths in the colon), identify what type they are, and monitor the quality of the procedure itself. Multiple studies showed that computer-aided detection increased the number of small polyps found, especially tiny ones measuring five millimeters or smaller, while computer-aided characterization allowed doctors to make real-time decisions about whether to remove or leave polyps in place. These artificial intelligence tools could improve patient outcomes by catching more dangerous growths and helping doctors decide which polyps need to be removed and which ones are safe to leave alone. The researchers concluded that using all three types of artificial intelligence tools together—detection, characterization, and quality monitoring—will likely provide the best results for patients, though more research is needed to prove that these tools actually reduce cancer deaths.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and GLP-1 Receptor Agonists After Acute Kidney Injury: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Sodium glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are nephroprotective and their use is recommended for adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The role of SGLT2i and GLP-1 RAs in patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) is unknown. This systematic review aimed to estimate the effect of SGLT2i or GLP-1 RAs on clinical outcomes in AKI. We systematically searched Embase, MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and clinical trials registries for observational studies and clinical trials from database inception to July 3, 2025. Included studies evaluated adults (≥ 18 years) with AKI during a hospitalization and compared patients subsequently exposed to either SGLT2i or GLP-1 RAs to a non-exposed control group. Random effects meta-analyses were performed. Six studies related to SGLT2i (five observational, one randomized trial) and one related to GLP-1 RAs (one observational) met eligibility criteria (N = 432,048 patients). SGLT2i/GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with lower odds of major adverse kidney events (MAKE) (OR 0.63, 95% CI 0.46-0.86) and all-cause mortality [odds ratio (OR) 0.36, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.21-0.62] compared to controls. The odds for kidney replacement therapy were lower with SGLT2i therapy in the three studies where it was evaluated (OR 0.61, 95% CI 0.40-0.93). Sensitivity analyses restricted to SGLT2i data were consistent with the overall findings [MAKE OR 0.63 (95% CI 0.42-0.95); Mortality OR 0.34 (95% CI 0.18, 0.65)]. Exposure to SGLT2i or GLP-1 RAs after AKI, examined primarily in observational studies, was associated with improved clinical outcomes. These findings are promising and warrant evaluation in randomized clinical trials.© 2026 ACCP Foundation, Ltd.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether two types of diabetes and kidney disease medications called SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists could help patients who experienced acute kidney injury, which is a sudden loss of kidney function during hospitalization. The team searched medical databases for studies comparing patients who received these medications after their kidney injury to patients who did not receive them, finding seven studies involving over 432,000 patients total. Patients who took these medications after acute kidney injury had significantly better outcomes, including lower rates of major kidney problems, lower death rates, and less need for kidney replacement therapy compared to those who did not take the medications. These findings suggest that these medications may help protect the kidneys and improve survival in people recovering from acute kidney injury, though most of the evidence came from observational studies rather than rigorous controlled trials. The researchers concluded that while these results are encouraging, larger and more carefully controlled studies are needed to confirm whether these medications should become standard treatment for patients recovering from acute kidney injury.

title: Menopausal hormone therapy and breast cancer: Balancing risks and benefits.
abstract: Menopausal hormone therapy remains the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and plays an important role in the prevention of bone loss and fractures. When initiated earlier in menopause, hormone therapy may have some favorable cardiovascular effects, though it is not recommended for cardiovascular disease prevention. Although these benefits are established, perceptions of safety have long been shaped by concerns about breast cancer risk. Evidence accumulated over the past two decades has helped to refine our understanding of the risk of breast cancer associated with hormone therapy, showing that risk varies by hormone therapy formulation, duration of use, and patient-specific factors. For example, combined estrogen-progestogen therapy has been associated with a higher risk of developing breast cancer while estrogen-alone therapy has been linked to reductions in both breast cancer incidence and mortality. The choice of progestogen also matters, with observational evidence indicating that micronized progesterone may have a more favorable breast cancer risk profile than some synthetic progestins. Beyond regimen and duration of use, outcomes are further influenced by timing of initiation and route of administration, underscoring the importance of tailoring therapy to the individual. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the benefits and risks of hormone therapy with a focus on breast cancer and risk modifiers to guide evidence-based clinical decision-making in menopause management. llm_summary: Menopausal hormone therapy is the most effective treatment available for hot flashes and night sweats that women experience during menopause, and it also helps prevent bone loss and broken bones, though many women worry about whether it increases breast cancer risk. Researchers reviewed decades of scientific evidence to understand how different types of hormone therapy affect the risk of developing breast cancer and found that the risk depends on several factors including which specific hormones are used, how long a woman takes the therapy, and her individual health characteristics. The study showed that when estrogen and a synthetic progestin are combined, breast cancer risk goes up, but when estrogen is used alone, breast cancer cases and deaths actually decreased, and using a natural form of progesterone called micronized progesterone appeared safer than some man-made versions. The timing of when a woman starts hormone therapy, how she takes it (such as by pill or patch), and her personal medical history all matter significantly in determining whether the benefits outweigh the risks for her specific situation. This review highlights that doctors need to carefully consider each woman's individual circumstances and the latest evidence when deciding whether hormone therapy is the right choice, and it identifies areas where more research is still.

title: Treatment-specific prognostic performance of ELN 2022, ELN 2024, and Beat AML 2024: a real-world AML validation study.
abstract: Real-world validation of the European LeukemiaNet (ELN) 2022, ELN 2024, and Beat Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) 2024 across different therapies is needed. We evaluated 426 patients with AML (median age, 68 years; 60% male) treated from 2016 to 2025. ELN 2024 (55%, 24%, and 20%), ELN 2022 (20%, 20%, and 60%), and Beat AML 2024 (21%, 38%, and 41%) assigned patients to favorable-, intermediate-, and adverse-risk groups with variation. Less-intensive treatment (LIT) had lower complete remission (CR) odds than intensive chemotherapy (IC). For CR prediction, ELN 2022 (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.763) and Beat AML 2024 (AUC, 0.759) outperformed ELN 2024 (AUC, 0.718). With a median follow-up of 49.8 months, the median overall survival (mOS) was 15.7 months. Each system stratified mOS (all P < .001); overall c-index favored ELN 2022 (0.640) and Beat AML 2024 (0.635) over ELN 2024 (0.601). For patients treated with IC, ELN 2022 (0.680) and Beat AML 2024 (0.664) exceeded ELN 2024 (0.601); for patients treated with LIT, ELN 2024 and Beat AML 2024 identified a favorable group with better mOS, whereas ELN 2022 failed to discriminate between favorable and intermediate risk. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation improved mOS; in time-dependent analysis, adverse risk by Beat AML 2024 (hazard ratio [HR], 4.0), ELN 2024 (HR, 3.0), and ELN 2022 (HR, 2.5) remained independently unfavorable. Overall, Beat AML 2024 was the most informative in IC, and ELN 2024/Beat AML 2024 better identified favorable patients in LIT.© 2026 American Society of Hematology. Published by Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers examined how well three different risk classification systems work for predicting outcomes in acute myeloid leukemia, a serious blood cancer, because doctors need accurate tools to guide treatment decisions. The study evaluated 426 patients with this cancer who received various treatments between 2016 and 2025, comparing how three scoring systems (ELN 2022, ELN 2024, and Beat AML 2024) categorized patients into risk groups and predicted their chances of responding to treatment and surviving. The results showed that the older ELN 2022 system and the newer Beat AML 2024 system were better at predicting treatment response and overall survival compared to the ELN 2024 system, though the performance varied depending on whether patients received intensive chemotherapy or less intensive treatments. For patients receiving intensive chemotherapy, Beat AML 2024 performed best, while for patients receiving gentler treatments, both ELN 2024 and Beat AML 2024 better identified patients with favorable outcomes, suggesting that different risk systems may work better for different treatment approaches. title: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis regimen for patients undergoing deep inferior epigastric perforator flap breast reconstruction.
abstract: Patients undergoing deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flap breast reconstruction are at increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE) due to prolonged operative times, cancer-associated hypercoagulability, and postoperative immobility. Despite this risk, consensus is limited regarding standardized prophylaxis regimens for this population. We assessed VTE incidence in patients undergoing DIEP flap breast reconstruction after implementing a standardized, multimodal VTE prophylaxis regimen.We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent DIEP flap breast reconstruction at our institution between October 2021 and July 2024. Patients were subjected to a standardized VTE prophylaxis regimen including preoperative education and subcutaneous heparin injection, intraoperative efficiency techniques, and a postoperative protocol consisting of early ambulation, sequential compression devices, compressive garments, and a 2-week course of enoxaparin sodium. Patient characteristics, operative details, and VTE outcomes were analyzed.In a cohort of 110 patients, 187 DIEP flap reconstruction procedures were performed by one surgeon. Mean patient age was 49.3 years, and mean body mass index was 29.7. The VTE rate directly attributable to DIEP flap reconstruction was 0%. One VTE event occurred-an upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) 119 days postoperatively that was associated with intravenous access during a revision procedure. No lower-extremity DVTs or pulmonary embolisms were reported.Implementation of a standardized, comprehensive VTE prophylaxis regimen encompassing preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative measures can result in a remarkably low VTE rate in patients undergoing DIEP flap breast reconstruction. This safe, effective regimen may eliminate the need for risk-based pharmacologic stratification tools such as the Caprini model.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Patients who undergo deep inferior epigastric perforator flap breast reconstruction, a surgical procedure that uses tissue from the abdomen to rebuild the breast after cancer, face a higher risk of developing blood clots because of the long surgery time, cancer-related changes in blood chemistry, and reduced movement after the operation. Researchers looked back at records from 110 patients who had this surgery between October 2021 and July 2024 to see how well a comprehensive blood clot prevention plan worked, which included blood-thinning injections before surgery, special techniques during the operation, and medications plus compression devices after surgery. The study found that out of 187 surgical procedures performed, there were zero blood clots directly caused by the breast reconstruction surgery itself, with only one blood clot occurring much later and in a different context unrelated to the original operation. These results suggest that using a complete, step-by-step approach to prevent blood clots throughout the entire surgical process can be highly effective and may reduce the need for complicated risk assessment tools that doctors currently use to decide which patients need blood clot prevention medication. Future research should confirm whether this standardized prevention plan works equally well across different hospitals.

title: Efficacy and safety of hemostatic net in facelift and rejuvenation surgeries (browlift and necklift): A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Facelifts are commonly associated with postoperative complications. The hemostatic net has emerged as a promising approach to reduce these events. The aim of this meta-analysis was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the hemostatic net in facelift.The PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were systematically searched up to May 2025 for studies evaluating the hemostatic net in facelift and rejuvenation surgeries (browlift and necklift). Statistical analysis was performed using R version 4.4.1 with a random-effects model for single-arm meta-analysis, reporting outcomes per 100 observations. The primary outcome was hematoma incidence. Secondary outcomes included seroma, necrosis, ischemia, infection, hyperemic marks, persistent hyperpigmentation, and sensory deficits.Eight studies (1617 patients) were included. The outcomes incidences were hematoma: 0.14 per 100 (95% CI: 0.00 to 0.58; I² = 23.8%); seroma: 2.16 per 100 (95% CI: 0.00 to 9.32; I² = 85.4%); necrosis: 0.36 per 100 (95% CI: 0.00 to 1.14; I² = 3.4%); ischemia: 1.10 per 100 (95% CI: 0.00 to 6.56; I² = 94.7%); infection: 0.62 per 100 (95% CI: 0.00 to 4.35; I² = 70.4%); hyperemic marks: 12.70 per 100 (95% CI: 0.74 to 34.96; I² = 97.5%); persistent hyperpigmentation: 0 per 100 (95% CI: 0.00 to 0.14; I² = 0%); and sensory deficits: 0 per 100 (95% CI: 0.00 to 0.33; I² = 0%).Minimal incidence of hematoma, seroma, necrosis, ischemia, and infection was observed. llm_summary: Facelifts and similar facial rejuvenation surgeries often lead to unwanted side effects like bruising and fluid buildup, so doctors have been testing a special hemostatic net, which is a thin mesh designed to control bleeding and reduce complications. Researchers reviewed eight published studies involving 1,617 patients who had facelift, browlift, or necklift procedures using this hemostatic net technique and analyzed the rates of various complications that occurred after surgery. The results showed that the hemostatic net was very effective at preventing serious problems, with extremely low rates of bruising, fluid collection, tissue death, infection, and permanent nerve damage. The only notable side effect was temporary redness and marks on the skin that appeared in about 13 out of every 100 patients, but these marks completely disappeared within two to three months without causing any lasting discoloration. These findings suggest that the hemostatic net is a safe and effective tool for surgeons to use during facial rejuvenation procedures, though more research with larger patient groups would help confirm these promising results.

llm_summary: Background:  Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurring seizures, which are sudden bursts of electrical activity in the brain that can cause loss of consciousness, convulsions, or other symptoms. Advanced imaging techniques, which are specialized scanning methods that create detailed pictures of the brain, have become increasingly important tools for doctors to identify the specific areas of the brain causing seizures so they can plan the most effective treatments.

title: Implanted Devices for Management of Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: Background and MR Imaging Considerations.
abstract: Advances in the field of neuromodulation provide patients with medically refractory epilepsy without surgical options the possibility of effective alternative treatments. Three FDA approved electronic neuromodulation devices now exist, vagal nerve stimulation (VNS), responsive neurostimulation (RNS), and deep brain stimulation (DBS). MRI plays a central role in defining stimulation targets. Essential MR safety conditions must be strictly adhered to. Some situations require off-label MR scanning, such as the presence of more than one neuromodulation system or during MR guided therapy, (eg, laser interstitial thermal ablation). Active engagement of well-trained MR safety expert MR physicists is essential in these scenarios.Copyright © 2025 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Many people with epilepsy, a brain condition that causes seizures, cannot control their seizures with medication alone and need other treatment options. Researchers reviewed three electronic devices that have been approved by the FDA, the government agency that regulates medical devices, which can be implanted in the body to help reduce seizures through a process called neuromodulation, or stimulating specific nerves and brain areas. These three devices are vagal nerve stimulation, which stimulates a nerve in the neck, responsive neurostimulation, which detects and responds to abnormal brain activity, and deep brain stimulation, which sends electrical signals directly into the brain. The study emphasizes that magnetic resonance imaging, commonly called an MRI scan, is crucial for planning where to place these devices and that strict safety rules must be followed when patients with these implants undergo MRI scans. In complex situations where patients have multiple devices or need special imaging procedures, the researchers stress that highly trained MRI safety experts must be involved to protect patients from potential harm.

title: Neuroimaging and the Epilepsy Journey.
abstract: This article reviews the modern pathway of epilepsy care with a focus on how neuroimaging supports treatment decisions and guides surgical intervention for patients who are drug-resistant. The article details the roles of noninvasive and invasive diagnostic approaches including structural computed tomography and MR imaging, video-scalp electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring, PET, ictal/interictal single-photon emission computed tomography, magnetoencephalography, and invasive EEG monitoring, and it describes how these modalities are integrated to localize the epileptogenic zone and target surgical resection, laser ablation, or neuromodulation. A detailed case study illustrates the practical application of multimodal presurgical evaluation and stereoelectroencephalography-guided resection.Copyright © 2025 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Epilepsy is a serious brain condition where patients experience repeated seizures, and some people do not respond well to medication alone, making it crucial to find better ways to help them. This article reviews how doctors use different types of brain imaging and monitoring tools, such as MRI scans, special cameras that track brain activity called EEG monitors, and PET scans, to understand where seizures are starting in the brain. By combining information from multiple imaging and monitoring methods, doctors can pinpoint the exact area of the brain causing the seizures and decide whether surgery, laser treatment, or electrical stimulation devices would help the patient. The article includes a real patient example showing how doctors used advanced imaging and a special type of electrode monitoring called stereoelectroencephalography to guide surgical removal of the problem area in the brain. This comprehensive approach to using multiple imaging tools together helps doctors make better treatment decisions and improve outcomes for people with epilepsy who do not respond to medication.

title: The Association of p27 With Prostate Cancer Outcomes: A Secondary Analysis of NRG/RTOG 8610 and 9202.
abstract: The cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p27 is a well-profiled modulator of cell cycle progression. Low nuclear p27 levels have been demonstrated to have a negative prognostic impact on outcomes in patients undergoing prostatectomy. The prognostic value of p27 after radiation therapy (RT) for prostate cancer is unknown.Levels of p27 were evaluated in pre-RT prostate biopsy samples from 2 randomized, phase 3 trials, NRG/RTOG 8610 and 9202, which treated patients with RT with or without androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). Nuclear p27 was analyzed using immunohistochemistry and quantified using automated imaging analysis. The association of p27 as both a continuous and categorical measure (≤ median vs > median) with clinical outcome was estimated using both univariable (UVA) and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. The primary clinical outcome measure was overall survival, and secondary measures were disease-specific survival (DSS), disease-free survival, distant metastases, and biochemical failure.In the analytical cohort (n = 361), no association of p27 with overall survival was observed on UVA. The only statistically significant association observed on UVA was between categorical p27 high levels and DSS (hazard ratio [HR] 1.57 [95% CI, 1.01-2.43], P = .044) in the combined cohort. However, a similar association was not observed with DSS when analyzing continuous p27 (P = .09). On multivariable analyses, no statistically significant association was observed between p27 and any evaluated clinical outcome measure (all P > .05).This study produced insufficient evidence to conclude that nuclear p27 level is prognostic of outcome in patients undergoing RT ± ADT. The observed trend was opposite in direction to the prior observations in the postprostatectomy literature, which served as a basis for this study. Given this, these data generate the hypothesis that the negative prognostic value of low nuclear p27 level in patients undergoing prostatectomy may be obviated by the receipt of RT ± ADT. Although this does appear congruent with known mechanistic differences between the two treatments, further studies are required to confirm this finding.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a protein called p27, which controls how cancer cells divide, could predict treatment outcomes in prostate cancer patients receiving radiation therapy with or without hormone therapy. The study analyzed tissue samples collected before treatment from 361 patients enrolled in two large clinical trials, measuring p27 levels using a microscope-based imaging technique and then tracking patient outcomes over time. The results showed almost no meaningful connection between p27 levels and whether patients survived, remained cancer-free, or developed spreading cancer, with only one weak statistical finding that did not hold up when analyzed differently. Surprisingly, this finding contradicted earlier research in patients who had surgery instead of radiation, suggesting that radiation therapy might work differently than surgery and could eliminate any negative effects of low p27 levels. The researchers concluded that more studies are needed to understand whether p27 actually matters for predicting outcomes in radiation therapy patients, since their evidence was too weak to draw firm conclusions.

title: Liver transplantation is the major determinant of ≥10-year survival in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has a poor long-term prognosis due to high recurrence and cirrhosis-related mortality, even after potentially curative treatments such as liver transplantation (LT), surgical resection, or ablation. This study aimed to identify factors associated with ≥10-year survival in HCC patients.A retrospective cohort study was conducted among HCC patients diagnosed between 2004 and 2022 using the National Cancer Database. Multivariable Cox regression was used to identify predictors of overall survival, and logistic regression was used to identify predictors of ≥10-year survival.Among 249,600 HCC patients, 177,585 (71.2%) died within 5 years, 8613 (3.5%) died at 5-10 years, 54,988 (22.0%) were alive with <10 years of follow-up, and 8219 (3.3%) survived ≥10 years. LT, resection, and ablation were performed in 6.6%, 9.3%, and 11% of patients, respectively. Compared with ablation as the reference group, LT [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 11.96, 95% confidence interval (CI): 11.27-13.29] and resection (aOR: 2.83, 95% CI: 2.57-3.08) increased the odds of ≥10-year survival, while non-curative treatments reduced the odds compared with ablation (aOR: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.47-0.55). Cox regression results were consistent with the logistic model, confirming the association. Decision tree analysis confirmed LT as the dominant determinant of long-term survival. Black individuals were associated with lower odds of ≥10-year survival (aOR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.820-0.96) and decreased likelihood of receiving LT (aOR: 0.73, 95% CI: 0.55-0.96).LT offers the best chance of ≥10-year survival in HCC. Ensuring equitable access is essential, especially for Black patients who have lower transplant rates and worse outcomes.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma, a type of liver cancer, has very poor long-term survival rates because the disease often comes back and patients may develop serious liver damage even after treatment. Researchers examined data from nearly 250,000 liver cancer patients diagnosed between 2004 and 2022 to figure out which treatments helped people survive for at least ten years. They found that liver transplantation, which means replacing a diseased liver with a healthy one from a donor, was by far the best option for long-term survival, increasing the chances of living ten years or more by almost twelve times compared to ablation, a procedure that destroys cancer cells with heat or cold. The study also revealed an important problem: Black patients were less likely to receive liver transplants and had worse overall survival rates, suggesting that access to this life-saving treatment is not equal across different groups. These findings show that liver transplantation offers the best hope for long-term survival in liver cancer patients, and doctors and hospitals need to work harder to make sure all patients, especially Black patients, have fair access to this treatment option.

title: Current Concepts to Muscle-Based Procedures to Treat Upper Limb Spasticity: Shoulder and Elbow Deformities.
abstract: Muscle-based procedures have been the mainstay of surgical treatment of spastic upper limb deformities, in particular when muscle contractures are a main contributor to the deformity. The type of muscle-based procedures that are utilized to correct a spastic deformity is dependent upon the presence of volitional motor activation and the magnitude of muscle contracture. These procedures can markedly improve patient's quality of life and enhance upper limb function. llm_summary: Muscle-based surgical procedures have become the standard treatment for upper limb spasticity, which is a condition where muscles become stiff and contracted, particularly when muscle tightness is a major cause of deformity in the shoulder and elbow. The choice of which surgical procedure to use depends on two main factors: whether the patient can still voluntarily control their muscles and how severe the muscle contracture or tightness is. These surgical treatments can significantly improve patients' quality of life by restoring better function and movement in the upper limb. However, successful outcomes require a team approach involving multiple healthcare specialists and clear communication between doctors and patients or their caregivers to make shared decisions about treatment. The authors emphasize that comprehensive care planning and collaborative decision-making between all parties involved are essential components for achieving the best possible surgical results.

title: Outcomes of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in acute myeloid leukemia: the 3-site Mayo Clinic experience.
abstract: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is a rare but fatal complication of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and contemporary data on its clinical and genomic correlates remain sparse. We retrospectively identified 19 adults with AML who developed HLH across 3 Mayo Clinic sites (2020-2024) and compared them with 73 patients with AML without HLH. HLH occurred at a median of 34 days from AML diagnosis (range, 0-472) and was associated with fever, multiorgan dysfunction, and rapidly rising biomarkers. Morphologic hemophagocytosis was observed in only 18% of cases, underscoring its poor sensitivity. HLH was associated with markedly inferior overall survival (median, 5.7 vs 14.8 months, P = .005), including within adverse risk and TP53-mutated AML subsets. When modeled as a time-dependent covariate, HLH remained strongly associated with inferior survival (hazard ratio [HR], 3.9; P < .001). Genomic profiling demonstrated enrichment of TP53 (58%), NF1 (16%), and RAD21 (11%) mutations, with tumor suppressor and/or DNA damage repair pathway alterations in 68% vs 34% of controls (P = .009). On multivariable analysis, HLH (HR, 3.1; P = .003) and adverse-risk cytogenetics (HR, 2.2; P = .040) independently predicted worse survival. Age of ≥65 years was associated with accelerated HLH onset (14 vs 84 days, P = .032) and higher mortality (HR, 13.4; P = .005). All patients received high-dose corticosteroids; some received tocilizumab or ruxolitinib, and none received etoposide. Despite diverse leukemia-directed therapies, only 3 patients achieved long-term survival. Collectively, these findings indicate that AML-associated HLH arises predominantly in older patients with genomically unstable leukemias, portends poor prognosis, and warrants biomarker-guided surveillance and improved targeted immunomodulatory strategies with antileukemic therapy.© 2026 American Society of Hematology. Researchers at Mayo Clinic reviewed medical records from 2020 to 2024 and identified 19 patients with leukemia who developed this immune condition and compared them to 73 leukemia patients who did not develop it. Patients who developed this complication had much shorter survival times, living a median of 5. 7 months compared to 14. 8 months for those without it, and genetic testing showed these patients had more mutations in genes responsible for controlling cell growth and repairing damaged DNA.

title: Regulation of Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress by Empagliflozin in Doxorubicin-Induced Cardiotoxicity in Rats.
abstract: Although Doxorubicin (Dox) is an effective anticancer drug, it can cause severe cardiotoxicity. While several mechanisms have been proposed to explain Dox-induced cardiomyopathy (DIC), strategies to prevent it remain limited. In previous research on isolated cardiomyocytes, we identified that Empagliflozin (EMPA), an antidiabetic drug, mitigated Dox-induced ER stress and apoptosis. In this in vivo study using rats, we further investigated EMPA's potential in preventing and treating DIC. Rats administered a cumulative dose of 15 mg/kg Dox exhibited significant cardiovascular damage, including left ventricular cavity dilation, decreased left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), ER dilation, mitochondrial defects and vacuole formation. These structural changes were linked to the activation of ER-stress pathways (PERK, IRE1 and ATF6) and upregulation of apoptotic proteins initiated by ER stress. When EMPA (10 mg/kg/day) was administered either prophylactically or concurrently with Dox, it significantly attenuated adverse LV remodelling and preserved LVEF. Additionally, EMPA prevented ER stress and subsequent apoptosis in the myocardium of the Dox + EMPA-treated group. These findings suggest that EMPA offers cardioprotective benefits in DIC, likely through the inhibition of ER-stress-induced myocardial injury.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Doxorubicin is a powerful cancer drug that unfortunately damages the heart in many patients, but current ways to prevent this damage are limited. Researchers tested whether empagliflozin, a diabetes medication, could protect rat hearts from doxorubicin damage by giving the drug before or during cancer treatment and measuring changes in heart function and cellular stress. The rats treated with doxorubicin alone showed severe heart problems including enlarged heart chambers, weakened pumping ability, and damaged internal structures, along with activation of stress pathways that trigger cell death. When empagliflozin was added to the treatment, it significantly reduced these harmful changes, preserved heart function, and prevented the cellular stress and death that normally occurs from doxorubicin exposure. These results suggest that empagliflozin could be a promising way to protect cancer patients' hearts during doxorubicin treatment, though more research in humans will be needed to confirm these benefits.

title: Refractory, Resistant and Recurrent Cytomegalovirus Infections in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients: Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection remains one of the most prevalent and consequential post solid organ transplant (SOT) infections. Treatment is often challenging, especially when dealing with refractory and resistant CMV infections.We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study of SOT recipients with clinically significant CMV infection (csCMVi) during 2010-2016. The primary outcome was early refractory CMV infection and secondary outcomes were drug resistance, CMV recurrence, and mortality. Analysis was done with Kaplan-Meier, univariable logistic regression analysis, and multivariable Cox regression.We included 145 SOT recipients with csCMVi, majority were liver transplant (49%). Most common induction was an anti-IL-2 antibody (43.9%). The majority (n = 82; 56.5%) were CMV D+/R- mismatch and presented asymptomatic infection (50.3%). After the initial 3 weeks of antiviral therapy, 13 (8.9%) patients had probable refractory csCMVi; most of them (10 [76.9%]) were CMV D+/R- mismatch. Longer time after transplant had lower risk (OR 0.68; CI 0.48-0.95, p = 0.029) while lower absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) had a higher risk of early refractory csCMVi (OR 1.54; CI 1.01-2.44, p = 0.048). Drug-resistant csCMVi occurred in 7 patients (4.8%); a high initial CMV DNA level was associated with resistant csCMVi (OR 2.00; CI 1.08-3.93, p = 0.031). 25 patients (17.2%) experienced recurrent csCMVi within 6 months. 30 patients (20.7%) died; refractory, resistant or recurrent CMV infections were not associated with mortality.Refractory csCMVi is associated with a low ALC and an earlier onset after transplant. Resistant csCMVi is associated with high initial CMV DNA levels. Recurrence of csCMVi is common and potentially associated with low ALC at the end of antiviral treatment.© 2026 John Wiley & Sons A/S.
