llm_summary: Hematology fellowship programs, which train doctors to specialize in blood disorders, often have inconsistent teaching methods and unclear learning goals across different training sites. Researchers at Mayo Clinic developed and tested a structured educational program for fellows rotating through blood cancer services by first surveying trainees about their learning experiences and then creating a standardized curriculum with weekly disease-focused lessons and organized teaching materials. After implementing this new curriculum during the 2022-2023 academic year, fellows reported major improvements including better access to educational materials, clearer learning objectives, and stronger connections between classroom teaching and actual patient care. The results showed that the quality of education improved significantly and became less dependent on individual doctors' teaching styles, suggesting this approach could help other training programs create more consistent and effective learning experiences. title: Comparison of Multiligament Reconstruction in Individuals With BMI >30 and <30 kg/m2.
abstract: Despite the growing clinical relevance of obesity in the context of multiligament knee injuries, there remains a paucity of data evaluating patient-reported outcomes in this population.To compare clinical and functional outcomes, including postoperative patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and complication/revision rates, of multiligament knee reconstruction (MLKR) in individuals with a body mass index (BMI) >30 kg/m2 versus <30 kg/m2 at a minimum 2-year follow-up.Case series; Level of evidence, 4.A retrospective review was performed to identify all patients who underwent MLKR between 2001 and 2022 at a single institution. Patients with a BMI >30 kg/m2 were propensity-matched to patients with a BMI <30 kg/m2 on a 1:1 basis by age, sex, laterality, and Schenck classification (knee dislocation). Medical records were reviewed for patient characteristics, time to surgery, year of surgery, number and type of ligament interventions, graft choice, single versus staged reconstruction, and concomitant injuries. Postoperative clinical examination findings and PROMs for each cohort, including visual analog scale score, Tegner activity scale score, Lysholm score, and International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) subjective score, were analyzed and compared. Postoperative complication and revision rates were evaluated and compared.Of 158 patients, 79 patients with a BMI <30 kg/m2 (mean age, 31.0 ± 11.5 years; mean BMI, 25.8 ± 3.0 kg/m2) were matched to 79 patients with a BMI >30 kg/m2 (mean age, 32.8 ± 9.5 years; mean BMI, 37.1 ± 5.8 kg/m2). There were no significant differences between cohorts regarding age, sex, laterality, and Schenck classification (P≥ .100); however, patients in the BMI >30 kg/m2 group had greater numbers of posterior cruciate ligament reconstruction. The mean follow-up was 7.5 ± 4.8 years for the BMI <30 kg/m2 cohort and 7.2 ± 4.8 years for the BMI >30 kg/m2 cohort (P = .229). Patients with a lower BMI (<30 kg/m2) had significantly better postoperative mean IKDC (79.3 ± 18.7 vs 67.9 ± 21.2; P = .004), Lysholm (85.1 ± 17.1 vs 75.7 ± 21.0; P = .007), and Tegner (5.1 ± 2.0 vs 4.4 ± 1.7; P = .041) scores. The BMI >30 kg/m2 group also had significantly more postoperative complications (P = .028). However, there was no significant difference between the 2 cohorts in terms of reoperation rate or conversion to total knee arthroplasty (P≥ .189).Patients who undergo MLKR and have a BMI >30 kg/m2 demonstrate significantly decreased postoperative PROMs when compared to patients with a BMI <30 kg/m2. Increasing BMI significantly increased the incidence of complication rates after MLKR.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether people with obesity who undergo multiligament knee reconstruction surgery, which repairs multiple torn ligaments in the knee, have different outcomes compared to people without obesity. The study looked back at medical records from 158 patients treated between 2001 and 2022, matching 79 patients with a body mass index (a measure of body weight relative to height) above 30 with 79 patients with a body mass index below 30, and followed them for an average of about seven years. Patients with a higher body mass index reported significantly lower satisfaction scores after surgery and experienced more complications like infections or blood clots, though the number of patients needing additional surgery was similar between the two groups. title: LATS1/2-CD38 Metabolic Rewiring Links Senescence to Intraplaque Thrombosis.
abstract: Atherothrombosis, which underlies most acute coronary syndromes and is driven by intraplaque thrombosis, preferentially occurs in regions of disturbed blood flow (d-flow). Although LATS1/2 (large tumor suppressor kinases 1 and 2) are known regulators of endothelial mechanotransduction, the mechanisms by which d-flow connects endothelial senescence, proliferation, and intraplaque thrombosis remain poorly understood.We investigated endothelial cell (EC)-specific roles of LATS1/2 using inducible EC-specific knockout mice in a partial carotid ligation model. Spatial multiomics of human and mouse plaques was performed using imaging mass cytometry, COMET sequential immunofluorescence, and spatial metabolomics.Tamoxifen-induced deletion of both Lats1 and Lats2 (homozygous) in ECs caused fatal edema and increased vascular permeability. In contrast, Lats1het(±)/Lats2 homo(-/-)-EC-specific knockout mice survived and developed spontaneous atherothrombotic plaques with neovascularization. Spatial proteomics revealed that LATS1/2 loss induced a senescence-associated stemness phenotype driven by CD38 upregulation. Spatial metabolomics showed sulfite and taurine accumulation, indicating SUOX (sulfite oxidase) deficiency. CD38 suppressed SUOX, demonstrated a switch into the reverse mode of mitochondrial complex V, increased succinate dehydrogenase activity, and promoted ATP consumption. Despite ATP depletion, glutamate metabolism and the citric acid cycle flux increased, sustaining EC proliferation under energetic stress. This senescence-associated stemness state promoted both proliferation and senescence, leading to fragile, leaky neovessels and intraplaque thrombotic lesions. Pharmacological CD38 inhibition attenuated these phenotypes. Similar EC states were observed in human plaques.Loss of LATS1/2 in ECs induces a CD38-associated senescence-associated stemness-like phenotype that promotes intraplaque thrombosis through mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming, including changes consistent with reverse-mode operation of mitochondrial complex V. These findings define a mechanistic link between disturbed flow, endothelial metabolic reprogramming, and intraplaque thrombosis and hemorrhage.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how blood vessel cells respond to disturbed blood flow, which is a major cause of heart attacks and strokes when blood clots form inside fatty plaques in arteries. They used genetically modified mice and advanced imaging techniques to study what happens when two proteins called LATS1 and LATS2 are removed from blood vessel cells, and they compared their findings to human artery samples. When these proteins were lost, blood vessel cells entered an unusual state where they both aged rapidly and acted like stem cells, while a protein called CD38 triggered changes in how cells produce energy that led to weak, leaky blood vessels and dangerous blood clots inside plaques. The researchers discovered that blocking CD38 with drugs could reverse these harmful changes, suggesting a potential new treatment approach for preventing heart attacks and strokes. These findings reveal how disturbed blood flow causes blood vessel cells to reprogram their metabolism in ways that promote dangerous clot formation, opening new possibilities for understanding and treating atherothrombotic disease.

title: Impact of repeated ovulation induction and superovulation on ovarian reserve and early embryo development in obese and PCOS-like mouse models.
abstract: Women with obesity or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) often require repeated ovulation induction (OI) due to ovulatory dysfunction and infertility. However, the cumulative effects of repeated stimulation on ovarian function and embryo development remain poorly understood.The present study aimed to understand the consequences of repeated OI and/or repeated superovulation (SO) on preimplantation embryonic development in obese (high-fat diet-induced) and PCOS (high-fat diet and dehydroepiandrosterone-induced) mouse models.Control (without any metabolic disorder), obese, and PCOS mice were divided into three experimental groups. The mice in one round of superovulation (SO1) were injected with 5 IU intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of pregnant mare serum gonadotropin, followed by 10 IU of human chorionic gonadotropin 48 h later. In the repeated superovulation (SO3) group, mice were subjected to three rounds of superovulation with a gap of 9 days between each superovulation. Mice in the OI3 + SO3 group were administered with three doses of CC (50 mg/kg body weight, i.p., gap of 9 days between each CC injection), followed by three rounds of superovulation.Both single and three rounds of superovulation resulted in decrease in primordial follicles and a moderate increase in atretic follicles in obese and PCOS mice. Reduction in the number of ovulated oocytes, increased rate of abnormal fertilization, decrease in blastocyst rate and elevated DNA damage in blastocysts were observed in in vitro fertilization-derived embryos.These findings demonstrate compromised embryonic development following repeated ovarian stimulation.The study highlights need for mild ovarian stimulation strategies in metabolically compromised patients undergoing infertility treatments.© 2026 The Author(s) (or their employer(s)). llm_summary: Women with obesity or polycystic ovary syndrome, a condition affecting hormone levels and ovulation, often need repeated fertility treatments to help them get pregnant, but doctors do not fully understand how these repeated treatments affect the ovaries and developing embryos. Researchers studied three groups of mice—normal mice, obese mice, and mice with a condition similar to polycystic ovary syndrome—and gave them different combinations of fertility drugs over time to see what happened to their ovaries and embryos. The results showed that even a single round of fertility treatment reduced the number of healthy egg-producing structures in the ovaries of obese and polycystic ovary syndrome mice, and repeating the treatment three times caused even more damage, including increased abnormal fertilization and fewer healthy embryos. The embryos that did develop showed signs of DNA damage, suggesting that repeated ovarian stimulation harms the quality of eggs and the early development of embryos in women with metabolic disorders. These findings suggest that doctors should consider gentler, less intensive fertility treatment approaches for patients with obesity or polycystic ovary syndrome to protect their ovarian health and improve the chances of healthy embryo development.

title: Circulating Tumor High Risk HPV DNA as the HPV-Specific Test in Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma Patients.
abstract: The uses for circulating tumor high risk human papillomavirus DNA (ctHPVDNA) in the diagnostic work-up and treatment of HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (HPV( +)OPSCC) patients are actively being investigated. We evaluated the concordance of ctHPVDNA with tissue-based HPV testing (p16 immunohistochemistry (IHC), DNA in situ hybridization (ISH), and/or RNA ISH) to assess its performance as a primary diagnostic test for patients' HPV status.We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of patients evaluated at a tertiary care multidisciplinary oropharyngeal cancer clinic with suspected HPV( +)OPSCC who underwent pre-treatment ctHPVDNA testing (HPV types 16, 18, 31, 33, 35) via the NavDx assay.Of 236 patients with OPSCC, 190 (81%) had a positive ctHPVDNA result. 41 (17%) were negative, and 3 (1%) were indeterminate. Of the 190 patients with a positive ctHPVDNA result, 190 (100%) had positive tissue-based HPV testing. Of the 41 patients with a negative result, 34 (83%) had positive tissue-based HPV testing and 7 (17%) were negative. ctHPVDNA demonstrated a sensitivity of 85% (95% CI 79-89%), specificity of 100% (95% CI 59-100%), NPV of 17% (95% CI: 7-32%), and PPV of 100% (95% CI 98-100%).The high specificity and PPV of ctHPVDNA indicate that in the setting of a positive result and high clinical suspicion, it may not be necessary for pathologists to test subsequent cytology or tissue specimens that are diagnostic for SCC for p16 or HPV. In the setting of a negative ctHPVDNA result, however, our findings indicate that HPV testing of a pathology specimen must still be performed.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a blood test for human papillomavirus DNA, a virus linked to certain throat cancers, could reliably identify patients with HPV-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, which is a type of cancer in the back of the throat. The study looked back at records from 236 patients who had suspected throat cancer and received a blood test called the NavDx assay that detects high-risk HPV types, then compared these results to traditional tissue samples examined under a microscope. The blood test correctly identified HPV in all 190 patients who tested positive, meaning it had perfect accuracy when it showed a positive result, but it missed HPV in 34 out of 41 patients who tested negative on the blood test yet still had HPV in their tissue samples. These findings suggest that when the blood test shows HPV is present, doctors may not need to do additional tissue testing to confirm the diagnosis, but when the blood test is negative, tissue samples must still be examined because the blood test can miss some cases. Future work should focus on understanding why the blood test sometimes fails to detect HPV that is present in tissue samples and whether this test can.

title: Predicting late radiation-associated neurocognitive and endocrine toxicity in patients with brain tumors.
abstract: Neurocognitive and endocrine dysfunction are potential complications of cranial irradiation. However, risk factors are poorly understood, impeding accurate prognostication and exploration of potential preventive interventions. The objective of this study was to evaluate the prognostic value of various vascular and genotypic risk factors for the development of radiation-related toxicities.This single-institution retrospective cohort study included patients with metastatic and malignant primary brain tumors who received cranial irradiation as part of their initial tumor-directed therapy. Demographic and treatment characteristics were collected, as well as putative vascular and genotypic risk factors. Univariate, multivariate, and machine-learning analyses were performed using five pre-specified measures of radiation-related toxicity. The primary outcome was change in mini-mental status exam (MMSE).Eighty patients (53% male, mean age 55.7, 53% primary and 44% metastatic brain tumors) were included. Elevated homocysteine and ApOE4 genotype were the strongest predictors of MMSE decline in the multivariate model (OR 3.96 [6.5-200, p < 0.001 and 2.85 [1.92-27.6], p = 0.004). Elevated homocysteine was associated white matter change on MRI and both physician and patient assessment. ApoE4 allele was associated with new endocrine deficiency, and physician assessment. An online nomogram provides risk predictions for each of the five late toxicity outcomes: ( https://afranklin22.shinyapps.io/PRMMSERadiationRiskFactors/ ) CONCLUSION: Two pre-treatment laboratory values (elevated homocysteine and ApOE genotype) were strongly associated with post-radiation neurocognitive and endocrine dysfunction using a variety of domains. Our predictive algorithm can aid clinicians in stratifying baseline risk and should be validated in prospective trials and with additional metrics of ND.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Radiation therapy used to treat brain tumors can cause serious side effects including memory problems and hormone imbalances, but doctors have struggled to predict which patients will experience these complications. Researchers studied eighty patients with brain tumors who received radiation treatment, collecting information about their health history, genetics, and blood chemistry to identify warning signs that might predict future problems. The study found that two specific factors measured before treatment—high levels of a substance called homocysteine in the blood and a genetic variation called ApoE4—were the strongest predictors of memory decline and hormone problems after radiation. These findings suggest that doctors could use simple blood tests and genetic screening before treatment to identify which patients are at highest risk and might benefit from extra monitoring or preventive care. The researchers created an online tool to help doctors estimate each patient's individual risk, though they note that these results need to be confirmed in larger studies before being widely used in clinical practice.

title: A multisociety consensus statement on a new common definition and diagnostic criteria for PSVD or NCPF.
abstract: Noncirrhotic portal hypertension has historically been described using heterogeneous and region-specific terminology-such as idiopathic portal hypertension (IPH), noncirrhotic portal fibrosis (NCPF), obliterative portal venopathy, and nodular regenerative hyperplasia-leading to substantial variability in diagnosis, reporting, and international research collaboration. Differences in guideline definitions from major societies (AASLD, EASL, and APASL), together with the presence of characteristic histologic lesions in patients without clinically overt portal hypertension, have further complicated disease classification. To address these challenges, a large, multisociety, international initiative was convened to harmonize nomenclature and diagnostic criteria. Representatives from liver, pathology, and pediatric hepatology societies across the Americas, Europe, and Asia participated in a structured consensus process that included specialized working groups and external Delphi validation. The initiative produced a globally harmonized and implementable diagnostic framework. Consensus was reached that the terms porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD) and NCPF may be used interchangeably when identical diagnostic criteria are applied, and that they should be written as PSVD or NCPF. The diagnosis was defined as fundamentally clinicopathological, requiring integrated assessment. Core principles include the need for a high-quality liver biopsy (≥10 mm), mandatory exclusion of cirrhosis, and systematic exclusion of specific alternative conditions. Importantly, the consensus recognizes that PSVD or NCPF may be diagnosed even without clinical portal hypertension and may coexist with other liver diseases, provided cirrhosis is excluded. Standardized major and minor histologic criteria were developed collaboratively by expert pathologists and externally validated. Features of portal hypertension were harmonized into specific and nonspecific categories applicable to routine clinical practice. An integrated diagnostic scoring system incorporating histology, clinical features, associated conditions, and concommitant etiologies was developed and validated using the Delphi method. This consensus provides the first internationally endorsed, unified framework for the diagnosis of PSVD or NCPF. Its global implementation is expected to reduce diagnostic variability, improve comparability across regions, and facilitate the development of robust, internationally harmonized clinical and translational research cohorts.© 2026. llm_summary: Noncirrhotic portal hypertension, a condition where blood pressure builds up in liver vessels without the liver being scarred, has been described using many different names and definitions across different countries and medical organizations, making it difficult for doctors to diagnose patients consistently and for researchers to collaborate internationally. A large group of liver specialists, pathologists, and pediatric doctors from around the world came together to create one unified definition and set of diagnostic rules that everyone could use the same way. The group agreed that the condition should be called porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder or noncirrhotic portal fibrosis interchangeably, and they developed clear guidelines requiring a high-quality liver tissue sample, confirmation that the liver is not scarred, and a systematic check to rule out other conditions. This new standardized framework means that doctors worldwide can now diagnose this condition more consistently, patients in different regions will receive more comparable care, and researchers can more easily work together on studies using patients with the same clearly defined disease. The implementation of these unified diagnostic criteria is expected to reduce confusion in clinical practice and enable stronger international research efforts to better understand and treat this liver condition.

title: Medical 3-D Printing Within a Health Care Facility.
abstract: Within the widespread use of medical 3-D printing at health care facilities (HCFs), the scope and complexity of patient-specific anatomic models and anatomic (surgical) guides are expanding. The authors formed a multidisciplinary panel to seek consensus regarding best practices for 3-D printing at an HCF.At the request of the ACR, a 14-member panel was formed with members nominated by 10 professional societies. This multidisciplinary team represented those involved in health care 3-D printing. The panel made statements and recommendations in five areas: (1) general statements, (2) practice recommendations, (3) quality and safety recommendations, (4) government relations recommendations, and (5) economics recommendations. Discussions and three rounds of meetings were conducted to reach consensus.The panel members reached unanimous or near unanimous consensus on 25 statements and recommendations. The recommendations focused on consistent, safe, and sustainable 3-D-printed parts derived from medical images.This multidisciplinary collaboration represents consensus results on best practices regarding medical 3-D printing. These recommendations frame the typical workflow and provide a contemporary reference regarding common elements to the clinical procedure of 3-D printing at HCFs.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Medical three-dimensional printing, which creates physical models of body parts from imaging scans, is becoming more common in hospitals and health care facilities, so experts wanted to establish clear guidelines for how it should be done safely and effectively. A group of fourteen specialists from ten different professional organizations came together to discuss and agree on the best practices for using three-dimensional printing in medical settings. Through multiple meetings and discussions, the panel reached agreement on twenty-five recommendations covering five main areas: general practices, how to perform the work, quality and safety standards, government relations, and costs. The recommendations focus on making sure that three-dimensional printed parts are made consistently, safely, and in a way that can continue long-term by using information from medical images like scans. These agreed-upon guidelines now provide hospitals and health care facilities with a clear roadmap for how to set up and run three-dimensional printing programs that follow current best practices.

title: QTc Prolongation in Stress-Induced Cardiomyopathy: A Case of Stabilization With Temporary High-Rate Pacing.
abstract: Stress-induced cardiomyopathy (SCMP) is a transient cardiac syndrome often mimicking acute coronary syndrome. It is commonly associated with QT prolongation and can lead to serious dysrhythmias.A 73-year-old man with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder developed SCMP during an acute chronic obstructive pulmonary disorder exacerbation, complicated by marked QTc prolongation (>650 ms) and recurrent pulseless polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Invasive coronary angiography showed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Arrhythmias persisted despite electrolyte correction. Ultimately, pacing at 100 beats/min shortened QTc and prevented arrests.Although often self-limiting, stress cardiomyopathy may cause QT prolongation and arrhythmias. An underutilized therapy is high-rate pacing, which shortens QT and reduces early afterdepolarizations.QT prolongation is not uncommon in SCMP, and severe prolongation often occurs, predisposing to polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and cardiac arrest. llm_summary: Stress-induced cardiomyopathy is a temporary heart condition that can occur during extreme physical or emotional stress and sometimes looks like a heart attack, but it can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems including a prolonged QT interval, which is an electrical timing issue in the heart. A 73-year-old man with severe lung disease developed this condition during a lung crisis and experienced a dangerously prolonged QT interval of over 650 milliseconds along with repeated episodes of a life-threatening irregular heartbeat called polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Tests showed that his coronary arteries were not blocked, and even after doctors corrected his electrolyte levels, the dangerous heart rhythms continued to occur. The doctors successfully treated him by using a pacemaker set to pace his heart at 100 beats per minute, which shortened his QT interval and stopped the dangerous heart rhythms from happening. This case demonstrates that high-rate pacing is an underutilized but highly effective treatment option for managing severe QT prolongation and life-threatening arrhythmias in patients with stress-induced cardiomyopathy.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy for Intermediate- and High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Retrospective Observational Cohort Study.
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Systemic thrombolysis is recommended for high-risk PE, but risk of major bleeding limits its use despite its efficacy. While mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has emerged as an alternative reperfusion strategy, real-world safety data remains limited. The objective of this single-center retrospective observational cohort study was to characterize the safety profile and procedural complications of MT.MethodsAdult patients with intermediate-risk and high-risk PE who underwent MT at a quaternary academic medical center between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2024, were included. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, procedural, outcome, and mortality data were collected. Major adverse events and bleeding were defined according to established criteria.ResultsFrom a total of 103 screened patients, 65 were included. Of these, 22 (34%) were classified as high-risk and 43 (66%) as intermediate-risk. Baseline demographics were similar between groups. High-risk patients demonstrated greater clinical disease severity, with higher mean Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (PESI) scores (188.5 vs 122.4). Clinical deterioration prior to MT occurred in 35% of intermediate-risk patients. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) consultation rate (32% vs 7%), peri-procedural ECMO use (18% vs 2.3%), major bleeding (27% vs 4.7%), and in-hospital mortality (36% vs 11.6%) were higher in the high-risk group. Thrombus removal was achieved in 77% and 88% of high- and intermediate-risk patients, respectively. High-risk patients had longer ICU (mean 4 vs 1.3 days) and hospital stays (mean 21.5 vs 6.4 days), higher thirty-day mortality (36% vs 14%), and lower 90-day survival (59% vs 79%).ConclusionsMT achieved high rates of thrombus removal in both groups. In this retrospective cohort, high-risk patients had greater baseline clinical severity and was associated with higher bleeding rates, greater resource utilization, including ECMO consultation and peri-procedural use, prolonged ICU and hospital stays, as well as increased mortality.

llm_summary: Blood clots in the lungs, called pulmonary embolism, are a serious health problem that can cause death, and doctors have traditionally used blood-thinning medications to treat severe cases even though these medications carry a risk of dangerous bleeding. Researchers looked back at records from 65 patients who had a procedure called mechanical thrombectomy, which uses a catheter device to physically remove blood clots from the lungs, comparing 22 patients with the most severe clots to 43 patients with moderately severe clots treated between 2017 and 2024. The procedure successfully removed clots in 77 percent of the most severe cases and 88 percent of the moderate cases, but patients with the most severe clots experienced more bleeding complications, longer hospital stays, and higher death rates both during their hospital stay and within 90 days. These results suggest that mechanical thrombectomy can effectively remove blood clots in both severe and moderate cases, though patients with the most severe clots face greater risks and need more intensive care support, including life support machines in some cases. Future studies with larger patient groups and longer follow-up periods would help doctors better understand when this.

title: Feasibility of Capillary Self-Collected Blood Specimens for Routine Outpatient Laboratory Testing.
abstract: Capillary self-collection (CSC) devices allow patients to collect blood samples at home, potentially reducing outpatient phlebotomy visits. This study aimed to (a) assess the patient experience with multiple commercially available CSC devices; (b) determine which laboratory tests are commonly ordered together, which could reduce the need for appointments; and (c) evaluate the analytical performance of these tests using CSC samples.User experience for 3 CSC devices was evaluated. Clinical feasibility was determined by comparing test results in paired sera collected by venipuncture (VP) and CSC devices. VP samples were centrifuged within 2 h and tested immediately. CSC sera were centrifuged and tested both immediately and after delayed processing to simulate shipping temperature extremes (-20°C or 40°C). Basic metabolic panel, lipid panel, thyroid function cascade, and prostate-specific antigen were evaluated. Differences between VP and CSC collections were characterized according to their statistical and clinical differences.Patients reported CSC devices were easy to use and painless. Clinically significant differences between VP and CSC sera processed immediately were limited to potassium and bicarbonate. Following delayed processing of CSC serum samples (48 h at room temperature), clinically significant differences in potassium, bicarbonate, and glucose were observed. Frozen samples could not be analyzed. A 48 h delay at 40°C caused clinically significant differences in all analytes except creatinine, lipid panel, prostate-specific antigen, and the thyroid cascade.Potassium, bicarbonate, and glucose were not stable at room temperature in CSC sera. CSC serum specimens may be a viable option but require analyte-specific evaluation and consideration of transportation conditions.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether patients could safely collect their own blood samples at home using special finger-prick devices instead of visiting a clinic for traditional needle draws from the arm. The study tested three different self-collection devices by having patients use them and comparing the results to blood samples collected by trained phlebotomists, then checking how the samples held up under different storage conditions like extreme heat and cold. Patients found the self-collection devices easy and painless to use, and most test results matched well between home-collected and clinic-collected samples when processed right away. However, potassium, bicarbonate, and glucose levels changed significantly when samples sat at room temperature for two days, and freezing the samples made them impossible to test. The findings suggest that home blood collection could reduce clinic visits for some routine tests, but the samples need careful handling during shipping and some measurements like potassium require special attention to timing and temperature.

title: Coronary Artery Proximity to Potential Ablation Sites in Children: The Case for Careful Consideration.
abstract: Coronary artery (CA) injury from catheter ablation is an uncommon complication, but the risk is under-recognized. The risk for CA injury significantly increases when a CA is within 3 mm of the site of ablation, but CA imaging to assess for CA proximity to ablation sites is not commonly performed in children prior to ablation.The aim of the study was to assess CA proximity to potential ablation sites.A retrospective review of all coronary computed tomography angiograms (CTAs) in pediatric patients <18 years of age at Mayo Clinic from 2017 through 2023 was conducted. The proximity of CAs to potential ablation sites in the coronary sinus and the appendage bases were measured.Seventy-two CTAs in 67 patients >15 kg and <18 years old were included. Median age was 12 years, and median weight was 41 kg. In right dominant CA circulation, 23/36 (64%) had a CA within 3 mm of the coronary sinus. In left and co-dominant CA circulation, 26/26 (100%) had a CA within 3 mm of the coronary sinus. The right CA was within 3 mm of the appendage base in 49/69 (71%). The circumflex CA was within 3 mm of the appendage base in 50/68 (74%).Most pediatric patients have a CA ≤ 3 mm from potential ablation sites in the coronary sinus and base of the appendages. Precautions should be taken to avoid CA damage before performing catheter ablation in these areas.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Coronary artery injury, which happens when blood vessels near the heart get damaged during a heart rhythm treatment procedure called catheter ablation, is a serious but often overlooked risk in children. Researchers reviewed heart imaging scans from sixty-seven children under eighteen years old taken between 2017 and 2023 to measure how close the coronary arteries were to the areas where doctors typically perform ablation procedures. The study found that most children had coronary arteries positioned within three millimeters of common ablation sites, with nearly all children having this dangerous proximity in one particular area called the coronary sinus. Because coronary artery damage becomes significantly more likely when a blood vessel is within three millimeters of the ablation site, doctors should take special precautions and use imaging to check artery location before performing these procedures on children. These findings suggest that heart specialists need to be more careful and deliberate when planning ablation treatments in young patients to prevent accidental injury to the coronary arteries.

title: Comparison of [18F]flortaucipir and [18F]MK6240 for the detection of tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease (HEAD): a multicentre, prospective, cross-sectional, within-participant study.
abstract: Tau PET imaging has emerged as a critical biomarker for Alzheimer's disease, informing diagnosis, staging, and therapeutic selection. We investigated whether PET tracer selection alters tau detection.We conducted a prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, within-participant comparison of [18F]flortaucipir (Tauvid), currently used in clinical settings in the USA and Europe, and [18F]MK6240, an investigational tau PET tracer. Participants were recruited from eight north American sites and underwent tau PET, amyloid-β (Aβ) PET, and detailed cognitive assessments. Tau PET with both agents was acquired within a 45-day window. Coprimary outcomes were the discriminative accuracy for Alzheimer's disease-related cognitive impairment and the frequency of tau positivity in early medial temporal lobe (MTL) and late neocortical regions. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05361382.Between March 2, 2022, and Aug 27, 2025, 775 individuals were enrolled, with 682 completing all procedures (373 [55%] female, 309 [45%] male; 38 [6%] aged 19-27 years, 214 [31%] aged 50-65 years, and 430 [63%] aged 65-89 years). 32 (5%) participants identified as Hispanic or Latino. 637 (93%) identified as White, 24 (4%) as Black or African American, 16 (2%) as Asian, and five (1%) as other. In addition, 49 (7%) individuals were identified as being from a rural area. [18F]MK6240 showed greater accuracy than [18F]flortaucipir in distinguishing Alzheimer's disease from non-Alzheimer's disease impairment (area under the curve 0·93, 95% CI 0·89-0·95 vs 0·86, 0·75-0·91; p<0·0001). Among the older adults, tau positivity status was concordant in 560 (87%) for MTL and 603 (94%) for neocortical regions. In cognitively unimpaired participants, [18F]MK6240 identified twice as many MTL-positive cases as [18F]flortaucipir (n=54 [15%] vs n=23 [6%]). Prevalence ratio in Aβ-positive was 2·43 (95% CI 1·50-3·94; p=0·0003), identifying 23 additional cases per 100. Among discordant cases, 75 (89%) were [18F]MK6240-positive only and had higher Aβ burden (p<0·0001), APOEε4 frequency (p<0·0001), and cognitive impairment (p=0·0043) than those negative on both tracers. Neocortical tau positivity was more frequent with [18F]MK6240 than with [18F]flortaucipir in cognitively impaired individuals (80 [28%] vs 46 [16%]). Prevalence ratio in Aβ-positive was 1·74 (95% CI 1·32-2·29; p<0·0001), identifying 15 additional mild cognitive impairment and 21 dementia cases per 100.Tau PET tracer selection influences the frequency of detection of tau pathology across the ageing and Alzheimer's disease spectrum. Compared with [18F]flortaucipir, [18F]MK6240 identified more individuals with tau pathology in cognitively unimpaired and cognitively impaired individuals, with direct implications for patient stratification in clinical trials and more precise guidance for therapeutic decision-making.National Institute on Aging.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined two different imaging tests that detect tau, a harmful protein that builds up in the brains of people with Alzheimer's disease, because choosing the right test could help doctors diagnose the disease earlier and select better treatments. The study compared how well two tau imaging tracers, called flortaucipir and MK6240, could identify Alzheimer's disease in 682 participants across eight North American medical centers who received both scans within 45 days of each other. The newer tracer MK6240 was significantly better at distinguishing Alzheimer's disease from other types of brain problems, and it found twice as many cases of early tau buildup in cognitively unimpaired older adults compared to the currently used flortaucipir tracer. The cases where only MK6240 detected tau had more signs of Alzheimer's disease risk, including higher amounts of another harmful brain protein called amyloid-beta and genetic risk factors. These findings suggest that which imaging tracer doctors choose can significantly affect how many patients are identified as having tau pathology, which has important implications for enrolling patients in clinical trials and making decisions about which treatments to recommend.

title: Prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in adults with cancer: an International Cardio-Oncology Society (IC-OS) and Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer (MASCC) clinical practice statement.
abstract: Cardiovascular (CV) toxicity is prevalent in cancer survivors due to shared risk factors, direct CV injury from cancer therapy (CT), and development/exacerbation of CV risk factors during treatment. Succinct guidance on the minimum standard of CV care required of cancer care providers (CCPs) can improve outcomes for survivors. This clinical practice statement (CPS) is aimed at CCPs focused on identification, prevention, and management of CVD in individuals with cancer.The International Cardio-Oncology Society and Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer identified members with expertise across oncology, cardiology, and cancer survivorship. Key questions/areas of practice recommendations related to CV risk and CVD were identified across the cancer trajectory.Working groups performed targeted literature reviews and consensus was reached for all recommendations.5 over-arching clinical practice recommendations for CCPs were identified: (1) perform a CV risk assessment prior to starting systemic CT (2) identify and facilitate CV-related care during CT; (3) ensure measures are taken to mitigate the risk of cancer therapy related CV toxicity (CTR-CVT) prior to and during CT; (4) monitor CV status and risk factors during therapy and refer to the appropriate health care provider if CV risk factors are uncontrolled or new signs/symptoms develop; and (5) re-assess CV risk following completion of CT (periodically for those with advanced disease on life long treatment) and develop a CV surveillance plan.CCPs play a pivotal role in identifying and addressing CTR-CVT. This CPS provides specific, succinct, and actionable behaviours that can be readily implemented in cancer care globally.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Cancer survivors often develop heart and blood vessel problems because cancer treatments can directly damage the heart, combined with shared risk factors like high blood pressure and high cholesterol. An international team of cancer doctors and heart specialists created a practical guide with five main recommendations for cancer care providers to prevent and manage these cardiovascular complications throughout a patient's cancer journey. The recommendations include assessing heart health before starting cancer treatment, identifying heart problems during treatment, taking steps to protect the heart before and during therapy, monitoring heart status and referring patients to heart specialists when needed, and reassessing heart health after treatment ends. These five straightforward steps give cancer care providers specific actions they can take right away to reduce heart damage from cancer therapy and improve the long-term health of cancer survivors. This clinical practice statement offers practical, actionable guidance that cancer care teams around the world can implement to better protect their patients' hearts during and after cancer treatment.

title: Embracing technology to improve peripheral intravenous access and care: A consensus statement from vascular access experts and patients.
abstract: To develop expert consensus on peripheral venous access devices (PVAD) and associated care practices, and to formulate guidance recommendations aimed at improving peripheral venous access and management, including the integration of vein visualization technology. This is particularly important for patient populations with peripheral venous depletion, who often present with compromised vasculature that complicates successful PVAD access and increases the risk of complications. Preserving vascular integrity in these patients is essential for maintaining treatment pathways and preventing long-term vascular damage.A multi-phase approach to consensus development was used consisting of the following: (1) a literature review, (2) a survey and consultation with a vascular access expert panel (n = 9), and (3) a consultation meeting with patient and public representatives (n = 2).Survey results and consultation findings from the expert panel demonstrated consensus for 14 of 24 statements. Further analysis resulted in a total of four key problem statements on peripheral venous access and care, and 11 recommendations for future development. Following review by patient and public representatives, three additional recommendations were added, and three existing recommendations were refined. The final consensus statement reflects four problem statements with 14 recommendations.This expert consensus presents 14 evidence-informed statements designed to strengthen practice, improve patient safety, and enhance clinician confidence and competence. Central to these recommendations is the adoption of routine structured pre-insertion vessel assessment using vein visualization technology where appropriate to minimize vessel trauma, and promote more consistent, high-quality vascular access care.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how to improve the way doctors and nurses place small tubes called peripheral intravenous catheters, which are needles inserted into veins to deliver medicine or fluids, especially for patients whose veins are difficult to access. The team used a three-step approach that included reviewing medical literature, surveying nine vascular access experts, and consulting with two patient representatives to develop recommendations based on evidence and real-world experience. The experts reached agreement on fourteen key recommendations, with the most important being the routine use of vein visualization technology, which is a device that helps doctors see veins more clearly before inserting the catheter. These recommendations aim to reduce damage to blood vessels, lower the risk of complications, and help healthcare workers feel more confident and skilled when placing these catheters. The consensus statement provides practical guidance that could help protect patients' veins from long-term damage and improve the overall quality of care for people who need repeated intravenous access.

A systems-based approach to haematology involves understanding how blood disorders connect to and affect the entire body rather than viewing them as isolated problems.

title: Determinants of Quality of Life in Patients with Immune-Checkpoint-Inhibitor Induced Secondary Adrenal Insufficiency.
abstract: Limited data are available on quality of life (QoL) and adrenal crises in patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced secondary adrenal insufficiency (ICI-SAI).To 1) characterize the presentation, management, and outcomes of patients with ICI-SAI; 2) compare outcomes of ICI-SAI with other etiologies of secondary adrenal insufficiency (oSAI);  and 3) identify variables associated with QoL and adrenal crisis.In this single-center cross-sectional study, adults with ICI-SAI or oSAI (2018-2025) completed questionnaires assessing symptoms, management, adrenal crises, and the Addison disease-specific QoL survey (AddiQoL).Outcomes AddiQoL score and adrenal crisis events.Patients with ICI-SAI (n=109) were older (median age 66 vs 60 years), more often women (59% vs 43%), and more frequently diagnosed within one year of symptom onset (88% vs 42%, P<0.001), compared to patients with oSAI (n=139). Patients with ICI-SAI had higher AddiQoL scores (median 87 vs 85, P=0.020). In a multivariable analysis of age, sex, glucocorticoid dose and type, insurance support and duration of SAI, ICI-SAI remained independently associated with higher AddiQoL (estimate 5.4, P=0.010). The prevalence of reported adrenal crises within the prior year was similar between groups (15% vs 14%, P=0.782). In a multivariable analysis, higher AddiQoL scores were independently associated with lower odds of adrenal crisis (OR of 0.57, 95% CI 0.42-0.76).Patients with ICI-SAI report better QoL compared with patients with other causes of SAI, despite similar adrenal crisis rates. These differences may be related to earlier diagnosis and differing clinical contexts, underscoring the importance of timeline recognition and patient-centered management.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined quality of life in patients who developed a condition called secondary adrenal insufficiency, which is a rare side effect where the immune system fighting cancer damages the adrenal glands that produce stress hormones, as this complication has not been well studied. The study compared 109 patients who developed this condition from cancer immunotherapy drugs with 139 patients who developed the same condition from other causes, asking them to complete surveys about their symptoms, treatment, health crises, and overall well-being. Patients whose condition was caused by cancer drugs reported better quality of life scores compared to those with other causes, even though both groups experienced similar rates of dangerous adrenal crises where hormone levels drop suddenly. The researchers found that better quality of life was linked to lower chances of experiencing these dangerous crises, and the cancer drug group may have felt better because their condition was caught and diagnosed much faster than in other patients. These findings suggest that how quickly doctors recognize and treat this condition matters greatly for patient well-being, highlighting the importance of early detection and personalized care approaches for people dealing with this serious side effect.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Anselamimab in Immunoglobulin Light Chain Amyloidosis: Results From the Randomized CARES Trials.
abstract: In immunoglobulin light chain (AL) amyloidosis, amyloid fibrils cause organ dysfunction. Anselamimab, a monoclonal antibody, selectively binds to amyloid fibrils, accelerating their clearance.Newly diagnosed patients with European modification of Mayo 2004 stage IIIa or IIIb AL amyloidosis were randomly assigned to receive anselamimab or placebo with cyclophosphamide, bortezomib, and dexamethasone (with or without daratumumab). The primary end point was a hierarchical composite of time to all-cause mortality (ACM) and frequency of cardiovascular hospitalizations (CVHs), analyzed using the Finkelstein-Schoenfeld test and win ratio estimation.Among 406 randomly assigned patients, the primary end point win ratio for anselamimab versus placebo was 1.11 (95% CI, 0.83, 1.50; P = .332) and the hazard ratio (HR) for ACM was 0.80 (95% CI, 0.57, 1.13; P = .290). CVH rates in the anselamimab and placebo groups were 0.59 (95% CI, 0.42, 0.83) and 0.89 (95% CI, 0.55, 1.43), respectively (P = .145). Among patients with kappa isotype (n = 72), the win ratio was 2.06 (95% CI, 0.98, 4.31; P = .100) and anselamimab reduced ACM by 62% versus placebo (HR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.17 to 0.86; nominal P = .012), and CVH by 71% (IRR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.10 to 0.87; nominal P = .028) with improvements in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Score. There was no clinical benefit observed in the lambda population. Anselamimab was generally well-tolerated; safety data were comparable between treatment arms overall.Treatment with anselamimab, an antifibril antibody used alongside antiplasma cell dyscrasia therapy, while not meeting the primary end point in the overall population, significantly improved ACM and CVH in patients with kappa AL, potentially offering a new therapeutic option for this isotype.

llm_summary: Immunoglobulin light chain amyloidosis is a serious disease where abnormal proteins clump together and damage organs like the heart, so researchers tested a new antibody drug called anselamimab designed to break down these protein clumps. The study involved over 400 newly diagnosed patients who were randomly assigned to receive either anselamimab or a placebo along with standard chemotherapy drugs to stop the abnormal protein production. While anselamimab did not improve outcomes in the overall group of patients, it showed significant benefits for the smaller group of patients with a specific type of abnormal protein called kappa, reducing deaths by 62 percent and heart-related hospitalizations by 71 percent. These results suggest that anselamimab could become a valuable new treatment option specifically for patients with the kappa type of this disease, though more research is needed to confirm these findings. The drug was generally safe and well-tolerated by patients, making it a promising candidate for further testing in larger studies focused on the kappa patient population.

title: Adenotonsillectomy is associated with increased risk and disease activity in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a key environmental risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS), and tonsils and adenoids serve as a primary viral reservoir. This study investigates the potential role of adenotonsillectomy in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS) risk and relapse rate.POMS participants and controls were recruited from 16 pediatric MS clinics between 1 November 2011 and 1 July 2017. Clinical and demographic information, including history of adenotonsillectomy, EBV serostatus, and HLA-DRB1*15:01:01 status, were collected. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between adenotonsillectomy and MS risk. In addition, negative binomial regression offset by follow-up time was used to assess the relationship between adenotonsillectomy and relapse rate in POMS participants with available follow-up data.The case-control analysis included 359 POMS participants and 560 pediatric controls. Individuals with a history of adenotonsillectomy had a 63% increased odds of MS (adjusted odds ratio (OR) = 1.63, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.01-2.64, p = 0.046). Among the 239 POMS participants with available follow-up data, adenotonsillectomy was associated with a twofold increase in annualized relapse rate (adjusted incidence rate ratio (IRR) = 2.00, 95% CI = 1.15-3.48, p = 0.013).Prior adenotonsillectomy was associated with increased risk of MS and greater relapse rate in pediatric patients, suggesting a potential interplay between EBV, immune regulation, and MS pathogenesis.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether removing tonsils and adenoids, which are small glands in the throat that help fight infections, might increase the risk of multiple sclerosis, a disease where the immune system damages the brain and spinal cord. The study compared 359 children with pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis to 560 healthy children and found that those who had their tonsils and adenoids removed were 63 percent more likely to develop the disease. Among the children already diagnosed with multiple sclerosis who had follow-up information available, those who had undergone the surgery experienced twice as many disease flare-ups per year compared to those who had not had the procedure. The findings suggest that tonsils and adenoids may play an important role in protecting against multiple sclerosis, possibly because they help control a common virus called Epstein-Barr virus that is linked to the disease. These results indicate that doctors and families should carefully consider the benefits and risks of removing tonsils and adenoids in children, and further research is needed to understand exactly how this surgery affects the immune system and disease development.

title: Empowering Compassionate Care: Elevating the Role of the Palliative Care Registered Nurse.
abstract: Over the past 2 decades, the landscape of serious illness has changed dramatically, with patients living longer and undergoing prolonged treatment. This has increased the need for specialty palliative care (PC) in both inpatient and outpatient settings. Specialty PC teams are interprofessional, composed of diverse healthcare professionals who collaborate seamlessly to provide whole-person care. The palliative care registered nurse plays a pivotal role on the PC team by enhancing communication, holistic compassionate care, and expert care coordination. This article explores the multifaceted specialty palliative care registered nurse role, providing examples of how this role can be used to expand the reach of PC. Specific examples include the expansion of the registered nurse role on an interprofessional PC team to deliver integrative nursing interventions and opportunities for ongoing professional development to meet the complex needs of patients and families impacted by serious illness.Copyright © 2026 by The Hospice and Palliative Nurses Association. llm_summary: Over the past twenty years, patients with serious illnesses have been living longer and receiving more extended treatments, which has created a growing need for palliative care, a type of medical care focused on comfort and quality of life rather than cure, in both hospital and outpatient settings. Palliative care teams are made up of different types of healthcare professionals, including registered nurses, who work together to provide complete care that addresses a patient's physical, emotional, and spiritual needs. The registered nurses on these teams play a crucial role by improving communication between patients and doctors, delivering compassionate and whole-person care, and coordinating all the different services patients need. This article examines how registered nurses in palliative care can expand their responsibilities on the team by offering specialized nursing treatments and pursuing additional training to better meet the complex needs of seriously ill patients and their families. By strengthening the registered nurse role and providing opportunities for professional growth, palliative care teams can reach more patients and families who need support during serious illness.

The Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System is a database where doctors and patients can report side effects and health problems that occur after taking medications, which researchers use to identify patterns and safety concerns.

title: Comparative efficacy and safety of different doses of intravenous thrombolytics in acute ischemic stroke: a GRADE-assessed network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: To compare the efficacy and safety of different doses of intravenous thrombolytic agents in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and guide optimal dose selection. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL until March 2025 to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating alteplase (tPA), tenecteplase (TNK), reteplase, and recombinant human prourokinase (rhPro-UK) at any dose in patients with AIS. Analysis was performed using R software, and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled. Primary outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), 90-day mortality, excellent functional outcome (defined as modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score 0-1), and functional independence (defined as mRS 0-2). We included 21 RCTs (16,643 patients). Compared to tPA (0.9 mg/kg), tPA (0.6 mg/kg) was associated with a significantly lower risk of sICH (RR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.27-0.86), while TNK (0.4 mg/kg) showed a higher risk (RR = 1.88, 95% CI: 1.06-3.35). No significant differences were observed in 90-day mortality, functional independence, or serious adverse events across interventions. Reteplase (18 + 18 mg) (RR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.05-1.21) and TNK (0.25 mg/kg) (RR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.01-1.10) significantly improved 90-day excellent functional recovery compared to tPA (0.9 mg/kg). TNK (0.32 mg/kg) showed the lowest risk probability for any ICH and parenchymal hemorrhage. Some safety outcomes showed dose-dependent effects: lower-dose tPA and intermediate-dose TNK reduced ICH risk compared to higher doses, while mortality and functional independence remained comparable across doses.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined different doses of clot-busting medications given through the vein to treat patients who have had a stroke caused by a blood clot in the brain. The team reviewed 21 previous studies involving over 16,000 patients and compared four different medications at various doses to see which worked best and caused the fewest side effects. They found that lower doses of one medication called tPA caused fewer dangerous brain bleeds, while two other medications called reteplase and a lower dose of TNK helped more patients recover well three months after their stroke. The study showed that some medications had dose-dependent effects, meaning that using the right amount mattered for safety, though death rates and overall independence remained similar across the different treatment options tested. These findings suggest that doctors may need to carefully choose the right medication and dose for each stroke patient to balance the benefits of dissolving the clot with the risk of causing bleeding in the brain.

title: [Knowledge of resuscitation cardiopulmonary and first aid among rehabilitation personnel: a cross-sectional study].
abstract: Rehabilitation settings involve patients with complex conditions and active therapeutic interventions, which may increase the risk of clinical emergencies. Adequate training in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and first aid is essential for healthcare professionals in these environments. This study aimed to assess prior training, theoretical knowledge, and self-perceived preparedness for clinical emergencies among rehabilitation healthcare staff.A cross-sectional study was conducted using an anonymous survey administered to physiotherapists, occupational therapists, speech therapists, and nursing assistants working in rehabilitation units of a university hospital. The questionnaire collected sociodemographic data, information on previous CPR and first aid training, theoretical knowledge assessed through clinical scenarios, and self-perceived preparedness for emergencies.Of the 86 professionals invited, 57 responded and, after exclusion of two incomplete questionnaires, 55 surveys were included in the analysis (63.9%). CPR training had been received by 87.2% of participants, while 47.3% (n=26) had completed a first aid course. Only 14.5% considered their previous training sufficient. Higher theoretical knowledge scores were observed among participants who had completed both CPR and first aid training (mean 7.05/10; P=.03). Self-perceived preparedness was reported by 27.3% of respondents, with higher scores observed in this group (P=.011). No significant differences were observed according to years of professional experience.Despite a high prevalence of CPR training, perceived preparedness for clinical emergencies remains low. Combined training in CPR and first aid is associated with higher knowledge scores and greater perceived preparedness, supporting the implementation of structured and context-specific training programs.Copyright © 2026 Sociedad Española de Rehabilitación y Medicina Física. llm_summary: Rehabilitation centers care for patients with serious health conditions who receive active treatment, which means medical emergencies can happen and staff need to be prepared to respond quickly. Researchers surveyed fifty-five healthcare workers including physical therapists, occupational therapists, and nursing assistants at a hospital rehabilitation unit to find out how much training they had received in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR, which is chest compressions and rescue breathing to restart a stopped heart) and first aid, and how confident they felt handling emergencies. While most workers had received CPR training at some point, less than half had taken a first aid course, and only about one in seven felt their training was actually sufficient for real emergencies. Workers who had completed both CPR and first aid training together scored higher on knowledge tests and felt more prepared for emergencies than those with only one type of training. The findings suggest that rehabilitation centers should create regular, specialized training programs that combine CPR and first aid instruction to better prepare their staff for the medical emergencies that can occur in their settings.

title: Legionella 5S rRNA PCR melting temperature analysis discriminates high-risk species associated with disease severity.
abstract: Legionella species are important causes of community-acquired pneumonia. The diagnostic performance and clinical implications of a fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based real-time PCR assay targeting the Legionella 5S rRNA gene were evaluated, with emphasis on melting temperature (Tm) analysis to differentiate detected species and associated clinical outcomes. A retrospective multicenter cohort study of adults with laboratory-confirmed Legionella infection between 2019 and 2025 was conducted. PCR crossing point (Cp) and Tm data were analyzed and compared with species identified in culture from respiratory specimens. Associations between Tm and clinical outcomes were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Among 51,489 PCR tests performed, 823 (1.6%) were positive. Among 376 Legionella infections, PCR demonstrated the highest diagnostic yield. Among patients undergoing all three diagnostic tests, the addition of PCR increased detection from 49% with urine antigen and culture combined to 100% (P < 0.001). Of 189 PCR-positive patient specimens with available Tm data, Tm showed a bimodal distribution, being either <66°C or ≥66°C. A Tm cutoff of ≥66°C discriminated L. pneumophila/L. longbeachae from other Legionella species with excellent performance (AUC, 1.00). Overall, 29.6% of infections had a Tm <66°C, consistent with non-pneumophila/non-longbeachae Legionella species. Infections due to L. pneumophila/L. longbeachae, which correspond to high Tm values in the study assay, were independently associated with ICU admission (adjusted odds ratio, 2.85; 95% CI, 1.33-6.11; P = 0.007), but not 90-day mortality. Real-time PCR targeting the Legionella 5S rRNA gene provides superior detection compared to culture and/or urine antigen testing and enables higher-risk species discrimination through Tm analysis.IMPORTANCENearly one-third of Legionella infections in this cohort were attributable to non-pneumophila species, highlighting limitations of diagnostic strategies reliant on Legionella urine antigen testing or L. pneumophila PCR. The findings suggest that species-level inference can be derived from melting-temperature data generated during routine PCR testing. Incorporating validated melting-temperature interpretation into reporting workflows may improve epidemiologic surveillance and clinical understanding of characteristics of Legionella pneumonia.

llm_summary: Legionella bacteria cause serious lung infections that are difficult to diagnose because standard tests like urine checks and culture methods often miss cases. Researchers tested a new blood test method called PCR, which detects genetic material from the bacteria, on over 51,000 samples from patients with suspected Legionella infections between 2019 and 2025. The PCR test found infections in 823 samples and was much better at detecting the disease than older methods, increasing detection rates from 49 percent to 100 percent when combined with traditional tests. By measuring the temperature at which the genetic material breaks apart during the test, doctors could identify which dangerous species like Legionella pneumophila were present, and patients with these high-risk species were nearly three times more likely to need intensive care unit admission. This new approach could help doctors quickly identify the most serious cases and improve how hospitals track and understand these infections in their communities.

title: Socioeconomic deprivation, rurality, and travel distance negatively impact survival in early-stage pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma but are not associated with stage at diagnosis.
abstract: The interactions between social determinants of health (SDOH) and survival across stages in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are poorly understood. Our aims were to determine the associations of socioeconomic deprivation indices, rurality indices, and travel distance with PDAC stage at diagnosis and overall survival.Using the Rochester Epidemiology Project that encompasses the 27-county region of southeastern Minnesota and west-central Wisconsin, we retrospectively identified patients diagnosed with PDAC (1/1/10-12/31/20). Socioeconomic deprivation was defined using neighborhood-level Area Deprivation Index (ADI) quartiles and individual-level HOUSES index quartiles. Rurality was defined by Rural-Urban Commuting Area codes. Travel distance (miles) was calculated between residential address and Mayo Clinic. Primary measures were diagnosis stage and overall survival, analyzed via multi-level statistical models when appropriate.We identified 1095 patients with PDAC (median age 72 years (63-80). For stage I PDAC, patients experienced worse survival across four SDOH summaries, from least to most deprived ADI quartile (adjusted HR (aHR) 5.59, 95% CI 2.15-14.50; p = 0.0019; least to most deprived HOUSES quartile (aHR 1.99, 95% CI 1.29-3.06; p = 0.022); increased distance (aHR 3.09, 95% CI 1.75-5.44; p = 0.0005); urban to large rural areas (aHR 2.39, 95% CI 1.28-4.46; p = .0008). None of the examined SDOH were associated with late-stage diagnosis or survival in stages II-IV.Socioeconomic deprivation, rurality, and travel distance were associated with worse survival in early-stage PDAC. These determinants were not associated with delayed diagnosis. Targeted interventions for reducing healthcare disparities in early-stage PDAC may be needed to maximize the benefits of intercepting cancer early.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how social factors like poverty, rural location, and distance to medical care affect survival rates for people with pancreatic cancer, a serious disease affecting the pancreas. The study looked back at medical records for over one thousand patients diagnosed with pancreatic cancer in Minnesota and Wisconsin between 2010 and 2020, measuring their neighborhood wealth levels, how rural or urban their homes were, and how far they lived from the nearest major hospital. The results showed that patients with early-stage pancreatic cancer who lived in poorer neighborhoods, in rural areas, or far from medical centers had significantly worse survival outcomes, even though these social factors did not affect whether their cancer was caught at an early or late stage. These findings suggest that while catching cancer early is important, patients from disadvantaged backgrounds may not be getting the same quality of care or treatment after diagnosis as those with more resources. Future efforts should focus on improving healthcare services and support for early-stage pancreatic cancer patients from lower-income and rural communities to help them survive longer after their diagnosis.

This study examines how basal cell carcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma, which are the two most common types of skin cancer, develop over time in patients with these blood disorders in different patterns.

title: Preoperative onapristone-XR in postmenopausal women with progesterone receptor-positive (PgR+)/HER2-negative early breast cancer: SOLTI-1802 ONAWA trial results.
abstract: Onapristone, a type-1 antiprogestin, has been tested for advanced breast cancer (BC), but its activity in early-stage, hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative BC has not been fully explored. The ONAWA trial (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04142892- Registered on January 6, 2021) was a single-arm study evaluating the preoperative effects of onapristone with extended-release formulation (ONA-XR) (50 mg BID for 21 days) in postmenopausal women with Progesterone Receptor-positive (PgR+)/HER2-negative early BC. No complete cell cycle arrest (CCCA) was achieved at day 21, however ONA-XR significantly suppressed tumor proliferation with a Ki-67 geometric mean change of -17.78% (CI95 -39.76% to 12.20%) particularly in tumors with baseline PgR≥90% (-46.21%; CI -63.02% to -21.76%). Immunohistochemistry showed suppression of phospho-Ser294-PgR and p-STAT3, indicating effects on proliferation and endocrine pathways. Treatment also induced a shift to a more endocrine-sensitive phenotype. Of the 10 patients, 60% experienced adverse events, including one grade 3 increase in gamma-glutamyltransferase. In conclusion, ONA-XR showed early tumor proliferation suppression, particularly in high PgR-expressing tumors, supporting its potential for further clinical evaluation.© 2025. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined a new drug called onapristone with extended-release formulation, which is a type of hormone-blocking medication, to see if it could help treat early-stage breast cancer in postmenopausal women whose tumors were positive for progesterone receptors (meaning the cancer cells respond to the hormone progesterone) and negative for HER2 (a protein that drives some breast cancers). In this small trial, ten postmenopausal women with this specific type of breast cancer took the medication twice daily for 21 days before surgery to measure how well it worked. The drug successfully slowed down tumor growth, particularly in patients whose tumors had high levels of progesterone receptors, with tumor cell division decreasing by nearly half in these cases. Although the medication did not completely stop cancer cells from dividing, it showed promise by shifting the tumors toward a more hormone-sensitive state and suppressing key proteins involved in cancer growth. These early results suggest that onapristone with extended-release formulation deserves further testing in larger groups of patients to determine if it could become a useful treatment option for this type of breast cancer.

title: Monoclonal gammopathy of clinical significance: a multisystem review.
abstract: Monoclonal gammopathy of clinical significance (MGCS) is a general term that encompasses a spectrum of non-malignant clinical disorders that are directly caused by monoclonal immunoglobulins (monoclonal proteins) produced by clonal plasma cell proliferative disorders. It is best considered as a collection of specific disorders that represent non-malignant progression of monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS). This review provides a comprehensive overview of MGCS, highlighting its pathophysiology, diagnostic approach, clinical manifestations, and current management strategies across multiple organ systems. The spectrum of MGCS includes specific renal, neurological, cutaneous, hematological, and ocular diseases, as well as multisystem disorders such as POEMS syndrome, Schnitzler syndrome, cryoglobulinemia, and TEMPI syndrome. The diagnosis of MGCS is often challenging as it requires establishing a causal link between a monoclonal protein and the specific disease entity or clinical manifestation. Treatment strategies vary by disease and target the underlying monoclonal protein-producing clone or are directed to limit the effects of the monoclonal protein. As clinical trials remain limited, current management relies on mechanistic insights and observational studies. Increased awareness of MGCS and its organ-specific clinical features is crucial for providing timely diagnosis and delivering targeted interventions that may reverse or halt disease progression.© 2026. llm_summary: Monoclonal gammopathy of clinical significance, or MGCS, refers to a group of non-cancerous diseases caused when certain immune cells produce abnormal proteins that damage various parts of the body including the kidneys, nerves, skin, blood, and eyes. This review article examines the causes, how doctors diagnose it, what symptoms patients experience, and how doctors currently treat these conditions across different organ systems. The researchers found that MGCS includes many specific diseases such as POEMS syndrome and cryoglobulinemia, which are conditions where abnormal proteins clump together and cause damage, and that diagnosing MGCS is difficult because doctors must prove the abnormal protein is actually causing the disease. Treatment approaches differ depending on which disease a patient has, but generally focus either on stopping the cells that make the abnormal protein or on reducing the damage the protein causes. Because large-scale clinical trials testing new treatments are limited, doctors currently rely on smaller studies and their understanding of how these diseases work, making it important for healthcare providers to recognize MGCS early so patients can receive targeted treatment that might stop or reverse their condition.

title: The evolving comorbidity landscape of rheumatoid arthritis.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with a wide spectrum of comorbidities that substantially influence quality of life and long-term outcomes. These include extra-articular manifestations, cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular accidents, dementia, malignancy, infection, mental health disorders and osteoporosis. Patterns of comorbidity in RA have evolved over the past three decades, with declining prevalence of some complications alongside persistently high or increasing burdens of interstitial lung disease, anxiety and depression. Shifts in the comorbidity landscape probably reflect advances in RA management, including the expanded use of biologic and targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) and a widespread adoption of treat-to-target strategies. Consideration of comorbidity-specific epidemiology, the potential effect of DMARDs on comorbidity risk and opportunities to address both RA and comorbid disease are increasingly relevant in clinical care. Preventive strategies, including selected enhanced screening approaches such as those for cervical cancer, interstitial lung disease, cardiovascular disease and osteoporosis, form an important component of comprehensive RA management. Awareness of the changing comorbidity landscape could support more integrated and individualized care for people with RA.© 2026. Springer Nature Limited.

llm_summary: Rheumatoid arthritis, a disease where the immune system attacks the joints, often comes with other serious health problems that affect how well people live and their long-term health outcomes. Researchers reviewed how the mix of these additional health conditions has changed over the past thirty years, finding that while some complications have become less common, others like lung disease and mental health issues such as anxiety and depression remain stubbornly high or are getting worse. These changes in the pattern of health problems likely happened because doctors now have better medicines to treat rheumatoid arthritis, including newer biologic drugs and targeted treatments that work differently than older medications, along with a strategy of treating patients aggressively until their disease is controlled. Healthcare providers should now pay closer attention to screening patients for specific conditions like cervical cancer, lung disease, heart disease, and weak bones, while also considering how different arthritis medicines might affect a patient's risk of developing other health problems. Understanding how the landscape of these accompanying health conditions has shifted over time can help doctors provide more personalized and complete care that addresses both the arthritis itself and any other health issues their patients may develop.
