llm_summary: Researchers examined whether exercise helps patients who receive dialysis treatment, a medical procedure that filters waste from the blood when kidneys no longer work properly. The team reviewed thirty-one previous studies involving twenty-five hundred thirty-five patients and compared groups that did structured exercise like walking or strength training against groups that received usual care without special exercise programs. The results showed that exercise significantly improved patients' muscle strength, their ability to walk longer distances, and their ability to stand up and sit down repeatedly, with improvements that doctors consider meaningful and important. However, exercise did not increase the actual amount of muscle tissue patients had or improve their nutritional markers like protein levels in the blood. The findings suggest that while exercise is valuable for helping dialysis patients stay stronger and more physically capable, additional strategies focusing on nutrition and reducing inflammation in the body may be needed to more effectively prevent muscle loss in this population.

title: Acute Toxicity From Short-Course Radiation Therapy for Rectal Cancer: A Single-Institution Experience.
abstract: Short-course radiation therapy (SCRT) is an important neoadjuvant treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer. Although SCRT offers logistical advantages and possibly reduced toxicity compared to long-course chemoradiation, emerging data have raised concerns about long-term outcomes and underrecognized adverse effects. This study examines acute toxicities after SCRT, including a poorly understood syndrome, acute lumbosacral plexopathy (ALSP).Patients with locally advanced rectal cancer treated between 2016 and 2022 with neoadjuvant SCRT (25 Gy/5 fractions) were retrospectively analyzed. Acute toxicity was assessed up to 30 days after SCRT completion. ALSP was defined as pelvic or buttock pain with or without radiation down the lower extremities. Patients without reported ALSP were matched to cases based on N stage, tumor location, treatment position, and treatment modality, and the lumbosacral plexus and psoas muscles were contoured for matched patients. Dosimetric and clinicodemographic variables were compared for patients with and without toxicity using the Mann-Whitney U test and χ2 test.Among 71 patients identified, the median age was 56 years, and approximately half were female. The 30-day incidence of any-grade toxicity was 75%; one-third of first toxicities occurred more than 10 days after the start of SCRT. Notably, 10 (14%) patients developed ALSP, presenting at a median of 2.5 days after treatment initiation and resolving within 1 week. Most were treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or acetaminophen, but 2 required additional medications. ALSP was not associated with planning target volume dose, small bowel dose, lumbosacral plexus dose, or muscle composition parameters.Three-quarters of patients treated with SCRT develop any acute toxicity, and ALSP was identified in 14% of patients. All cases of ALSP were transient, without late sequelae. These findings highlight the importance of toxicity surveillance beyond the treatment window. Future work should identify predictors of ALSP and potential mitigation strategies.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a treatment called short-course radiation therapy, which delivers high doses of radiation to rectal cancer tumors over just five days instead of the usual longer treatment period, because doctors wanted to understand what side effects patients experience during and shortly after this faster approach. The study looked back at records from 71 patients treated between 2016 and 2022, tracking any harmful effects that occurred within 30 days after their radiation finished and paying special attention to a nerve pain condition in the lower back and buttocks area that had not been well studied before. Three out of every four patients developed some type of side effect within 30 days, and surprisingly, one out of seven patients experienced sudden nerve pain in the lower back and buttocks area, though all of these cases went away within a week without causing lasting damage. The researchers found that this nerve pain condition was not connected to how much radiation reached certain areas or muscles, which means doctors still need to figure out what actually causes it and how to prevent it from happening. Future research should focus on identifying which patients are most likely to experience this nerve pain and developing ways to reduce its occurrence, since the study shows that careful monitoring for side effects needs to continue even after.

title: Updates in Person-Centered Rehabilitation for Critically Ill Patients.
abstract: Modern patient-centered rehabilitation for critically ill patients focuses on physical, cognitive, psychological, and social recovery to reduce long-term impairments after critical illness. Core strategies include the ABCDEF (A2F) bundle/ICU Liberation, humanization programs, and symptom management. Based on the capabilities of individual patients, frequent assessments in these dimensions are performed to develop person-centered goals and interventions. Early mobilization, cognitive stimulation, delirium prevention and nonpharmacological management, empathic communication, ICU diaries, and family involvement should begin within 24 to 72 hours after ICU admission. The dosage and delivery of these interventions should be adapted to the capabilities and needs of individual patients.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Modern medical care for patients recovering from serious illnesses in intensive care units now focuses on helping them heal in four important ways: physically, mentally, emotionally, and socially. Healthcare teams use a structured approach called the ABCDEF bundle, which is a set of evidence-based practices designed to support recovery, along with programs that treat patients with compassion and manage their symptoms carefully. Doctors and nurses perform regular assessments across all four areas of recovery to create personalized goals and treatments that match what each patient can handle. Key interventions like getting patients moving early, stimulating their thinking, preventing confusion, using kind communication, keeping written records of their hospital stay, and involving family members should all begin within the first one to three days after a patient enters the intensive care unit. The intensity and method of delivering these treatments must be adjusted based on each individual patient's current abilities and specific needs to ensure the best possible long-term recovery.

title: Use of Machine-Learning Models to Identify Clinical Features Associated With A Future Clinical Worsening Event in Patients With Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
abstract: Clinical worsening events are increasingly recognized as a meaningful outcome in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). We applied machine-learning models to real-world data to identify clinical features that may predict clinical worsening events in PAH. Data were obtained retrospectively from the electronic health records of adults diagnosed with PAH at Mayo Clinic locations (January 2015-December 2019). Machine-learning LASSO regularized logistic regression models were developed to analyze the association between 100 clinical features and occurrence of clinical worsening events. In total, 455 patients were included (mean age 62.1 years; 59.3% female). Of these, 232 (51.0%) experienced a clinical worsening event after a median (quartile 1, quartile 3) of 10.9 (4.1, 21.4) months. The best-performing model had an area under the curve of 0.78, sensitivity of 78%, and specificity of 59%. The model identified 11 clinical features associated with clinical worsening events in PAH with a non-zero coefficient: baseline age, body mass index (BMI), creatinine level, red cell (erythrocyte) distribution width (RDW), mean pulmonary arterial pressure, pulmonary vascular resistance, sodium concentration, and QT interval, along with dyspnea, number of clinic visits, and other forms of heart disease within a 1-month window before a clinical worsening event. Baseline RDW and BMI, and number of clinic visits within the 1-month window were statistically significantly associated with clinical worsening events. Our study used machine-learning models to identify clinical features associated with risk of clinical worsening events in PAH. Automation of risk prediction could lead to earlier therapeutic intervention to optimize patient outcomes.© 2026 Johnson & Johnson. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether computer programs could predict which patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, a serious lung disease affecting blood vessels, would experience a worsening of their condition. They studied 455 patients at Mayo Clinic locations between 2015 and 2019, using information from medical records to train machine-learning models, which are computer systems that learn patterns from data to make predictions. The computer models identified eleven clinical features that were connected to patients getting worse, including factors like age, body weight, kidney function measured by creatinine levels, blood cell measurements, and how often patients visited the clinic in the month before worsening. The best-performing model was able to correctly identify about 78 percent of patients who would experience clinical worsening, suggesting that automated risk prediction tools could help doctors intervene earlier with treatments to improve patient outcomes. This research shows promise for using artificial intelligence to spot high-risk patients with this disease, though further testing and refinement would be needed before these tools could be used in everyday clinical practice.

title: The Legacy and Long-Term Impact of Dr. Albert L. Rhoton Jr.: Contributions of Rhoton Fellows to the Field of Neurosurgery.
abstract: Professor Albert J. Rhoton Jr., MD, is renowned for his groundbreaking dissections, marking a monumental achievement in the field of neuroanatomy. Alongside his anatomical contributions, he also passed on his knowledge and skills to numerous fellows, leaving behind a profound legacy. Despite the widespread recognition of his influence, little quantitative work has been done to characterize the scholarly impact of his alumni.Data were collected on Rhoton fellows, including fellowship years, country of origin, current institutions, and titles, practice settings, and leadership roles. Scholarly productivity was evaluated by assessing publication counts, including publications before and after the fellowship, and publications focused on surgical anatomy. Additionally, H-indices and citation counts were recorded. Other variables analyzed included ownership of a surgical anatomy laboratory, and participation in organizing hands-on courses.We analyzed 118 alumni from diverse countries. There was a significant increase in publication output following the fellowship, with publications rising from an average of 7 to 76 ( p  < 0.001). Fellows from high-income countries had higher research productivity than those from middle-income countries, with greater average H-index ( p  = 0.003), publication count ( p  = 0.01), and citation score ( p  = 0.003). Overall, 65% of fellows pursued academic practice, with 18% owning a laboratory and 30% involved in hands-on courses.Dr. Rhoton's mentorship has shaped a generation of neurosurgeons who continue his legacy. His fellows have established careers worldwide, leading in academia, professional organizations, and surgical training. Their global impact underscores the lasting value of structured mentorship in neurosurgery.Thieme. All rights reserved.

title: Machine Learning Models to Evaluate County-Level Incidence of Diagnosed Diabetes and Sociodemographic Factors.
abstract: To evaluate county-level incidence of diagnosed diabetes and key sociodemographic factors in a high-dimensional, nonlinear setting.This temporally aggregated observational study used US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data on county-level incidence of diagnosed diabetes, from 2004 to 2019, and 34 sociodemographic factors from public databases. We defined counties as higher-burden if diabetes incidence was >12.6 per 1000 persons (1 standard deviation [SD] above sample mean). As relationships between sociodemographic factors and diabetes incidence may be nonlinear and involve complex interactions, we trained three machine learning models to estimate incidence (elastic net regression), classify counties as higher-burden (eXtreme Gradient Boosting [XGBoost], support vector machine [SVM]), and identify feature importance. Model performance was evaluated using fivefold cross-validation, with stratified folds for XGBoost and SVM models.Overall, 500 of 3114 counties (16.1%) were of higher-burden. Elastic net regression showed good predictive performance for estimating diabetes incidence (R 2 0.78 [95% CI, 0.75-0.80]). For classification of higher-burden counties, SVM and XGBoost showed high discrimination with AUROC of 0.962 (95% CI, 0.948-0.974) and 0.957 (95% CI, 0.941-0.971), respectively. Sensitivity analyses using alternative definitions of higher-burden counties (mean + 0.75 × SD; mean + 1.25 × SD) yielded comparable results. Across all three models, key county-level features contributing to model predictions were percentages of children living with grandparent householders and of people withLimited English.Machine learning models demonstrated consistent performance in estimating and classifying county-level diabetes incidence, with high discrimination for identifying higher-burden counties. Sociodemographic factors, including children living with grandparent householders, may inform tailored public health interventions.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether computer programs could predict which counties in America have higher rates of diagnosed diabetes by looking at neighborhood characteristics like family living situations and language spoken at home. The study used diabetes information collected from 2004 to 2019 across more than three thousand counties and tested three different machine learning models, which are computer programs that learn patterns from data to make predictions. The computer programs performed very well, correctly identifying counties with high diabetes rates about ninety-six percent of the time, and found that certain factors like children living with grandparents and people who speak limited English were the strongest predictors of diabetes in a community. These findings suggest that public health officials could use this type of computer analysis to focus diabetes prevention and treatment programs in neighborhoods where they are needed most based on specific community characteristics. Future work should test whether using these predictions to target health programs actually helps reduce diabetes rates in real communities.

title: Oral P2Y12 inhibitors only versus cangrelor in critically ill patients requiring percutaneous coronary interventions supported by microaxial flow pumps.
abstract: Oral P2Y12 inhibitors (P2Y12i) may have reduced efficacy in critically ill patients undergoing Impella-supported PCI. The intravenous P2Y12i cangrelor offers rapid and reversible platelet inhibition, but its role in this setting remains unclear.Comparison of outcomes in patients undergoing Impella-supported PCI receiving oral P2Y12i only versus loading with cangrelor.We analyzed consecutive patients managed at a Swiss tertiary cardiology facility who underwent Impella-supported PCI. Patients received either (1) oral P2Y12i or (2) cangrelor followed by oral P2Y12i. Periprocedural major bleeding (BARC ≥ 3) within 48 h, in-hospital major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and 6-month MACE were analyzed.Among 295 patients, 201 received oral P2Y12i and 94 received cangrelor. Patients in the oral P2Y12i group were less likely to present with STEMI (55.7% versus 67.0%) or cardiogenic shock (55.2% versus 72.3%), whereas high-risk protected PCI was more frequent (17.9% versus 6.4%) compared to cangrelor group. No significant differences were observed in major bleeding, in-hospital MACE and 6-month MACE. Major bleeding was numerically lower in the oral P2Y12i group (26.4% versus 33.0%, p = 0.2). Early stent thrombosis rates were relatively low and not significantly different (1.0% versus 2.1%, p = 0.6). Presentation with cardiogenic shock was associated with a higher risk for post-PCI major bleeding (OR 7.09, 95%CI 2.97-18.49) and 6-month MACE (HR 2.01, 95% CI 1.01-3.97).In Impella-supported PCI, cangrelor was associated with no statistically significant differences in outcomes compared to oral P2Y12i, with consistent results after adjustment. Given the observational design, these findings require confirmation in randomized trials.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a fast-acting blood thinner called cangrelor works better than regular oral blood thinners in very sick heart patients who need emergency procedures to open blocked arteries while supported by a small mechanical heart pump called an Impella. The study compared 295 patients at a Swiss hospital, with 201 receiving only oral blood thinners and 94 receiving cangrelor followed by oral blood thinners, and tracked their bleeding complications and heart problems during their hospital stay and six months later. The results showed no significant differences between the two groups in terms of major bleeding, heart attacks, or other serious heart events, though the oral blood thinner group had slightly lower bleeding rates that were not statistically significant. These findings suggest that cangrelor does not provide additional benefits over standard oral blood thinners in this critically ill patient population, which could simplify treatment decisions and reduce costs. However, because this was an observational study that simply tracked what happened rather than randomly assigning patients to treatments, the researchers emphasize that these results need to be confirmed through more rigorous randomized trials before changing clinical practice.

title: Outcomes of Radiotherapy With or Without Dose Escalation to Lymph Node Metastases Detected by PET PSMA or Conventional Imaging in Node-Positive Prostate Cancer: A Real-World Multicenter Propensity Score-Matched (PRIMENOD) Analysis.
abstract: To evaluate the impact of PSMA PET versus conventional imaging for staging, and the effect of dose escalation (DE) to metastatic lymph nodes in cN1 prostate cancer patients treated with EBRT and ADT.A retrospective multicenter analysis included 197 propensity score-matched patients (77 staged with PSMA PET, 120 with conventional imaging) treated with EBRT and ADT, with or without DE to lymph node metastases. Matching criteria were T stage, nodal involvement, imaging modality, Gleason score, and ADT duration. Primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival (MFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), locoregional control (LRC), and toxicity.Median follow-up was 42 months (IQR: 25-59). Median EQD2 (alpha/beta=1.5) to elective nodes was 46 Gy, and to metastatic nodes, 66 Gy (PSMA PET) and 63 Gy (conventional imaging). The 3-year MFS was 80.5% (95% CI: 71.3-90.8%) for PSMA PET and 77.2% (95% CI: 69.5-85.8%) for conventional imaging; 5-year MFS was 59.3% versus 65.8% (P=0.57). OS at 5 years was 82.2% (PSMA PET) and 77.4% (conventional imaging) (P=0.72). On multivariable analysis, ISUP grade group 3-5 predicted earlier metastasis (HR: 4.03, 95% CI: 1.61-10.06; P=0.003); higher prostate dose (EQD2 ≥113 Gy) improved MFS (HR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.30-0.95; P=0.033); long-term ADT (≥24 mo) improved OS (HR: 0.38, 95% CI: 0.19-0.78; P=0.009). No significant difference in toxicity was observed between groups.PSMA PET staging and nodal dose escalation >60 Gy were safe but did not improve MFS, OS, or LRC. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether using advanced imaging called PSMA PET scans, which highlight cancer cells in the body, could improve treatment outcomes for prostate cancer patients with lymph node involvement, and whether giving higher radiation doses to cancerous lymph nodes would help. The study followed 197 patients treated with radiation therapy and hormone therapy, comparing those staged with PSMA PET imaging to those staged with standard imaging, and measuring whether some patients benefited from receiving extra radiation doses to their affected lymph nodes. After tracking patients for an average of three and a half years, the results showed that PSMA PET staging and higher radiation doses to lymph nodes did not significantly improve survival rates or prevent cancer from spreading compared to standard imaging and lower doses. The study did find that patients with more aggressive cancer types and those who received higher total radiation doses to the prostate itself had better outcomes, while longer hormone therapy lasting two years or more improved overall survival. Although PSMA PET imaging and dose escalation to lymph nodes proved safe with no increased side effects, these approaches did not provide the survival benefits researchers had hoped for, suggesting that other factors like cancer aggressiveness and prostate radiation dose may be more important.

title: Validation of NT-proBNP cutoff points for heart failure diagnosis in adults with CHD in the outpatient clinic and emergency department.
abstract: Empirical data support the use of N-terminal pro-B-type brain natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) for heart failure (HF) rule-in and rule-out in patients with acquired heart disease, but similar data are lacking in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD). The purpose of this study was to assess diagnostic performance of conventional NT-proBNP cutoff points for HF diagnosis (rule-in and rule-out) in adults with CHD.Retrospective study of adults with CHD and NT-proBNP measurement in the outpatient clinic (outpatient cohort) or in the emergency department (ED) (2003-2023). HF diagnosis was based on clinical assessment at the time of NT-proBNP measurement. Logistic regression was used to assess the diagnostic performance of conventional NT-proBNP cutoff points (<125 pg/ml for HF rule-out and ≥250 pg/ml for HF rule-in in the outpatient setting; <300 pg/ml for HF rule-out and ≥450 pg/ml for HF rule-in in the ED setting).The outpatient cohort comprised 3961 patients (age 45 ± 16 years), and NT-proBNP <125 pg/ml ruled-out HF with 86% sensitivity, while NT-proBNP level ≥250 pg/ml ruled-in with 68% specificity. The ED cohort comprised 687 patients (age 49 ± 16 years) and NT-proBNP level <300 pg/ml ruled-out HF with 82% sensitivity, and NT-proBNP level ≥450 pg/ml ruled-in HF with 75% specificity.These data support the use of these NT-proBNP levels for HF screening in the CHD population, which in turn would enable early detection and treatment of HF.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a blood test called NT-proBNP, which measures a protein that increases when the heart is stressed, could help doctors diagnose heart failure in adults born with heart defects. The study looked back at medical records from over 4,600 patients seen between 2003 and 2023, measuring their NT-proBNP levels in either an outpatient clinic or emergency department and comparing those results to whether doctors had diagnosed them with heart failure at that time. The results showed that in the outpatient clinic, an NT-proBNP level below 125 correctly ruled out heart failure in 86 percent of cases, while a level of 250 or higher correctly identified heart failure in 68 percent of cases, and similar patterns held true in the emergency department with slightly different cutoff numbers. These findings suggest that doctors can safely use these same blood test cutoff points for patients with congenital heart disease that are already used for patients with other types of heart disease, which could help catch heart failure earlier and start treatment sooner. Future research should continue to validate these results and explore whether using this blood test actually leads to better outcomes for patients with con.

title: Cost-effectiveness of frontline eltrombopag with immunosuppressive therapy for severe aplastic anemia.
abstract: The randomized phase 3 RACE trial demonstrated eltrombopag used in conjunction with traditional immunosuppressive therapy (IST) to be an efficacious treatment for severe aplastic anemia. However, eltrombopag can pose a significant cost burden. Using clinical data from the RACE trial, we performed the first cost-effectiveness analysis of frontline eltrombopag plus IST in adults with newly diagnosed severe aplastic anemia across all accepted willingness-to-pay (WTP) thresholds from the United States modified societal perspective. The primary outcome was the incremental net monetary benefit across WTP thresholds of $50,000-$150,000/quality-adjusted life year (QALY) with base-case WTP threshold of $120,000/QALY. Frontline eltrombopag plus IST versus frontline IST alone accrued discounted costs of $593,000 and $561,000, and discounted QALYs of 11.53 and 10.73, respectively, with a per-patient incremental net monetary benefit of $64,000 [95% credible interval -$91,000 to $262,000] favoring frontline eltrombopag plus IST. Deterministic sensitivity analyses demonstrated that the 6-month overall response risk ratio (with versus without frontline eltrombopag) had the greatest effect on model results. In probabilistic sensitivity analysis, frontline eltrombopag with IST was favored in 78% of 10,000 second-order Monte Carlo iterations, as well as 58% and 82% of 10,000 iterations at WTPs of $50,000 and $150,000/QALY, respectively. At current pricing, frontline eltrombopag is the cost-effective therapeutic strategy in adults with severe aplastic anemia in the US. Longer-term clinical and patient utility data will likely help further clarify the cost-effectiveness of eltrombopag in this setting.

llm_summary: Severe aplastic anemia is a serious blood disorder where the bone marrow fails to produce enough blood cells, and researchers wanted to know whether adding a drug called eltrombopag to standard treatment would be worth the extra cost. The study used information from a major clinical trial called RACE to compare the cost and health benefits of treating newly diagnosed patients with eltrombopag plus traditional immune-suppressing therapy versus traditional therapy alone. The results showed that while eltrombopag plus standard therapy cost about thirty-two thousand dollars more per patient, it provided additional health benefits measured as quality-adjusted life years, which means extra years of good health quality. At the current price, adding eltrombopag to standard treatment appears to be a cost-effective choice for treating severe aplastic anemia in the United States, meaning the extra health benefits justify the additional expense. However, researchers noted that gathering more long-term information about how patients actually feel and function over time would help confirm whether this treatment approach remains the best choice financially.

title: Support Strategies and Policy Recommendations to Manage the Aftermath of an Emergency or Traumatic Situation.
abstract: Nurses in all practice areas are often thrust into emergency situations, requiring them to act swiftly to protect the health and safety of their clients. Once the emergency is over, they seamlessly return to their regular duties, driven by the belief that the work never stops, that nursing is a 24 hour job, and that selflessness is a nursing virtue. Occupational exposure to traumatic events can lead to adverse outcomes like posttraumatic stress disorder and secondary traumatic stress, which impact nurse well-being, patient safety, and workforce stability. This article presents a framework for managing the aftermath of such events.Copyright © 2025 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Nurses regularly face emergency situations that require them to act quickly to protect their patients, but they often push through the emotional toll of these traumatic experiences without taking time to recover. Exposure to traumatic events at work can lead to serious mental health problems like posttraumatic stress disorder, which is a condition where people experience ongoing fear and distress after a frightening event, and secondary traumatic stress, which happens when healthcare workers absorb the trauma of their patients. These mental health issues not only harm nurses' own well-being but also affect the quality of care they provide to patients and can lead to nurses leaving the profession. The authors of this article developed a framework, which is a structured plan or guide, to help manage what happens after nurses experience traumatic situations at work. This framework and the policy recommendations included in the article aim to support nurses in recovering from traumatic events and to improve overall safety and stability in the nursing workforce.

title: Recent national trends in pelvic and paraaortic lymphadenectomy in gynecologic oncology fellowship training programs: ACGME data from 2019-2025.
abstract: To investigate trends in surgical experience performing pelvic and paraaortic lymphadenectomies by gynecologic oncology (GO) fellows in the U.S.Summary statistics for ACGME GO training programs were obtained from the ACGME public reporting system. The ACGME data only contains this short time frame. For each academic year spanning 2019-2020 through 2024-2025, the national mean procedure count was extracted for pelvic and paraaortic lymphadenectomies.Over the past 5 years there has been a significant decline in the number of pelvic (p = 0.0004) and paraaortic (p = 0.002) lymphadenectomies being performed by GO fellows in the U.S. During this same time there was a progressive significant upward trend in the number of SNL performed (p = 0.003). The mean procedure count declined from 61 to 38 on pelvic and 36 to 18 on para-aortic and SLN increased from 63 to 96.Gynecologic oncology training experience in performing both pelvic and paraaortic lymphadenectomy has declined. The decline may have implications that extend to training in radical pelvic surgery.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined how much training gynecologic oncology fellows, which are doctors specializing in cancer surgery of the female reproductive system, are getting in performing lymphadenectomies, a surgical procedure to remove lymph nodes from the pelvis and abdomen. The study looked at national data from training programs across the United States between 2019 and 2025 to track how many of these lymph node removal procedures fellows were performing each year. The results showed that over this five-year period, the number of pelvic lymph node removals declined significantly from 61 procedures per fellow to 38, while abdominal lymph node removals dropped even more dramatically from 36 to 18 procedures per fellow. At the same time, fellows were increasingly performing a newer technique called sentinel lymph node biopsy, which involves removing only the first few lymph nodes most likely to contain cancer, with numbers rising from 63 to 96 procedures per fellow. These findings suggest that gynecologic oncology training programs may need to reconsider their surgical curriculum to ensure fellows maintain adequate experience with traditional lymph node removal techniques, since this decline could affect their ability to perform complex.

title: Oral Tonabersat Connexin-43 Modulator for Diabetic Macular Edema with Good Vision (DRCR Retina Network Protocol AN).
abstract: Evaluate oral tonabersat, a connexin-43 hemichannel modulator, on central subfield thickness (CST) in eyes with center-involved diabetic macular edema (CI-DME) and good vision.Phase II randomized, double-masked clinical trial.One hundred twenty-nine adults with CI-DME and visual acuity (VA) 20/32 or better, from 24 US sites.Participants randomly assigned 1:1- to 80-mg tonabersat (N = 64, [71 eyes]) or placebo (N = 65, [73 eyes]) for 6 months.Change in OCT CST.Overall, 37% of participants were female, with a mean age of 63 years. In tonabersat and placebo groups, respectively, the baseline mean CST was 359 and 362 μm; the mean (standard deviation [SD]) change in CST from baseline to 6 months was -15 (55) μm and +5 (51) μm; (adjusted mean difference: -16 [95% confidence interval (CI), -34 to 2], P = 0.08). A post hoc analysis limiting anti-VEGF effect showed adjusted mean difference: -21 [95% CI, -38 to -3], P = 0.02. Among participants with thinner eyes at baseline (CST <75 μm above threshold; tonabersat [n = 45] vs. placebo [n = 43]), adjusted mean difference was -2 μm (95% CI, -26 to 22). For thicker eyes (CST ≥75 μm above threshold; tonabersat [n = 20] vs. placebo [n = 24]), mean difference was -51 μm (95% CI, -83 to -19). The mean (SD) change in best-corrected VA from baseline to 6 months was: tonabersat 0.0 (5.7) letters versus placebo -0.4 (5.7) letters (adjusted mean difference: 0.82 [95% CI, -1.56 to 3.21], adjusted P = 0.39). Dizziness was more common with tonabersat (27% vs. 8%), headaches more common with placebo (17% vs. 6%), and drowsiness rates were 11% in both groups.There was no statistically significant improvement in CST at 6 months in the tonabersat versus placebo groups. However, a post hoc analysis limiting anti-VEGF impact demonstrated significant benefit in the tonabersat group. Aside from increased dizziness, consistent tonabersat safety concerns were not identified. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new oral medication called tonabersat, which works by modulating connexin-43 (a protein that controls how cells communicate), to see if it could reduce swelling in the macula, the central part of the eye responsible for detailed vision, in people with diabetic macular edema who still had good eyesight. The study involved 129 adults from 24 sites across the United States who were randomly assigned to receive either 80 milligrams of tonabersat or a placebo pill for six months while researchers measured changes in the thickness of the macula using eye imaging scans. The main analysis showed no statistically significant difference between the tonabersat and placebo groups in reducing macular thickness, though a follow-up analysis that accounted for the effects of other treatments suggested tonabersat might have some benefit. The medication was generally well tolerated, though dizziness occurred more frequently in the tonabersat group compared to placebo, while vision remained stable in both groups. The researchers concluded that while the initial results were not conclusive, the hints of a positive biological effect warrant further investigation into how tonabersat and similar medications might.

title: Cost-effectiveness of vorasidenib in treatment of isocitrate dehydrogenase-mutated low-grade glioma.
abstract: Vorasidenib is Food and Drug Administration-approved for treatment of grade 2 isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas and has demonstrated a benefit in progression-free survival compared to a placebo. This study assessed the cost-effectiveness of this treatment strategy compared to standard treatment: observation or chemoradiation (CRT).The authors used an integrated Markov model to compare quality-adjusted life-years (QALY) gained and cost-effectiveness of patients with IDH-mutated low-grade glioma (LGG) treated with vorasidenib, observation, or CRT. Outcomes were expressed as incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) per QALY gained. Treatment is considered cost-effective if it meets the commonly accepted willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000 per QALY gained.Based on model parameters, vorasidenib demonstrated an ICER of $356,756 per QALY when compared to CRT. When compared to observation, vorasidenib demonstrated an improved ICER of $215,191 per QALY. On one-way sensitivity analysis compared to observation, median cost of vorasidenib and median overall survival were most likely to affect ICER with only marginal changes on analysis of other model factors. For ICER to become ≤$100,000 compared to observation, the cost of vorasidenib would need to drop to below $14,072 monthly or have a median survival gain of at least 11.9 years. The probabilistic sensitivity analysis demonstrated that vorasidenib was favored in none of 5000 Monte Carlo iterations.Using the best available data, the current price of vorasidenib does not meet commonly accepted cost-effectiveness thresholds in treatment of IDH-mutated LGGs.© 2026 American Cancer Society.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a new drug called vorasidenib offers good value for money in treating a specific type of brain tumor called low-grade glioma that has an IDH mutation, which is a genetic change found in cancer cells. The team used a mathematical model to compare the costs and health benefits of treating patients with vorasidenib, watching and waiting without treatment, or using chemotherapy combined with radiation therapy. The results showed that vorasidenib costs far more than the standard threshold doctors use to decide if a treatment is worth the price, requiring patients to pay over two hundred thousand dollars for each year of healthy life gained compared to observation. For vorasidenib to become affordable by standard medical economics measures, the monthly cost would need to drop from its current price to below fourteen thousand dollars, or the drug would need to extend patients' lives by nearly twelve additional years. Based on the best available information, the current price of vorasidenib does not represent good value for money in treating this type of brain tumor, suggesting that either the drug's cost needs to decrease significantly or additional evidence of greater benefits is needed.

title: The child opportunity index and its association with resting and exercising blood pressure in children: a Chicago metro area pilot study.
abstract: To determine whether there are differences and a spatial distribution of blood pressure (BP) measures based on Child Opportunity Index (COI) score quintiles among children aged 13-18 years old who reside in IL.A retrospective analysis of a cardiopulmonary exercise testing database was conducted to examine associations between neighborhood opportunity (measured by COI scores) and pediatric BP. BP differences across COI quintiles were analyzed using ANOVA and chi-square tests, with multivariable regressions (adjusting for age and BMI) and local bivariate analysis used to assess associations and spatial patterns.Among 1354 children, those in the lowest COI quintile were more often Black or Latinx and had the highest BMI (p < 0.01); maximal pulse pressure differed across COI quintiles (p = 0.046), and COI showed only modest independent associations with maximal diastolic BP and pulse pressure, while BMI was the strongest predictor of all BP measures (p < 0.01). Geographic Information System analysis did not yield statistically significant spatial outcomes in the data sample.Findings suggest that while neighborhood opportunity shows limited independent associations with BP measures, BMI remains a dominant predictor of BP variation among children in IL, underscoring the need to address obesity-related risk in pediatric cardiovascular health.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether children living in neighborhoods with fewer opportunities and resources had higher blood pressure, since where you live can affect your health. The study looked back at exercise test records from 1,354 children aged 13 to 18 years old in the Chicago area and compared their blood pressure measurements to a neighborhood opportunity score that measures things like access to good schools and jobs. Children from the lowest opportunity neighborhoods were more likely to be Black or Latino and had higher body weight, and while blood pressure did vary somewhat across different neighborhood opportunity levels, body weight was by far the strongest factor predicting high blood pressure in these children. The findings suggest that although where children live matters for their health, excess weight is a much more important driver of blood pressure problems in young people in Illinois. Future efforts to prevent heart disease in children should focus heavily on addressing childhood obesity while also continuing to study how neighborhood conditions affect young people's health.

title: Femoral nerve palsy in brace treatment for developmental dysplasia of the hip : incidence and outcomes in a prospective international cohort.
abstract: Femoral nerve palsy is a potential complication of brace treatment for children with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). Little is known about its causes, and previous studies have been limited by their small sample size, retrospective design, and/or being single-centre series. The aim of this study was to examine the risk factors for femoral nerve palsy in the largest prospective cohort of children to date with DDH treated using an orthosis.A global multicentre prospective database of children with DDH was analyzed. Those treated primarily using an orthosis were included. Mixed-effects logistic regression was used to identify risk factors for the development of femoral nerve palsy, including sex, age at the time of diagnosis and application of an orthosis, the type of orthosis, the location of the femoral head, femoral head cover, and α angle. Both univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted.The study included 3,008 children (5,012 affected hips) who were enrolled from 21 centres in seven countries; 99 hips (2.0%) in 94 children (3.1%) developed a femoral nerve palsy, which occurred at a median of seven days (IQR 6 to 21) after the application of a brace. A significantly increased proportion of children who developed a femoral nerve palsy were treated in a Pavlik harness compared with those who did not develop a femoral nerve palsy (84.0% (n = 79) vs 61.9% (n = 1,804); p < 0.001). Univariate analyses identified a lower percent cover of the femoral head (odds ratio (OR) 0.87 (95% CI 0.84 to 0.91); p < 0.001) and lower α angle (OR 0.82 (95% CI 0.76 to 0.89); p < 0.001) to be significantly associated with the development of femoral nerve palsy. These risk factors remained significant in the multivariate model.This is the largest multinational study to date evaluating the incidence and risk factors for the development of a femoral nerve palsy in these children. The incidence of femoral nerve palsy was 3.1%. The severity of DDH was identified as a significant risk factor for its development. The use of a Pavlik harness was significantly associated with the development of a femoral nerve palsy. Understanding the factors which influence its development will be important to optimize outcomes of treatment in children with DDH.© 2026 Schaeffer et al.

llm_summary: Femoral nerve palsy, which is a temporary or permanent weakness or paralysis of the nerve that controls leg movement, is a known risk that can happen when children with developmental dysplasia of the hip (a condition where the hip joint does not form properly) are treated with braces. Researchers from 21 medical centers across seven countries tracked 3,008 children wearing hip braces to understand how often this nerve injury occurred and what factors made it more likely to happen. The study found that about 3 out of every 100 children developed femoral nerve palsy, usually within a week of putting on the brace, and children treated with a specific type of brace called a Pavlik harness had a higher risk than those using other braces. The severity of the original hip problem was the strongest predictor of nerve injury, meaning children with more serious hip dysplasia were more likely to experience this complication. These findings will help doctors choose the safest treatment approaches and monitor high-risk patients more carefully to prevent this serious side effect.

title: Deep Sedation With a Natural Airway is a Viable Alternative to General Anesthesia With Endotracheal Tube for Isolated Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Implantation.
abstract: There is growing interest in utilizing deep sedation with a natural airway rather than general endotracheal anesthesia (GETA) for cardiac catheterization procedures due to the presumed hemodynamic benefits and faster postprocedural recovery, although a paucity of data supports these assumptions. We hypothesized that the periprocedural complication rate would be lower in patients undergoing transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation (TPVI) under deep sedation with a natural airway versus those under GETA. We performed a retrospective chart review of 85 patients undergoing isolated TPVI at a large academic medical institution. A logistical regression adjusting for age was performed. The primary outcome was periprocedural complication rate, including access site rebleeding, hematoma, conversion to GETA, arrhythmia requiring intervention, cardiac arrest, blood transfusion, and postoperative nausea and vomiting. Significantly more patients in the GETA group experienced complications compared with the deep sedation group (41.2% vs 14.7%, P = .015). The secondary outcomes included vasopressor use, recovery location, and procedural, anesthesia, and recovery times. The median procedure time was shorter in the sedation group by 38 minutes (P = .010), and anesthesia time was shorter by 50 minutes (P = .001). Overall, we found that deep sedation is feasible for TPVI and in this retrospective study was associated with decreased periprocedural complications.Copyright © 2026 by the American Association of Nurse Anesthesiology.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether keeping patients awake but deeply sedated during heart valve replacement procedures could be safer than putting them completely to sleep with a breathing tube. The team reviewed medical records of eighty-five patients who had transcatheter pulmonary valve implantation, which is a minimally invasive procedure to replace a faulty valve in the heart, comparing those who stayed awake with sedation to those who were fully anesthetized. Patients who remained awake with deep sedation experienced significantly fewer complications like bleeding, blood clots, and irregular heartbeats, with only about fifteen percent having problems compared to forty-one percent in the fully anesthetized group. The sedation approach also allowed procedures to finish about thirty-eight minutes faster and reduced the total time patients needed anesthesia by fifty minutes, potentially leading to quicker recovery. While this study suggests that deep sedation with a natural airway is a safe and effective option for this type of heart procedure, more research is needed to confirm these findings and determine which patients benefit most from each approach.

title: Exploring Opioid Prescriber Decision-Making: A Qualitative Study.
abstract: To explore the opioid decision-making process of prescribers in primary care, surgery, and subspecialty pain management.This was a multistage qualitative-qualitative study with clinicians involved in opioid prescribing and management from a single healthcare organization with locations in Minnesota, Florida, Arizona, and Wisconsin. Clinicians in this study included physicians, nurse practitioners (NPs), and physician assistants (PAs) practicing in primary care, surgery, or pain medicine. The interview guide was organized in three domains of a conceptual model for opioid use: (1) prescriber characteristics, (2) patient characteristics, and (3) practice environment characteristics. Individual interviews (N = 20) were performed first, and data were summarized using a rapid template-based approach. Subsequently, focus groups (FGs) (N = 4) were conducted with an additional 21 clinicians to confirm and explore interview results. Data from interviews and FGs were analyzed using a common codebook.Findings were organized as decision factors into the three domains. Factors in the prescriber domain included characteristics such as formal pain management training, as well as factors that influenced knowledge and beliefs (e.g., advice from or observation of supervising clinicians and expert colleagues). Decision factors in the patient domain included patient pain etiology, comorbid medical or mental health conditions, and demographic characteristics. Clinicians' perceptions of these factors, such as viewing older age as having lesser risk for opioid misuse, influenced prescribing decisions. Clinicians also described challenges associated with "legacy patients" whose therapy was previously managed by a different clinician. Primary care clinicians, in particular, expressed difficulties managing post-surgical or trauma-related pain after care transition. Relevant decision factors reported by prescribers in the practice environment domain included guidelines and practice oversight. Most participants reported practicing in an environment that promoted conservative opioid use and having access to standardized institutional guidelines that reduced perceived decision-making burden. Clinicians described how they used prescribing guidelines to help them communicate with patients about opioid use and prescribing decisions.Intersecting prescriber, patient, and practice environment factors shape opioid analgesic prescribing decisions. Available resources in the practice environment, including peer input and institutional guidelines, may support clinician decision-making and conversations with patients at the point of care, including in cases where patients have complex histories or personal characteristics that influence decision making.© 2026 Mayo Clinic. llm_summary: Researchers examined how doctors and other healthcare providers decide whether to prescribe opioids, which are powerful pain medications that carry risks of addiction and misuse. The study involved interviews with twenty clinicians and focus groups with twenty-one additional clinicians from a large healthcare organization across four states, asking them about the factors that influence their prescribing decisions. The findings showed that three main areas shape these decisions: the clinician's own training and beliefs about pain management, the patient's specific situation including their age and medical history, and the healthcare setting's guidelines and oversight policies. Clinicians reported that having clear institutional guidelines and advice from experienced colleagues helped them make better decisions and talk with patients about opioid use, especially for complex cases involving patients with complicated medical histories. These results suggest that supporting doctors with good guidelines and peer input at the moment they make prescribing decisions could help improve how opioids are used in healthcare.

title: Protocol for Neuro-Oncology Anywhere: Deploying Mayo Clinic's remote cognitive assessment battery and wearable device monitoring platform while assessing the impact of metformin on cognition and quality of life in patients with history of cranial radiation.
abstract: Cognitive symptoms are among the most frequently reported issues in cancer patients treated with cranial radiation, yet they remain inadequately assessed in clinical practice and are suboptimally treated. Cranial radiation is an integral part of treatment for primary and metastatic brain tumors that contributes to progressive and irreversible cognitive decline with currently limited therapeutic options. Development of effective interventions that can prevent or delay this neurocognitive toxicity requires accurate assessment of symptom burden. However, formal neuropsychological testing is resource intensive and time consuming. Repeated in-person assessments are often not feasible for cancer patients who must travel great distances to specialized cancer centers. The Neuro-Oncology Anywhere (NOA) study is a fully decentralized clinical trial with an overarching goal to evaluate remote cognitive assessments while simultaneously evaluating benefits of health promotion through use of a wearable watch device and metformin in preventing radiation-related cognitive decline. The primary objective of this study is to determine the feasibility of completing serial remote cognitive, activity/sleep, and self-reported assessments among patients who have previously received cranial radiation. Key secondary objectives are to assess satisfaction of patients with remote monitoring, evaluate adherence to study drug, and compare neurocognitive function scores and the impact of receiving metformin and health promotion with a wearable device compared to wearable device alone. Determination of the remote platform's feasibility among patients with brain tumors will provide a strong scientific foundation for routinely integrating scalable remote cognitive assessment strategies into future clinical trials, enabling accelerated evaluation of potentially effective interventions unconstrained by geographic limitations.NCT06377696.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Patients who receive radiation treatment to the head for brain tumors often experience memory and thinking problems that get worse over time, but doctors struggle to properly test and treat these issues because formal brain testing takes a lot of time and requires patients to travel to specialized centers. Researchers created a new study called Neuro-Oncology Anywhere that tests whether patients can do cognitive assessments, or thinking and memory tests, from home using remote technology instead of traveling to a hospital. The study also examines whether a common diabetes medication called metformin combined with a wearable watch device that tracks activity and sleep might help prevent or slow down the thinking problems caused by radiation. The main goal is to see if remote testing is practical and works well for patients, which could eventually allow doctors to test new treatments for radiation-related brain damage without requiring patients to travel long distances. If this remote testing approach proves successful, it could change how cancer centers evaluate new treatments and help more patients access cognitive assessments and potential therapies regardless of where they live.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) Receptor Agonists and Cutaneous Biology: Implications for Skin Disease and Longevity.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have expanded from metabolic therapeutics to agents with broad effects on inflammation, tissue repair, cutaneous and adipose biology, and aging-related pathways. Clinicians increasingly encounter cutaneous manifestations and aesthetic sequelae with important implications for dermatologic counseling and multidisciplinary care.To review current evidence regarding GLP-1RA effects on skin biology, inflammatory dermatoses, wound healing, cutaneous adverse events, and aesthetic aging.A narrative review of clinical, translational, and mechanistic literature was performed, emphasizing psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, wound repair, skin hypersensitivity reactions, autoimmune blistering disease, and facial volume loss associated with pharmacologic weight reduction.GLP-1RAs are hypothesized to improve inflammatory skin conditions and wound repair through anti-inflammatory, immunometabolic, and proreparative pathways. Yet, their use may also be associated with injection-site reactions, hypersensitivity eruptions, rare autoimmune blistering disorders, and clinically significant facial deflation and skin laxity. Current evidence is strongest for mechanistic plausibility and observational clinical signals, whereas dermatology-specific randomized trials remain limited.GLP-1RAs exert bidirectional effects on cutaneous biology. Recognition of both therapeutic opportunities and potential aesthetic or adverse sequelae is important, with patient counseling ideally occurring within a multidisciplinary framework that integrates metabolic benefits with skin health and appearance.Copyright © 2026 by the American Society for Dermatologic Surgery, Inc. llm_summary: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, which are medications originally developed to help people with diabetes and weight loss, are now being studied for their effects on skin health and aging. Researchers reviewed existing scientific evidence from clinical studies and laboratory research to understand how these medications affect various skin conditions, wound healing, and the appearance of aging skin. The review found that these medications may help improve inflammatory skin diseases like psoriasis and hidradenitis suppurativa through anti-inflammatory effects, but they can also cause unwanted side effects including injection-site reactions, allergic rashes, and facial volume loss that makes skin appear deflated and loose. While the evidence suggests these medications have promise for treating certain skin conditions, most of the current research is based on observations and laboratory studies rather than large-scale clinical trials specifically designed to test skin outcomes. Doctors should discuss both the potential skin benefits and possible aesthetic side effects with patients taking these medications as part of a comprehensive care plan that considers overall health, appearance, and quality of life.

title: Reduced Epidermal p21 Expression Is Identified in Some Subjects on Systemic GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: A Hypothesis-Generating Pilot Study of Metabolic Modulation in Human Skin Senescence.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) exert systemic metabolic and anti-inflammatory effects that may be relevant to cellular senescence, a key driver of skin aging. However, human cutaneous data are lacking.To explore whether systemic GLP-1RA therapy translates to a detectable reduction in cutaneous senescence, quantified by epidermal p21 expression and supported by AI-driven facial imaging.In this controlled observational pilot study, 3 male adults (GLP-1RA n = 2; GLP-1RA-naïve control n = 1) underwent 3-mm punch biopsies from a standardized, sun-protected gluteal site to isolate intrinsic aging. Senescence was quantified through blinded whole-epidermis digital annotation of p21-positive nuclei. Clinical phenotypes were assessed using noninvasive cheek measurements and AI-based facial age estimation.The cohort demonstrated divergence in senescence-associated biomarkers correlating with GLP-1RA exposure. The GLP-1RA-naïve control exhibited 8.0% (n = 2,062 nuclei) epidermal senescence. By contrast, participants with 163 and 62 days of GLP-1RA exposure showed reduced senescence burdens of 2.4% (n = 2,045) and 0.6% (n = 1,636), respectively. Automated facial age estimation remained concordant with chronological age across subjects.Systemic GLP-1RA exposure is associated with a substantial reduction in epidermal p21 expression in some subjects, suggesting a senomorphic effect and supporting further mechanistic studies at the interface of metabolic regulation and skin aging.Copyright © 2026 by the American Society for Dermatologic Surgery, Inc. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a popular diabetes and weight loss medication called GLP-1 receptor agonists might slow down skin aging by reducing cellular senescence, which is the process where cells stop dividing and contribute to wrinkles and aging. The study involved taking small skin samples from three men, two of whom were taking the medication and one who was not, and then counting special aging markers called p21 in their skin cells using a microscope and computer analysis. The results showed that the two men taking the medication had much lower levels of these aging markers in their skin compared to the man who was not taking it, with one showing a reduction from eight percent down to less than one percent. These findings suggest that the medication might have a protective effect on skin aging by reducing the buildup of senescent cells, which could open up new ways to think about treating skin aging through metabolic drugs. However, because this was a very small pilot study with only three participants, much more research is needed to confirm whether this effect is real and to understand exactly how the medication might be working to slow skin aging.

llm_summary: Researchers identified and characterized a previously unknown variant of a human immune system gene called HLA-DPA1*03:25, which is important because understanding genetic variations helps doctors better match organ donors with transplant recipients and predict how patients will respond to certain treatments. The team used next generation sequencing, a modern DNA reading technology that can identify tiny differences in genetic code, to study this new gene variant in detail. The key finding was that this new variant differs from known versions by just a single letter change in the genetic code at position 96 in the third section of the gene. This discovery adds to the growing catalog of human genetic diversity and may help medical professionals provide more personalized care by better understanding how different people's immune systems work. Future research will likely focus on determining whether this variant has any practical effects on immune function or transplant outcomes in patients who carry it.

title: Extracellular Vesicles as Enabling Biomarkers for New Approach Methodologies to Support the US Food and Drug Administration Modernization Act 3.0.
abstract: The FDA Modernization Act 3.0 represents a pivotal shift in biomedical research by formally removing the requirement for animal testing and enabling regulatory acceptance of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs). This transition creates an urgent need for robust, human-relevant biomarkers that can anchor NAM-generated data within regulatory decision-making, particularly for first-in-human studies. Extracellular vesicles (EVs), owing to their biological stability, accessibility and rich molecular cargo, may be well positioned to fulfil this role. EVs reflect dynamic cellular states and intercellular communication, making them mechanistically informative readouts of pharmacology, toxicity, immune modulation and disease biology across human-derived model systems. This Perspective outlines how EV-based biomarkers can support the qualification, standardization, and regulatory acceptance of NAMs, with particular emphasis on ex vivo platforms such as organoids, microtissue systems, organ-on-chip devices and perfused tissue slices. We highlight the advantages of EVs for longitudinal, non-destructive sampling, representation of human variability, and integration with quantitative systems pharmacology and physiologically based pharmacokinetic models. Finally, we discuss the scientific, operational and regulatory challenges that must be addressed and argue that coordinated leadership from the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles (ISEV) is essential. The convergence of regulatory reform and EV science presents a timely call to action to establish EVs as foundational biomarkers in next-generation, human-centric drug development.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: The FDA Modernization Act 3. 0 has removed the requirement for animal testing in drug development, creating an urgent need for better human-based methods to test whether new medicines are safe and effective. Researchers examined how extracellular vesicles, which are tiny particles released by cells that carry important biological information, could serve as reliable markers or signals to measure how drugs affect human tissue systems grown in laboratories. Extracellular vesicles are particularly useful because they are stable, easy to collect without harming tissue, and contain rich information about what cells are doing, making them ideal for tracking drug effects, toxicity, immune responses, and disease changes across human-derived model systems like organoids and organ-on-chip devices. Using extracellular vesicles as biomarkers could help researchers monitor drug responses over time without destroying tissue samples, better represent how different people respond to medicines, and integrate this information with computer models that predict how drugs move through the body.

title: Proton Therapy for Head and Neck Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma: A Multi-institutional Review.
abstract: To evaluate efficacy and toxicity (CTCAE v4.0) outcomes in patients with adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) treated with proton beam therapy (PBT).From 2012 through 2023, 79 patients with non-metastatic ACC were treated with PBT and enrolled on the Proton Collaborative Group (PCG) registry. Kaplan-Meier analyses quantified locoregional control (LRC), disease-free survival (DFS), and overall survival (OS). ACC patients receiving reirradiation with PBT were excluded from this analysis.Median follow-up was 3 years (0.01-6.72). Twenty-six patients were unable to undergo surgery and received definitive PBT versus postoperative PBT (n=53). Median postoperative PBT dose was 66 GyE and 70 GyE for definitive patients treated with conventional fractionation. Most patients had localized disease (n=75); few had nodal metastases (n=4). 62% were locally advanced (T3-T4) at the time of PBT treatment. 3-year Locoregional control (LRC) for all patients was 98% [95% CI (94.3, 100)]. Advanced T-staging, positive margins and definitive-intent PBT were not associated with worsened LRC. 3-year Progression free survival (PFS) was 80.5% (70.6, 91.7). Patients receiving definitive intent PBT had lower but nonsignificant PFS (73.3% vs. 83.8%, p-0.075). Advanced T-staging and positive margins did not have worsened PFS. Overall survival at 3 years was 89.2% (81.4, 97.8). Acute grade 3 toxicities occurred in 16 patients, the most common included the following: mucositis (n=5), oral pain (n=3), and dermatitis (n=5). Late grade 3 toxicity (n=2) included middle ear inflammation (n=1) and skin ulceration (n=1). There were no grade 4+ toxicities.PBT appears to be highly efficacious in providing LRC for patients with ACC including those patients treated with definitive intent. PBT toxicity was acceptable. Longer follow-up is needed.© 2026 The Author(s).

title: Deep Brain Stimulation of the Nucleus Accumbens Modulates Effort-Based Decision-Making and Phasic Dopamine Release in Male Wistar Rats.
abstract: The initiation and sustained expression of motivated behaviour is strongly regulated by mesolimbic dopamine (DA) release within the nucleus accumbens (NAc). Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has demonstrated efficacy in treating refractory psychiatric disorders characterised by dysfunctional motivated drive and related behaviours. However, the neurobiological mechanisms underlying DBS effects at the local and circuit levels remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of NAc DBS on effort-based decision-making and local phasic DA neurotransmission in male Wistar rats. Male Wistar rats (N = 8) were trained on a concurrent fixed ratio 5/chow effort-related choice task (ERCT) until stable baseline performance was reached. On the test day, animals underwent a 2-h session of high-frequency NAc DBS (130 Hz; 90 μs pulse width; 500 μA) immediately prior to behavioural testing, with additional testing conducted on subsequent days to assess prolonged effects. In a separate experiment, the effects of identical NAc DBS parameters (or sham) on ventral tegmental area (VTA)-evoked (120 pulses; 60 Hz; 2 ms pulse width; 200-500 μA) DA release in the NAc core were quantified using fast-scan cyclic voltammetry in urethane-anesthetised rats (N = 12). Acute bilateral NAc DBS transiently reduced overall food-related motivation while maintaining effort-based choice bias. In parallel, NAc DBS significantly suppressed VTA-evoked NAc DA release compared to sham, although a moderate reduction was also observed in sham controls. DA reuptake kinetics remained unchanged across groups. NAc DBS transiently suppresses overall food-related motivation while maintaining effort-based decision-making. llm_summary: Researchers examined how deep brain stimulation, a procedure where electrical pulses are sent to specific brain regions, affects motivation and a brain chemical called dopamine in rats. The study involved training rats to choose between working hard for food pellets or eating readily available chow, then applying electrical stimulation to a brain area called the nucleus accumbens, which controls motivation and reward. When the rats received this brain stimulation, they showed reduced overall desire for food but still maintained their preference for choosing the harder task, and their dopamine levels decreased compared to rats that did not receive stimulation. These findings suggest that deep brain stimulation may work by reducing dopamine activity in ways that lower overall motivation while preserving the ability to make effort-based decisions. This research could help scientists better understand how deep brain stimulation might help people with psychiatric disorders involving low motivation, though more studies are needed to confirm whether these effects in rats apply to humans.

title: Patient characteristics and incidence of in-hospital events in spontaneous coronary artery dissection and suspected concurrent Takotsubo syndrome: A report of the iSCAD registry.
abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) and spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) are both more common in middle-aged women and often share similar triggers, such as emotional or physical stress. This study aimed to examine the characteristics and in-hospital prognosis of patients with SCAD and possible concomitant TTS.Patients from the iSCAD Registry with completed questionnaires, case report forms, and available coronary angiography and ventriculography adjudicated by a core lab were included. In the absence of follow-up imaging confirming resolution of the wall motion abnormalities a definitive diagnosis of TTS cannot be established, therefore this pattern will be referred to throughout the manuscript as TTS-like angiographic pattern (TVP). Coexistent TVP was defined by classic apical ballooning or wall motion abnormalities discordant with the dissected coronary territory. In-hospital events included recurrent myocardial infarction (MI), cerebrovascular accident, heart failure (HF) requiring diuretics, and new arrhythmias. Patient characteristics and in-hospital events were compared between TVP and non-TVP groups.Among 259 study participants, 44 (17.0%) were identified with coexistent TVP. There were no significant differences in age, cardiovascular risk factors, anxiety or depression history, recreational substance use, emotional or physical stressors, or extracoronary vascular abnormalities between the TVP and non-TVP groups. Patients with TVP were more likely to present with ST-segment elevation MI, left ventricular dysfunction, left anterior descending artery involvement, and abnormal myocardial perfusion compared to non-TVP patients. Furthermore, TVP patients had a higher incidence of experiencing in-hospital events (34.1% vs. 13.1%; p < 0.001), primarily driven by new arrhythmias (21.4% vs. 6.4%; p = 0.002) and HF (10.0% vs. 2.0%; p = 0.010). After multivariable adjustment, coexistent TVP remained associated with in-hospital events.In this SCAD cohort, patients with concurrent TVP had a greater risk of new arrhythmias or HF during hospitalization.URL: http://www.clinicaltrials.gov. llm_summary: Researchers examined patients who experienced spontaneous coronary artery dissection, which is a sudden tear in a heart blood vessel, to understand what happens when this condition occurs alongside Takotsubo syndrome, a temporary heart weakness usually triggered by stress. The study included 259 patients from a registry who had completed medical records and heart imaging tests reviewed by specialists, with 44 patients showing signs of both conditions occurring together. Patients with both conditions were more likely to have serious heart problems during their hospital stay, including dangerous heart rhythms and heart failure requiring fluid-removing medications, compared to those with only the artery dissection. The researchers found that even after accounting for other health factors, patients with both conditions had a significantly higher rate of dangerous in-hospital events, with new irregular heartbeats being the most common complication. These findings suggest that doctors should watch more carefully for complications in patients who develop both spontaneous coronary artery dissection and Takotsubo syndrome at the same time.

title: Role of the Emergency Medicine Pharmacist in the Management of Boarding Patients: An Opinion of the Emergency Medicine Practice and Research Network of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy Endorsed by the SAEM Academy of Emergency Medicine Pharmacists and the Society of Emergency Medicine Pharmacists.
abstract: As emergency department (ED) crowding and patient boarding reach critical levels nationwide, the role of the emergency medicine pharmacist (EMP) must be both defined and safeguarded. While EMPs are increasingly valued for their contributions to acute care, their responsibilities often unintentionally expand during periods of operational strain, particularly when admitted patients remain in the ED for prolonged durations. EMPs should ideally be resourced to remain focused on time-sensitive, high-risk medication management where their expertise is most impactful and not be used as default providers for all pharmacotherapy needs during ED boarding. This perspective outlines our position on the ideal scope of EMP practice during times of congestion, advocating for clearly defined role boundaries, strategic collaboration with other pharmacy team members, and system-level support to prevent dilution of emergency care. EMPs must be empowered to prioritize critical ED workflows, support resuscitations, and lead initiatives in education, protocol development, and patient safety, without being overextended by responsibilities that can be absorbed by other team members.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Emergency departments across the country are becoming dangerously overcrowded, with admitted patients sometimes waiting in the emergency room for hours or days before moving to hospital beds, which creates pressure on the specialized pharmacists who work in these departments. A group of pharmacy and emergency medicine experts came together to write a position paper outlining how emergency medicine pharmacists, who are medication specialists trained to work in fast-paced emergency settings, should focus their work during these periods of extreme crowding. The experts argue that these pharmacists should concentrate on time-sensitive, high-risk medication decisions where their specialized training makes the biggest difference, rather than being stretched thin to handle all medication needs for patients waiting in the emergency department. The recommendations emphasize that emergency medicine pharmacists need clear job boundaries, support from other pharmacy team members, and system-level changes so they can stay focused on critical emergency care tasks like supporting resuscitations and developing safety protocols. Without these protections and support systems in place, emergency medicine pharmacists risk becoming overwhelmed by routine medication tasks that other team members could handle, which would prevent them from doing the specialized emergency work where they are most valuable.

title: Defining surgeon experience thresholds for the reduction in complications and revisions after shoulder arthroplasty: a meta-analysis of 332,542 patients.
abstract: Shoulder arthroplasty utilization has increased substantially, with a growing proportion of cases performed by surgeons early in the learning curve. Surgeon-volume definitions vary widely across the literature, and although higher volume is generally associated with better outcomes, there is no consensus on the thresholds that define high volume. This study aimed to determine shoulder arthroplasty cases/yr thresholds at which complication and revision risks diverge between low- and high-volume surgeons.PubMed, Cochrane, and Google Scholar were queried through December 2025. Inclusion criteria consisted of comparative studies evaluating the number of complications and revisions after shoulder arthroplasty across different categories of surgeon experience. Five different thresholds of cases/yr were established to perform the analysis and define high- and low-volume surgeons: 5 cases/yr, 10 cases/yr, 14 cases/yr, 20 cases/yr, and 25-28 cases/yr.Eight studies with 332,542 patients were included. At the 5 cases/yr threshold, low-volume surgeons had higher odds of complications (odds ratio [OR] = 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.28-1.55; P< .001) and revision (OR = 1.41; 95% CI, 1.28-1.57; P< .001). At the 10 cases/yr threshold, there were no differences in complications (OR = 1.21; 95% CI, 0.94-1.56; P= .14) or revision (OR = 1.18; 95% CI, 0.90-1.54; P= .22). At the 14 cases/yr threshold, revisions were similar (OR = 1.15; 95% CI, 0.89-1.48; P= .28). At the 20 cases/yr threshold, revision did not differ (OR = 1.15; 95% CI, 0.87-1.52; P= .34). At the 25-28 cases/yr threshold, low-volume surgeons had higher odds of complications (OR = 1.39; 95% CI, 1.11-1.75; P= .004) and revision (OR = 1.22; 95% CI, 1.15-1.30; P< .001).This study identified surgeon-volume thresholds for shoulder arthroplasty of 5 cases/yr and 25-28 cases/yr, which may possibly define low-to-medium and medium-to-high-volume thresholds, respectively. Patients treated by surgeons below these thresholds had higher risks of complications and revision compared with those treated by surgeons above the respective thresholds.© 2026 Published by Elsevier Inc. on behalf of American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons.
