llm_summary: Researchers examined whether certain immune system markers called myositis autoantibodies, which are proteins the body produces against its own muscles, could help doctors identify lung disease in patients with inflammatory muscle conditions. The team looked back at medical records from over one thousand patients tested for these autoantibodies between 1997 and 2022 at a single hospital to see how often patients with positive antibody tests developed interstitial lung disease, which is a condition where lung tissue becomes scarred and stiff. They found that patients with positive autoantibody tests were significantly more likely to develop lung disease compared to those without these antibodies, and those with both antibodies and lung disease showed more severe symptoms including poor blood circulation in fingers, joint pain, and signs of inflammation. The results suggest that testing for myositis autoantibodies could help doctors identify which patients are at higher risk for developing lung complications and may represent a distinct group of patients who need closer monitoring. However, the researchers noted that their findings come from a single hospital and were based on past medical records, so more research at multiple centers would be needed to confirm these results and understand how to best use this information in clinical practice.

title: Incidence and Outcomes of Refractory Septic Shock per Consensus Clinical Criteria: A Multicohort Retrospective Study.
abstract: Consensus clinical criteria for refractory septic shock were recently developed, but the incidence and outcomes with these criteria are unknown. There were two aims: 1) to describe the incidence of refractory septic shock and 2) to assess outcomes of patients with septic shock meeting refractory septic shock criteria compared with those who did not.Multicohort, retrospective study. For aim 1, a descriptive epidemiologic study was designed to ascertain the cumulative incidence of refractory septic shock in patients with septic shock. For aim 2, a cohort study was conducted to compare hospital mortality between patients meeting refractory septic shock clinical criteria compared with those who did not.Large U.S. health system from 2012 to 2024.Adults (age ≥ 18 yr) meeting both Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Adult Sepsis Event and Sepsis-3 clinical criteria for septic shock. llm_summary: Researchers examined a serious condition called refractory septic shock, which occurs when patients with life-threatening blood infections do not respond well to standard treatments like blood pressure medications, to understand how often it happens and how it affects survival rates. The study looked back at medical records from a large U. S. hospital system between 2012 and 2024, tracking nearly 16,000 patients who had septic shock and measuring whether they met specific criteria for the refractory form, which was defined as needing high doses of blood pressure medication combined with high levels of a substance called lactate in the blood. About one in five patients with septic shock, or roughly 3,400 people, met the criteria for refractory septic shock, and these patients had a death rate of 64 percent compared to much lower rates in patients without this condition.

title: Predicting Treatment Response After Total Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer.
abstract: To develop a predictive model for pathological complete response (pCR) after total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) to inform selection for watch-and-wait (W/W).Patient selection for W/W after TNT for locally advanced rectal cancer remains challenging.An ensemble of tabular foundation models was fine-tuned in adults with clinical stage II or III microsatellite stable primary rectal adenocarcinoma undergoing TNT and total mesorectal excision (TNT+TME) from 2018-2023 to predict pCR, using pre-TNT, post-TNT and pre-TME variables. This model was externally validated on patients having TNT and W/W (TNT+W/W) to predict persistent clinical complete response (pcCR; the absence of local regrowth, distant metastases, or persistent near-cCR). Area under the receiver operator curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and Brier score were calculated with 95% confidence intervals (CI).Among 308 patients that underwent TNT+TME (median age 56; 40% female), the model predicted pCR with an AUROC 0.71 (95% CI 0.65-0.77), AUPRC 0.44 (95% CI 0.35-0.57), and was well calibrated with a Brier score of 0.17 (95% CI 0.15-0.20). llm_summary: Researchers examined how to better predict which patients with advanced rectal cancer will have a complete response to chemotherapy and radiation before surgery, which could help doctors decide whether patients need surgery or can safely skip it. The team developed a computer prediction model using information from 308 patients who received chemotherapy and radiation followed by surgery, training the model to identify which patients would have no remaining cancer cells after treatment. The model performed well at predicting complete response in the surgery group, and when tested on a separate group of 83 patients who chose to skip surgery and be monitored instead, it accurately predicted which patients remained cancer-free without needing the operation. This predictive tool could help doctors and patients make better decisions about whether surgery is necessary after chemotherapy and radiation, potentially allowing some patients to avoid surgery while still catching any cancer that returns. The researchers note that the model needs further testing and adjustment before it can be widely used in everyday clinical practice to guide treatment decisions for rectal cancer patients.

title: Physical Attractiveness and Chances of Being Invited to Interview With a Medical Residency Program: Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Applicants participating in the Residency Match generally submit a photograph through the Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS). Studies demonstrate that subjectively more attractive applicants are more likely to succeed during job recruitment, including a paper related to the Residency Match.This study further investigates the relationship between an applicant's attractiveness and the likelihood that they are invited to interview with a residency program to explore if more attractive applicants are more likely to be invited to interview when controlled for demographic and academic variables. If there are enough data suggesting that an ERAS photograph being visible prior to the interview gives an unfair advantage to more attractive applicants, this practice might be reconsidered by some residency programs or by ERAS itself.Residency directors were surveyed on application review practices. Programs that viewed ERAS photographs prior to deciding whether to invite an applicant to interview were asked to share ERAS files of all reviewed applicants of the 2022 Match. A machine learning model was used to determine attractiveness scores for ERAS photographs. The scores ranged from 1 to 10, where 1 represents the least attractive and 10 represents the most attractive. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed considering attractiveness scores, demographics, and professional characteristics. The primary outcome of interest was an invitation to an interview with a residency program.The residency program response rate was 47.5% (29/61). Among 2681 unique applications to 10 specialties in a single academic health system, the median attractiveness score for all applicants was 6.02 (IQR 5.54-6.55). The univariable analysis indicated a 19% higher invitation likelihood with a 1-point increase in attractiveness. After adjusting for demographics and professional experiences, the association lost statistical significance. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether medical school graduates applying for residency positions receive unfair advantages based on physical attractiveness, since applicants submit photographs as part of their application materials. The study collected application files from residency programs that review photographs before deciding which candidates to interview, then used a computer program to score how attractive each applicant's photo appeared on a scale from one to ten. When looking at the raw data alone, applicants with higher attractiveness scores were nineteen percent more likely to get invited for interviews, but this advantage disappeared when researchers accounted for other important factors like grades, test scores, and background information. The findings suggest that while attractiveness might seem to matter at first glance, it does not actually give applicants a real edge once their academic qualifications are considered. These results could help residency programs and application services decide whether showing photographs before making interview decisions creates unfair bias against less conventionally attractive candidates.

title: Uterine Leiomyomas Across the Menopausal Transition.
abstract: Leiomyomas remain highly prevalent by midlife, with persistent racial disparities in age at onset and tumor burden. Although they are traditionally expected to regress after menopause, longitudinal data demonstrate variable behavior, with many leiomyomas persisting, some regressing modestly, and a subset continuing to grow. This structured, nonsystematic review of the contemporary literature was conducted using PubMed and Embase, supplemented by guideline and reference review, with the objective of guiding the evaluation and management of uterine leiomyomas across the menopausal transition. In perimenopausal and postmenopausal patients, abnormal uterine bleeding and pelvic pain require systematic evaluation to exclude endometrial pathology and alternative causes. Transvaginal ultrasonography with structured assessment provides the foundation for evaluation, and magnetic resonance imaging serves as an adjunct when findings are indeterminate or clinical concern is elevated. No single imaging feature reliably distinguishes benign leiomyoma from leiomyosarcoma, and the prevalence of unsuspected leiomyosarcoma at surgery remains low, increasing with age. Management should be individualized and symptom driven, incorporating patient age, comorbidities, hormonal exposures, imaging findings, and preferences, with expectant management appropriate for asymptomatic patients and intervention reserved for refractory symptoms or diagnostic uncertainty.Copyright © 2026 by the American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists. llm_summary: Uterine leiomyomas, which are noncancerous tumors that grow in the uterus, remain common in middle-aged women and affect different racial groups differently in terms of when they develop and how large they grow. Researchers reviewed recent medical literature from scientific databases to understand how these tumors behave as women go through menopause and to guide doctors on how to evaluate and treat them during this life stage. Contrary to what doctors traditionally expected, these tumors do not always shrink after menopause; instead, some stay the same size, some shrink a little, and some continue to grow. When women in or past menopause experience abnormal bleeding or pelvic pain, doctors need to carefully check whether the symptoms come from the tumors themselves or from other conditions like cancer of the uterine lining. The best approach to treatment should be personalized based on each woman's age, overall health, symptoms, and preferences, with doctors recommending watchful waiting for women without symptoms and medical or surgical treatment only when symptoms become difficult to manage or when there is uncertainty about the diagnosis.

llm_summary: The 2026 guidelines for treating acute ischemic stroke, which occurs when a blood clot blocks blood flow to the brain, have been updated to help doctors manage these medical emergencies more effectively. The authors created a focused review of these new guidelines specifically for radiologists, who are doctors that specialize in medical imaging like CT and MRI scans. The updated guidelines keep many of the proven recommendations from before while adding new guidance about imaging procedures, hospital care, and treatment methods such as clot-busting medications given through veins and mechanical devices that remove clots from blood vessels. Importantly, the 2026 guidelines now include expanded advice for medium-sized blood vessel blockages and provide recommendations for treating strokes in children, which were largely missing from previous versions. These changes are expected to improve how radiologists perform their imaging work in stroke patients and ultimately help doctors provide faster and better treatment to people experiencing strokes.

title: Kainic acid pig model of hippocampal epilepsy.
abstract: Translational large-animal models that can accommodate human-scale implantable devices are essential for advancing neuromodulation therapies in epilepsy. This study establishes a kainic acid (KA)-induced porcine model of mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (mTLE) using clinical imaging, stereotactic surgery, and a fully implantable neural stimulator-recorder (INSR) device designed for humans. Seven pigs (six KA-treated and one saline control) underwent MRI-guided stereotactic implantation of electrodes targeting bilateral hippocampus (HPC) and anterior thalamus (ANT), followed by intra-hippocampal KA or saline infusion. Local field potentials (LFP) were recorded continuously with synchronized video monitoring. Seizures and LFP interictal epileptiform-like discharges (IEDs) were quantified using validated automated detectors. Histology was performed in the saline control and the longest surviving KA-treated pig. Intra-hippocampal KA infusion induced acute status epilepticus in all treated pigs (6/6). Four animals survived to chronic monitoring with spontaneous seizures observed in three pigs (2,733 seizures; mean duration of 27.2 ± 17.6 s). IEDs were observed in bilateral HPC of all animals, including saline control, with higher rates in the lesioned HPC (p < 0.0001). While the IED morphology is consistent with epileptiform activity, IEDs alone are not specific for epilepsy and physiological transients (e.g. sharp-wave ripples) and injury-related hyperexcitability or strain-specific hyperexcitability cannot be excluded. Histological analysis revealed patchy neuronal loss and cytoarchitectural changes in HPC. This porcine model reproduces electrophysiological features of human mTLE. This approach provides a powerful translational bridge for developing and testing next-generation INSR and neuromodulation strategies in freely behaving large animals.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined a new way to study epilepsy, a brain condition that causes repeated seizures, by creating a pig model that mimics the human form of the disease affecting the hippocampus, which is the brain region involved in memory and seizure control. The team used brain imaging and precise surgical techniques to implant recording devices directly into the brains of pigs, then triggered epilepsy-like activity by injecting a chemical called kainic acid into the hippocampus while monitoring electrical brain activity continuously. The pigs that received the chemical injection developed seizures and showed abnormal electrical patterns in their brain recordings that matched what doctors see in human epilepsy patients, with three of the four surviving animals experiencing thousands of spontaneous seizures over the study period. This pig model is important because it allows researchers to test new brain stimulation treatments and recording devices that are designed for human use in a large animal that has a brain size and structure similar to humans. The findings provide a valuable stepping stone for developing and testing next-generation treatments for epilepsy before they are tested in human patients, though researchers note that some of the electrical patterns observed could be caused by brain injury rather than true epilepsy.

title: A first-in-human, open-label multicentre Phase 1 study of the orally administered E7386 in patients with selected advanced neoplasms.
abstract: We present data from the Phase 1 open-label Study 101 of E7386, an oral protein-protein interaction inhibitor reported to block the CBP/β-catenin interaction, in patients with solid tumours.Eligible patients (across the UK and US) aged ≥18 years had advanced/recurrent solid tumours (dose-escalation) or CTNNB1-mutated hepatocellular carcinoma (dose-expansion). Primary objectives were to assess safety/tolerability and determine the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) of E7386.Thirty-eight patients received study drug (dose-escalation: n = 32; expansion: n = 6; dose-range: 5-120 mg twice daily [BID]); 60.5% received ≥3 prior anticancer medications. Dose-limiting toxicities (grade-2 lethargy and grade-2 decreased appetite) occurred in 1 patient (20 mg BID cohort). The RP2D was determined as 120 mg BID. Most (94.7%) patients experienced treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs), most frequently nausea (65.8%) and vomiting (60.5%), which were primarily grade 1/2 and well-managed with antiemetics. No grade 4/5 TRAEs were noted. Pharmacokinetic exposure increased with increasing dose, although large intersubject variability was observed. No objective responses were noted; stable disease (SD) was observed in 36.8% of patients, including SD ≥ 23 weeks in 18.8% of patients (dose-escalation).E7386 demonstrated a manageable safety profile, a dose-dependent pharmacokinetic profile, and some disease stabilisation in heavily pretreated patients with advanced solid tumours.NCT03264664 https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03264664 .© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new oral drug called E7386 that works by blocking a specific protein interaction involved in cancer cell growth, testing it for the first time in human patients with advanced solid tumors across medical centers in the United Kingdom and United States. The study involved 38 patients who took increasing doses of the drug ranging from 5 to 120 milligrams twice daily, with the primary goal of determining the safest and most effective dose while monitoring for side effects. The drug was generally well tolerated, with the most common side effects being nausea and vomiting that were mild to moderate in severity and manageable with standard medications, and no serious life-threatening side effects occurred. While the drug did not shrink any tumors, about one-third of patients experienced stable disease meaning their cancer did not grow worse, and some patients maintained this stability for at least 23 weeks. The researchers concluded that E7386 shows promise as a treatment option with an acceptable safety profile and recommend testing the highest dose of 120 milligrams twice daily in future studies to better understand its effectiveness against cancer.

title: Migraine and Stroke Risk in Postmenopausal Women in the Women's Health Initiative.
abstract: Migraine is a known risk factor for stroke in women of reproductive age, although its relationship with stroke among postmenopausal women remains unclear. We assessed the association between migraine history and incident stroke in a sample of postmenopausal women.We included women enrolled in the Women's Health Initiative, a large US longitudinal cohort study of postmenopausal women, and excluded those with previous stroke or those with missing data on key variables. The primary exposure was self-reported, physician-diagnosed migraine at baseline, and the primary outcome was incident stroke (total, ischemic, or hemorrhagic). Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to test the cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs) between migraine history and total, ischemic (overall and by subtype), and hemorrhagic stroke, sequentially adjusted for age, traditional cardiovascular risk factors, and female-specific risk factors (age at menopause, age at menarche, menstrual irregularity, presence of vasomotor symptoms, parity, breastfeeding, and use of menopausal hormone therapy). We then quantified the association between a history of migraine and total stroke by age at baseline (in 5-year age groups) using multivariable models. Data on the presence of aura and migraine frequency were not available.Participants (N = 130,277) had a median age of 63 years (interquartile range [IQR] 57-69). A total of 5,743 incident stroke events occurred over a median follow-up period of 19.9 years (IQR 9.1-25). In multivariable models, there was no significant association between migraine history and total stroke (HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.99-1.17), but there was a significant association between migraine history and ischemic stroke (HR 1.12, 95% CI 1.02-1.23). In planned secondary analysis of ischemic subtypes, the associations were most pronounced in the cardioembolic (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.98-1.39) and undetermined (HR 1.14, 95% CI 0.98-1.33) categories. Migraine was not associated with hemorrhagic stroke (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.67-1.09). Risk did not differ significantly by age group.Over 20 years of follow-up, postmenopausal women with a history of migraine had a higher risk of ischemic stroke, but not total or hemorrhagic stroke. Along with other factors, a history of migraine should be considered a risk marker when assessing ischemic stroke risk after menopause.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether migraines increase the risk of stroke in women after menopause, since previous studies had shown this connection in younger women but the relationship was unclear for older women. The study followed over 130,000 postmenopausal women in the United States for an average of nearly 20 years, tracking which women had a history of migraines and which ones experienced strokes during that time. Women with a history of migraines had a higher risk of ischemic stroke, which is the most common type of stroke caused by blood clots, but migraine history did not increase the risk of total strokes or hemorrhagic strokes, which are caused by bleeding in the brain. These findings suggest that doctors should consider a woman's migraine history as one of several warning signs when evaluating her risk for ischemic stroke after menopause. The study was limited because researchers did not have detailed information about whether the migraines included visual disturbances called aura or how often the women experienced migraines, which could have provided a more complete picture of the relationship between migraines and stroke risk.

title: Granulomatous prostatitis as a cause of elevated PI-RADS scores on multiparametric MRI: insights from a single institution cohort.
abstract: Granulomatous prostatitis (GP) frequently mimics prostatic adenocarcinoma on multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), producing elevated PI-RADS scores and diagnostic challenges. We retrospectively analyzed 63 patients with biopsy-proven GP (without concurrent prostate cancer) and paired mpMRI (2019-2025) to correlate radiologic and histopathologic findings. Median age was 66 years (range 41-80), median PSA 6.2 ng/mL (range 0.1-26.4), and median percentage of biopsy parts involved (PPI) was 36% (range 6-100%). PI-RADS distribution: 2 (14%), 3 (22%), 4 (24%), 5 (40%). High PI-RADS scores (4-5, n = 40, 63%) correlated with higher median PPI (48% vs. 17%, p = 0.01) vs. low PI-RADS scores (2-3, n = 23, 37%), but not PSA (6.4 vs. 5.3 ng/mL, p = 0.68). Among high PI-RADS cases, 25% had prior BCG therapy. One patient with sarcoidosis presented with PI-RADS 5 and 93% PPI. GP produces a broad PI-RADS spectrum; recognizing this imaging variability is essential for accurate diagnosis and avoiding unnecessary procedures.© 2026. llm_summary: Granulomatous prostatitis, which is inflammation of the prostate gland caused by certain infections or immune conditions, can look very similar to prostate cancer when doctors examine it with special imaging scans called multiparametric MRI, creating confusion about whether a patient actually has cancer. Researchers studied 63 patients who had biopsy-proven granulomatous prostatitis (confirmed by tissue samples) and compared their MRI scan results to their actual tissue findings between 2019 and 2025 to understand how often this condition was mistaken for cancer. The study found that 63 percent of patients received high cancer-suspicion scores on their MRI scans, and these high scores were more common in patients whose prostate tissue showed more extensive inflammation, though their blood PSA levels (a protein measured to screen for prostate cancer) did not predict the scan results. Understanding that granulomatous prostatitis can produce a wide range of imaging appearances that mimic cancer is crucial for doctors to avoid recommending unnecessary biopsies or treatments for patients who do not actually have prostate cancer. Future research should help doctors develop better ways to distinguish between this inflammatory condition and actual.

title: Engagement of the TCR against an oncolytic virus generates a population of effector CAR T cells with potent antitumor activity.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy faces many challenges against solid tumors including T cell exhaustion and poor CAR durability. Here, we show that engaging the CAR T cell endogenous T cell receptor (TCR) using an oncolytic virus enhances CAR T cell functionality, durability, and therapy. Upon combination therapy of solid tumors with CAR T cells and vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV), a subpopulation of antiviral, TCR-primed CAR T cells was generated with enhanced effector functions, altered activation states, and differential gene and protein expression when compared to non-TCR-primed CAR T cells. Single-cell RNA sequencing showed clonal expansion of anti-VSV CAR T cells and enhancement of effector-associated genes with VSV-mediated CAR T cell expansion. CD4 T cells played a pivotal role in the development of these TCR-primed CAR T cells. These results provide a strong rationale both for a novel use of systemic oncolytic virotherapy and for directly exploiting the CAR T cell TCR to fine tune the CAR T cell phenotype and function.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a promising but challenging cancer treatment called CAR T cell therapy, which uses immune cells engineered to fight tumors but often loses effectiveness against solid cancers because the cells become exhausted and worn out. The team combined CAR T cells with an oncolytic virus, which is a virus that naturally attacks cancer cells, to see if this dual approach could improve the treatment's power. They discovered that when the virus activated the cancer-fighting cells' natural immune receptors alongside their engineered cancer-targeting abilities, it created a special population of stronger, more durable immune cells with enhanced ability to kill tumors. The study showed that these dual-activated cells had different gene patterns and activation states compared to cells activated only by their engineered receptors, and that helper immune cells called CD4 T cells were crucial for creating this improved cell population. These findings suggest that combining oncolytic viruses with CAR T cell therapy could be a new strategy to make cancer immunotherapy more effective and longer-lasting for patients with solid tumors.

title: Obinutuzumab or Tacrolimus in Primary Membranous Nephropathy.
abstract: Studies of obinutuzumab, a type II anti-CD20 antibody, have shown efficacy in the treatment of hematologic cancers and autoimmune diseases. An evaluation of the efficacy and safety of obinutuzumab in patients with primary membranous nephropathy is needed.In a phase 3 trial, we randomly assigned adults with primary membranous nephropathy in a 1:1 ratio to receive intravenous obinutuzumab or oral tacrolimus. The primary end point was complete remission (defined as a urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio of 0.3 or lower and a stable estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR]) at week 104. Key secondary end points were complete or partial remission at week 104, complete remission at week 76, a sustained reduction in the eGFR of at least 30%, duration of complete remission, and change in the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System Fatigue T score from baseline to week 104. Fixed-sequence hierarchical testing was performed. Safety was assessed.A total of 142 patients underwent randomization. At week 104, complete remission was observed in 26 of 71 patients in the obinutuzumab group and in 4 of 70 patients in the tacrolimus group (37% vs. 6% with multiple imputation for missing data; adjusted difference, 31 percentage points; 95% CI, 18 to 44; P<0.001). The analyses of complete or partial remission at week 104 and complete remission at week 76 also showed a significant treatment effect. The analysis of a sustained eGFR reduction did not show a significant treatment effect; thus, subsequent end points in the hierarchy were not formally tested for significance. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher were reported in 16 patients (22%) in the obinutuzumab group and in 13 patients (19%) in the tacrolimus group; serious adverse events occurred in 12 (17%) and 10 (14%), respectively. There were 61 and 57 infections per 100 patient-years in the obinutuzumab and tacrolimus groups, respectively; 3 and 4 serious infections per 100 patient-years; and 11 and 14 serious adverse events per 100 patient-years. Adverse drug reactions with obinutuzumab included infusion-related reactions, respiratory tract infections, and neutropenia. One patient in each group died during escape therapy.Obinutuzumab was superior to tacrolimus in inducing complete remission in patients with primary membranous nephropathy. (Funded by F. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new treatment called obinutuzumab, a type of antibody medication, to see if it could help patients with primary membranous nephropathy, a kidney disease where the immune system damages the filtering structures in the kidneys. In this clinical trial, 142 adult patients were randomly assigned to receive either obinutuzumab through an intravenous injection or tacrolimus through oral tablets, and researchers tracked their progress over two years to see which treatment worked better at reducing protein loss in urine and preserving kidney function. Obinutuzumab proved significantly more effective than tacrolimus, with 37 percent of patients receiving obinutuzumab achieving complete remission (meaning protein levels dropped to healthy ranges and kidney function stabilized) compared to only 6 percent in the tacrolimus group. Both treatments caused similar rates of side effects, though obinutuzumab patients experienced more infusion-related reactions and respiratory infections while tacrolimus patients had slightly higher rates of serious infections overall. These results suggest that obinutuzumab could become an important new treatment option for patients with primary membranous nephropathy, though doctors will need to continue monitoring its.

title: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia/Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma: Mayo Clinic Systematic Management and Risk-Adapted Therapy for Lymphoid Malignancies (lySMART) Consensus Guidelines 2026.
abstract: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is the most frequent leukemia in adults in the United States, with roughly 24,000 new cases expected in 2026 and more than 220,000 people currently living with the disease. During the past 2 decades, advancements in biologic insights and treatment options have significantly enhanced the outcomes for patients with CLL. Treatment paradigms have shifted decisively from chemoimmunotherapy to targeted agents. Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors, B-cell lymphoma 2 inhibitors, and anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies now form the backbone of frontline care, with therapy tailored by genetic risk, comorbidities, and patient preferences. For relapsed or refractory disease, sequencing of covalent and noncovalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors, B-cell lymphoma 2 inhibitors, and cellular therapies, including chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, has expanded options and improved outcomes in high-risk settings. Richter transformation of CLL represents an area of unmet need as most contemporary series report survival of less than 24 months. title: Secular Trends and Predictors of Frequent Cannabis Use From 2002-2019 in the United States.
abstract: To evaluate the trajectory of prevalence of frequent cannabis use from 2002 to 2019 in the United States and its predictors.We investigated individuals 12 years of age or older from the National Survey on Drug Use and Health from 2002 to 2019. Main outcomes were the changing prevalence of cannabis use, frequent cannabis use (defined as 100 to 365 days of use in the past year), and associated factors.A total of 1,005,421 participants were included. The prevalence of frequent cannabis use doubled from 4.0% in 2002 to 7.8% in 2019 (P<.001). The young adult population was the primary driver of frequent cannabis use. Males were always the majority of frequent cannabis users, but the rate of increase was higher in females. Predictors of frequent cannabis use were male sex (odds ratio [OR], 1.98; 95% CI, 1.93 to 2.03) and young adults 18 to 25 years of age (OR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.82 to 2.02). Black, Native American, and mixed-race individuals were associated with frequent cannabis use, as was not having a college degree and lower family income. Frequent smoking (OR, 3.84; 95% CI, 3.74 to 3.95) and frequent alcohol use (OR, 2.52; 95% CI, 2.41 to 2.63) were also associated with frequent cannabis use.Frequent cannabis use in young adults in the United States has increased rapidly. Male sex, race, frequent smoking or alcohol use, low family income, and education level were significant predictors, suggesting population strategies for mitigation of frequent recreational cannabis use and health consequences.Copyright © 2026 Mayo Foundation for Medical Education and Research. llm_summary: Researchers examined how often Americans use cannabis, the plant that produces marijuana, because understanding this trend helps public health officials plan prevention efforts and understand health risks. The study looked at survey data collected from over one million people aged twelve and older between 2002 and 2019 to track how frequent cannabis use changed over time and which groups of people were most likely to use it regularly. The results showed that frequent cannabis use, defined as using cannabis between one hundred and three hundred sixty-five days per year, doubled from four percent of the population in 2002 to nearly eight percent by 2019. Young adults between eighteen and twenty-five years old drove most of this increase, and the study found that men were more likely than women to use cannabis frequently, though women's use rates grew faster than men's rates. The research identified several risk factors for frequent cannabis use including being male, being a young adult, smoking cigarettes often, drinking alcohol frequently, having lower family income, and not having a college degree, suggesting that public health programs should focus on these populations to reduce cannabis use and its potential health effects.

title: The 2023 clinical laboratory genetics workforce in the United States: trends, challenges, and evolving practices.
abstract: This study analyzed data from the National Coordinating Center for the Regional Genetics Networks (NCC) 2023 electronic survey to gather insights on current workforce trends and challenges faced by clinical laboratory geneticists in the United States. The analysis included demographics, certifications, career stages, practice patterns, staffing, reimbursement practices, and burnout levels. A total of 375 clinical laboratory geneticists responded to the survey (36.9% response rate). The workforce predominantly identifies as White and female, with limited representation from African-American/Black, Latinx/Hispanic, and Native American groups. The field includes both experienced professionals and newer entrants, with up to 25% of respondents anticipating retirement within the next decade and another 27% uncertain of retirement timeline. Technician/technologist staffing shortages were reported by over half of respondents and included other key laboratory roles such as genetic counselors and variant scientists. Concerns about reimbursement practices for new technologies and increased complexity in test interpretation were expressed by nearly 33% of respondents. Inequities in reimbursement for PhD-trained clinical laboratory directors were identified, along with increased staff strain and heightened burnout, especially among mid-career professionals. Together, these findings underscore the urgent need for dedicated strategic initiatives to enhance workforce diversity, address staffing and compensation disparities, improve resource allocation, and alleviate burnout to ensure a sustainable future for clinical laboratory geneticists.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined the current state of the clinical laboratory genetics workforce in the United States because understanding staffing trends and challenges is important for maintaining quality genetic testing services that help diagnose diseases. The study collected survey responses from 375 genetic laboratory professionals out of about 1,000 invited participants, asking them about their backgrounds, job roles, work experiences, and concerns about their careers. The results showed that the workforce is mostly white and female with limited diversity, that many experienced workers plan to retire soon, and that laboratories struggle to hire enough technicians and genetic counselors to keep up with demand. Nearly one-third of respondents worried about getting paid fairly for new and complex genetic tests, and many workers reported feeling burned out and stressed, particularly those in the middle stages of their careers. These findings highlight the urgent need for the field to recruit more diverse workers, pay people fairly regardless of their education level, and create better working conditions to prevent experienced professionals from leaving the field.

title: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS®) society guidelines for gynecologic oncology: 2026 update.
abstract: This is the third updated enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS®) society guideline presenting a consensus for optimal perioperative care in gynecologic oncology surgery.A database search of publications using Embase and PubMed was performed (2018-2025). Studies for key elements within the ERAS gynecologic oncology protocol were selected with emphasis on meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, and large prospective cohort studies. These studies were then reviewed and graded according to the grading of recommendations, assessment, development and evaluation (GRADE) system.All recommendations on ERAS protocol items are based on best available evidence. The level of evidence for each item is presented accordingly.The updated evidence base and recommendation for items within the ERAS gynecologic oncology perioperative care pathway are presented by the ERAS® society in this consensus review. Gynecologic surgeons may consider incorporating these recommendations into perioperative pathway design, with efforts to achieve consensus within their practice where feasible.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: The Enhanced Recovery After Surgery society created updated guidelines to help doctors provide the best possible care for patients undergoing surgery for gynecologic cancers, which are cancers affecting the female reproductive system. Researchers searched medical databases from 2018 to 2025 and reviewed high-quality studies including randomized controlled trials, which are experiments where patients are randomly assigned to different treatment groups to test which works best. They evaluated all the evidence using a standardized system called GRADE that rates how reliable and trustworthy each piece of research is. The updated guidelines present recommendations for every step of a patient's surgical journey, from before the operation through recovery, based on the strongest available scientific evidence. Gynecologic surgeons can now use these evidence-based recommendations to design their own surgical care pathways that work best for their patients and hospital settings.

title: Beyond diameter: emerging imaging biomarkers for risk stratification in thoracic aortic aneurysms.
abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is a relatively common, under-recognised and lethal condition. Yet, current management remains anchored on absolute diameter for prophylactic repair, despite many dissections occurring below surgical thresholds-particularly in women. This review synthesises evidence showing that while rigorous standardisation of imaging is foundational, diameter alone is insufficient for accurate risk prediction. We appraise clinically available biomarkers beyond size: indexed metrics (Aortic Size Index, Aortic Height Index, Indexed Aortic Area) that adjust for body habitus-especially relevant in women; morphological descriptors (ascending length, arch tortuosity, aortic volume) that capture geometry; dynamic and biomechanical measures (growth rate, regional deformation, distensibility/stiffness) that reflect disease activity and advanced modalities (four-dimensional flow MRI, vascular deformation mapping) that quantify haemodynamics such as flow displacement and wall shear stress. Functional aortic markers-including central blood pressure, aortic stiffness, pulsatile arterial load and arterial age-independently predict expansion and improve risk stratification when combined with diameter. Furthermore, recognition of sex differences in TAA growth and outcomes supports sex-informed, precision aortic imaging and functional approaches to risk assessment. Future priorities include prospective multicentre validation, actionable sex-specific thresholds and multidisciplinary collaboration to translate these tools into personalised surveillance and timely intervention.© Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2026. llm_summary: Thoracic aortic aneurysms, which are dangerous bulges in the main blood vessel leaving the heart, are a serious but often overlooked health problem that doctors currently assess mainly by measuring the width of the aorta to decide when surgery is needed. This review examined evidence showing that relying only on diameter measurements is not enough to predict which patients are at highest risk, especially women, since many dangerous tears happen in people below the size threshold that typically triggers surgery. Researchers found that additional measurements beyond simple width—such as adjusted size metrics that account for body size, descriptions of the aorta's shape and geometry, measurements of how fast the aorta is growing, and advanced imaging that shows blood flow patterns and wall stress—can better identify at-risk patients. These additional tools, combined with measurements of how stiff the aorta is and how hard the heart has to work to pump blood, can improve doctors' ability to predict which patients need closer monitoring or earlier surgery and show that men and women may need different assessment approaches. Future work should test these new measurement methods in large studies across multiple hospitals and develop specific guidelines for men and women separately so doctors can personalize care and intervene at.

title: Chronic kidney disease in cirrhosis: a study of inpatients from a global perspective.
abstract: The prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD), defined as a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 for >3 months, is rising in the global population.To assess the global prevalence of CKD in cirrhosis and how it impacts the prognosis of these patients.The Chronic Liver Disease Evolution and Registry for Events and Decompensation consortium prospectively enrolled non-electively admitted cirrhosis patients from 127 sites globally, each with up to 100 patients. Data collected were demographics, comorbid conditions, cirrhosis history, hospital course and patient outcomes. Patients were divided into those with (CKD+) and without CKD (CKD-) and compared. We also compared patients from different World Bank income strata.Of 7040 inpatients enrolled, the global prevalence of CKD was 18.17%, with the highest prevalence observed in high-income countries (HICs), which paralleled their higher prevalence of metabolic syndrome. CKD+ patients had lower median enrolment GFR (32 (21, 44) mL/min/1.73 m2) when compared with CKD- patients (88 (63, 117) mL/min/1.73 m2, p<0.0001), associated with a more complex history of cirrhosis complications, with ascites occurring in 76.5% of CKD+ versus 61.1% of patients with CKD- (p<0.0001). The most common in-hospital complication was the development of AKI (59.4%) in CKD+ versus 27% in CKD- patients (p<0.0001). CKD was associated with higher in-hospital and 30-day postdischarge mortality (both p<0.0001).The presence of CKD negatively impacts the prognosis of admitted patients with cirrhosis in a global cohort. Meticulous management of ascites and lifestyle changes, especially in HICs, may improve the outcome of these patients.© Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2026. No commercial re-use. llm_summary: Chronic kidney disease, which means the kidneys are not filtering waste from the blood as well as they should over a long period of time, is becoming more common around the world and can make liver disease more serious. Researchers studied over seven thousand patients admitted to hospitals with cirrhosis, which is severe liver damage, across 127 medical centers in different countries to understand how often kidney disease occurs alongside liver disease and how it affects patient outcomes. They found that about eighteen percent of patients with cirrhosis also had chronic kidney disease, with higher rates in wealthy countries, and these patients had much worse kidney function and more complications like fluid buildup in the belly compared to those without kidney disease. Patients with both cirrhosis and chronic kidney disease were much more likely to develop acute kidney injury during their hospital stay and had higher death rates both during hospitalization and within thirty days after leaving the hospital. The researchers suggest that doctors should focus on carefully managing fluid buildup and encouraging healthy lifestyle changes, especially in wealthy countries, to help improve survival rates for patients who have both liver cirrhosis and chronic kidney disease.

title: Deep learning for H&E-based meningioma molecular classification and outcome prediction: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: The introduction of genomic profiling as a tool for molecular classification and clinical outcome prediction has revolutionised the care of patients with brain tumours. Artificial intelligence (AI) provides advanced avenues to convert complex genomic information into routinely available patient-level information. In this study, we aimed to evaluate whether deep learning could robustly characterise molecular subtypes, predict risk of recurrence, and identify salient chromosome copy number alterations in haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue samples of the most common brain tumour, meningioma.For this retrospective, multicentre, model development and validation study, we created a cohort of meningioma cases with paired DNA methylation and matched digitised H&E images. The cohort included a training dataset consisting of a cross-section of real-world clinical cases from the National Cancer Institute (USA; n=439) and a dataset comprising real-world clinical cases from the University Health Network (Canada; n=166). A second test dataset consisting of WHO grade 2 meningiomas after gross total resection (from the Mayo Clinic, USA; n=67) was used for additional clinical validation. We trained and validated five dedicated deep learning models to use H&E staining alone to predict the following: molecular classification of meningiomas (ie, molecular groups 1-4 [MG1-4], which are associated with homogeneous biology and clinical outcomes); three relevant chromosome arm aneuploidies (1p loss, 1q gain, and 22q loss); and DNA methylation-based 5-year progression-free survival risk group (high vs low). Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and balanced accuracy were used to assess classifier performance, and differences in progression-free survival between groups predicted to be at high or low risk of recurrence were compared using the log-rank test.Our deep learning classifier achieved balanced accuracies of 87-97% for predicting meningioma molecular group from H&E staining when an output probability threshold of 0·4 was used. AUCs were 0·98 (95% CI 0·97-1·00) for MG1 versus other molecular groups, 0·96 (0·94-0·99) for MG2 versus other molecular groups, 0·81 (0·74-0·88) for MG3 versus other molecular groups, and 0·88 (0·83-0·94) for MG4 versus other molecular groups. AUCs for chromosome-level alterations were 0·86 (0·80-0·92) for chromosome 1p loss, 0·86 (0·79-0·93) for chromosome 22q loss, and 0·79 (0·65-0·91) for chromosome 1q gain. The dedicated outcome prediction model was prognostic for progression-free survival after adjusting for WHO grade, extent of resection, and patient age (hazard ratio 3·49, 95% CI 1·54-7·91; p=0·0028).To our knowledge, this study is the first to apply deep learning models that can, beyond diagnosis, identify molecular subtypes and predict outcomes in a single brain tumour entity (meningioma) using H&E staining alone. To date, treatment tailoring and individualised risk prediction for meningioma have only been possible using resource-intensive genomic profiling. The study shows the broad clinical utility of applying AI modelling to readily available H&E-stained samples to democratise access to genomic information globally.Canadian Institutes of Health Research and Brain Tumour Charity.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined whether artificial intelligence could analyze routine tissue stains to predict which meningiomas, the most common brain tumors, would come back after treatment and what type of tumor a patient had based on genetic information. The team trained computer programs using tissue samples and genetic data from nearly 700 patients across three medical centers, teaching the artificial intelligence to recognize patterns in standard microscope slides that matched specific tumor types and genetic changes. The deep learning models successfully identified tumor subtypes with very high accuracy between 87 and 97 percent and could predict which patients faced a higher risk of tumor recurrence, even when accounting for other factors like how much of the tumor was removed. This breakthrough is important because it means doctors could potentially use inexpensive, routine tissue stains instead of expensive genetic testing to guide treatment decisions and predict outcomes for meningioma patients worldwide. The study represents a major step toward making personalized cancer care more accessible globally by using artificial intelligence to unlock genetic information hidden within standard medical images that hospitals already have.

title: Oral small molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist aleniglipron in people with overweight or obesity: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2b trial.
abstract: Aleniglipron is an oral, small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP1-RA) in development for obesity treatment. The ACCESS phase 2b placebo-controlled, double-blind study randomized 230 adults (mean BMI 39.5 kg m-2, 54% female) with obesity or overweight to examine the effects of once-daily aleniglipron escalated every 4 weeks to 45, 90 or 120 mg. At week 36, the trial met its primary endpoint with a placebo-adjusted LS mean (95% confidence interval) body-weight change from baseline of -8.2% (-11.1 to -5.3%), -9.8% (-12.5 to -7.2%) and -11.3% (-13.9 to -8.6%) for the aleniglipron 45-, 90- and 120-mg arms, respectively (P < 0.0001, all doses versus placebo), with no apparent weight-loss plateau at the end of the double-blind period. Continued weight loss was observed at the interim analysis (median treatment duration of 20 weeks) of the ongoing open-label extension. Gastrointestinal events were generally mild to moderate and decreased in frequency over time, with little to no recurrence of vomiting after reintroduction following permitted dose interruptions. Treatment-related discontinuations were 10.4% across aleniglipron arms, with no events of drug-induced liver injury. Clinically relevant weight reductions of up to 11.3% with a tolerability profile consistent with the GLP-1RA class support further development of aleniglipron for obesity treatment. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new oral medication called aleniglipron, which is a small molecule that activates GLP-1 receptors (proteins in the body that help control appetite and blood sugar), to see if it could help people with obesity or excess weight lose weight. The study involved 230 adults with an average body mass index of 39. 5 who took either aleniglipron at three different doses (45, 90, or 120 milligrams once daily) or a placebo (inactive pill) for 36 weeks in a double-blind trial where neither the patients nor researchers knew who received the real drug. By week 36, all three doses of aleniglipron produced significant weight loss compared to placebo, with the highest dose resulting in an 11. 3 percent reduction in body weight, and participants continued losing weight even at the end of the study period.

title: Brief Review: Rethinking Colonic Redundancy in Gastroenterology.
abstract: Dolichocolon (DC), or colonic redundancy, is an elongated and tortuous colon described as early as 1820, yet it remains underrecognized in clinical gastroenterology. Advances in imaging and motility assessment offer new insights into its prevalence, mechanisms, and clinical implications.To summarize current evidence on the anatomy, epidemiology, and potential clinical significance of DC and to explore possible pathophysiological mechanisms linking this variant to gastrointestinal disorders.A targeted literature review of studies published between 1900 and 2024 was conducted using PubMed and Scopus with search terms including dolichocolon, colonic redundancy, and redundant colon. Publications addressing anatomy, motility, symptom associations, and disease relevance were included.Though epidemiological data are limited, it has been estimated that DC affects 10-20% of the population and is associated with constipation, volvulus, and, possibly, inflammatory bowel disease. Proposed mechanisms include segmental stasis and ischemia in redundant loops, altered neuromuscular signaling, and increased mucosal surface area promoting immune-microbiota interactions. Despite its potential importance, DC is rarely noted in modern radiology reports, contributing to under-recognition in clinical practice.Colonic redundancy represents a common anatomic variant with potentially overlooked clinical implications. Standardized radiologic characterization and prospective studies are needed to clarify its role in gastrointestinal disorders and to guide future diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.© 2026. llm_summary: Dolichocolon, which is an abnormally long and twisted colon, has been known to doctors since 1820 but remains largely overlooked in modern medical practice despite affecting an estimated 10 to 20 percent of people. Researchers reviewed scientific studies published between 1900 and 2024 to understand what we know about this colon condition, including how common it is, what causes it, and how it might relate to digestive problems. The review found that dolichocolon is connected to constipation, a dangerous twisting of the colon called volvulus, and possibly inflammatory bowel disease, with potential causes including poor movement of stool through redundant loops, changes in nerve and muscle signaling, and increased surface area that may affect immune system interactions with gut bacteria. The main problem is that radiologists rarely mention dolichocolon in their imaging reports, which means doctors and patients often do not realize this anatomical variation exists or understand its importance. Future research using standardized methods to identify and study dolichocolon is needed to clarify its true role in causing digestive disorders and to develop better ways to diagnose and treat patients who have this condition.

title: Use of corticosteroids for adult chronic pain interventions: sympathetic and peripheral nerve blocks, trigger point injections - guidelines from the American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine, the American Academy of Pain Medicine, the American Society of Interventional Pain Physicians, and the International Pain and Spine Intervention Society.
abstract: There is potential for adverse events from corticosteroid injections, including increase in blood glucose, decrease in bone mineral density and suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis. Published studies note that doses lower than those commonly injected provide similar benefit.Development of the practice guideline was approved by the Board of Directors of American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine with several other societies agreeing to participate. The scope of guidelines was agreed on to include safety of the injection technique (landmark-guided, ultrasound or radiology-aided injections); effect of the addition of the corticosteroid on the efficacy of the injectate (local anesthetic or saline); and adverse events related to the injection. Based on preliminary discussions, it was decided to structure the topics into three separate guidelines as follows: (1) sympathetic, peripheral nerve blocks and trigger point injections; (2) joints; and (3) neuraxial, facet, sacroiliac joints and related topics (vaccine and anticoagulants). Experts were assigned topics to perform a comprehensive review of the literature and to draft statements and recommendations, which were refined and voted for consensus (≥75% agreement) using a modified Delphi process. The United States Preventive Services Task Force grading of evidence and strength of recommendation was followed.This guideline deals with the use and safety of corticosteroid injections for sympathetic, peripheral nerve blocks and trigger point injections for adult chronic pain conditions. All the statements and recommendations were approved by all participants after four rounds of discussion. The Practice Guidelines Committees and Board of Directors of the participating societies also approved all the statements and recommendations. The safety of some procedures, including stellate blocks, lower extremity peripheral nerve blocks and some sites of trigger point injections, is improved by imaging guidance. The addition of non-particulate corticosteroid to the local anesthetic is beneficial in cluster headaches but not in other types of headaches. Corticosteroid may provide additional benefit in transverse abdominal plane blocks and ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric nerve blocks in postherniorrhaphy pain but there is no evidence for pudendal nerve blocks. There is minimal benefit for the use of corticosteroids in trigger point injections.In this practice guideline, we provided recommendations on the use of corticosteroids in sympathetic blocks, peripheral nerve blocks, and trigger point injections to assist clinicians in making informed decisions.© American Society of Regional Anesthesia & Pain Medicine 2026. llm_summary: Corticosteroid injections are commonly used to reduce pain in conditions affecting nerves and muscles, but doctors have worried about potential side effects like increased blood sugar levels and weakened bones. Major medical organizations came together to review all available scientific evidence and create clear guidelines about when and how to safely use these steroid injections for adults with chronic pain. The experts found that imaging guidance like ultrasound improves safety for certain procedures such as nerve blocks in the lower body, and that steroids added to numbing medication help with cluster headaches but provide minimal benefit for trigger point injections into muscle knots. The guidelines recommend that doctors use lower doses of steroids than are commonly given, since research shows that smaller amounts work just as well while reducing the risk of harmful side effects. These recommendations will help doctors make better decisions about whether to use corticosteroid injections and how to use them safely for their patients with ongoing pain.

title: Characterizing SMN1 hybrid and deletion alleles using large-scale SNP array-based SMA carrier screening.
abstract: Most spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) carrier screening assays quantify SMN1 exon 7 copy number, providing limited information about the prevalence or structure of SMN1-SMN2 hybrid alleles generated through gene conversion. As long-read sequencing (LRS) studies begin to resolve these alleles at high resolution, typically in modest cohorts, large population-scale data remain essential for defining the broader allele-frequency context in which such structural signatures occur.We evaluated SMN1 exon 7 and exon 8 copy number in 18,015 individuals undergoing expanded carrier screening using a SNP-based array. Carriers were classified by deletion pattern, and representative cases underwent droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) to distinguish contiguous deletions from gene-conversion-derived hybrid alleles based on coordinated SMN1/SMN2 exon and intron copy number profiles.Among 457 carriers (2.5%), exon 7-only deletions accounted for ~ 53%, while exon 7 + 8 deletions comprised ~ 47%. ddPCR showed that exon 7-only deletions predominantly represented SMN1-SMN2 hybrid alleles, whereas exon 7 + 8 deletions reflected contiguous loss of both exons. Isolated exon 8 deletions were rare (~ 0.05%) and likewise exhibited hybrid architecture. This distribution contrasts with earlier population studies reporting a predominance of exon 7 + 8 deletions and indicates that hybrid alleles constitute a substantial proportion of SMN1 deletion alleles in the general population.While hybrid resolution is not required for routine SMA carrier detection, the unexpectedly high prevalence of hybrid alleles highlights an important category of SMN1 structural variation that merits deeper investigation. These population-scale data provide a framework to guide and contextualize future LRS-based analyses aimed at resolving SMN1 gene-conversion tracts, allele structures, and potential modifier variants relevant to SMA pathogenesis and therapeutic response. Together, these findings support a more comprehensive understanding of SMN1 allele diversity as genomic technologies advance toward high-resolution characterization of the SMN locus.Clinical trial number: not applicable.© 2026. llm_summary: Spinal muscular atrophy is a serious genetic disease caused by problems with a gene called SMN1, and doctors screen people to see if they carry a copy of this faulty gene, but current tests only count how many copies exist without showing the exact structure of the genetic changes. Researchers tested blood samples from over 18,000 people using a special DNA chip technology to look at two different parts of the SMN1 gene and then confirmed their findings with a more detailed test called droplet digital PCR, which can distinguish between different types of genetic deletions. The study found that about 2. 5 percent of people were carriers, and surprisingly, more than half of the carriers had a type of genetic change called hybrid alleles, which are created when parts of two similar genes swap places, rather than simple deletions where chunks of DNA are completely missing. These findings show that hybrid alleles are much more common in the general population than scientists previously thought, which is important because understanding all the different types of genetic changes helps doctors better predict how the disease might develop and how patients might respond to new treatments.

title: Reducing Inequalities in Stroke Events-Hemorrhagic Disparities (RISE-HD): a 10-Year Longitudinal Study in Florida.
abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) are less common than ischemic strokes but carry higher mortality and disability. Despite declining mortality, disparities across racial, socioeconomic, and geographic groups persist.We analyzed inpatient data from the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (2013 - 2024). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Associations with mortality were assessed for race/ethnicity, sex, insurance type, geographic region, and rural residence using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for the Elixhauser Comorbidity Index. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate time to in-hospital mortality.Among 120,529 patients (mean [SD] age 67.9 [15.5] years; 48.4% female), 5,232 (4.5%) lived in rural areas, but only 426 (0.4%) received care at rural hospitals. Most patients were White non-Hispanic (57.7%) or Black non-Hispanic (17.5%). The largest shares came from Central (23,792 [20.6%]), Southeast (20,641 [17.9%]), and Southwest (18,823 [16.3%]) Florida. Annual admissions increased from 6,690 (5.6%) in 2013 to 14,407 (12.0%) in 2023, the last complete year of data, while 2024 data represent a partial reporting period. In-hospital mortality declined significantly (P < .001). Higher mortality was associated with Black race (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.07-1.20); Medicaid (OR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.71-1.97) and other insurance (OR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.75-1.97); Northwest (OR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.03-1.21) and South regions (OR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.13-1.30), and rural residence (OR, 1.3; 95% CI, 1.19-1.41; all P < .01).In-hospital mortality from hemorrhagic stroke mortality has declined, yet significant racial, geographic, and socioeconomic disparities persist. Black patients, those with Medicaid or other non-Medicare insurance, rural residents, and those in Northwest and South Florida face higher mortality. Targeted system-level strategies are needed to address these inequities.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined a decade of hospital records from Florida to understand why some patients suffer worse outcomes from hemorrhagic strokes, which are bleeding strokes in the brain that are less common than other types but more deadly and disabling. The study looked at over 120,000 patients admitted to hospitals between 2013 and 2024, tracking their survival rates and comparing outcomes across different racial groups, insurance types, and geographic regions. While overall survival rates improved significantly over the ten-year period, major disparities remained, with Black patients, those on Medicaid insurance, rural residents, and people living in Northwest and South Florida experiencing higher death rates from these strokes. These findings suggest that access to quality care and healthcare resources are not equally distributed across different communities in Florida, putting certain groups at greater risk. The researchers conclude that hospitals and health systems need to develop targeted strategies to reduce these inequalities and ensure all stroke patients receive equally effective treatment regardless of their race, income level, or where they live.

title: Glymphatic system dysfunction in epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: The glymphatic system mediates clearance of metabolic waste via astrocytic aquaporin-4-mediated cerebrospinal fluid-interstitial fluid exchange. Structural prerequisites for glymphatic dysfunction are established in epilepsy, yet no quantitative neuroimaging synthesis exists. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify DTI-ALPS-derived proxy marker of glymphatic impairment in epilepsy and assess its clinical correlates.Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD420251275885), PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through December 2025 for human observational studies reporting DTI-ALPS indices in epilepsy with healthy controls. Pooled mean differences and correlation coefficients were estimated under random-effects models with REML. Newcastle-Ottawa Scale tools were used for quality assessment. Publication bias was assessed via Egger's test and trim-and-fill analysis.Seventeen studies were included; fifteen (n = 1,255; 675 patients with epilepsy, 580 controls) contributed to the primary meta-analysis. DTI-ALPS values were significantly reduced in epilepsy versus controls (MD -0.157, 95% CI -0.197 to -0.116; p < 0.0001, I2 = 73%). Reductions were consistent across epilepsy subtypes, but subgroup analyses were underpowered and should be interpreted cautiously (Q = 3.43, p = 0.18). Disease duration showed the strongest inverse correlation (r = - 0.392; p = 0.0014), while age at epilepsy onset showed a modest association (r = - 0.148; p = 0.020). Trim-and-fill-adjusted estimates remained significant (MD -0.107, 95% CI -0.156 to -0.059).DTI-ALPS, as an indirect proxy marker of glymphatic function, is consistently reduced in epilepsy syndromes and correlates with disease chronicity. These findings support DTI-ALPS as a candidate neuroimaging biomarker of cumulative glymphatic burden; however, its current biomarker potential is limited by substantial heterogeneity, possible medication confounding, and the exclusive East Asian representation of available evidence. Longitudinal, multicenter studies with standardized protocols across diverse populations are needed to determine its reproducibility.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether the brain's waste-clearing system, called the glymphatic system, stops working properly in people with epilepsy by reviewing and combining data from seventeen studies that measured brain imaging markers in patients and healthy volunteers. They found that people with epilepsy had significantly lower scores on a brain imaging test that measures how well the glymphatic system is functioning compared to people without epilepsy, and this reduction was consistent across different types of epilepsy. The longer someone had epilepsy, the more their glymphatic system appeared to be damaged, suggesting that the disease's cumulative effects over time harm the brain's ability to clear away harmful waste products. These findings suggest that brain imaging markers could potentially become a useful tool for doctors to track epilepsy progression and understand how the disease damages the brain, though more research is needed to confirm this. The researchers noted that their conclusions are limited because most studies came from East Asia, the results showed significant variation between studies, and future research in different populations with standardized methods is necessary before this imaging marker can be reliably used in clinical practice.

title: Combined fat and sugar intake reshapes the tumor microenvironment through hypoxia and lipogenic pathways in breast cancer.
abstract: Breast cancer is the most prevalent malignancy worldwide. Beyond genetic factors, dietary components like palmitic acid (PA) and sucrose modulate tumor progression and microenvironment dynamics. However, their combined mechanistic impacts on tumor-stroma crosstalk remain undefined. We investigated how dietary PA and sucrose affect breast cancer growth and the tumor microenvironment using a murine model.Mice received Control, high-PA (HPOD), high-sucrose (HCD), or combined (HPCD) diets. We assessed tumor growth, metabolic parameters, membrane fatty acids, histopathology, proliferative indices, and microenvironment markers (CD8, F4/80, α-SMA, HIF-1α, FASN). In vitro assays evaluated PA and fructose effects on LM3 cells and fibroblasts.HCD and HPCD markedly promoted tumor growth versus Control and HPOD. HPOD increased membrane saturated fatty acids, whereas HCD elevated ω-6 PUFAs. Both HCD and HPCD increased macrophage infiltration (F4/80 +), while HPCD specifically activated cancer-associated fibroblasts (α-SMA). HIF-1α protein increased across all experimental diets without mRNA alterations, suggesting post-transcriptional stabilization. FASN protein upregulation occurred in HCD and HPCD, while Fasn mRNA increased specifically in HCD. In vitro, combining PA and fructose enhanced LM3 cell proliferation and viability while reducing apoptosis. Additionally, this co-treatment specifically increased fibroblast viability.Diets rich in PA and sucrose drive breast cancer progression through distinct mechanisms. Carbohydrates transcriptionally activate FASN-mediated lipogenesis, whereas their combination with PA remodels the tumor microenvironment via CAF activation and HIF-1α post-transcriptional stabilization. These findings highlight specific dietary components as critical variables in cancer progression, offering potential implications for nutritional interventions and targeted therapies.© 2026. llm_summary: Breast cancer is the most common cancer in women worldwide, and while genetics play a role, what people eat can also influence how the disease develops and spreads. Researchers studied how two common dietary components—palmitic acid found in fatty foods and sucrose found in sugary foods—affect breast cancer growth in mice, either eaten separately or together. They discovered that diets high in sugar alone or combined with high fat significantly increased tumor growth, and the combination specifically activated cancer-supporting cells called fibroblasts while increasing immune cells called macrophages that can promote tumor progression. The findings suggest that carbohydrates activate a protein called FASN that helps cancer cells make more fat, while the combination of fat and sugar together changes the environment around tumors in ways that help cancer spread. These results point to the importance of dietary choices in cancer development and could lead to new nutritional recommendations and treatments that target how diet influences cancer growth.

title: Benign metastasizing leiomyoma: a rare case of osseous involvement.
abstract: Benign metastasizing leiomyoma is a rare entity characterized by the metastasis of histologically benign smooth muscle tumors that originate from uterine leiomyomas. Patients are typically women with a history of uterine leiomyomas for which they have undergone operative treatment. Benign metastasizing leiomyoma most frequently involves the lungs but has been described in other locations. Osseous involvement is rare, with less than 20 cases reported in literature, the majority occurring in the spine. The current case is that of a 67-year-old female with a history of breast carcinoma with multiple lytic osseous lesions involving the pelvis and scapula, initially suspected to represent metastatic disease. Following multi-modality imaging workup including radiographs, CT, MRI, and PET/CT, biopsy revealed benign metastasizing leiomyoma. This case illustrates the multimodality imaging appearance of this rare entity. Radiographs and CT typically show well-defined lytic lesion(s) without aggressive periosteal reaction. On MRI, lesions are often T1 and T2 hypointense, with diffuse enhancement following the administration of contrast. Lesions typically display no or mild FDG uptake on PET/CT, however, varying levels of FDG uptake have been reported in literature. Benign metastasizing leiomyoma with osseous involvement is a rare but clinically significant entity that requires a high index of suspicion in women with a history of uterine leiomyomas and new bone lesions. Radiologists should be aware of this entity so that they may include benign metastasizing leiomyoma in the differential diagnosis when appropriate.© 2026. llm_summary: Benign metastasizing leiomyoma is a rare condition where smooth muscle tumors that start in the uterus spread to other parts of the body, even though the tumors themselves are not cancerous. This condition most commonly spreads to the lungs, but bone involvement is extremely uncommon, with fewer than twenty cases reported in medical literature. Researchers described a case of a sixty-seven-year-old woman with a history of uterine tumors who developed multiple bone lesions in her pelvis and shoulder blade that initially appeared to be cancer spread from her breast. Using multiple imaging techniques including X-rays, CT scans, MRI scans, and PET scans along with a tissue sample, doctors confirmed the lesions were actually benign metastasizing leiomyoma rather than cancer. Doctors and radiologists should consider this rare condition when evaluating women with a history of uterine tumors who develop new bone lesions, as recognizing this disease is important for avoiding unnecessary cancer treatments.

title: Hypercontractile Phenotype at Rest in Chronic Coronary Syndromes Predicts Impaired Functional Reserve and Increased Mortality.
abstract: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) identifies a hypercontractile phenotype (HP) in chronic coronary syndromes (CCS), characterized by elevated resting left ventricular (LV) elastance (Force = systolic blood pressure/end-systolic volume).To evaluate the prognostic significance and functional correlates of HP.In a prospective multicenter study, 10,677 CCS patients underwent resting TTE to assess LV ejection fraction (EF), stroke volume (SV), and force by quantitative volumetric echocardiography. All patients were followed for the endpoint of all-cause mortality. In a subset of 5,834 patients, stress echocardiography (exercise or dobutamine) was performed for LV contractile reserve (LVCR) and heart rate reserve (HRR).Patients were stratified into Force quintiles (Q1-Q5). HP patients exhibited lower SV at rest (Q5=34.8±12.3 vs. Q1-Q4=57.4 ± 19.1 mL; p<0.01) and higher EF at rest (Q5=64.8±6.9% vs. Q1-Q4= 58.1±8.7%, p<0.01). During a median follow-up of 24 months (interquartile range=12- 40 months), 509 deaths occurred. The exposure-adjusted death rate was lowest in Q3 (3.53-4.51 mmHg/mL; 1.03 per 100 person/years) and higher in Q1 (≤2.62 mmHg/mL, 2.88), Q2 (2.63-3.52 mmHg/mL, 1.86), Q4 (4.52-6.11 mmHg/mL,1.56), and Q5 (HP, >6.11 mmHg/mL; 1.88; p<0.0001 vs. Q1 and Q3). Multivariable analysis identified HP (Q5; HR 1.531 vs Q3, 95% CI 1.116-2.099; p=0.006) and EF (HR 0.963, 95% CI 0.953-0.972; p<0.0001) as independent predictors of death. During exercise or dobutamine stress, HP showed reduced LVCR (ΔEF: Q5 = 4.3± 9.4% vs. Q1-Q4 = 7.0±9.3%; p<0.001) and blunted HRR (Q5 = 1.77± 0.33 vs. Q1-Q4 = 1.85±0.39; p<0.01). All patients with force-based LV contractile reserve >4.1 (present in 185, 3.2% of the population) survived.CCS patients with HP assessed by resting TTE demonstrate higher mortality and multilayered functional impairment, including reduced LV contractile and chronotropic reserves. HP improved the prediction of mortality by EF. A "stronger" heart is, in fact, functionally and prognostically weaker.© The Author(s) 2026.
