llm_summary: Salvage prostatectomy, which is surgery to remove the prostate gland after cancer returns following radiation treatment, has historically been avoided because doctors worried about serious complications and poor results for patients. Researchers reviewed medical literature from multiple databases to examine how this surgery is currently being used, what outcomes patients experience, and what new surgical techniques are improving the procedure. The review found that modern imaging technology helps doctors better identify which patients will benefit most from surgery, and that ten-year survival rates without cancer recurrence range from twenty-eight to fifty-three percent, with cancer-specific survival between sixty-five and eighty-three percent. While salvage prostatectomy still carries higher complication rates than initial prostate removal surgery, serious problems like rectal injury have decreased significantly, and robotic surgery approaches show promise for improving patient continence, or the ability to control urination. This research suggests that salvage prostatectomy remains a valuable treatment option for patients with prostate cancer that returns after radiation, especially when performed by experienced surgeons using modern techniques and careful patient selection.

title: Comparative Analysis of Leaflet Materials, Stent Materials, and Stent Cell Density for Bileaflet Transcatheter Mitral Valve Design.
abstract: The biomechanical performance of bileaflet transcatheter mitral valves (TMVs) depends on complex interactions between leaflet material behavior and stent design. However, the contributions of leaflet materials and constitutive models, stent materials, and stent geometry to valve function and durability remain poorly understood.A parametric finite element study was conducted using a CAD model of a bileaflet TMV subjected to physiological pressure loading. Five leaflet material models were evaluated: 3 glutaraldehyde-fixed tissues-bovine pericardium (BP; FBP1, FBP2) and porcine pericardium (PP; FPP)-and 2 unfixed tissues-bovine (UBP) and porcine pericardium (UPP). BP was modeled as a linear elastic (FBP1) and Ogden (FBP2). Each was paired with 2 stent materials, cobalt chromium (CoCr) and nitinol, and 3 stent cell densities (low, medium, high), yielding 30 configurations. Von Mises stresses and relative leaflet opening were quantified.UPP achieved the largest opening (30-32%) with the lowest leaflet 99th percentile stresses (0.048-0.050 MPa), while FBP1 produced the smallest opening (8-9%) and highest leaflet stresses (0.077-0.078 MPa). Leaflet 99th percentile stress was strongly inversely correlated with valve opening (Spearman r=-0.9, p<0.01). Stent material had a negligible effect on valve opening but affected stent stress notably, with nitinol exhibiting about 2-3 orders of magnitude lower stresses compared to CoCr. Increasing stent cell density improved stress distribution with only a modest reduction in opening.Leaflet material model was the primary determinant of bileaflet TMV biomechanical performance, whereas stent material and cell density exerted secondary but meaningful effects. These findings offer insights that may guide the design of more optimized TMV replacement devices.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined how different materials and designs affect the performance of artificial mitral valves, which are devices placed inside the heart to replace damaged valves that control blood flow. The team used computer simulations to test thirty different combinations of valve designs, comparing five types of leaflet materials (the flapping parts of the valve) paired with two types of stent materials (the supporting framework) and three different stent densities. The results showed that unfixed porcine pericardium, which is tissue from a pig's heart lining that has not been chemically treated, opened the widest and experienced the lowest stress levels, while fixed bovine pericardium from a cow's heart lining opened the least and experienced the highest stress. The choice of leaflet material was far more important than the stent material or density in determining how well the valve worked, though nitinol, a special metal alloy, performed much better than cobalt chromium in reducing stress on the supporting framework. These findings could help doctors and engineers design better artificial heart valves that last longer and function more effectively in patients who need valve replacement surgery.

title: Portal Vein Thrombosis in Pediatric Liver Transplantation With Technical Variant Grafts: An International Multicenter Analysis of Risk and Prognostic Factors.
abstract: The adoption of technical variant grafts has expanded the donor pool for pediatric liver transplantation, but it also poses a risk of portal vein thrombosis (PVT). This study evaluated risk and prognostic factors of PVT in children undergoing liver transplantation with technical variant grafts.A total of 3137 pediatric patients from 19 centers were included: 470 received split/reduced deceased donor grafts and 2667 received living donor grafts. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify risk factors, whereas time-dependent Cox models were used to assess the impact on survival.PVT occurred in 102 patients (3.3%) and was associated with increased mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-7.25; P = 0.027) and graft loss (adjusted hazard ratio, 9.97; 95% CI, 4.90-20.3; P < 0.001). Risk factors included younger age, lower weight, higher Pediatric End-Stage Liver Disease score, longer cold ischemia and operation times, higher graft-to-recipient weight ratio, increased red blood cell transfusions, and biliary atresia. After adjusting for center, lower weight (odds ratio, 0.84 per kg; 95% CI, 0.71-1.00; P = 0.047) and biliary atresia (odds ratio, 2.34; 95% CI, 1.10-5.00; P = 0.027) remained predictors. Five-year patient (88.4% versus 93.1%) and graft survival (82.7% versus 96.3%) were significantly inferior in patients with PVT.Low-weight children with biliary atresia constituted a high-risk group, highlighting the necessity for early detection and management.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined a serious complication called portal vein thrombosis, which is a blood clot in a major vein leading to the liver, in children who received liver transplants using grafts that were either split from deceased donors or came from living donors. The study included 3,137 children from 19 medical centers around the world and used statistical analysis to identify which factors increased the risk of developing blood clots and how this complication affected survival rates. Portal vein thrombosis occurred in 102 children, or about 3 percent of the group, and these children had much worse outcomes including higher rates of death and loss of their transplanted liver. The researchers found that children who weighed less, had a condition called biliary atresia (a disease affecting bile ducts), had longer surgery times, and received more blood transfusions were at higher risk for developing blood clots. Children with low body weight and biliary atresia represented the highest-risk group, suggesting that doctors should watch these patients especially carefully after transplant and act quickly if problems develop.

title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging Parameters Predict New-Onset Symptoms of Heart Failure in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a heritable cardiac disorder characterized by increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness, often leading to heart failure (HF). HF represents a significant burden and is a challenging condition to diagnose in individuals with HCM. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging provides detailed insights into cardiac assessment, but its role in predicting new onset of HF symptoms in patients with HCM remains unknown. This study aimed to identify CMR predictors associated with the development of HF symptoms in individuals with HCM.This study was a single center retrospective cohort study that included HCM patients treated at a tertiary referral center in the United States who underwent at least 1 CMR exam, had no HF symptoms at baseline CMR and had a minimum follow-up period of 1 year. Clinical data were collected by review of electronic medical records from 1998-2018. CMR data were collected by analysis of CMR images by blinded expert cardiac radiologist. The primary outcome was new onset of HF symptoms defined as NYHA class ≥ II at follow up. Kaplan-Meier analyses, and univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazard analyses were performed.Of 1,462 patients diagnosed with HCM who had at least 1 CMR, 276 HCM patients without HF symptoms at baseline were included in the study cohort. Average age at CMR was 52.7 ± 17.7 years and 93 (33.3%) were female. Median maximum left ventricular wall thickness was 19 mm (IQR 17-22) with a median LV ejection fraction of 71% (IQR 66-77). Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was detected in 150 (56.2%) patients (60.7% had mild; 30.7% moderate; 8.6% severe). During a median follow-up period of 6.3 years, 93 patients developed HF symptoms (NYHA class II in 56 (60.2%); class III in 31 (33.3%); and class IV in 6 (6.5%). Multivariable analysis adjusted for age showed that LA enlargement (HR 1.626; 95% CI 1.01-2.62; p=0.045) and LV mass index (HR 1.014; 95% CI 1.007-1.022; p= <0.001) at initial CMR along with sex (HR 1.7; 95% CI 1.074-2.691; p=0.023) were independent predictors of new onset of HF symptoms in patients with HCM. Conclusions Nearly half of the patients with HCM developed HF symptoms within 6.3 years. Left atrial enlargement, LV mass index, and sex were independent predictors of new onset of HF symptoms in HCM patients. These findings emphasize the value of CMR in HF risk assessment, in providing insights in management and improving outcomes in patients with HCM.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a genetic heart condition where the heart muscle becomes abnormally thick, and many patients with this condition eventually develop heart failure, which makes it difficult for the heart to pump blood effectively. Researchers examined heart imaging scans called cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, or CMR, from 276 patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who did not have heart failure symptoms when they started the study, and they followed these patients for an average of six years to see who developed heart failure symptoms. Nearly half of the patients developed heart failure symptoms during the follow-up period, and the researchers found that three factors visible on the initial imaging scans predicted which patients would develop these symptoms: an enlarged left atrium (the upper chamber of the heart), a higher left ventricle mass index (a measure of how thick the heart muscle is), and being female. These findings suggest that doctors can use cardiac magnetic resonance imaging to identify which patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are at highest risk for developing heart failure, which could help guide treatment decisions and improve patient outcomes. Future research should confirm these results in other patient groups and explore whether early.

title: Efficient and reliable measles reprogramming platform for the generation of human iPSC.
abstract: We previously established the measles virus (MeV) vector for reprogramming somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs); however, efficiency was limited to 0.2%. Here, we present the next generation that reprograms with an average efficiency of up to 2.3% and with similar or superior efficiency to the Sendai system. Twenty of the ninety iPSC isolated clones were amplified and analyzed. All clones showed a strong induction of endogenous pluripotency-associated markers SSEA-4, TRA-1-81, TRA-1-60, and NANOG. Analysis of the N mRNA transcript over passages showed rapid elimination of the vector from the iPSC at or before passage four. The pluripotency propensity was further analyzed using spontaneous and guided differentiation into three germ layers. All clones showed similar ability to differentiate into hematopoietic, pancreatic, and neuronal progenitor cells. In conclusion, this study shows that this new MeV reprogramming vector has a comparable or higher reprogramming efficiency than currently available systems and offers faster vector elimination from iPSCs. It uses a lower multiplicity of transduction as it uses a single vector versus multiple vectors. Finally, MeV produces iPSCs that can differentiate into multiple cell types. This makes MeV an efficient reprogramming platform for iPSC generation from patient samples.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers developed an improved version of a measles virus-based system that can reprogram regular human cells into induced pluripotent stem cells, which are special cells that can transform into almost any cell type in the body. The new system works much better than their previous version, achieving a success rate of 2. 3 percent compared to just 0. 2 percent before, and it performs as well as or better than other existing methods like the Sendai system. All twenty clones of stem cells they tested showed the correct markers of pluripotency and could be cleared of the virus by the fourth passage, meaning the viral vector disappeared quickly from the cells.

title: Low-density lipoproteins in human serum competitively inhibit the binding and entry of vesicular stomatitis virus.
abstract: Vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) is a promising anticancer agent but rapidly loses its infectivity in human serum. Here, we demonstrate that low-density and very low-density lipoproteins (LDLs and VLDLs) compete with VSV-G-displaying vectors for occupancy of cellular LDL receptors (LDLRs). Infectivity of VSV-G-displaying vectors was reduced two- to three-logs in the presence of heat-inactivated human serum but not if the serum was depleted of lipoproteins. The inhibitory effect was replicated in serum-free media supplemented with physiological concentrations of purified lipoprotein particles that contain the LDLR-binding protein Apo B-100, and the degree of inhibition correlated with the concentration of LDL or VLDL. When VSV-G was retargeted to the epidermal growth factor receptor, competitive inhibition by human serum or by LDL/VLDL was no longer observed. Similar results were obtained when VSV-G was retargeted to other receptors. Our findings demonstrate that serum LDL and VLDL competitively block the entry of VSV-G-displaying viral particles, but this barrier for in vivo delivery can be circumvented through a display of a receptor-targeting ligand on VSV-G.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Vesicular stomatitis virus, a type of virus being studied as a potential cancer treatment, loses its ability to infect cells very quickly when exposed to human blood, which limits its usefulness as a medical therapy. Researchers tested how different components of blood affect the virus's ability to enter cells and found that fatty particles called lipoproteins, which naturally circulate in the bloodstream to carry cholesterol, were blocking the virus from attaching to and entering cancer cells. The study showed that when these fatty particles were removed from blood samples, the virus worked much better, and when purified fatty particles were added back, they reduced the virus's effectiveness by two to three times depending on the concentration. The researchers discovered that this blocking problem could be solved by modifying the virus to target different cell receptors instead of the ones that fatty particles also use, which suggests a practical way to make virus-based cancer treatments work better inside the body. These findings could help scientists design improved versions of virus-based cancer therapies that can survive in the bloodstream and reach tumors more effectively.

llm_summary: Background:  Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, or CTEPH, is a serious lung condition where blood clots get stuck in the lung's blood vessels and cause high blood pressure in those vessels. Venular remodeling refers to changes in the structure of small veins in the lungs, and this reply discusses whether these changes are a core part of CTEPH itself or represent a separate disease process altogether.

title: Prospective and external evaluation of an AI model for continuous and early prediction of moderate and severe AKI in critically ill patients.
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a major complication in critically ill patients, burdening both patients and healthcare systems. We previously introduced an AI-based model for early and continuous prediction of ICU-acquired AKI (ICU-A-AKI-2/3). In this study, we enhanced the model to better handle missing data, a common challenge in clinical settings. The upgraded model was validated in both retrospective and prospective cohorts, demonstrating improved robustness and predictive performance.The model was validated in retrospective cohorts from three countries (US, Netherlands, Italy; N = 70,107 ICU admissions) across 176 ICUs. It was then prospectively validated in three European hospitals (Italy, Spain; N = 329) from May to October 2023. Using an XGBoost classifier, the model analyzes clinical data from ICU patients to predict hourly risk probabilities for AKI stages 2 and 3, as defined by KDIGO.In retrospective cohorts, the AI model achieved an auROC greater than 0.89 for early detection of ICU-A-AKI-2/3. Prospective validation showed auROCs between 0.82 (95% CI 0.73-0.92) and 0.96 (95% CI 0.92-0.99) across hospitals, with a mean lead time of approximately 14 h.This enhanced AI model offers timely prediction of ICU-A-AKI-2/3 episodes, as demonstrated across diverse cohorts. Its high predictive performance represents a significant advancement in integrating AI into clinical workflows, enhancing AKI management and improving clinical outcomes in ICU settings.© 2026. llm_summary: Kidney damage, called acute kidney injury, is a serious problem that affects many patients in intensive care units and costs healthcare systems a lot of money. Researchers developed and improved an artificial intelligence computer program that can predict which patients will develop moderate to severe kidney damage by analyzing their medical information hour by hour. The upgraded program was tested using patient records from hospitals in the United States, Netherlands, and Italy involving over 70,000 patients, and then tested prospectively, meaning doctors used it in real time with 329 new patients in European hospitals from May to October 2023. The artificial intelligence model successfully predicted kidney damage with high accuracy, correctly identifying problems more than 14 hours before they happened in most cases. This advancement could help doctors catch kidney damage earlier and treat patients better, though more testing in different hospitals and settings would help confirm these promising results.

title: Prognostic Value of Tricuspid Regurgitation in Pulmonary Hypertension and Among the Different WHO Groups.
abstract: Secondary tricuspid regurgitation (STR) is frequently observed in patients with pulmonary hypertension (PH). Whether it independently confers mortality risk beyond the associated right ventricular (RV) dysfunction remains unknown.The aim of this study was to evaluate the prognostic significance of STR in patients with PH other than related to left-sided valve disease or reduced ejection fraction and across the individual World Health Organization (WHO) groups of PH.Patients with RV systolic pressures ≥50 mm Hg on echocardiography between 2010 and 2023 and measured RV free wall longitudinal strain were identified retrospectively. Primary tricuspid valve disease, reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, significant left-sided valve disease, congenital heart disease, decompensated cirrhosis, malignancy, and dialysis were exclusion criteria. PH was classified according to the WHO group classification. Patients were followed for all-cause mortality.Of 1,318 patients (mean age 67 years, 61% women, 29% with moderate or greater STR, median RV free wall longitudinal strain 19%), WHO groups 1, 2, 3, and 4 PH were present in 33%, 11%, 32%, and 12%, respectively. Patients with moderate or greater STR were more symptomatic and congested and had worse RV function and pulmonary pressures. Over a median 1.5 years (Q1-Q3: 0.3-4.6 years), 454 patients died. Moderate or severe STR was associated with mortality independent of various RV function measures or RV-pulmonary arterial coupling. This remained true across the individual WHO groups of PH.Moderate or severe STR conferred mortality risk in patients with PH without left-sided valve disease or reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, beyond what can be explained by the associated RV dysfunction or impaired RV-pulmonary arterial coupling. Whether STR may represent an additional therapeutic target in certain subgroups with PH requires future investigation.Copyright © 2026 American College of Cardiology Foundation. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a common heart valve problem called tricuspid regurgitation, which involves blood leaking backward through a valve on the right side of the heart, increases the risk of death in patients with pulmonary hypertension, a condition where blood pressure in the lungs becomes dangerously high. The study looked back at records from over 1,300 patients between 2010 and 2023, excluding those with other heart or liver conditions that could affect the results, and followed them to see who died and when. They found that patients with moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation were more likely to die during the study period, even after accounting for how poorly the right side of the heart was pumping blood. This increased death risk from tricuspid regurgitation held true across all different types of pulmonary hypertension, suggesting the valve problem itself poses a danger beyond just the heart weakness it causes. The researchers concluded that tricuspid regurgitation may be an important target for future treatment in pulmonary hypertension patients, though more research is needed to determine which patients would benefit most from focusing on fixing this valve problem.

title: National and state-level trends in digestive diseases in the United States, 1990 to 2021.
abstract: Digestive diseases are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, placing a substantial burden on healthcare.Data from the 2021 Global Burden of Disease study were analyzed for all 50 US states and the District of Columbia. Temporal trends were quantified using estimated annual percentage changes, and correlations with the Socio-Demographic Index were assessed using Pearson's correlation.From 1990 to 2021, total incident digestive diseases cases rose from 20.1 to 26.2 million, a 30.5% increase, while age-standardized incidence rates declined by 9.8%. Age-standardized disability-adjusted life year (DALY) rates decreased by 7.7%, and death rates fell by 5.9%. Most digestive diseases showed declining DALY rates; however, cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases increased by 4.5% and remained the highest contributor to DALYs, with a 9% rise in mortality. Inflammatory bowel disease also increased, with DALYs rising by 12% in males and 23% in females; mortality rose by 64% in females versus 44% in males.These findings reveal both progress and persistent disparities, with higher burdens among women and states with a lower Socio-Demographic Index. Targeted interventions and resource allocation are warranted to address these inequities.

llm_summary: Digestive diseases, which affect the stomach, intestines, and related organs, cause significant illness and death in the United States and place a heavy burden on the healthcare system. Researchers analyzed health data from all fifty states and Washington D. C. collected between 1990 and 2021 to track how digestive diseases have changed over time and how they affect different populations. While the total number of people with digestive diseases increased by about thirty percent over this period, the rate of new cases adjusted for population age actually decreased, and deaths from most digestive diseases went down.

llm_summary: Background:  Blood bags are containers used to store donated blood for medical transfusions, which are procedures where blood from a donor is transferred into a patient who needs it. Dark spots or discoloration that appear on blood bags can indicate contamination or degradation of the stored blood, which is a serious concern because transfusing compromised blood could harm patients.

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications Versus Manual Methods For Literature Retrieval: A Comparative Analysis.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative and large language models, is being used in nursing education, practice, and scholarly writing. Generative AI applications have been specifically examined for their use in conducting literature reviews with evidence supporting reduced production time of scholarly work. However, there has been limited investigation of their levels of accuracy with identifying references for a literature review.The purpose of this study was to compare human-generated citations of literature reviews with AI literature-review generated citations.Using a comparative exploratory design, references from 4 human-written literature reviews, 2 published and 2 unpublished, on 4 different topics, were compared to references derived from 2 AI literature applications, Consensus and Elicit. Three prompting strategies were utilized, including prompts generated using ChatGPT-4. Agreement between the AI and human references was evaluated.The percent of agreement between AI and human generated reference lists ranged from 0% to 63.6%. The Consensus application had a greater overall mean rate of match (21.3%) as compared to Elicit (3.7%). The use of a ChatGPT-4 prompt did not significantly impact results, and there were no differences based on published or unpublished literature reviews.The 2 literature-based applications examined in this study offered a glimpse of their potential use and limitations. The use of an AI literature review application may support but not replace human work.

llm_summary: Artificial intelligence tools that use large language models, or computer programs trained on vast amounts of text data, are becoming popular in nursing education and research, but there are questions about how accurate they are at finding scientific papers for literature reviews. Researchers compared the references that two artificial intelligence applications called Consensus and Elicit found against the references that human researchers had selected for four different literature reviews on various topics. The results showed that the artificial intelligence tools only matched the human-selected references between zero and sixty-four percent of the time, with Consensus performing better at about twenty-one percent agreement compared to Elicit at less than four percent. These findings suggest that while artificial intelligence applications can help speed up the process of finding research papers and save time, they cannot be trusted to work alone and must be checked by human researchers. Future studies should continue testing these tools to understand their strengths and weaknesses better before they become standard practice in nursing research and education.

title: Prognostic Role of Admission Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Updated Meta-Analysis of 33,049 Patients.
abstract: To evaluate the association of admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) with functional outcomes, intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), and mortality in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS).We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Embase from inception until December 17, 2024. Studies examining admission NLR as a predictor for functional outcomes, ICH, and mortality in AIS patients were included. A meta-analysis was performed using pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Subgroup analyses were conducted based on treatment modality, time of measurement, hemorrhage type, and ethnicity. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics, and publication bias was evaluated using Egger's test.Sixty observational studies (33,049 patients), including 59 cohort studies and one cross-sectional study, were included. Higher admission NLR was significantly associated with unfavorable functional outcomes (OR: 1.10, 95% CI: [1.07, 1.14]), ICH (OR: 1.06, 95% CI: [1.03, 1.09]), and mortality (OR: 1.06, 95% CI: [1.04, 1.08]). Subgroup analysis indicated that NLR was associated with poor outcomes in AIS patients receiving mechanical thrombectomy and intravenous thrombolysis.Admission NLR is significantly associated with unfavorable functional outcomes, ICH, and mortality in AIS patients. Its predictive value remained evident in the MT and Asian subgroups; however, the association with unfavorable functional outcomes was not significant in the non-Asian subgroup, and the association with mortality in the IVT subgroup was also not significant. Given its accessibility and cost-effectiveness, NLR holds promise as a routine biomarker for stroke prognosis.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a simple blood test measuring the ratio of two types of white blood cells called neutrophils and lymphocytes could predict which stroke patients would have worse outcomes. The team reviewed sixty studies involving over thirty-three thousand patients with acute ischemic stroke, which occurs when a blood clot blocks blood flow to the brain, and analyzed how this blood cell ratio measured at hospital admission related to patient recovery, brain bleeding, and death. They found that patients with higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios had significantly worse functional recovery, were more likely to experience brain bleeding, and had higher death rates compared to those with lower ratios. This blood test appears particularly useful for predicting outcomes in patients who received mechanical thrombectomy, a procedure where doctors use a catheter to physically remove the blood clot from the brain, and in Asian populations, though the results were less consistent in other groups. Because this blood test is quick, inexpensive, and already routinely available in hospitals, doctors could potentially use it as a standard tool to identify stroke patients at highest risk and guide treatment decisions.

title: IL15-mediated crosstalk between LSECs and CD8⁺ tissue-resident memory T cells drives alcohol-associated hepatitis.
abstract: Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) is a severe inflammatory liver condition driven by dysregulated immune responses. CD8 T cells accumulate in the liver during AH, yet their functional role remains poorly defined.A murine NIAAA chronic-binge model with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge was used. Single-cell RNA sequencing of liver and blood immune cells defined CD8 T cell subsets, followed by pathway analysis and reanalysis of human AH datasets. Spatial relationships were validated by immunohistochemistry of human AH liver tissue with CD8 TRM and liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) co-staining. LSEC-CD8 T cell interactions were examined using in vitro co-culture, and signaling pathways were assessed by bulk RNA sequencing and phospho-protein analyses. IL15 function was evaluated by in vivo neutralization.Single-cell RNA sequencing in the murine AH model revealed a distinct population of CD8 tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM) with heightened activation and proinflammatory cytokine production. Analysis of human AH liver single-cell RNA sequencing data, along with immunohistochemistry validation, supported CD8 TRM enrichment in diseased tissue. IL15 emerged as a prominent pathway linked to TRM activation, and IL15 blockade reduced TRM abundance and attenuated EtOH/ lipopolysaccharide-induced liver injury. Mechanistically, LSECs not only provided a structural niche for TRM retention but also amplified IL15 signalling. In vitro, coculture experiments demonstrated that LSECs intensified activation in pre-stimulated CD8 T cells in a stimulus-dependent manner: under IL15 stimulation, LSECs boosted effector function without inducing cell death, whereas under T-cell receptor stimulation, LSECs drove hyperactivation and activation-induced cell death. Bulk RNA-seq and phospho-protein analysis identified the PI3K-AKT pathway as a shared pathway enhanced by LSEC coculture in activated CD8 T cells. These findings define a context-dependent mechanism in which LSECs promote IL15-driven signaling through AKT pathway amplification, promoting TRM persistence and inflammatory activity in AH.IL15-associated signaling within the hepatic microenvironment, shaped by LSEC-CD8 T-cell interactions, promotes activation and persistence of CD8 TRM cells in AH. Targeting the IL15-LSEC-AKT axis may disrupt pathogenic TRM niches and represent a promising therapeutic strategy for severe AH.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Alcohol-associated hepatitis is a serious liver disease caused by excessive drinking that triggers harmful inflammation in the body, and understanding how immune cells contribute to this damage could lead to better treatments. Researchers used mouse models of chronic alcohol exposure combined with bacterial toxins and analyzed immune cells from both mice and human patients to identify which cells were most active in diseased livers. They discovered that a specific type of immune cell called tissue-resident memory T cells accumulated in the liver and became highly activated, and these cells were being stimulated by a chemical messenger called IL15 that was produced by liver blood vessel cells. When the researchers blocked IL15 in mice, the harmful immune cells decreased and liver damage improved, suggesting that targeting this communication pathway between blood vessel cells and immune cells could reduce disease severity. These findings point toward a new potential treatment approach for severe alcohol-associated hepatitis that focuses on interrupting the IL15 signaling pathway, though further research will be needed to test whether this strategy works safely and effectively in human patients.

title: Mapping the continuum of procedural bariatric care: real-world weight loss after endoscopic and surgical interventions.
abstract: Obesity is a chronic, relapsing disease for which lifestyle and pharmacologic therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, can achieve meaningful weight loss but are often limited by tolerability, access, and weight recurrence after discontinuation. Consequently, metabolic and bariatric interventions play a central role in the management of moderate to severe obesity. However, real-world comparative data spanning endoscopic and multiple surgical modalities remain limited.We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adults undergoing endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG), sleeve gastrectomy (SG), Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB), or biliopancreatic diversion with duodenal switch (BPD-DS) at a single tertiary academic center. Patients with concurrent anti-obesity pharmacotherapy were excluded. The primary outcome was percent total body weight loss (TBWL%) at 12 months (± 2 months). Secondary outcomes included categorical TBWL thresholds (> 10%, > 15%, > 20%, > 25%, > 30%) and percent excess weight loss (EWL%). Multivariable linear regression was used to identify independent predictors of TBWL.Among 2,825 patients (79.3% female; mean age 47.5 ± 11.9 years; mean baseline BMI 45.6 ± 7.9 kg/m2), 183 underwent ESG, 699 SG, 1,813 RYGB, and 130 BPD-DS. Mean 12-month TBWL differed significantly by procedure (p < 0.001): ESG 14.1 ± 9.3%, SG 23.6 ± 9.4%, RYGB 31.0 ± 8.3%, and BPD-DS 36.8 ± 8.7%. The likelihood of achieving higher categorical TBWL increased with procedural intensity, whereas EWL values demonstrated less pronounced separation, particularly between RYGB and BPD-DS. In adjusted analyses, procedure type was the strongest independent predictor of TBWL (p < 0.001), with younger age, female sex, absence of diabetes, and lower baseline BMI also associated with greater weight loss.Endoscopic and surgical bariatric interventions are associated with distinct yet overlapping weight loss profiles at one year, reflecting differences in mechanism, invasiveness, and patient selection. While absolute TBWL varies across modalities, convergence in EWL highlights the influence of baseline adiposity and the importance of metric selection. These findings provide practical benchmarks to support individualized, patient-centered decision-making across the full continuum of metabolic therapies.© 2026. llm_summary: Obesity is a serious long-term health condition that often comes back even after people lose weight through diet, exercise, or medications, so doctors use various weight loss procedures to help people with moderate to severe obesity. Researchers studied nearly 2,800 patients who received one of four different weight loss treatments: a minimally invasive procedure called endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty that uses a camera to reshape the stomach, surgical sleeve gastrectomy that removes part of the stomach, gastric bypass surgery that reroutes the digestive system, or a more complex surgery called biliopancreatic diversion with duodenal switch. After one year, patients who had the more invasive surgeries lost significantly more weight than those who had the less invasive endoscopic procedure, with weight loss ranging from 14 percent of total body weight for the endoscopic procedure to nearly 37 percent for the most complex surgery. The type of procedure was the strongest factor determining how much weight patients lost, though younger patients, women, those without diabetes, and people with lower starting weights also tended to lose more weight overall. These findings help doctors and patients choose the right weight loss treatment by showing what results to.

title: Genetic screening for CSF1R variants in patients with dementia, parkinsonism, and multiple sclerosis.
abstract: To determine the frequency of colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor gene (CSF1R) variants in a cohort of Mayo Clinic patients with different neurodegenerative disorders.Blood samples collected from patients diagnosed in the past five years with early-onset (18-60 years) cognitive impairment, atypical parkinsonism and primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS) were screened for variants in the CSF1R gene using Sanger sequencing. For individuals with CSF1R variants, clinical data were analyzed. An online tool, SIFT (https://sift.bii.a-star.edu.sg/), was applied to predict possible impact of CSF1R variants. Moreover, the identified CSF1R variants were expressed in HEK293 cells, and their effects on CSF1R phosphorylation were assessed by western blotting.Samples from 310 patients with dementia (n = 135), PPMS (n = 96) and atypical parkinsonism (n = 79) were analyzed. Two novel CSF1R variants in the heterozygous state were identified: p.G872V (c.2615G > T) in a 60-year-old male with atypical parkinsonism and moderate microangiopathic leukoencephalopathy on MRI and p.K864Q (c.2590A > C) in a 45-year-old female with behavioral variant of frontotemporal lobar degeneration with extensive tau pathology who died by suicide. The latter patient was also a carrier of a MAPT gene mutation: p.N279K; c.837T > G. SIFT analysis predicted both CSF1R variants to be deleterious. Both patients had a positive family history for dementia. In vitro studies confirmed that both CSF1R p.K864Q and p.G872V variants disturbed CSF1R phosphorylation with a stronger effect for CSF1R p.G872V.CSF1R-related disorder (RD) is often mis- and underdiagnosed. Genetic testing for CSF1R-RD should be applied more often in cases of early-onset neurodegenerative disorders with a combination of cognitive, psychiatric, and motor symptoms and a positive family history.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a specific gene called CSF1R, which controls how certain brain cells develop and function, carried harmful changes in patients with early-onset brain disorders including dementia, movement problems similar to Parkinson's disease, and a type of multiple sclerosis. The team collected blood samples from 310 patients at Mayo Clinic and used genetic testing to search for variations in the CSF1R gene, then studied how these variations affected the gene's activity in laboratory cells. They discovered two new harmful CSF1R variations: one in a man with movement problems and brain damage visible on imaging, and another in a woman with behavioral changes and memory loss who also carried a second genetic mutation. Laboratory testing confirmed that both of these genetic variations disrupted how the CSF1R gene normally functions, with one variation showing a stronger disruptive effect than the other. The researchers concluded that genetic testing for CSF1R-related disorders should be used more frequently in patients with early-onset brain diseases that combine thinking problems, mood or behavior changes, and movement difficulties, especially when multiple family members have experienced similar conditions.

title: Toward the Future: A Race-Agnostic, Bayesian Approach to Defining Glomerular Filtration for Personalized Drug Dosing.
abstract: Accurate assessment of renal function is fundamental to dosing renally eliminated drugs. For decades, serum creatinine-based estimating equations have been used to approximate glomerular filtration rate (GFR) for this purpose. While these equations perform reasonably well at the population level, they exhibit substantial individual-level imprecision and inaccuracy. Simultaneously, recent efforts to remove race from estimating equations addressed important ethical concerns but did not resolve the core limitation of population-based estimation for individual drug dosing. In this perspective, we argue that personalized dosing requires a shift away from demographic surrogates toward direct measurement of renal clearance and clarify when incremental therapeutic complexity is warranted. We review the limitations of endogenous biomarkers, discuss the role of cystatin C, and propose exogenously measured GFR using iohexol integrated within a Bayesian pharmacometric framework as a clinically actionable approach to individualized drug dosing. Practically, this framework can be implemented by administering a small iohexol dose, collecting sparse timed samples, estimating absolute mGFR and its uncertainty with Bayesian software, and using that posterior estimate to refine renal dose selection.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Doctors have long used blood tests measuring a substance called creatinine to figure out how well a person's kidneys are working, which helps them decide what dose of medicine to give patients. However, these blood tests are not very accurate for individual patients even though they work reasonably well when looking at large groups of people. Researchers propose a new approach that uses a special test substance called iohexol, which is injected into the body in small amounts, combined with mathematical modeling to directly measure how well each person's kidneys filter waste. This personalized method would involve giving patients a tiny dose of iohexol, collecting a few blood samples over time, and using computer software to calculate each person's exact kidney function and how confident doctors should be in that measurement. By shifting away from population-based estimates toward direct measurement tailored to individual patients, doctors could more accurately prescribe the right doses of kidney-filtered medications and improve drug safety for everyone.

title: Pediatric epilepsy surgery: Global survey of invasive explorations.
abstract: Invasive presurgical evaluation plays a key role in pediatric epilepsy surgery, particularly in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-negative cases, by guiding resective, disconnective, or ablative procedures. This International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery Taskforce study provides an updated global overview of current invasive evaluation practices.Group-level data were collected from 61 epilepsy surgery programs (49 pediatric-only) in 29 countries across six continents. Included were children and adolescents who underwent presurgical evaluation and epilepsy surgery in 2023. The study was designed to enable comparison with the similar ILAE survey conducted in 2004.A total of 2427 patients were included. Invasive evaluations were performed in 21.1% of cases, most frequently in North America (33.7%, higher than Europe: 18.0%, p = .003). Among invasive cases, 32.3% had no detectable MRI abnormalities. The main indication for invasive evaluation was seizure onset localization (88.1%), followed by motor or sensory mapping (17.2%) and language mapping (14.2%). Stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) was the predominant technique (19.8% overall, 93.6% of invasive cases), more common in North America (30.0%, p = .021) and less common in South America (7.4%, p < .001). Subdural electrodes were used in only 3.2% of invasive cases, and combined depth and subdural approaches in 3.2%. SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC) was performed in 40.9% of SEEG cases, most commonly in Asia (63.8%). In 16.2% of invasive evaluations, patients did not proceed to resection, disconnection, or ablation, with the highest rate in Europe (28.5%).This global survey provides the first broad overview of invasive evaluation practices in pediatric epilepsy surgery across participating centers worldwide. It highlights the widespread adoption of SEEG, declining use of subdural electrodes, and increasing application of SEEG-guided RF-TC. llm_summary: Researchers examined how doctors around the world use invasive brain monitoring techniques to help children with epilepsy who are candidates for surgery, particularly those whose brain scans appear normal. The study collected information from 61 epilepsy surgery programs across 29 countries in 2023, tracking 2,427 children and adolescents to understand current surgical evaluation practices and compare them to similar data collected nearly 20 years earlier. The findings showed that invasive monitoring was used in about one out of every five cases, with a technique called stereoelectroencephalography (which involves placing thin electrodes deep in the brain to record electrical activity) becoming the most popular method, while older techniques using surface electrodes were used much less frequently. Importantly, the study revealed that about one in six patients who underwent invasive monitoring did not go on to have surgery, suggesting that doctors are still working to better identify which children will benefit most from surgical treatment. These results highlight how pediatric epilepsy surgery has evolved and point to the need for improved methods to select the right patients for invasive evaluation and surgery.

title: High-Dose Methotrexate as CNS Prophylaxis in Ultra High-Risk Large B-Cell Lymphoma: An International Multicenter Analysis.
abstract: In large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), use of high-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX) to prevent CNS relapse (so-called CNS prophylaxis) remains controversial. International guidelines continue to recommend HD-MTX in patients deemed ultra high risk (UHR) because of a lack of robust data specific to these subgroups. This study was designed to examine the impact of HD-MTX specifically in UHR patients.Data from two previous retrospective analyses were combined to produce a cohort of UHR patients (≥1 of the following criteria: CNS international prognostic index score 5-6; testicular, renal/adrenal, or breast involvement; ≥3 extranodal sites), treated with or without HD-MTX. The primary outcome was CNS relapse rate (isolated or concurrent with systemic relapse) measured from diagnosis with additional landmark analysis of all responding patients with no progression event at 6 months.Analyses were performed on 1,923 patients meeting UHR criteria. No significant difference in 3-year CNS relapse rate was observed between no HD-MTX (n = 1,051) versus HD-MTX patients (n = 872), including in multivariable analyses adjusting for baseline characteristics (3-year rate, 9.3% v 8.1%; adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 0.82 to 1.57]). Analyses restricted to isolated CNS relapse also confirmed no difference (5.9% v 5.7%; adjusted HR, 1.03 [95% CI, 0.69 to 1.53]). In the landmark analysis (no HD-MTX n = 782, HD-MTX n = 773), no difference in 3-year CNS relapse was observed (6.7% v 6.6%, adjusted HR, 0.95 [95% CI, 0.62 to 1.44]).To our knowledge, this is the largest international comparative data set of patients with LBCL with UHR features showing no significant reduction in CNS relapse with HD-MTX in all UHR or in any individual subgroup. Despite inherent limitations of retrospective analyses, the data strongly support previous studies in suggesting HD-MTX prophylaxis has no meaningful benefit for most patients.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a high-dose chemotherapy drug called methotrexate could prevent cancer from spreading to the brain in patients with a serious type of blood cancer called large B-cell lymphoma who had extra risk factors for this complication. They combined data from nearly two thousand ultra high-risk patients, some of whom received the preventive drug and some who did not, and tracked how many developed brain cancer over three years. The study found no meaningful difference in brain cancer rates between the two groups, with about nine percent of patients without the drug and eight percent with the drug developing this complication. These findings suggest that giving this expensive and potentially toxic drug to all ultra high-risk patients may not be necessary, contrary to what current medical guidelines recommend. The researchers acknowledge that their study has limitations because it looked back at past patient records rather than randomly assigning patients to treatment groups, but the results strongly suggest that doctors should reconsider whether this preventive treatment truly helps most patients.

title: On the Use and Application of Virtual Reality in Diagnostic Radiology.
abstract: Immersive technologies, particularly virtual reality (VR), have significantly advanced since their inception in the mid-twentieth century. In recent years, the development of affordable, high-quality VR systems has catalyzed their application across various fields, including diagnostic radiology. Radiologists can use VR to navigate complex anatomical structures in three dimensions, enhancing their understanding of spatial relationships and pathology and helping them visualize and interpret diagnostic medical images. This article explains the history of immersive technologies, how VR is currently being used in diagnostic radiology, and assesses prospects for future applications. Integration with artificial intelligence could lead to more sophisticated simulations, enhancing diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment plans. VR's role in teleradiology is expected to grow, facilitating remote consultations and virtual collaboration among radiologists, improving accessibility for patients in underserved regions.© 2026. llm_summary: Virtual reality, which is technology that creates immersive three-dimensional environments, has become more affordable and practical in recent years, making it useful for medical professionals like radiologists who interpret medical images. Radiologists can now use virtual reality systems to explore complex body structures in three dimensions, which helps them better understand how different parts of the body relate to each other and identify diseases or abnormalities more clearly. The article reviews the history of immersive technologies, explains how virtual reality is currently being used in the field of diagnostic radiology, and discusses what possibilities exist for future medical applications. Combining virtual reality with artificial intelligence, which is computer technology that can learn and make decisions, could create more advanced simulations that improve how accurately doctors diagnose diseases and create treatment plans tailored to individual patients. Virtual reality is also expected to play a growing role in teleradiology, which is the practice of sharing medical images and consultations between doctors in different locations, allowing patients in remote or underserved areas to access better medical care.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether reducing a blood protein called plasminogen could help the liver recover faster after surgical removal of part of the liver, since excessive blood clotting can interfere with healing. In mouse experiments, they used a genetic technique called siRNA to reduce plasminogen levels and found that this approach actually helped liver cells multiply and regenerate more quickly after surgery. In a human clinical trial called HeLiX, patients who received tranexamic acid, a medication that reduces blood clotting by blocking plasminogen, had significantly lower rates of post-hepatectomy liver failure, which is a serious complication that can occur after liver surgery. These findings suggest that anti-fibrinolytic strategies, which are medications that prevent the breakdown of blood clots, could become a new treatment option to help patients recover better after liver surgery and prevent dangerous complications. Future research will need to confirm these results and determine the best way to use these medications in clinical practice to improve outcomes for liver surgery patients.

title: Palliative and End-of-Life Care Utilization in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Population-Based Study.
abstract: Little is known about end-of-life trajectories in survivors of cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction (AMI-CS) who die beyond their index admission, or utilization of palliative care services in AMI-CS survivors.This study aimed to examine long-term palliative and end-of-life care among AMI-CS survivors.This was a population-based, retrospective cohort of AMI-CS survivors in Ontario, Canada, from 2009 to 2020 who died during longitudinal follow-up.We identified 3,881 AMI-CS survivors (2009-2020) who died after discharge and before March 2024. The median survival time was 1,096 days (IQR: 312-2,139 days). Overall, 2,100 patients (54.1%) died in acute care, with no difference between those who did and did not receive palliative care. Patients who did not receive palliative care were more likely to die in intensive care units (ICU) than those who did (23% vs 17%, absolute standard difference 0.15). Most patients received palliative care in the final year of life (n = 2,485, 64%); 1,057 patients (42.5%) had outpatient visits, 505 patients (20.3%) had inpatient palliative care consultations, and 327 patients (13.2%) had palliative care hospitalizations. Palliative care, however, was most commonly initiated in the last 14 days of life (1,185 patients, 47.7%). Earlier palliative care referrals were associated with reduced rates of dying in hospital (adjusted OR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.42-0.65) and ICU (adjusted OR: 0.34; 95% CI: 0.26-0.45).Early and intermediate term palliative care involvement was associated with reduced risk of death in hospital and ICU. Such consultation may improve end-of-life outcomes in AMI-CS survivors.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how patients who survived a life-threatening heart condition called cardiogenic shock (when the heart cannot pump enough blood to the body) during a heart attack used palliative care services, which are medical treatments focused on comfort rather than curing the disease, during the years after their initial hospital stay. The study looked at nearly 3,900 patients in Ontario, Canada, between 2009 and 2020 who survived their initial heart attack but died later, tracking how often they received palliative care and where they spent their final days. The researchers found that most patients did not receive palliative care until the last two weeks of their lives, even though more than half of all patients ended up dying in hospitals rather than at home or in other settings. Patients who started palliative care earlier, rather than waiting until the very end, were significantly less likely to die in hospitals or intensive care units, suggesting that earlier involvement of comfort-focused care improved their end-of-life experiences. These findings suggest that doctors should consider referring heart attack survivors to palliative care services sooner after discharge, as this approach may help patients avoid spending their final days in intensive hospital settings.

llm_summary: Cells in our bodies can enter a state called senescence, where they stop dividing and accumulate in tissues as we age or develop diseases, which contributes to many age-related health problems. Researchers used advanced technology to examine individual cells from different human tissues and map out the various types of senescent cells, discovering that these cells have different characteristics depending on which tissue they come from and what surrounds them. The study revealed that senescent cells are not all the same and that they follow tissue-specific patterns, meaning cells in the heart behave differently from cells in the brain or skin. These findings could help doctors identify new markers or signs to detect senescent cells in patients and develop targeted treatments that specifically remove or manage these problematic cells. The research provides a foundation for creating new therapies aimed at slowing aging and treating age-related diseases by understanding and targeting the different types of senescent cells in our bodies.

title: Medical Therapy for NF2-related Schwannomatosis: A Systematic Review of Current Evidence.
abstract: To synthesize the available evidence on medical therapies investigated for the management of NF2-related vestibular schwannomas (VS).Systematic review.Not applicable.NF2-related VS patients.Systemic medical therapies.Tumor control and hearing outcomes.Thirty studies met inclusion criteria: 18 investigated bevacizumab, 5 mTOR inhibitors, 5 tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), and 2 the vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR) vaccine. Bevacizumab demonstrated the most consistent activity, with hearing improvement in up to 61% of patients, stable hearing in up to 84%, and tumor response in up to 60% (Level 4 evidence). Outcomes for mTOR inhibitors were variable, with 1 study stopped for futility, while others reported up to 100% hearing and tumor stability (Level 4 evidence). Five different TKIs showed hearing improvement rates ranging from 17 to 60% and tumor responses of 10 to 23.5% (Level 4 evidence). llm_summary: Researchers examined medical treatments for neurofibromatosis type 2, a genetic condition where patients develop tumors called schwannomas that grow on nerves and can cause hearing loss and other serious problems. The team reviewed thirty studies that tested four different types of drug therapies to see which ones could slow tumor growth or help patients keep their hearing. Bevacizumab, a drug that blocks blood vessel growth to tumors, showed the most promise with hearing improvement in up to 61 percent of patients and tumor control in up to 60 percent, while other drugs like tyrosine kinase inhibitors and messenger target of rapamycin inhibitors produced more mixed results with lower success rates. Although these findings suggest bevacizumab is the most effective option currently available, the evidence comes mostly from small studies without comparison groups, meaning doctors cannot yet be certain which treatment works best or how long the benefits last. Researchers emphasize that larger, well-designed clinical trials comparing these treatments directly are urgently needed to help doctors make better treatment decisions for patients with this serious genetic condition.

title: Spatial biomarker discovery via interpretable semantic learning in histopathology.
abstract: Spatial biomarkers are critical for precision oncology but remain challenging to systematically discover due to the complexity of whole-slide images. We present PathPrism, an interpretable AI framework for spatial biomarker discovery and virtual experimentation. Unlike black-box models, PathPrism encodes tissue architecture into pathologically informed spatial features, enabling transparent modeling of prognosis, molecular alterations, and therapy response. Applied to 7,000 patients with colorectal cancer across 11 cohorts, PathPrism uncovered hundreds of biomarkers predictive of survival, MSI, BRAF, and TP53 mutations, and stratified chemotherapy benefit in stage II/III disease. Building on these interpretable findings, PathPrism uses large language models as auxiliary tools to generate hypotheses grounded in spatial semantics. We further introduce VirtualWSI, a platform for semantic perturbation within an interpretable spatial biomarker atlas. PathPrism provides a scalable and interpretable framework for spatial biomarker discovery.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers developed a new artificial intelligence tool called PathPrism that can analyze tissue samples from cancer patients in a way that doctors and scientists can actually understand and trust, rather than using hidden computer processes that nobody can explain. The team tested this tool on tissue samples from seven thousand colorectal cancer patients across eleven different research groups to find patterns that predict how well patients will survive, whether their cancer has specific genetic changes, and how they might respond to chemotherapy treatment. The artificial intelligence discovered hundreds of these predictive patterns in the tissue structure and also used large language models, which are advanced computer programs trained on vast amounts of text, to help generate new scientific ideas based on what it found. This breakthrough matters because doctors could eventually use these discoveries to personalize cancer treatment plans for individual patients based on what their specific tissue samples look like under the microscope. The researchers also created a virtual platform that lets scientists test what would happen if they changed certain features in the tissue samples, opening up new ways to understand cancer biology and develop better treatments.

title: Clinical Outcomes After Endoscopic Management of Low-Risk and High-Risk T1b Esophageal Adenocarcinoma: A Patient-Level Pooled Analysis of International Studies.
abstract: Endoscopic eradication therapy (EET) is standard of care for T1a esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). There are limited data regarding long-term outcomes of EET for T1b EAC. The aim of this study was to assess clinical outcomes after endoscopic management of low-risk and high-risk T1b EAC via a pooled analysis of individual patient-level data.A pooled analysis of studies reporting endoscopic management of T1b EAC was conducted. Inclusion required endoscopic resection revealing T1b EAC with negative deep margins. High-risk T1b EAC was defined by presence of: SM2/3 or deep (>500 μm) submucosal invasion, lymphovascular invasion, or poor grade of differentiation. Clinical outcomes included all-cause and EAC-related mortality, intraluminal recurrence, and extraluminal metastases.Of 418 studies identified, 7 with 216 patients were included (84% men, 94% White). The median (IQR) follow-up was 48.1 (25.5-68.1) months. High-risk T1b EAC was observed in 114 (53%) patients. Baseline clinical characteristics were mostly similar between groups. Although the rates of intraluminal recurrence in the low-risk and high-risk groups were comparable (15% vs. 22%, p=0.30), the high-risk group had a five-fold significantly higher risk of extraluminal metastases (11% vs. 2%, p=0.01). Both all-cause and EAC-related mortality were significantly higher in the high-risk group (logrank p=0.04).In this international pooled analysis, rates of extraluminal metastases and EAC-related mortality were very low in patients with low-risk T1b EAC, supporting the role of EET in this group. However, outcomes were significantly worse for the high-risk T1b group, suggesting careful patient selection and shared decision making in this population.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how well a minimally invasive procedure called endoscopic eradication therapy works for treating a type of early-stage esophageal cancer called T1b adenocarcinoma, which is cancer that has grown slightly deeper into the esophagus wall. The study combined patient information from seven international research projects involving 216 patients who underwent this endoscopic procedure, tracking their health outcomes for an average of four years to see who developed cancer recurrence or spread. Patients with low-risk tumors, meaning their cancers had favorable characteristics, had very low rates of cancer returning or spreading to other parts of the body, while patients with high-risk tumors, meaning their cancers had more aggressive features, experienced five times more distant spread and higher death rates from cancer. These findings suggest that endoscopic eradication therapy is a safe and effective treatment choice for patients with low-risk T1b esophageal cancer, but doctors should be more cautious and have detailed conversations with patients who have high-risk tumors before choosing this approach. The research shows that careful selection of which patients receive this procedure is important, and future studies should explore whether high-risk patients might.

title: Transferrin receptor 1 binds human parvovirus B19 VP1u to facilitate entry.
abstract: Human parvovirus B19 (B19V) displays a strict tropism for erythroid progenitor cells, which is governed by the VP1 unique domain (VP1u). This domain mediates cell-specific uptake through interaction with an unknown cellular receptor, termed VP1uR. Proximity labeling in permissive erythroid cells identifies transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1/CD71) as a predominant membrane protein associated with VP1u. VP1u constructs colocalize with TfR1 at the cell surface of erythroid cells. Incubation with anti-TfR1 antibody OKT9 abolishes binding and uptake of recombinant VP1u. While OKT9 efficiently inhibits B19V uptake and infection, it does not block virus binding to host cells. Direct binding assays confirm interaction of VP1u with human TfR1. Using cryo-EM we solved the 2.4 Å structure of the TfR1-VP1u complex, mapping the binding site. These findings establish TfR1 as the previously unknown receptor, VP1uR, required for B19V uptake.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Human parvovirus B19 is a virus that specifically infects blood-forming cells in the bone marrow, and scientists needed to understand how it recognizes and enters these cells to develop better treatments. Researchers used advanced laboratory techniques including proximity labeling, which identifies proteins that are close together, and cryo-electron microscopy, a method that creates detailed three-dimensional images of molecules, to discover that a protein called transferrin receptor 1 acts as the entry point the virus uses to get inside cells. The team found that the virus's unique outer protein domain binds directly to transferrin receptor 1 on the surface of blood-forming cells, and blocking this receptor with an antibody prevented the virus from entering cells and causing infection. This discovery reveals the specific molecular lock and key mechanism that allows parvovirus B19 to target blood cells, which could help scientists develop new drugs or vaccines to stop the virus from infecting people. Future research will likely focus on using this knowledge to create treatments that block this interaction and prevent the serious complications that can occur when this virus infects patients with weakened immune systems or blood disorders.

title: Scrolling for Surgery: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Evaluation of Labiaplasty Discourse on TikTok.
abstract: Labiaplasty has experienced growing popularity, with over 10,800 procedures performed annually in the USA. Discussions about this surgery are shifting to social media, particularly TikTok, where health information is often presented with limited regulation or oversight. This raises concerns about the accuracy, quality, and influence of labiaplasty-related content.We conducted a cross-sectional observational study analyzing the 110 most relevant TikTok videos under the term "labiaplasty" (July-August 2025). Video characteristics, engagement metrics (likes, shares, comments), and creator types were recorded. Content quality was assessed using the Global Quality Scale (GQS) by human reviewers and an AI model (ChatGPT-4.5-turbo). Sentiment analysis of video comments was performed by two human raters and the AI model. Statistical analyses included Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests.Surgeons (52%) and patients (40%) produced most videos, primarily on educational (39%) or postoperative (28%) content. Overall, median human-rated GQS was 3.5 [IQR, 2.13-4.88], while the AI median was 3 [IQR, 2-4]. Videos with ≥2000 likes were more often created by patients (52% vs. 32%, p=0.012) and had significantly lower GQS scores (human: 2.5 vs. 4, p=0.003; AI: 2 vs. 3, p<0.001). Human inter-rater reliability for sentiment classification was slight (κ=0.161), with minimal agreement between AI and humans (κ=0.077).Labiaplasty content on TikTok is predominantly generated by surgeons and patients, yet lower-quality videos achieve higher engagement. Surgeons should proactively create accurate, relatable content to counterbalance misinformation. Refinement of AI tools is needed for reliable quality and sentiment assessment on social media.This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. llm_summary: Labiaplasty, a surgical procedure on the female genitalia, has become increasingly popular with over 10,800 procedures performed yearly in the United States, and discussions about this surgery are now spreading rapidly on TikTok where health information often lacks proper medical oversight. Researchers examined 110 of the most popular TikTok videos about labiaplasty by measuring how many likes and comments they received, who created them, and whether the information was accurate and helpful using both human reviewers and artificial intelligence software. The study found that while surgeons and patients created most of the videos, the videos that received the most engagement and popularity actually had lower quality information, suggesting that accurate medical content was being overshadowed by less reliable material. These results highlight a concerning gap where misinformation about surgery spreads more easily on social media than trustworthy content, which could influence people's decisions about whether to have this procedure. Surgeons need to create more engaging and relatable educational content to compete with lower-quality videos, and artificial intelligence tools need improvement before they can reliably assess the accuracy and tone of health information on social media platforms.

title: Cerebral Proliferative Angiopathy: Imaging Spectrum and Diagnostic Insights.
abstract: Cerebral proliferative angiopathy (CPA) is a rare cerebrovascular malformation that differs fundamentally from classic arteriovenous malformations (AVMs). Unlike AVMs, CPA is characterized by a diffuse vascular network intermingled with normal brain parenchyma, absence of a compact nidus or dominant feeders, and transdural supply. We conducted a comprehensive review of 75 published studies comprising 153 patients to summarize the full imaging spectrum. CPA most commonly presents in adolescence or young adulthood, with a slight female predominance, and generally involves the supratentorial brain, spanning multiple lobes. On CT and MRI, CPA typically demonstrates dispersed cortical flow voids and serpiginous enhancing vascular channels, with secondary findings like ischemia, cortical atrophy, calcifications, hemorrhage, and variable venous drainage patterns. Perfusion and metabolic imaging consistently reveal widespread hypoperfusion and impaired cerebrovascular reserve, supporting its ischemia-driven pathogenesis. DSA shows an absence of dominant feeders, proximal arterial stenoses, frequent transdural collaterals, rarely flow-related aneurysms, and modest venous enlargement. It can occasionally have a progressive nature, with risks of delayed infarction, hemorrhage, and neurologic deficits. Multimodal imaging is essential for distinguishing this under-recognized yet clinically important entity from AVMs and other mimics, because management differs substantially. A standardized reporting framework may help refine diagnostic criteria and improve clinical outcomes.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

llm_summary: Cerebral proliferative angiopathy is a rare and often misunderstood condition where abnormal blood vessels grow throughout the brain in a scattered pattern, unlike the more common arteriovenous malformations that form compact clumps of tangled vessels. Researchers reviewed seventy-five published studies covering one hundred fifty-three patients to understand how this condition appears on medical imaging scans like CT and MRI and to help doctors recognize it more easily. The condition typically shows up as dispersed abnormal blood vessels mixed in with normal brain tissue, often causing reduced blood flow to the brain, and can lead to serious complications like stroke or bleeding. Because cerebral proliferative angiopathy requires different treatment approaches than other similar-looking vascular conditions, doctors need better ways to identify it accurately using multiple imaging techniques and a standardized checklist of diagnostic features. The researchers suggest that developing clearer diagnostic guidelines and reporting standards could help doctors catch this condition earlier and improve outcomes for patients who suffer from this rare but serious brain disorder.

title: National Mentorship Network for Support of Minoritized General Surgery Residents in the US.
abstract: More than one-third of surgery residents-most of whom identified as non-White-report a lack of meaningful mentorship at their home institution. The purpose of this study was to (1) develop a program to assist residents who lack mentorship at their home institutions, (2) evaluate a national mentorship network 1-year postimplementation, and (3) identify areas for improvement.The Association for Academic Surgery (AAS) and the Surgical Education Culture Optimization based on National comparative Data (SECOND) trial partnered to create a national mentorship network to address the lack of local mentorship. A total of 123 resident mentees were recruited through SECOND trial intervention programs, and 85 mentors were recruited and trained through AAS. Residents were matched with faculty mentors outside their institutions based on desired mentor qualities. After 1 year, participants were surveyed.Residents were 73.2% female, 61.4% non-White or Hispanic, and 13.6% lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, or queer; 95.1% identified with at least 1 minoritized identity. One-year evaluations were completed by 44 residents (35.8%) and 38 faculty (44.7%). Of 44, 30 (68.2%) residents were enrolled due to unmet mentorship needs at their home institution, with 53.3% (16 of 30) wanting an identity-concordant mentor. Of 44, 34 (77.3%) resident respondents had met with their mentors. Mental health was addressed by 44.1% (15 of 34) of pairs; 64.7% of residents rated their mentors as a good fit, and 44.1% reported their mentors had provided them with opportunities they would not have otherwise had. Of faculty, 68.4% agreed, "Participation in this program has been meaningful to me." Suggestions for improvement included participation reminders (39.7%) and discussion guides (25.3%).A national mentorship network may help compensate for the lack of local identity-concordant mentorship.Copyright © 2026 by the American College of Surgeons.
