llm_summary: Ovarian cancer patients often benefit from drugs called PARP inhibitors, which work by exploiting a weakness in cancer cells that lack proper DNA repair abilities, but many patients develop resistance to these treatments over time. Researchers examined whether blocking a protein called PAK1 could make PARP inhibitors more effective by studying cancer cells in the laboratory and testing the approach in animal models and patient-derived samples. The team found that reducing PAK1 levels or using a drug called IPA-3 to inhibit it made cancer cells more sensitive to the PARP inhibitor olaparib, and combining both treatments caused more DNA damage and cell death than either treatment alone. These results suggest that adding a PAK1 inhibitor to standard PARP inhibitor therapy could help overcome drug resistance and improve treatment outcomes for ovarian cancer patients. Further clinical trials in human patients will be needed to confirm whether this combination approach is safe and effective enough to use in real-world medical practice.

title: Watch and Wait in practice: Adherence to surveillance after nonoperative management for rectal cancer.
abstract: Surveillance after neoadjuvant therapy and complete clinical response, known as "Watch and Wait," is an accepted treatment approach for locally advanced rectal cancer. Watch and Wait replaces surgical resection with rigorous surveillance for early identification of regrowth. However, there are scant data on adherence to surveillance. This study aimed to assess the adherence to Watch and Wait and the receipt of optimal surveillance.A multicenter cohort of patients diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma from 2021to 2022 was retrospectively reviewed. Patients who underwent Watch and Wait after neoadjuvant therapy and complete clinical response were included. The primary endpoint was receipt of National Comprehensive Cancer Network guideline-based surveillance. Patients were stratified by receipt of optimal surveillance, defined as completion of all required imaging and endoscopic surveillance elements during their analyzed time within Watch and Wait. Variables were compared with Fisher exact or Mann-Whitney U tests. The Kaplan-Meier method was used for time-to-event analysis.Fifty-three patients underwent Watch and Wait. Of these, 33 (62%) had optimal surveillance, with a median follow-up of 17 months. Those receiving optimal surveillance were younger (median age 54 vs 63 years, P = .04), and there were no differences by socioeconomic factors. On Kaplan-Meier analysis, the most common missed events leading to suboptimal surveillance were an endoscopic or imaging examination before 9 months and a full colonoscopy before 18 months.Of patients who underwent Watch and Wait, 62% received optimal surveillance. Patients were at greatest risk for missing the first required endoscopic or imaging surveillance and the first full colonoscopy. Patients undergoing nonoperative management are most likely to miss surveillance in the critical first year, during which regrowth occurs.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how well patients followed surveillance guidelines after choosing to skip surgery for rectal cancer, a treatment approach called Watch and Wait that relies on close monitoring instead of an operation to catch any cancer regrowth early. The study looked back at records from fifty-three patients diagnosed between 2021 and 2022 who received this nonoperative management approach after chemotherapy and radiation showed their cancer had completely disappeared. Only thirty-three patients, or about sixty-two percent, received all the recommended imaging scans and endoscopic examinations, which are procedures that allow doctors to look inside the body, with younger patients more likely to complete their full surveillance plan. The patients most commonly missed important checkups during the critical first year after treatment, particularly the first required imaging or endoscopic exam and the first full colonoscopy, which is when cancer regrowth is most likely to occur. These findings suggest that healthcare providers need to improve how they help patients stay on track with their monitoring schedules to ensure that any cancer returning is caught as early as possible.

title: Regional anesthesia in the emergency department: A review of key pharmacotherapeutic considerations.
abstract: Opioid-associated risks and the opioid epidemic have accelerated interest in multimodal analgesia in the emergency department (ED). Regional anesthesia offers a targeted approach with reduced risk of systemic adverse effects and is increasingly used under ultrasound guidance.This concise, evidence-based review explores pharmacological principles of local anesthetics describing key aspects of structure-activity relationship, providing context for agent selection. Additional considerations include dosing strategy, adjunctive medications, potential risks, toxicity mitigation, and operationalization of regional anesthesia in the ED.Regional anesthesia is used with increased frequency in the ED. Pharmacologic properties of commonly used local anesthetics and adjunctive agents determine their advantages and limitations as well as place in therapy. There are a variety of anesthetic agents, including amides (e.g., lidocaine, bupivacaine, ropivacaine, levobupivacaine) and esters (e.g., articaine, chloroprocaine) with differences in onset, duration, and toxicity profiles that influence agent selection in ED patient populations. Adjuncts such as epinephrine, dexamethasone, and alpha-2 agonists may extend nerve block duration or improve analgesia but introduce safety and operational considerations. Recognition of local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST) remains central to safe practice, underscoring the importance of weight-based dosing, ultrasound guidance, monitoring, and immediate access to lipid emulsion therapy. Systems-based approaches such as order sets, pharmacist involvement, and structured training support consistent and safe application of regional anesthesia in the ED setting.Safe integration of regional anesthesia in the ED requires pharmacologic literacy, standardized systems, and multidisciplinary support to optimize analgesia while minimizing risk.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: The overuse of opioid painkillers has led emergency doctors to look for safer pain relief methods, and regional anesthesia, which is numbing medication injected near nerves to block pain in specific body areas, has become increasingly popular as an alternative. This review examines the different types of numbing medications used in emergency departments, explaining how their chemical structures affect how quickly they work, how long they last, and what side effects they might cause. The researchers found that emergency doctors can choose from two main categories of numbing drugs called amides and esters, each with different strengths and weaknesses, and they can add other medications like epinephrine or steroids to make the numbing last longer or work better. A critical safety concern is that these numbing medications can sometimes enter the bloodstream and cause serious poisoning called local anesthetic systemic toxicity, which doctors can prevent by using the correct dose based on patient weight, using ultrasound to guide the injection, and having a special fat-based treatment available immediately if needed. To safely use regional anesthesia in emergency departments, hospitals need clear written protocols, involvement from pharmacists and other team members, and regular training so that doctors can.

title: Integration of Ustekinumab Biosimilars into Inflammatory Bowel Disease Care: Evidence, Implementation, and Patient-Centered Considerations.
abstract: The recent introduction of ustekinumab biosimilars represents a pivotal advancement in the management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), offering opportunities to enhance access to advanced therapy and reduce healthcare costs without compromising treatment efficacy. IBD, encompassing Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, imposes a substantial economic burden on patients and the health care system, with biologics driving most direct costs. Biosimilars have successfully reduced expenditures across various therapeutic classes, notably anti-tumor necrosis factor agents, and now extend these benefits to interleukin-12/23 inhibitors. This review summarizes the regulatory, clinical, and practical considerations for integrating ustekinumab biosimilars into IBD care in the United States. Food and Drug Administration approval is based on rigorous totality-of-evidence evaluations, leveraging pharmacokinetic, immunogenicity, and efficacy studies in sensitive populations such as moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, with regulatory extrapolation to IBD indications. Clinical trials of eight ustekinumab biosimilars have consistently demonstrated therapeutic equivalence, including maintenance of efficacy and safety following single or multiple switches from the reference product. Implementation in IBD practice requires careful navigation of operational and patient-centered challenges. Key considerations include coordination of intravenous induction and subcutaneous maintenance therapy across medical and pharmacy benefits, product-specific storage and device differences, and proactive mitigation of the nocebo effect through shared decision making and structured patient education. Ustekinumab biosimilars are poised to expand therapeutic accessibility and support healthcare cost containment. Successful adoption will depend on clinician familiarity, streamlined operational workflows, and patient-centered strategies to maintain confidence, minimize treatment disruption, and optimize long-term outcomes in IBD management.© 2026. llm_summary: Inflammatory bowel disease, which includes conditions like Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, costs patients and the healthcare system a lot of money, especially because the most effective treatments are expensive biologic drugs that are made from living cells. Ustekinumab biosimilars, which are more affordable copies of an existing expensive medication that work the same way in the body, have recently been approved and offer a chance to make advanced treatment more available while saving money without losing effectiveness. Researchers reviewed the evidence showing that eight different ustekinumab biosimilars have been tested and proven to work just as well as the original drug, even when patients switched from the original to the copy, with no safety concerns. To successfully use these cheaper versions in real medical practice, doctors and pharmacies need to work together smoothly, patients need clear education about why the switch is safe, and healthcare systems need to handle the different ways these drugs are stored and given to patients. Making these biosimilar medications a normal part of treating inflammatory bowel disease will require doctors to understand them better, hospitals to set up better systems for using them, and patients to feel confident that switching to a cheaper version won't harm their treatment results.

llm_summary: Background:  Pulmonary embolism, which occurs when a blood clot travels to the lungs and blocks blood flow, is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition that requires immediate treatment with blood-thinning medications. Bivalirudin is a type of anticoagulant drug that works by preventing blood clots from forming, and this article examines whether it could be a useful alternative treatment option for patients experiencing pulmonary embolism.

title: Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Aseptic Failure After Staged Exchange for Periprosthetic Joint Infection: High Rates of Reoperation and Reinfection.
abstract: Data are limited regarding the outcomes of revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for aseptic failure following the successful eradication of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) with two-stage exchange. The purpose of this study was to evaluate 5-year survivorship of revision TKA for aseptic failure in patients who have a history of two-stage exchange for PJI.We retrospectively reviewed 94 aseptic revision TKAs performed between 2000 and 2020 at a single institution in patients who had previously completed two-stage exchange for PJI in the same knee. The mean age was 65 years, the mean body mass index was 35, and 44% were women. The median number of surgeries before index aseptic revision TKA was four. There were no patients who met Musculoskeletal Infection Society criteria for PJI or had positive cultures at the time of aseptic revision. The most common indications for aseptic TKA revision included aseptic loosening (57%), instability (16%), and periprosthetic fracture (6%). The mean follow-up was seven years.The 5-year survivorships free of any reoperation and any revision were 57 and 66%, respectively. The 5-year survivorship free of reoperation for PJI was 80%. A total of 50 patients underwent reoperation, and nearly half of these were for PJI. The three most common indications for subsequent aseptic reoperation were extensor mechanism disruption, instability, and loosening. There were eight patients (9%) who ultimately required amputation for recurrent PJI.Revision TKA for aseptic failure following two-stage exchange for PJI is associated with a high reoperation rate (43%) and high reinfection rate (20%) at five years. These data highlight the importance of robust fixation and knee balancing at the time of reimplantation to avoid subsequent surgeries that may lead to reinfection. While most of the index aseptic revision TKAs were for indisputable indications, these results suggest that surgeons should exercise caution when offering surgery for relative indications in this setting.IV (retrospective study).Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers examined what happens when patients need another knee replacement surgery after successfully treating a serious knee infection through a two-stage surgical procedure, which involves removing the infected implant, treating the infection, and then placing a new implant. The study looked back at records from 94 patients who had this type of follow-up surgery between 2000 and 2020, tracking their outcomes over an average of seven years to see how many needed additional operations or experienced problems. The results showed that while most patients initially recovered well, 43 percent needed another operation within five years, and about 20 percent developed a new infection in that same timeframe. These findings suggest that even when surgeons successfully eliminate an infection and place a new knee implant, patients remain at higher risk for future complications compared to people getting their first knee replacement. Doctors should be cautious about recommending this surgery for minor or questionable reasons and should focus on achieving strong implant stability and proper knee balance during the initial replacement surgery to reduce the chances of needing more operations later.

title: Comparative safety of completion thyroidectomy following lobectomy versus total thyroidectomy in differentiated thyroid cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the operative safety of completion thyroidectomy (CT) following lobectomy compared with total thyroidectomy (TT) for differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC).PubMed, Ovid Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Web of Science were searched from their respective inception dates to October 2025 (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251178003).A total of 43,362 patients from twelve studies were included, of whom 6810 (15.7%) underwent CT. CT was associated with lower odds of transient hypocalcemia (OR = 0.46; 95% CI: 0.34 - 0.63; I2 = 68%) compared with TT, while rates of permanent hypocalcemia (OR = 0.78; 95% CI: 0.61 - 1.01; I2 = 16%), transient recurrent laryngeal nerve injury (OR = 0.99; 95% CI: 0.78 - 1.26; I2 = 30%), permanent recurrent laryngeal nerve injury (OR = 1.12; 95% CI: 0.94 - 1.34; I2 = 0%), and hematoma (OR = 1.34; 95% CI: 0.56 - 3.21; I2 = 0%) were similar.Our analysis demonstrated that CT appears to have a similar safety profile when compared with upfront TT in selected DTC patients.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether it is safer to remove half the thyroid gland first and then remove the remaining half later, compared to removing the entire thyroid gland all at once, in patients with differentiated thyroid cancer, which is a type of cancer that grows slowly. The team searched medical databases and reviewed twelve studies involving over 43,000 patients, with about 6,800 of them undergoing the two-stage removal approach. The results showed that patients who had their thyroid removed in two stages experienced fewer cases of temporary low calcium levels in the blood, while other serious complications like permanent low calcium levels and nerve damage occurred at similar rates in both groups. This finding suggests that removing the thyroid in two separate surgeries appears to be just as safe as removing it all at once for patients with this type of cancer. Future research should continue to monitor long-term outcomes and determine which patients benefit most from each surgical approach.

Despite advances in medical understanding and treatment options, this condition remains difficult to diagnose and manage effectively, which is why ongoing research and clinical attention continue to be important.

title: Next-generation sequencing for lymphoid neoplasms: Real-world utility from a clinical assay.
abstract: Although next-generation sequencing (NGS) has become the standard of care in myeloid neoplasms, the utility of lymphoma NGS (LNGS) in the clinical setting has not been well established. The goal of this study was to document the real-world use of LNGS panels and assess their prognostic, predictive, and diagnostic value. A total of 384 cases were retrospectively reviewed in conjunction with pathology reports, including 121, 183, and 80 tested for the limited B-cell lymphoma panel (25 genes), expanded B-cell lymphoma panel (46 genes), or T-cell lymphoma panel (22 genes), respectively. Specimen types included 170 (44.3%) bone marrow, 120 (31.3%) peripheral blood, and 93 (24.2%) formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue. 248/384 (64.6%) cases showed at least one mutation; 245/347 (70.6%) when excluding specimens known to be negative for lymphoma. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL/CLL, 40.6%) and mantle cell lymphoma (MCL, 9.6%) were the most common lymphoma types tested. Mutations with prognostic value were found in 228/384 (59.4%) cases. 125 (32.6%) tests provided predictive value for response or resistance to a specific therapy. 36 tests (9.4%) provided diagnostic value, aiding the pathologist in classifying disease or rendering a more definitive diagnosis. LNGS results are most useful as being prognostic in CLL/SLL and MCL, diagnostic in angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma and hairy cell leukemia, theranostic in lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, and diagnostic and prognostic in follicular lymphoma and T/NK-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia. Although clinical guidelines have not yet widely incorporated LNGS, when carefully designed and selectively ordered by clinicians and pathologists, the majority of tests do offer prognostic and predictive data which can aid in optimization of clinical management. The diagnostic value of LNGS testing is likely to increase with its further use and availability.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a genetic testing method called next-generation sequencing, which reads DNA to find disease-causing mutations, could help doctors better diagnose and treat lymphomas, which are cancers of immune system cells. The team reviewed 384 patient cases where genetic testing was performed on blood, bone marrow, or tissue samples, looking at which mutations were found and how useful that information was for patient care. The results showed that nearly two-thirds of the cases had at least one genetic mutation, and in most cases the mutations provided information about how the disease would progress or which treatments might work best. The genetic testing proved most helpful for certain types of lymphomas, such as chronic lymphocytic leukemia where it predicted disease outcome, and for other types like hairy cell leukemia where it helped confirm the diagnosis. Although medical guidelines have not yet fully adopted this genetic testing for lymphomas, the study suggests that when doctors and pathologists carefully choose which patients should be tested, the results can provide valuable information to guide treatment decisions and improve patient outcomes.

title: Gene expression and immunohistochemical phenotypes of high-grade epithelioid mesothelioma.
abstract: Grading of epithelioid mesothelioma (EM) has recently been reported to be predictive of survival. We investigated whether RNA expression profiles and immunohistochemical (IHC) markers could refine EG grading and potentially identify therapeutic targets. Forty-seven pleural mesothelioma biopsies were studied, including 6 sarcomatoid/desmoplastic mesothelioma (SM), 6 biphasic mesothelioma (BM), and 35 EM. We subclassified EM cases into low-(LG) and high-grade (HG) based on WHO classification. FFPE slides were used for RNA expression and IHC (BAP1, EZH2 and PD-L1) studies. RNA expression was profiled by nCounter PanCancer Pathways Panel (NanoString, 770 genes). In 35 EM, 14 were classified as EM-HG and 21 as EM-LG. RNA expression heat mapping demonstrated that EM-LG predominantly cluster together while EM-HG exhibit more heterogeneity with some cases exhibiting proximity to SM/BM. SM/BM demonstrated a noticeable different IHC profile compared to EM-LG: fewer BAP1 loss (25% vs 86%), higher expression of PD-L1 (mean 30.1%, range 0-80% vs mean 1.3%, 0-10%) and higher EZH2 (mean H score 136.3, 10-250 vs mean 57.1, 5-150). Similarly to EM-LG, EM-HG exhibited low PD-L1 expression with a mean TPS of 1.2%, suggesting limited clinical utility for PD-L1 IHC for EM-LG and EM-HG. A non-statistically significant trend for higher EZH2 expression in EM-HG (mean H score 88.3, 60-140) compared to EM-LG was seen. In conclusion, in addition to supporting histology grading of EM, our findings highlight that EM-HG cases display more heterogeneous expression profiles than EM-LG with some features in between EM-LG and SM/BM. Further data is needed to explore the potential clinical utility EZH2 IHC in the clinical management of pleural mesothelioma.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined tissue samples from patients with mesothelioma, a serious cancer caused by asbestos exposure, to understand how different types of this disease behave and respond to treatment. The study looked at forty-seven patient samples and analyzed the genes expressed in the cancer cells along with specific protein markers that might help doctors better classify and treat the disease. The researchers found that high-grade epithelioid mesothelioma, which is the most common type, showed much more variety in its genetic patterns compared to low-grade forms, and some cases even resembled other rarer types of mesothelioma. The study showed that a protein called PD-L1, which doctors thought might help identify patients who could benefit from certain immunotherapy treatments, was present at very low levels in most epithelioid mesothelioma cases, limiting its usefulness as a treatment guide. The findings suggest that doctors need more research to understand whether another protein called EZH2 could be helpful in managing mesothelioma patients, and that high-grade cases may need different treatment approaches than previously thought.

title: Atrial Functional Mitral Regurgitation: Contemporary Mechanisms, Imaging, and Perioperative Implications for Cardiothoracic Anesthesiologists and Intensivists.
abstract: Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Traditionally, secondary MR has been understood primarily as a ventricular disorder caused by structural and functional abnormalities of the left ventricle. However, atrial functional mitral regurgitation (AFMR) is increasingly recognized as a distinct pathophysiological entity characterized by left atrial and mitral annular dilatation despite relatively preserved left ventricular geometry and systolic function. AFMR is commonly encountered in older patients, particularly those with chronic atrial fibrillation, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, or both, and presents unique perioperative diagnostic and management challenges. Contemporary data further suggest that AFMR is not a single rigid phenotype, but rather a spectrum of atrial and annular remodeling with variable degrees of leaflet tethering and, in some patients, early ventricular overlap. Recent work has also shown marked variability among published AFMR definitions, with important consequences for prevalence, morphology, and prognosis. For the cardiothoracic anesthesiologist and intensivist, differentiating AFMR from classical ventriculogenic functional MR is essential because this distinction influences hemodynamic goals, volume management, and procedural planning. This review summarizes the mechanisms underlying AFMR, emphasizes the pivotal role of multimodality imaging in diagnosis, reviews current and emerging interventional strategies, and outlines practical perioperative considerations.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Secondary mitral regurgitation, a condition where the heart valve between the upper and lower left chambers leaks blood backward, causes serious health problems and deaths in many patients. Researchers reviewed current understanding of atrial functional mitral regurgitation, a specific type of this valve problem that occurs when the upper heart chamber and the valve ring stretch and enlarge even though the lower chamber still pumps normally. The review found that this condition is increasingly common in older patients with irregular heartbeats or heart failure, and it represents a spectrum of different patterns of heart remodeling rather than a single fixed disease. For doctors managing patients during heart surgery and in intensive care units, recognizing this type of valve problem is crucial because it requires different treatment approaches and fluid management strategies compared to other forms of mitral regurgitation. The authors emphasize that using multiple imaging techniques to diagnose this condition is essential, and they highlight that clearer definitions and more research are needed to better understand how to treat this growing problem in cardiac patients.

title: Prevalence of concomitant endometriosis in patients undergoing laparoscopic hysterectomy with suspected adenomyosis: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: To determine the prevalence of pathology-proven endometriosis in patients with suspected adenomyosis undergoing total laparoscopic hysterectomy (LH).This was a single-site retrospective cohort study performed at an academic medical center. 182 premenopausal patients with suspected adenomyosis underwent laparoscopic hysterectomy between 10/01/2015-10/31/2022 with surgeons with additional specialized training in surgical management of endometriosis. Close peritoneal inspection was performed at time of LH and any visible lesions were excised to capture all cases of endometriosis. Those with and without pathology-proven endometriosis were compared. An additional subanalysis was then performed excluding patients with any pre-operative imaging findings of endometriosis.Concomitant endometriosis was identified in 73.6% of patients with suspected adenomyosis (134/182). Of the patients with pathology-confirmed adenomyosis (93/182), 71.0% had concomitant endometriosis (66/93). Patients with endometriosis were more likely to have severe dysmenorrhea as a presenting symptom (74.6%) compared to patients without endometriosis (58.3%) (p = 0.036). These results remained significant within the subanalysis.Endometriosis was found in 73.6% of patients with suspected adenomyosis, which is higher than previously reported. This suggests a role for careful laparoscopic examination of the pelvis at time of hysterectomy in this population in order to account for all pathology. Further confirmation with a larger sample size and pain outcomes would assist with clinical decision-making and counseling.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined patients who were having their uterus removed through minimally invasive surgery because they were suspected to have adenomyosis, a condition where tissue similar to the uterine lining grows into the uterine muscle wall. In this study, doctors carefully inspected the pelvic area during surgery and removed any visible abnormal tissue, then tested all removed tissue to confirm what conditions were actually present. The researchers found that nearly three out of four patients with suspected adenomyosis also had endometriosis, which is a separate condition where tissue similar to the uterine lining grows outside the uterus in the pelvic area. Patients who had both conditions were more likely to experience severe menstrual pain compared to those who only had adenomyosis. The study suggests that careful examination of the pelvic area during surgery is important to find all disease present, though larger studies with more patients are needed to confirm these findings and understand how treatment affects pain relief.

title: Treatment strategies in giant cell arteritis and polymyalgia rheumatica: beyond glucocorticoids.
abstract: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) and polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) are closely related chronic inflammatory conditions. Glucocorticoids remain the cornerstone of treatment for both conditions, as they rapidly control inflammation and also reduce the risk of ischaemic complications in GCA. However, glucocorticoid therapy is often prolonged and associated with substantial treatment-related morbidity. In addition, many patients experience relapses during glucocorticoid maintenance therapy and can accrue vascular damage. Advances in understanding the immunopathology of GCA and PMR have led to the development of targeted therapies, particularly agents inhibiting the IL-6 pathway and, more recently, Janus kinase (JAK) signalling. IL-6 receptor inhibitors reduce the risk of disease relapse and allow for reduction in glucocorticoid use in both GCA and PMR, and JAK inhibition enables glucocorticoid sparing and lowers the risk of relapse in GCA. Optimal management of GCA and PMR requires close monitoring, careful assessment of disease activity and treatment-related toxicity, as well as individualized therapeutic strategies. Ongoing research continues to refine treatment algorithms and could help to define therapeutic targets across GCA and PMR. Emerging therapeutic options and evolving treatment algorithms reflect the dynamic and patient-centred nature of advancements in GCA and PMR management.© 2026. Springer Nature Limited.

llm_summary: Giant cell arteritis and polymyalgia rheumatica are two related long-term inflammatory diseases that currently rely heavily on glucocorticoids, which are steroid medications that reduce inflammation but can cause serious side effects when used for extended periods. Researchers reviewed how new targeted treatments, particularly drugs that block the IL-6 pathway (a chemical messenger involved in inflammation) and JAK inhibitors (medications that stop certain immune signals), are changing the way doctors manage these conditions. These newer medications help reduce disease flare-ups and allow patients to take lower doses of glucocorticoids, which means fewer harmful side effects from long-term steroid use. The best treatment approach for each patient requires careful monitoring of disease activity and side effects, with doctors tailoring therapy to individual needs rather than using a one-size-fits-all strategy. Ongoing research is continuing to improve treatment plans and identify which patients benefit most from these emerging therapies, reflecting a shift toward more personalized and patient-centered care for these inflammatory diseases.

llm_summary: Background:  Endotracheal intubation, which is the process of placing a breathing tube directly into the windpipe to help patients breathe, is a common emergency procedure that requires careful preparation to ensure the patient has enough oxygen in their blood before the procedure begins. Preoxygenation, the practice of giving patients extra oxygen before intubation, is traditionally done with a face mask, but this study examines whether noninvasive ventilation, which is a gentler form of breathing support that does not require a tube in the windpipe, might be a better way to prepare emergency patients for this critical procedure.

title: Clinical safety and regenerative potential of a purified exosome product in treating skin graft donor sites: A phase 1b trial.
abstract: The objective of this study was to determine the safety of the first clinically used purified exosome product (PEP) for open wounds. This was a phase 1b, prospective, open-label, controlled, randomized clinical trial of PEP in subjects with at least two equal sized split-thickness skin graft (STSG) donor site wounds with one donor site treated with standard of care (SOC) and the other treated with PEP. Patients were divided into low-dose PEP-only group and high-dose PEP-only group. Safety evaluations included occurrence of adverse events, laboratory values, vital signs, and physical examination findings. Wound healing was scored using Vancouver scar scale (VSS) and photographic wound assessment tool (PWAT). Seven subjects were included, with a mean age of 49.3 years. There were no adverse events related to the treatments. We observed comparable wound healing time between the treatments, with PEP-treated sites reaching 100% re-epithelialization at a median of 18.5 days (range, 6-29 days) and 19.25 days (range, 8-314 days) for SOC sites, without a significant difference. This study demonstrated that a single application of PEP at a dose as high as 20% was safe in human participants. Future large trials will be needed to validate PEP efficacy in re-epithelialization and determine its clinical and statistical significance.Copyright © 2026 British Association of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a new purified exosome product, which is a treatment made from tiny particles released by cells, could safely help heal wounds created when doctors remove skin for grafting procedures. The study involved seven patients who each had two matching wound sites, with one treated using standard care and the other treated with the new exosome product at either a low or high dose. The results showed that the new treatment was safe with no harmful side effects, and both the exosome-treated wounds and standard care wounds healed at similar speeds, reaching complete skin regrowth in about eighteen to nineteen days on average. Although this early trial demonstrated that the exosome product appears safe for human use, the researchers found no clear advantage over standard treatment in terms of healing speed or scar appearance. Larger and longer studies will be needed in the future to determine whether this new treatment actually works better than current methods and to understand its true benefits for patients with skin graft wounds.

title: Perioperative and oncologic outcomes of vascular resection after neoadjuvant therapy in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) with major vascular involvement is a technically challenging and biologically aggressive clinical scenario. Although vascular resection (VR) can be performed at experienced centers, the oncologic value of this approach depends on appropriate patient selection. We evaluated whether neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) may improve selection and outcomes among patients undergoing hepatectomy with concomitant VR.A single-institution cohort study of 349 patients who underwent resection for histologically confirmed iCCA between 2000 and 2024 was performed. Patients were stratified by VR status and, within the VR cohort, by receipt of NAT. Overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox regression, including an interaction term between NAT and VR.Twenty-eight patients (8.0%) underwent major VR, including 11 who received NAT. Compared with patients without VR, those undergoing VR had higher-risk disease and higher 90-day mortality, but similar long-term survival. Within the VR cohort, NAT-treated patients had more adverse baseline clinicopathologic features, yet recurrence occurred less frequently than after upfront VR (27% vs. 82%; p = 0.006). In adjusted analyses restricted to the VR cohort, NAT was associated with improved RFS (HR 0.21; p = 0.041). In the full cohort, the NAT×VR interaction was borderline significant (HR 0.27; p = 0.050), suggesting a potential concentration of the NAT-associated RFS benefit among patients requiring VR.In patients with iCCA requiring major vascular resection, NAT may improve biologic selection and may be associated with more favorable recurrence-free outcomes despite adverse baseline disease features. Given the small NAT + VR subgroup, these results should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and warrant validation in larger prospective multicenter cohorts.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd, BASO ~ The Association for Cancer Surgery, and the European Society of Surgical Oncology. llm_summary: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, a type of liver cancer that grows in the bile ducts inside the liver, is especially difficult to treat when it involves major blood vessels, and doctors need better ways to decide which patients should have surgery to remove these vessels. Researchers studied 349 patients who had surgery for this cancer between 2000 and 2024, comparing those who had their blood vessels removed during surgery with those who did not, and looking at whether giving chemotherapy before surgery helped improve outcomes. They found that 28 patients had major blood vessel removal, and among those patients, 11 received chemotherapy beforehand, which helped reduce how often the cancer came back after surgery even though these patients started with more serious disease. Patients who received chemotherapy before surgery had much lower rates of cancer returning compared to those who went straight to surgery, with only 27 percent experiencing recurrence versus 82 percent in the surgery-only group. Because the group of patients who received chemotherapy before blood vessel removal surgery was small, the researchers emphasize that these results are preliminary and need to be confirmed with larger studies involving multiple hospitals before doctors can confidently recommend this approach for all patients.

title: Competency-Based Medical Education in Ophthalmology: Perspectives of Residency Program Directors.
abstract: To assess ophthalmology program directors' (PDs) knowledge, attitude, and perceptions regarding the adoption of Competency-Based Medical Education (CBME) and Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs) in residency training.Cross-sectional study.An anonymous online survey was distributed across the Association of University Professors of Ophthalmology (AUPO) PDs directory over a two-month period. The survey assessed familiarity with CBME and EPAs, perceived barriers to implementation, and opinions on essential competencies for ophthalmology training.Ophthalmology Residency PDs across the U.S.55 complete responses were received. While 65.5% of PDs reported being familiar with CBME, only 43.6% felt confident explaining EPAs. Currently, only 22% of residency programs utilize EPA-based assessment. 60% of PDs agreed that better assessment tools are needed. 43.6% reported having extended training for at least one resident, and 60% indicated that some residents were competent to graduate early. Cataract surgery and Nd:YAG capsulotomy were ranked as the most essential surgical competencies, while strabismus surgery was ranked the lowest.PDs demonstrated overall support for integrating CBME and adopting EPA-based guidelines in ophthalmology residency training. These findings highlight the need for structured assessment frameworks and suggest that further research is needed to assess the impact of these initiatives on patient outcomes and resident performance.Copyright © 2026 Association of Program Directors in Surgery. llm_summary: Researchers examined what ophthalmology residency program directors, who oversee training for eye doctors, know and think about competency-based medical education, which is a training approach focused on ensuring doctors master specific skills rather than just completing a set amount of time. The study used an anonymous online survey sent to 55 program directors across the United States to ask about their familiarity with competency-based education and entrustable professional activities, which are specific tasks that doctors should be able to perform independently. While most program directors were familiar with competency-based education, fewer than half felt confident explaining entrustable professional activities, and only about one in five programs currently used this assessment method. The directors agreed that better tools are needed to measure whether residents have learned the necessary skills, and they identified cataract surgery as the most important surgical skill residents should master. These findings suggest that while program directors support moving toward competency-based training in eye surgery residency programs, more research and structured guidelines are needed to help programs successfully make this change.

Private kidney paired donation programs, which are run by for-profit companies rather than hospitals or non-profit organizations, have grown in recent years but raise concerns about how donors are guided through the process and whether these programs operate with sufficient oversight and public accountability.

title: Emerging Topics in Neurogenomics: Summary From Inaugural Child Neurology Society Genetics Summit.
abstract: The practice of child neurology has undergone a profound transformation over the past 2 decades, driven by advances in genetic testing that enable precise diagnosis, and the development of targeted therapies. Despite these advances, preparing and educating the child neurology workforce to confidently integrate neurogenomics into clinical care remains a significant challenge. To address this gap, our group conducted needs assessment surveys and developed the Child Neurology Society Genetics Curriculum, culminating this year in the inaugural Genetics Summit at the Child Neurology Society Annual Meeting. The summit was designed and led by a team of dual-trained neurogeneticists, genetic counselors, and medical educators, emphasizing practical, clinically relevant learning. Foundational sessions focused on principles of genetic testing and interpretation, followed by case-based modules illustrating real-world application in child neurology practice. The third component of the summit centered on emerging themes in neurogenomics, delivered through lobby-style talks that fostered continuous, bidirectional engagement with participants. Topics included effective collaboration with genetic counselors, equity and access to genetic testing, the role of rapid genomic sequencing in critically ill children, and considerations for clinical trial readiness. This paper synthesizes existing literature on these emerging domains alongside survey data and live audience participation from the summit, highlighting key educational gaps, evolving practice needs, and strategies to support scalable, interactive neurogenomics education for the child neurology community.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Child neurology has changed dramatically over the past twenty years because doctors can now use genetic testing to identify the exact cause of brain and nervous system disorders in children and can offer targeted treatments based on these findings. To help child neurologists feel confident using these genetic advances in their daily work, a group of medical experts created an educational program called the Child Neurology Society Genetics Curriculum and held a summit meeting where doctors could learn practical skills. The summit included three main parts: foundational lessons on how genetic tests work and what the results mean, real-world case examples showing how to use this knowledge with actual patients, and discussions about emerging topics like working with genetic counselors, making sure all children have fair access to genetic testing, using fast genetic sequencing for very sick children, and preparing patients for clinical trials. The educational program highlighted important gaps in what child neurologists currently know and identified new ways the field is evolving, such as the growing importance of genetic counselors as team members and the need to ensure that genetic testing is available to all children regardless of their background or resources. The researchers recommend continuing to develop interactive, practical education programs that help the entire child neurology community confidently use genetic information to diagnose and treat children.

This consensus statement from the International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation brings together leading experts to establish clear definitions, identify causes, and recommend best practices for diagnosing and treating this serious complication that can occur in the weeks and months following transplant surgery.

title: Impact of modern central nervous system radiation on multiple sclerosis relapse and progression.
abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) radiation is associated with primary demyelination and neurotoxicity in patients with existing demyelinating disorders. We examined the safety of modern ionizing-radiation techniques in multiple-sclerosis (MS) patients.Patients with MS undergoing CNS radiation for any reason between January 2005, and August 2024 were identified by chart review. Inclusion criteria were: 1) confirmed diagnosis of MS; 2) Receiving therapeutic radiation with a dose of greater than 5 Gray (Gy) to brain or spinal cord parenchyma; 3) Clinical neurology and brain MRI follow-up available following radiation.Thirty-three patients were included. Median age at radiation was 60 years (54--68 IQR) and median follow-up, 20 months (range 3-99). Radiation focused on the CNS in 15/33 (45%), 5 (15%) targeted locations adjacent to the CNS parenchyma (meningioma 4, trigeminal neuralgia 1), and 13 (39%), outside the CNS with > 5 Gy delivered to the CNS. Clinical MS course at radiation was relapsing remitting (19/33), secondary progressive (11/33), and primary progressive (3/33). Thirteen patients (39%) were on MS disease-modifying therapy. No clinical relapse or new-onset MS progression followed radiation. New T2 or gadolinium-enhancing lesions on T1 MRI occurred in 7/33. Radiation-field data were analysed with reference to location of 10 new demyelinating lesions in 7 patients. Most lesions lay outside the irradiated area (6/10). No patients with new lesions were on high-efficacy medications. Seven patients experienced increased expanded disability status scale (EDSS) pre-radiation to last follow-up by ≥ 1 point (median 1.5, range 1-7). One patient had known progressive disease while 5 patients' increased disability was thought secondary to their radiation indication (3 glioblastoma and 2 meningioma).Modern-day ionizing radiation to the CNS in patients with multiple sclerosis was not associated with clinical worsening but can potentially be associated with an increased risk of asymptomatic inflammatory MS disease activity.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether modern radiation therapy used to treat brain and spinal cord conditions could worsen multiple sclerosis, a disease where the immune system damages nerve tissue. The study reviewed thirty-three multiple sclerosis patients who received radiation therapy to the brain or spinal cord between 2005 and 2024, tracking their health for an average of twenty months afterward. The results showed that none of the patients experienced a clinical relapse or worsening of their multiple sclerosis symptoms after radiation, though seven patients did develop new inflammatory spots on brain scans that did not cause noticeable symptoms. While modern radiation techniques appear safe for multiple sclerosis patients in terms of preventing disease flare-ups, the findings suggest that radiation may still trigger some asymptomatic inflammatory activity, meaning inflammation without obvious symptoms. These results are encouraging for patients who need radiation therapy for other brain or spinal cord conditions, but doctors should continue monitoring these patients carefully with regular brain imaging to catch any changes early.

title: Advanced diffusion MRI tract signatures in Alzheimer's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and the FTD/PPA spectrum.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and primary progressive aphasia (PPA) are heterogeneous neurodegenerative syndromes with overlapping clinical features and substantial societal burden. Their phenotypic diversity, including atypical AD variants and multiple PPA subtypes, poses major challenges for early diagnosis and disease monitoring. Sensitive, non-invasive imaging biomarkers remain limited. Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) has evolved beyond conventional diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) to include multi-shell models such as neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI), free-water imaging (FWI), and fixel-based analysis (FBA), which offer increased microstructural specificity by probing neurite organization, extracellular water content, and fiber-specific degeneration. In this review of 54 dMRI studies spanning AD, DLB, FTD, and PPA spectrums, we identify both convergent microstructural patterns shared across techniques and disease-specific signatures revealed by advanced models. Canonical DTI findings demonstrate consistent syndrome-related alterations, including fornix and cingulum involvement in AD, widespread diffusivity increases in DLB, uncinate fasciculus degeneration in FTD, and arcuate fasciculus disruption in PPA. Advanced dMRI methods extend these observations by revealing disease-specific neurite and free-water alterations, associations with molecular imaging markers, and improved sensitivity to clinical severity, longitudinal cognitive decline, and microstructural progression. Across syndromes and subtypes, NODDI- and FBA-based metrics consistently outperform conventional DTI. Together, this review provides a comprehensive framework for interpreting advanced dMRI markers across the AD, DLB, and the FTD-PPA spectrum, and highlights their potential for refining disease characterization and tracking neurodegenerative progression.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: Alzheimer's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, frontotemporal dementia, and primary progressive aphasia are brain diseases that cause memory loss and thinking problems, but they are difficult to tell apart early on because they share similar symptoms. Researchers reviewed fifty-four studies that used advanced brain imaging scans called diffusion magnetic resonance imaging, which can detect tiny changes in how brain nerve fibers are organized and how water moves through brain tissue. The studies showed that each disease type damages specific brain pathways in recognizable patterns, such as damage to particular nerve bundles in Alzheimer's disease and different bundles in other dementia types. The newer, more detailed imaging methods were better at spotting these disease-specific changes and tracking how the diseases got worse over time compared to older, simpler imaging techniques. These advanced imaging tools could help doctors diagnose these diseases earlier and more accurately, and they could help researchers track whether new treatments are working.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Control-IQ+ Technology in Insulin-Treated Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in the United States.
abstract: Automated insulin delivery (AID) has been established as an effective therapy for individuals with type 1 diabetes. This analysis evaluates the clinical and economic outcomes of AID compared with multiple daily injections plus continuous glucose monitoring (MDI/CGM) in adults with type 2 diabetes.The IQVIA CORE Diabetes Model v10.0 was employed to simulate the impact of using the t:slim X2 insulin pump with Control-IQ+ technology (Control-IQ+) versus MDI/CGM over a 50-year period using data from the 2IQP randomized controlled trial (NCT05785832). Trial data informed cohort demographics, intervention effects and resource utilization while literature sources provided health state utilities and costs. Scenario analyses examined the effect of Control-IQ+ on reducing HbA1c based on alternative HbA1c progression estimates from the Swedish National Diabetes Registry and alternative resource use and treatment effects from real-world evidence.The base case analysis indicated that direct medical costs per individual for type 2 diabetes management with Control-IQ+ were $239 935 compared to $209 792 with MDI/CGM use. Control-IQ+ resulted in 0.51 additional quality-adjusted life years (QALYs: 10.36 vs. 9.85 for MDI/CGM), yielding an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of $59 417 per QALY, 95% CI: ($55 836, $62 998). In probabilistic sensitivity analyses, 89% of simulations produced ICERs below $100 000/QALY. ICERs across all scenarios remained below $100 000 per QALY.Control-IQ+ is associated with increased life expectancy, higher QALYs and reduced complication rates. These findings suggest that Control-IQ+ is cost-effective relative to MDI/CGM for managing patients with type 2 diabetes in the United States.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined whether an automated insulin pump with Control-IQ+ technology, which automatically adjusts insulin delivery based on blood sugar readings, could be a cost-effective treatment option for adults with type 2 diabetes compared to traditional multiple daily injections combined with continuous glucose monitoring. The study used computer modeling to simulate outcomes over fifty years, drawing on data from a randomized controlled trial that tested the pump technology against the standard injection method, and included information about costs and quality of life from medical literature. The results showed that while the automated pump cost about thirty thousand dollars more per person over the fifty-year period, it provided patients with an additional half year of healthy life and reduced serious diabetes complications. The cost of approximately fifty-nine thousand dollars per additional year of healthy life gained was considered cost-effective by healthcare standards, with eighty-nine percent of computer simulations showing the pump remained affordable even when assumptions were changed. These findings suggest that automated insulin pumps with Control-IQ+ technology could be a worthwhile investment for managing type 2 diabetes in the United States, though patients and healthcare providers should discuss whether the benefits justify the additional costs for individual situations.

The MBSAQIP database is a large collection of information from hospitals across the United States that tracks outcomes and trends in bariatric surgery procedures, allowing doctors and researchers to study patterns in how often patients need these follow-up operations and what factors influence their success.

title: Emergency Department-Initiated Hospice and Palliative Care Consultation Among Older Adults: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) play a critical role in caring for the aging population, particularly those nearing the end of life. Despite advances in integrating palliative care resources in the ED, targeted research on the impact of hospice and palliative care (HPC) consultations for older adults in ED settings remains limited. This systematic review protocol assesses the effects of ED-initiated HPC consultations on health outcomes and the quality of care for older adults.The objective of this systematic review is to synthesize the available evidence on the effectiveness of ED-initiated HPC consultations on the provision of advance care planning among older adults (≥60 years). Our review will focus on assessing several secondary outcomes, including mortality, hospital admissions, length of stay, repeat health service use, costs, and satisfaction levels among patients, caregivers, and clinicians.Following the PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols) reporting guidelines, our protocol outlines a comprehensive review of published studies. Systematic searches will be conducted in databases such as Medline, EMBASE, PubMed, Cochrane Trials database, and Web of Science from inception to present. Studies will be selected if they involve randomized, quasi-randomized, or observational designs examining the effectiveness of HPC interventions in the ED for older adults. Title, abstract and full text screening, risk of bias evaluation, and grading of the evidence will be completed independently and in duplicate by a group of emergency medicine and palliative care researchers. If feasible, a meta-analysis will be conducted using a random-effects model to evaluate the outlined outcomes.We will report descriptive statistics to describe the body of literature and we will pool absolute risk differences along with corresponding 95% CIs. llm_summary: Emergency departments serve as a critical entry point for older adults who are nearing the end of life, yet there is limited research on whether bringing in palliative care specialists (doctors trained in managing pain and improving quality of life) into the emergency room actually helps these patients. Researchers created a detailed plan to search through medical databases and review all available studies that examined what happens when emergency departments involve hospice and palliative care teams to help older adults make advance care plans (decisions about their future medical treatment). The review will look at whether these consultations affect important outcomes like mortality rates, hospital admissions, length of hospital stays, repeat visits to health services, costs, and satisfaction among patients, family members, and doctors. This systematic review addresses a significant gap in medical knowledge by focusing specifically on older adults in emergency settings, which could lead to better care practices and policies for this vulnerable population. The researchers plan to combine results from multiple studies using statistical methods to determine the true effectiveness of emergency department-initiated palliative care consultations for older adults.

title: Assessment and Clinical Management of Patients With Atopic Dermatitis Undergoing Patch Testing: Recommendations From an International Electronic Delphi Consensus.
abstract: Individuals with atopic dermatitis (AD) may be referred for patch testing to rule out allergic contact dermatitis (ACD). While past expert consensus outlines when and how to patch test these patients, clinical management and measurement of meaningful clinical improvement is particularly challenging in this population.To develop practical clinical recommendations in the assessment and management of patients with AD undergoing patch testing.An international modified electronic (e)Delphi consensus exercise was conducted among 18 AD and ACD experts.Following 4 rounds, a total of 21/24 (87.5%) clinical management statements and 15/18 (83.3%) clinical assessment statements reached consensus. Avoidance of cutaneous sources of allergens with positive (+, ++, and +++) and doubtful (+/-) reactions, use of hyporeactive products, and strict adherence to a "safe products list" of allergen-free products were recommended. Follow-up at approximately 3 months with assessment via both (1) patient-reported outcomes (PRO) and (2) clinician-reported outcomes (ClinRO) validated measurement tools were recommended to guide therapeutic decision-making.This eDelphi exercise establishes clear recommendations to manage, evaluate, and further treat patients with AD following patch testing.

llm_summary: People with atopic dermatitis, a chronic skin condition causing itching and inflammation, sometimes need patch testing to determine if they also have allergic contact dermatitis, which is an allergic reaction to substances touching the skin. An international group of eighteen skin disease experts used a structured online voting process called an electronic Delphi consensus to develop practical guidelines for managing these patients before, during, and after patch testing. The experts reached agreement on twenty-one management recommendations and fifteen assessment recommendations, including advice to avoid products containing allergens that tested positive, use gentle hypoallergenic products, and follow up with patients about three months after testing using both patient feedback and doctor observations to measure improvement. The study recommends that doctors assess patients using validated measurement tools that capture both what patients report about their own skin and what doctors observe clinically, rather than relying on just one type of measurement. These clear guidelines should help doctors better manage and treat patients with atopic dermatitis who undergo patch testing and need to avoid triggering substances in their daily lives.

title: Structured reasoning failures compromise LLM interpretation of clinical oncology notes.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show strong performance on clinical benchmarks, yet their reasoning reliability in real-world oncology care remains unclear. We evaluated LLM reasoning on authentic oncology notes using a novel hierarchical error taxonomy across two retrospective cohorts spanning breast, pancreatic, and prostate cancer. GPT-4 produced reasoning errors in 23.1% of note interpretations, the majority reflecting cognitive bias patterns. Errors were more frequent in recommendation tasks and were strongly associated with guideline-discordant recommendations and lower clinician-rated clinical impact scores. Confirmation bias, anchoring bias, and omission errors were most strongly linked to potentially harmful outputs. Compared to GPT-4, GPT-5.1 demonstrated reduced error rates and improved clinical performance but retained structured reasoning failure patterns. Automated LLM-based evaluators detected error presence but failed to reliably classify subtypes, and a preliminary self-mitigation strategy yielded only modest improvement. Endpoint accuracy alone may mask clinically meaningful reasoning failures. Therefore, evaluating and monitoring reasoning fidelity should be a prerequisite for safe deployment of LLMs in oncology decision support.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether large language models, which are artificial intelligence systems trained on vast amounts of text, can reliably interpret real patient notes from cancer doctors and provide safe medical recommendations. The team tested two versions of an AI system called GPT on actual oncology notes from patients with breast, pancreatic, and prostate cancer, looking for errors in how the AI reasoned through the information and made recommendations. The results showed that the AI made reasoning errors in about 23 percent of cases, with most errors stemming from cognitive biases, which are mental shortcuts that can lead to wrong conclusions, and these errors were especially common when the AI was asked to make treatment recommendations. The errors that involved confirmation bias (favoring information that supports an existing belief), anchoring bias (relying too heavily on the first piece of information), and missed information were most likely to lead to potentially harmful recommendations that disagreed with established medical guidelines. The researchers concluded that simply measuring whether an AI gets the right answer is not enough to ensure it is safe for use in cancer care, and that hospitals and clinics must carefully evaluate how the AI reasons through medical decisions before putting it into practice.

llm_summary: Women who receive radiation therapy for gynecologic cancers, which are cancers of the female reproductive organs, often experience side effects that affect their quality of life after treatment ends. A group of experts from the American Brachytherapy Society, an organization focused on a type of internal radiation therapy called brachytherapy, reviewed all available scientific evidence to create practical guidelines for caring for these patients after their treatment. The guidelines provide clear recommendations about how often patients should be checked by doctors, what imaging tests they might need, and how to manage common problems like pelvic floor dysfunction (weakness in the muscles that support the bladder and bowel) and sexual health issues that can result from radiation. The report offers specific advice on treatments such as vaginal dilators (devices used to prevent vaginal narrowing), physical therapy for the pelvic floor muscles, and hormone therapy to help manage vaginal dryness and other symptoms. These evidence-based recommendations help doctors provide better follow-up care and manage the physical side effects of cancer treatment, which can significantly improve how patients feel and function in their daily lives after radiation therapy.

title: Incidence of Nonindicated and Inadequate Ankle Stress Views.
abstract: Ankle stress view (ASV) radiographs and medial clear space (MCS) are important components for determining operative fixation of ankle fractures but variability in the appropriate use of indications and radiograph quality has yet to be thoroughly investigated. This is a case series of 130 patients who sustained an ankle fracture between 2012 and 2019. ASV radiographs were indicated for isolated Weber B fracture types with MCS < 4 mm on mortise views. Patient demographics, appropriate indications, adequacy of radiographs, and operative management were recorded. A MCS value of 4.9 mm served as our institution's operative threshold (area under the curve: 0.60, 95% confidence interval: 0.95 - 0.79). It was found that 36 of 130 (27%) patients had an ASV that was not indicated, and 40 of 130 (30%) had an ASV that was of inadequate quality. Notably, of the 40 patients with inadequately performed stress views, 24 (60%) underwent surgical intervention. Only 51% of ASV radiographs were appropriately indicated and adequately performed. (Journal of Surgical Orthopaedic Advances 35(2):103-106, 2026).

llm_summary: Ankle stress view radiographs, which are special X-ray images taken while applying pressure to the ankle, help doctors decide whether patients with ankle fractures need surgery, but doctors do not always use these images correctly or take them with good quality. Researchers studied 130 patients who had ankle fractures between 2012 and 2019 and checked whether stress view radiographs were ordered when they should have been and whether the images were clear enough to be useful. The study found that 27 percent of patients received stress view radiographs when they were not actually needed, and 30 percent of the stress view radiographs that were taken were of poor quality and difficult to interpret. Surprisingly, among the 40 patients who had low-quality stress view images, 24 of them still went on to have surgery, suggesting that doctors may have made treatment decisions without relying on these images. Overall, only about half of all stress view radiographs in this study were both appropriately ordered and of good enough quality to help guide treatment decisions.

title: Threading the needle: Tips and tricks for challenging percutaneous abdominopelvic biopsies.
abstract: The growing use of biomarker testing for personalized oncologic care has increased the demand for complex and repeated percutaneous biopsies in abdominal and interventional radiology practices. Challenging biopsies can be daunting, requiring a careful assessment of feasibility, safety, and risk tolerance. Several strategies can help optimize the chances of achieving success. Such strategies include leveraging the advantages of the modality chosen for image guidance, ensuring patient comfort, and the use of special techniques, such as IV contrast, navigational tols, and biopsy needle modifications. llm_summary: The growing need for personalized cancer treatment has led doctors to perform more complex biopsies, which are procedures where small tissue samples are taken from the body to test for cancer markers or genetic information. This review article provides practical guidance and helpful strategies for radiologists, who are doctors that use imaging technology like ultrasound and CT scans to guide these difficult biopsy procedures. The authors explain that success in challenging biopsies depends on carefully planning the procedure, choosing the right imaging method, keeping patients comfortable, and using special techniques such as contrast dye, navigation tools, and modified needles. These practical tips and tricks can help radiologists improve their chances of successfully obtaining good tissue samples from hard-to-reach areas in the abdomen and pelvis. By sharing these strategies, the article aims to make it easier for doctors to perform these important procedures safely and effectively for patients who need personalized cancer care.

title: Electrocardiographic parameters and outcomes in patients with cardiac amyloidosis and implantable cardioverter defibrillators.
abstract: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) is an infiltrative cardiomyopathy that can lead to various arrhythmias. Electrocardiogram (ECG) abnormalities have been reported in CA, though there is limited data on the prognostic significance of these findings.Between 1/1997 and 12/2019, we identified high arrhythmic-risk patients with CA who had clinically been treated with an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) to prevent sudden cardiac death from our multi-center practice. We studied baseline characteristics, comorbidities, echocardiograms, and ECG parameters. Regression models were used to evaluate the association of ECG characteristics with mortality or ICD shock while adjusting for baseline confounders.We identified 44 patients with CA who had ICD implantation for prevention of sudden cardiac death. Baseline characteristics included 9 (20.5%) females, 19 (43.0%) with AL CA, and 4 (9.1%) who were non-white. The mean age was 65 ± 11 years in those with AL CA and 71 ± 10 years in those with transthyretin CA. Indications for ICD implantation include syncope in 3 (7.0%) patients, ventricular arrhythmias in 16 (37.2%) patients, and both syncope and ventricular arrhythmias in 2 (4.7%) patients. Overall, ICD implantation was performed for primary prevention in 26 (59.1%) patients and for secondary prevention in 18 (40.9%) patients. Low voltage QRS was noted in 8 (42.1%) of AL CA cohort (p = 0.07) and 6 (25%) of ATTR CA cohort had LBBB (p = 0.08). Bradycardia was more prevalent in ATTR CA than in AL CA. In unadjusted analysis, only age and reduced ejection fraction were associated with death or ICD shock. There were no ECG parameters associated with death or ICD shock.In a high arrhythmic risk cohort of CA patients with ICDs, no specific ECG parameter was associated with increased all-cause mortality or ICD shock.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Cardiac amyloidosis is a serious heart disease where abnormal proteins build up in the heart muscle and can cause dangerous irregular heartbeats, so doctors sometimes implant devices called defibrillators to prevent sudden death in high-risk patients. Researchers studied 44 patients with cardiac amyloidosis who had received these implanted defibrillator devices between 1997 and 2019, examining their heart rhythm patterns on electrocardiograms (which are electrical recordings of the heart) along with other medical information to see if certain patterns could predict which patients would have worse outcomes. The study found that while some heart rhythm abnormalities like low voltage signals and left bundle branch block (a type of electrical delay in the heart) appeared more often in certain types of amyloidosis, none of these patterns were actually connected to patient death or the device delivering a shock. Only a patient's age and how well their heart was pumping blood were linked to death or device shock in this group of high-risk patients. These findings suggest that doctors cannot rely on standard heart rhythm patterns alone to predict which cardiac amyloidosis patients will have the worst outcomes, and more research is needed to find.

Tirzepatide is a newer diabetes and weight loss medication that has become increasingly popular, but this case report highlights an important safety concern where the drug may have interfered with how the body processes lithium, leading to dangerous buildup of the medication in a patient's bloodstream.

Artificial intelligence, which refers to computer systems designed to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence, is increasingly being explored as a tool to help nurses provide better and more efficient care to their patients.

title: Genetic Risk for Alzheimer Disease, Midlife Hypertension, and Dementia: The ARIC Neurocognitive Study.
abstract: Genetics represent a nonmodifiable risk factor for Alzheimer disease (AD), with 60%-80% heritability. Midlife hypertension is a modifiable risk factor for both dementia and death. Our primary objective was to determine how genetic risk for AD modifies the association between hypertension and dementia.The Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study is an ongoing community-based prospective cohort study of 4 US centers. We analyzed White and Black participants free of dementia at age 55 years with genotypes and blood pressure measured at visit 1 (1987-1989). Three genetic risk groups (low, medium, high) were defined based on tertiles of a race-specific AD polygenic risk score. Dementia was ascertained through cognitive testing, informant interviews, hospitalization, codes and death records. Death was ascertained through the National Death Index. We examined the association of midlife hypertension with incident dementia within 3 genetic risk groups using Cox proportional-hazards and cumulative incidence function estimations. We used age 55 years as the time origin, with left truncation to allow entry at ages older than 55 years; age on December 31, 2022, was the administrative censoring date.Among 8,931 White and 2,666 Black participants, the median follow up time was 26.6 and 23.8 years, the mean age was 54.0/53.5 years, and 53.0%/62.5% were female, respectively. After adjusting for demographics, midlife hypertension was significantly associated with dementia incidence across all genetic risk groups among White participants (low risk hazard ratio [HR] 1.29; 95% CI 1.07-1.55, medium risk HR 1.34; 95% CI 1.13-1.58, high risk HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.03-1.38) and among Black participants at high genetic risk (HR 1.31; 95% CI 1.04-1.66). Associations for low and medium genetic risk Black participants were consistent but not statistically significant. There were no significant differences in association of hypertension with dementia by AD genetic risk group. Individuals with hypertension had a 0%-2% higher probability of developing dementia by age 80 and a 6%-13% lower probability of dementia-free survival to age 80 years vs those without hypertension, across race and genetic risk groups.Genetic risk for AD does not modify the association between hypertension and dementia. These data support the fact that all individuals with hypertension are likely to benefit from antihypertensive treatment.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a person's genetic risk for Alzheimer disease, a brain condition that causes memory loss and confusion, could change how high blood pressure in middle age affects the chances of developing dementia later in life. The study followed over eleven thousand people from four different US cities for an average of about twenty-five years, starting when they were around fifty-five years old, and used genetic testing to divide them into three groups based on their inherited risk for Alzheimer disease. The results showed that people with high blood pressure in midlife had a higher risk of developing dementia across all genetic risk groups, but importantly, having a higher genetic risk for Alzheimer disease did not make the blood pressure problem worse or change how much it affected dementia risk. By age eighty, people with high blood pressure had between six and thirteen percent lower chances of living without dementia compared to those without high blood pressure, regardless of their genetic risk level or race. These findings suggest that treating high blood pressure in midlife could help prevent dementia in all people, since genetic risk does not reduce the benefits of managing this modifiable health condition.

title: Familial Aggregation of Parkinson Disease and Essential Tremor in Early and Late Onset Parkinson Disease Cohorts.
abstract: Early-onset Parkinson disease (EOPD) is associated with stronger genetic contributions than late-onset Parkinson disease (LOPD). However, the complex interplay between genetic susceptibility, family history, and environmental factors remains incompletely understood. This study assesses familial aggregation of PD and essential tremor (ET) among relatives of patients with EOPD and compares it with patients with LOPD.Patients with EOPD evaluated at the Mayo Clinic were identified, whereas patients with LOPD were identified through the Rochester Epidemiology Project record-linkage system. All cases with symptom onset between 1991 and 2020 were included.A total of 732 cases with EOPD and 469 with LOPD were included. EOPD patients were significantly more likely to have a positive family history of PD in parents (proportion ratio [PR] = 1.67, p = 0.049), second-degree relatives (PR = 2.54, p < 0.001), and all family members (PR = 1.63, p < 0.001). Similarly, they had higher frequency of family history of ET (PR = 1.47, p = 0.029). By contrast, patients with EOPD were less likely to have siblings with PD (PR = 0.38, p = 0.009).The higher prevalence of PD and ET family history in the EOPD cohort supports a stronger genetic contribution and may reflect enrichment for high-penetrance monoallelic variants. Conversely, the higher frequency of affected siblings in the LOPD cohort suggests a polygenic inheritance pattern with greater environmental contribution.
