llm_summary: Surgeons often need to measure the alignment of leg bones to plan knee replacement surgery, but standard knee X-rays do not show the upper part of the thighbone, making accurate measurements difficult. Researchers developed an artificial intelligence system trained to predict the correct alignment measurement from a simple knee X-ray by learning from patients who had both standard knee images and full-length leg X-rays taken close together in time. The artificial intelligence method was able to predict the alignment within one degree of accuracy, which is considered clinically useful, and it performed significantly better than two older methods that doctors have previously used. This new tool could help surgeons make better decisions about knee replacement surgery and could be especially valuable for patients who only have standard knee X-rays available rather than full-length leg images. The study demonstrates that artificial intelligence can solve a real problem in orthopedic surgery by extracting useful information from images that previously seemed to lack the necessary detail.

title: Does Color Doppler Twinkling Change Between Ultrasound Platform Generations? - A Comparison Using Breast Biopsy Markers.
abstract: Breast biopsy markers are used to mark biopsied tissues in the breast or axilla for potential future surgical excision. This study evaluated the color Doppler twinkling strength of 37 markers using two different ultrasound systems to assess if newer technology provides sufficient twinkling for clinical use.Thirty-seven breast biopsy markers (36 commercially available and one polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) research marker) were embedded in homogeneous gelatin phantoms and imaged using two ultrasound platforms (General Electric LOGIQ E9 and LOGIQ E10). Multiple linear and curvilinear transducers were evaluated. Two experienced breast radiologists independently scored twinkling strength in two separate sessions using an ordinal 0-4 scale, with scores ≥3 considered actionable twinkling. Statistical analyses included intra- and inter-observer reliability assessment, correlation analyses between twinkling scores and imaging parameters, and ordinal logistic regression modeling to evaluate system-, marker-, and transducer-level effects.Of the 37 biopsy markers evaluated, 14 exhibited measurable twinkling and were included in statistical analyses. Several markers that demonstrated weak or non-actionable twinkling on the E9 achieved consistently higher and actionable scores on the E10. Model-based analysis showed substantial system-dependent differences by transducers, with the L8-18i demonstrating the largest improvement on the E10 (odds ratio (OR) 251.11 [95% CI: 67.52-933.88]; p < 0.001). The PMMA marker demonstrated consistently high and reproducible twinkling across both systems (mean scores: E9 = 3.4, E10 = 3.6).Color Doppler twinkling by breast biopsy markers is strongly influenced by ultrasound system generation, transducer selection, and acquisition parameters.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether newer ultrasound machines produce better images of tiny markers that doctors place in breast tissue during biopsies to help locate areas for future surgery. The team tested 37 different biopsy markers using two generations of ultrasound equipment, including an older model and a newer model, along with various types of ultrasound probes, and had experienced radiologists rate how well they could see a special visual effect called twinkling that helps identify these markers. The results showed that the newer ultrasound machine produced noticeably better and more reliable twinkling effects for most markers compared to the older machine, with some markers showing weak or unusable twinkling on the older equipment but clear, usable twinkling on the newer one. These findings suggest that upgrading to newer ultrasound technology could help doctors more easily locate and identify breast biopsy markers during follow-up procedures, potentially improving patient care and surgical planning. The study also found that the choice of ultrasound probe and specific imaging settings significantly affected how well the markers appeared, indicating that doctors should carefully select their equipment and settings when looking for these markers in clinical practice.

title: Improved Oncologic Outcomes with Trimodality Therapy for Radiation-Associated Angiosarcoma of the Breast.
abstract: Radiation-associated angiosarcoma of the breast (RAASB) is a rare aggressive malignancy arising after breast irradiation. We previously reported that trimodality therapy showed high rates of pathologic complete response (pCR) and durable local control. Here we report an expanded cohort with longer follow-up to characterize the oncologic outcomes of this approach.With IRB approval, we performed a retrospective review of newly diagnosed RAASB patients operated at Mayo Clinic in Rochester 2000-2025. Trimodality therapy was defined as sequential induction chemotherapy, preoperative concurrent chemoradiation, and wide surgical resection; Mono/Dual therapy consisted of surgery +/- chemotherapy. Clinical characteristics, treatments, and oncologic outcomes were abstracted. RFS was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and reported with 95% confidence intervals (CI).Forty-three patients (median age 68 years [40-80]) were included; 24 Trimodality therapy and 19 Mono/Dual therapy. Age and extent of presenting disease was similar between the Trimodality and Mono/Dual therapy groups. All Trimodality patients received chemotherapy, chemoradiation, and wide resection with flap closure. Among Mono/Dual patients, none had radiation, 47% had chemotherapy, and 68% had wide resection, with flap closure in 58%. Eight-year recurrence free survival was superior in the Trimodality group at 96% [95% CI 87-100%], versus 50% [95% CI 30-86%] in the Mono/Dual group, p = 0.002. Eight-year overall survival was also superior in the Trimodality group at 94% [95% CI 84-100%], versus 65% [95% CI 45-95%] in the Mono/Dual group, p = 0.047.Trimodality therapy for RAASB demonstrates high rates of pCR, local control, and survival.© 2026. llm_summary: Radiation-associated angiosarcoma of the breast is a rare and aggressive cancer that develops in some women years after receiving radiation therapy for breast cancer treatment. Researchers at Mayo Clinic reviewed medical records of 43 patients diagnosed with this condition between 2000 and 2025, comparing outcomes between those who received a three-part treatment approach (chemotherapy drugs, radiation combined with chemotherapy, and surgery) versus those who received one or two of these treatments. Patients who received all three treatments together had much better results, with 96 percent remaining cancer-free after eight years compared to only 50 percent in the group receiving fewer treatments. The study also showed that patients in the three-part treatment group had better overall survival rates at 94 percent after eight years, compared to 65 percent in the other group. These findings suggest that combining chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery offers the best chance of controlling this aggressive cancer and improving long-term survival for patients.

title: A multi-omics approach investigating thrombolysis resistance in acute ischemic stroke thrombi.
abstract: Intravenous thrombolysis outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary widely due to heterogeneous clot responsiveness. Defining the molecular basis of thrombolysis resistance is critical to improving treatment efficacy. Sixty-one clots from 59 AIS patients underwent ex vivo thrombolysis with rtPA and were classified as resistant, undefined, or susceptible based on 1-h lysis rates. Quantitative proteomics was performed on a subset (n = 6/group) using mass spectrometry. Whole-genome sequencing (n = 13) explored genetic associations. Clot composition was assessed using Martius Scarlet Blue staining (n = 11) and correlated with thrombolysis. At 1 h, 37 clots were resistant (0- < 25% lysis), 11 undefined (25- < 40%), and 13 susceptible (40-80%). Clot composition did not correlate significantly with thrombolysis. Proteomics identified 124 differentially expressed proteins (≥ 1.5-fold, p < 0.05), including 108 downregulated and 16 upregulated in resistant clots. Downregulated pathways included oxidative phosphorylation, neutrophil extracellular trap signaling, and integrin-mediated adhesion, while granzyme A signaling and mitochondrial dysfunction were enriched. WGS revealed no group-specific variants. Thrombolysis resistance in AIS clots is not explained by histologic composition alone but is associated with coordinated proteomic alterations in mitochondrial bioenergetics, cytoskeletal organization, and adhesion pathways, identifying mitochondrial bioenergetic failure and integrin-mediated structural remodeling as key determinants of fibrinolysis resistance and potential therapeutic targets.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined why some blood clots in stroke patients resist treatment with a clot-dissolving medication called rtPA, which is important because understanding this resistance could help doctors treat strokes more effectively. The team collected blood clots from 59 stroke patients and tested how well rtPA could dissolve them in the laboratory, then analyzed the clots using advanced techniques including protein analysis and genetic sequencing to identify differences between clots that dissolved easily and those that resisted treatment. The study found that clots resistant to treatment had significantly lower levels of certain proteins involved in energy production within cells and in the structural connections that hold clots together, while the physical composition of the clots alone did not explain why some resisted treatment. These findings suggest that the key to thrombolysis resistance lies in how well the cells within the clot can produce energy and maintain their structural organization, pointing to potential new ways to make clot-dissolving treatments more effective. Future research should focus on developing new therapies that target these energy production and structural problems in resistant clots to improve outcomes for stroke patients who do not respond well to current treatments.

llm_summary: Background:  Multiple sclerosis is a disease where the immune system mistakenly attacks the protective covering of nerve fibers in the brain and spinal cord, causing problems with movement, sensation, and other body functions. Paroxysmal facial movements are sudden, involuntary twitches or spasms of the face muscles that occur in episodes, and while they can happen in various neurological conditions, they represent an important symptom to recognize when they occur in multiple sclerosis patients.

title: Beyond the pump: integrating the heart's endocrine function into early medical education.
abstract: The heart is commonly introduced in early medical education through its structural, mechanical, and electrophysiological roles. Although this framing remains foundational, it may underemphasize the heart's endocrine functions. Cardiac endocrine signaling, particularly natriuretic peptide physiology, offers a concise structure-function example linking anatomy, histology, cardiovascular physiology, and clinical biomarker interpretation.To synthesize scientific and educational principles of cardiac endocrine function and propose an anatomy-anchored framework for integration into pre-clerkship medical education.A librarian-assisted narrative review was conducted in May 2025 using representative literature from PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus, supplemented by historical, molecular, physiological, anatomical, and medical education sources. The search focused on cardiac endocrine function, natriuretic peptides, and medical education and yielded 23 abstracts. The aim was conceptual synthesis rather than systematic or exhaustive retrieval.The discovery of atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) and C-type natriuretic peptide (CNP) established the heart as an endocrine organ influencing renal, and cardiovascular homeostasis. The available medical education literature provides limited explicit guidance on how this topic should be introduced, and reinforced in early curricula. Integration of cardiac endocrine biology aligns with principles of cognitive integration, spiral curriculum design, and authentic learning. ANP and BNP/NT-proBNP are proposed as high-yield teaching examples: ANP links atrial structure and stretch to volume regulation, whereas BNP/NT-proBNP links ventricular wall stress to heart failure evaluation.Early integration of the heart's endocrine function into medical curricula may fortify structure-function reasoning, enhance systems thinking, and support mechanistic clinical reasoning. Rather than adding a separate curricular block, cardiac endocrine signaling can be incorporated through anatomy and histology, then reinforced in cardiovascular physiology, renal physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, and clinical reasoning. Aligning foundational instruction with modern cardiovascular science can improve learners' conceptual frameworks and better prepare them for clinical decision making.

llm_summary: Medical schools typically teach students about the heart's role as a pump, focusing on its structure and how it beats, but they often overlook the heart's ability to produce hormones that help regulate the body's fluid balance and blood pressure. Researchers reviewed scientific literature to develop a better way to teach medical students about the heart's hormone-producing function, particularly focusing on natural chemicals called natriuretic peptides that the heart releases. The study found that the heart produces three main types of these hormones, which work together to help the kidneys and blood vessels maintain proper fluid balance and that current medical education provides little guidance on how to teach this important concept. By integrating lessons about the heart's hormone function into existing anatomy, physiology, and biochemistry courses rather than creating a separate class, students can better understand how the heart's structure connects to its multiple roles in the body. This approach could help future doctors make better clinical decisions, especially when interpreting blood tests for heart failure and understanding how the heart maintains the body's overall balance.

title: Health Care-Associated Infections in U.S. Hospitals, 2023 versus 2015.
abstract: Prevalence surveys in U.S. hospitals showed that on any given day, 1 of 25 patients had a health care-associated infection in 2011, as compared with 1 of 31 patients in 2015. We repeated the survey in 2023 to assess changes in the prevalence of such infections.Using established methods, 10 Emerging Infections Program (EIP) sites recruited up to 25 hospitals each. Hospitals selected a survey day between May 1 and September 30, 2023. EIP staff reviewed medical records of randomly selected patients to identify health care-associated infections using National Healthcare Safety Network definitions. We described patient and hospital characteristics, compared the prevalence of health care-associated infections in 2023 and 2015, and estimated the national burden of health care-associated infections in 2023.In 2023, of 13,653 patients in 218 hospitals, 355 (2.6%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.3 to 2.9) had at least one health care-associated infection, as compared with 394 of 12,299 patients (3.2%; 95% CI, 2.9 to 3.5) in 199 hospitals in 2015. Approximately 60% of the health care-associated infections were not associated with devices or procedures. Among 151 hospitals in both surveys, patients were less likely to have a health care-associated infection in 2023 than in 2015, after adjustment for other factors (risk ratio, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.63 to 0.85). We estimated that there were 518,000 health care-associated infections (95% CI, 494,500 to 542,000) in U.S. hospitals in 2023.The prevalence of health care-associated infections was lower in 2023 than in 2015, with 1 of 38 patients on any given day having such an infection; however, the burden of health care-associated infections in U.S. hospitals continued to be high. A majority of the health care-associated infections that were identified were not associated with a device or procedure. llm_summary: Researchers examined how common infections that patients catch while staying in hospitals have changed over time, which matters because these infections can make people sicker and cost the healthcare system a lot of money. The study looked at patients in hospitals across the United States during the summer of 2023 and compared the results to similar data collected in 2015, using a method where they randomly selected patients and reviewed their medical records to identify infections that started during their hospital stay. They found that in 2023, about 2. 6 percent of hospital patients had at least one healthcare-associated infection, which was lower than the 3. 2 percent found in 2015, meaning roughly one out of every 38 patients had such an infection compared to one out of 31 patients eight years earlier.

title: Continuous or Fixed-Duration Maintenance Therapy in Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: Current treatment of newly diagnosed multiple myeloma involves lenalidomide maintenance therapy given until disease progression. The appropriate duration of maintenance therapy with lenalidomide has been unclear.In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled patients with standard-risk newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who were not undergoing up-front autologous stem-cell transplantation. After induction treatment with a proteasome inhibitor-lenalidomide combination, patients were randomly assigned to receive indefinite-duration (continuous) lenalidomide or fixed-duration lenalidomide (for 2 years). The primary end point was overall survival; the trial had 80% power to detect a 50% increase in median survival (from 5 years to 7.5 years), with a two-sided alpha level of 5%, 395 patients undergoing randomization, and 204 deaths occurring during 9 years of follow-up.At the end of induction, 516 patients were randomly assigned to the indefinite-duration group (260 patients) or the fixed-duration group (256 patients). At a median follow-up of 86 months, overall survival did not differ significantly between the groups. With 80 deaths in each group, overall survival at 7 years was 68.6% in the indefinite-duration group and 69.0% in the fixed-duration group (difference, -0.4 percentage points; 95 confidence interval [CI], -9.0 to 8.3; P = 0.93). Progression-free survival at 7 years was 36.1% in the indefinite-duration group and 29.7% in the fixed-duration group (difference, 6.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -2.6 to 15.4). The 5-year cumulative incidence of second primary cancers, excluding nonmelanoma skin cancer, was 11.2% with indefinite-duration lenalidomide and 8.3% with fixed-duration lenalidomide. More adverse events occurred with indefinite-duration lenalidomide; the incidence of nonhematologic events of grade 3 or higher was 48.2% with indefinite-duration therapy and 31.5% with fixed-duration therapy.In this phase 3 trial involving patients with standard-risk newly diagnosed multiple myeloma who were not undergoing up-front autologous stem-cell transplantation, indefinite-duration maintenance therapy after induction therapy did not result in significantly longer overall survival than fixed-duration maintenance therapy. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether patients with multiple myeloma, a blood cancer, should take a maintenance drug called lenalidomide continuously or for a fixed period of two years after their initial treatment. In this large clinical trial, over five hundred patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma received initial treatment with a combination of drugs, and then half were randomly assigned to take lenalidomide indefinitely while the other half took it for exactly two years. After following patients for nearly seven years, the researchers found that overall survival rates were nearly identical between the two groups, with about 69 percent of patients in each group still alive at the seven-year mark. The fixed-duration approach had a clear advantage because patients taking lenalidomide continuously experienced more serious side effects and a higher risk of developing second cancers compared to those who stopped after two years. These findings suggest that patients with standard-risk multiple myeloma who are not having stem cell transplants can safely stop lenalidomide maintenance therapy after two years without sacrificing their survival chances while reducing their exposure to harmful side effects.

title: Epstein-Barr virus antibodies and risk of non-Hodgkin lymphoma: a pooled analysis of four prospective cohorts.
abstract: Non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHLs) are among the most common cancers in the US, yet their etiology is mostly unknown. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a known driver of rare NHLs, but its role in common subtypes is unclear. We evaluated associations between antibodies to 16 EBV antigens, including 12 emerging markers (anti-: BARF1, BBRF1, BFRF1, BGLF2, BHRF1, BORF1, BPLF1, BRLF1, BXLF1, LF2, LMP1, VCAp40) and NHL risk in prediagnostic blood samples from 2134 case-control sets from 4 prospective cohort studies. Conditional logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Associations across multiple antibodies were summarized using a β‑weighted score (EBVAb score). Eight markers were positively associated with NHL risk. Anti-LMP1 was associated with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL; OR = 2.83, 95% CI: 1.12-7.19) only. Six lytic markers (anti-: BGLF2, VCAp40, BFRF1, BARF1, BHRF1, BXLF1) were associated with a 2-3 times higher risk of chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL). Lytic marker associations for DLBCL and follicular lymphoma (FL) were weaker, with exceptions: anti-BXLF1 and DLBCL: OR = 2.25, 95% CI: 1.33-3.81; anti-BHRF1 and FL: OR = 2.75, 95% CI: 1.22-6.18. Anti-EBV scores > 0 were associated with ~50% higher NHL risk, strongest for CLL/SLL (Tertile 3: OR = 2.43, 95% CI: 1.30-4.55). Select EBV antibodies may serve as markers of common NHL risk.© 2026. llm_summary: Non-Hodgkin lymphomas, which are cancers of the immune system cells, are common in the United States but doctors still do not fully understand what causes them. Researchers examined blood samples collected before diagnosis from over 2,000 people with lymphoma and compared them to people without the disease across four long-term health studies to see if antibodies to Epstein-Barr virus, a common virus that most people carry, were linked to lymphoma risk. They found that eight different Epstein-Barr virus antibodies were associated with higher lymphoma risk, with six of these antibodies showing particularly strong connections to a type called chronic lymphocytic leukemia, and people with high levels of multiple antibodies together had about 50 percent higher risk of developing any type of lymphoma. These findings suggest that measuring certain Epstein-Barr virus antibodies in blood tests could help doctors identify people at higher risk for developing common types of lymphoma before symptoms appear. Future research will need to confirm these results and determine whether monitoring these antibodies could help prevent lymphoma or catch it earlier in people who are at highest risk.

title: Interest in Robotics Outpaces Access: Results from a Survey of Practicing Plastic Surgeons.
abstract: While the launch of the da Vinci Surgical System catalyzed the expansion of robotic surgery across disciplines, adoption in plastic surgery remains modest. To explore this disconnect, this study surveys plastic surgeons to gauge interest, utilization, and perceived barriers to robotic surgery adoption.A 15-question survey on training, access, interest, and barriers to robotic procedures was developed on Qualtrics and distributed via email to members of the American Society of Plastic Surgeons (ASPS) in May 2024. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize responses.About 123 responses were collected among 3,512 survey recipients. Among respondents, 84.6% reported having access to a surgical robot; however, only 13.8% had training on robotic systems during residency, and only 12.2% utilized the technology for plastic surgery procedures. Interest in robotics was noted among 47.9% of respondents, particularly for deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) flap procedures (65.5%), rectus/Vertical Rectus Abdominis Myocutaneous (VRAM) flap (58.2%), and hernia repairs (27.3%). Key barriers to adoption included training requirements (63.9%), lack of demand (60.2%), increased operative time (54.6%), and financial concerns (26.9%). Additional obstacles cited were credentialing difficulties and skepticism about the necessity of robotics in plastic surgery.The present survey identified inadequate training, high costs, and limited demand as key barriers to the adoption of robotics in plastic surgery, reflecting the current lack of robotic integration into residency curricula, as well as the substantial investment and maintenance costs associated with robotic systems. Nevertheless, the strong interest in robotics highlights the need for expanded training programs, promotion of clinical benefits, and research quantifying potential downstream savings to overcome these barriers.Thieme. llm_summary: Robotic surgical systems like the da Vinci machine have become common in hospitals across many medical fields, but plastic surgeons have been slow to adopt this technology despite showing interest in it. Researchers surveyed plastic surgeons across the United States in May 2024 by sending a fifteen-question questionnaire to members of the American Society of Plastic Surgeons to understand why adoption rates remain low. The survey found that while most surgeons had access to robotic equipment at their hospitals, very few had received training on how to use it during their medical education, and even fewer actually used robots in their plastic surgery procedures. The main obstacles preventing wider use included the need for specialized training, lack of patient demand, longer surgery times, and high costs, though many surgeons expressed strong interest in using robots for specific procedures like breast reconstruction and hernia repairs. To increase the use of robotic surgery in plastic surgery, hospitals and training programs need to invest in teaching surgeons how to use these systems and conduct research to prove that the benefits outweigh the significant expenses involved.

title: GLUT9b- and ABCG2-mediated collecting duct urate transport uncovers a vasopressin-independent mechanism of renal water reabsorption.
abstract: Renal water reabsorption is classically regulated by vasopressin V2 receptor (V2R) signaling through cyclic AMP and protein kinase A, driving apical accumulation of aquaporin-2 (AQP2). However, collecting duct water handling is also modulated by vasopressin-independent mechanisms. Here, we examined intracellular soluble urate as a vasopressin-independent regulator of AQP2 trafficking. Intracellular urate accumulation in collecting duct cells was mediated by enhanced apical urate uptake via GLUT9b and reduced apical urate efflux through ABCG2, triggering phosphodiesterase-4 activation, reduced cAMP, and downstream AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation. The resulting AQP2 accumulation at the apical membrane was independent of V2R signaling, required ongoing endocytosis, and was associated with features of postendocytic apical trafficking of internalized AQP2. In vivo ABCG2 inhibition with probenecid increased apical AQP2 abundance and markedly attenuated tolvaptan-induced polyuria in both wild-type and Pkd1RC/RC autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) mice in a uricase-independent manner while preserving tolvaptan's ADPKD-modifying efficacy. In a phase II trial with tolvaptan-treated patients with ADPKD, probenecid reduced urine volume and nocturia frequency. Together, these findings support a vasopressin-independent urate/AMPK/AQP2 pathway that regulates renal water handling and, in a preclinical ADPKD model, can uncouple cyst growth attenuation from the dose-limiting aquaretic effects of V2R antagonism.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how the kidneys control water reabsorption through a previously unknown pathway that does not rely on the hormone vasopressin, which is the classical regulator of this process. They discovered that urate, a waste product from protein breakdown, accumulates inside collecting duct cells (the kidney structures that handle water) through two transport proteins called GLUT9b and ABCG2, which trigger a chain reaction that moves water channel proteins to the cell surface. In laboratory studies with mice and in a human trial with patients taking a kidney disease medication called tolvaptan, blocking one of these transport proteins with a drug called probenecid increased water reabsorption and reduced excessive urination without interfering with the medication's benefits. This finding is important because it suggests doctors could potentially reduce the unwanted side effect of excessive urination caused by certain kidney disease treatments by activating this alternative water-handling pathway. The research opens new possibilities for treating polycystic kidney disease, a genetic condition where cysts grow in the kidneys, by allowing patients to benefit from effective treatments while experiencing fewer bothersome urinary symptoms.

title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomics of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded biopsies reveals colitis-associated cell networks.
abstract: Imaging-based, single-cell, spatial transcriptomics (iSCST) of FFPE tissue enables comprehensive analysis of archived specimens while preserving spatial context, critical to an understanding of ulcerative colitis (UC) pathology. Here, we deployed a robust framework for applying iSCST to clinical FFPE mucosal biopsies from patients with UC or immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced colitis, as well as patients serving as healthy controls. iSCST using custom Xenium gene panels enabled precise detection of diverse cell subsets and disease-specific genes. We mapped transcriptionally distinct fibroblast subsets within mucosal niches, including inflammation-associated fibroblasts (IAFs), and identified colitis-specific neighborhoods formed by IAFs, monocytes, and neutrophils. Transcriptional signatures and spatial neighborhoods uncovered through iSCST were associated with vedolizumab (VDZ) response, with nonresponders exhibiting either an innate IAF-monocyte-neutrophil signature or adaptive gut-associated lymphoid tissue signature, while responders showed enrichment of an epithelial cellular neighborhood. These signatures were validated in an internal and an external dataset, supporting the existence of 2 distinct archetypes of treatment resistance to VDZ in UC. This iSCST framework provides a powerful approach for analyzing FFPE tissues, offering insights into colitis-associated cellular networks and identifying biomarkers to enhance patient risk stratification in routine clinical workflows.

llm_summary: Researchers examined tissue samples from patients with ulcerative colitis, a disease where the colon becomes inflamed and damaged, to better understand which cells are involved in the disease and why some patients don't respond to treatment. They used a special imaging technique that can identify individual cells and their genes in preserved tissue samples, allowing them to see exactly where different cell types were located and what genes they were using. The study found that certain types of immune cells called fibroblasts, monocytes, and neutrophils form specific patterns in inflamed tissue, and these patterns were different in patients who responded well to a drug called vedolizumab compared to those who did not respond. The researchers discovered two distinct patterns of cells in patients who didn't respond to the drug, suggesting there may be two different reasons why some people don't benefit from this treatment. These findings could help doctors predict which patients will respond to vedolizumab and potentially guide them toward better treatment options in the future.

title: Development and validity evidence of a knowledge assessment in genomics sequencing report interpretation for non-geneticist medical trainees.
abstract: Clinicians are increasingly expected to interpret genomic sequencing reports, yet tools to assess the proficiency of non-geneticist medical trainees in this important skill are lacking. This study aimed to develop a multiple-choice test to evaluate non-geneticist trainees' knowledge and skill in interpreting genomic reports and to systematically gather sufficient validity evidence supporting its use. An iterative, expert-informed yet practical approach was employed to design and refine the assessment, with validity evidence analyzed according to Messick's framework. The final 27-item test demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.9), and significant differences were seen between participant groups, with test scores correlating with participants' level of expertise. These findings support the utility of this assessment as a robust, low-stakes measure of genomic sequencing report interpretation skills among non-geneticist medical trainees.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Doctors who are not genetics specialists increasingly need to understand reports from genetic tests that look at a patient's DNA, but there were no good tools to measure whether medical trainees could actually do this well. Researchers created a test with twenty-seven multiple-choice questions designed to check whether non-specialist medical trainees could correctly interpret these genetic reports, and they carefully gathered evidence to prove the test was reliable and fair. The final test showed strong results, with questions that consistently measured the same skill, and trainees with more experience scored higher than those with less experience. This assessment tool can now be used as a straightforward way to measure whether medical trainees are learning to read and understand genetic test reports correctly. Future work should explore how this test can be used in training programs to help ensure that all doctors can confidently interpret genetic information for their patients.

title: Histone lysine methyltransferases KMT2C and KMT2D join the all-star tumor suppressor team in gastrointestinal cancer.
abstract: Members of the type 2 histone lysine methyltransferase family (KMT2s) are key drivers of enhancer activation and are the most mutated group of epigenetic regulators in different cancer types. Within this family, KMT2C and KMT2D have the highest mutational incidence across various cancers. To evaluate their role in gastric cancer, Wang et al. developed a Pten deficiency-driven genetically engineered mouse model with inducible loss of Kmt2c and Kmt2d in gastric epithelial cells. Through extensive in vitro, in vivo, and in silico analyses, the authors revealed that the concomitant loss of Kmt2c and Kmt2d promotes gastric carcinogenesis while enhancing antigen presentation and sensitivity to immunotherapy and targeted approaches like mTOR inhibition, highlighting the tumor-suppressive roles of KMT2C/D in gastric cancer and uncovering a vulnerability for this dismal condition.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how two genes called KMT2C and KMT2D, which control how cells read their genetic instructions, function as tumor suppressors in stomach cancer. The scientists created laboratory mice that lacked these genes in stomach cells and combined this with another cancer-promoting condition to study how cancer develops and progresses. They discovered that losing both of these genes together actually speeds up stomach cancer growth but makes cancer cells easier for the immune system to recognize and attack. This finding suggests that patients with stomach cancers lacking these genes might respond better to immunotherapy treatments that boost the immune system and to drugs that target a cellular growth pathway called mTOR. The research opens new possibilities for treating this deadly cancer by identifying which patients might benefit most from specific combination therapies based on their genetic makeup.

title: Anatomy Curriculum and Teaching Insights From Medical Students in the United Kingdom: A National Survey.
abstract: Undergraduate anatomy teaching in the UK has been progressively compressed, with reduced contact time and variable integration across medical programs. We examined final-year medical students' perceptions of anatomy teaching, focusing on total contact hours, longitudinal continuity, and exposure to traditional and emerging teaching modalities. A national cross-sectional survey was distributed to final-year students across 40 UK medical schools between December 2024 and February 2025. Satisfaction with anatomy teaching, perceived importance of anatomy for future practice, contact hours, continuity across program years, and exposure to specific teaching modalities and technologies were assessed. Comparative analyses used non-parametric tests and ANOVA with post hoc testing where appropriate. 628 students responded. Dissatisfaction was greatest for teaching quantity and continuity, whereas breadth, depth, and quality were rated more favourably. Students receiving more than 200 h of anatomy teaching reported significantly higher satisfaction than those receiving fewer than 200 h (p < 0.001). Satisfaction also varied by continuity pattern, with teaching delivered continuously over three or more years associated with higher satisfaction than shorter or non-continuous models (p < 0.01). Cadaveric dissection was the most preferred modality, but higher satisfaction was associated with exposure to selected adjuncts, particularly 3D imaging software and 3D printed models (both p < 0.001); VR/AR showed no significant association. Perceived importance of anatomy differed by intended specialty, with students interested in surgery rating anatomy as most important (p < 0.0001). Student dissatisfaction with UK undergraduate anatomy teaching appears to stem less from content coverage than from insufficient teaching time and poor longitudinal integration. Anatomy should be protected as a multi-year component of the curriculum, complemented by selectively integrated adjunctive tools rather than indiscriminate technology adoption.© 2026 American Association of Clinical Anatomists and British Association of Clinical Anatomists.

llm_summary: Anatomy education in UK medical schools has been shrinking over time, with students getting less classroom time and less consistent teaching throughout their studies, which prompted researchers to investigate how final-year medical students felt about their anatomy training. Researchers surveyed 628 final-year medical students across 40 UK medical schools between December 2024 and February 2025, asking them about their satisfaction with anatomy teaching, how many hours they spent learning anatomy, whether anatomy was taught continuously throughout their program, and what teaching methods they preferred. Students who received more than 200 hours of anatomy instruction reported significantly higher satisfaction than those who received fewer hours, and students whose anatomy teaching was spread across three or more years of their program were happier than those who had shorter or interrupted anatomy training. The study found that while students were satisfied with the quality and depth of what they learned, they were most frustrated by not having enough teaching time and by anatomy not being woven consistently throughout their entire medical education. The researchers concluded that UK medical schools should protect anatomy as a core subject taught over multiple years and should use selected tools like three-dimensional imaging software and printed models to support learning, rather than adopting every new technology available.

title: Sleeping Beauty mutagenesis identifies BACH2 and other regulators of CD8+ T-cell exhaustion, persistence in vivo, and CAR-T cell function under tumor-associated chronic antigen stimulation.
abstract: Genes that enhance T-cell function represent promising targets for improving engineered T-cell therapies for cancer. While extensive CRISPR knockout screens have identified key genes enhancing T-cell persistence, employing Sleeping Beauty (SB) insertional mutagenesis, which induces both gain-of-function (GOF) and loss-of-function (LOF) mutations via the generation of fusion transcripts with endogenous genes, may uncover additional critical factors that previous approaches have overlooked.We developed transgenic mice carrying Doxycycline (Dox)-inducible SB mutagenesis system (DiSBey) in primary T cells. Using DiSBey, we conducted screens for genetic alterations enhancing T-cell persistence under chronic antigen exposure. Specifically, CD8+ T cells from Dox-fed DiSBey mice were subjected to repeated anti-CD3 stimulation over 18 days to mimic chronic antigenic stimulation. We then identified SB transposon genomic insertion sites and corresponding fusion transcripts from the persistent DiSBey CD8+ T cells using enhanced-specificity tagmentation sequencing and RNA sequencing, respectively.Under chronic stimulation, SB-mutagenized CD8+ T cells exhibited improved persistence and reduced terminal exhaustion phenotype. Across six independent screens, we identified 38 genes that were recurrently targeted by the SB transposon T2/Onc2 and differentially expressed under chronic anti-CD3 stimulation. T2/Onc2 insertions into Bach2 and Elmo1 were recurrently identified at the genomic level and were associated with altered nascent transcript expression. Bach2, known as a key regulator of T-cell memory formation and resistance to chronic viral infection-induced exhaustion but less characterized in engineered T cells for cancer therapy, was found to counteract exhaustion in vitro and enhance in vivo tumor persistence in the B16-Ova tumor model. Further, we showed that ectopic Bach2 expression levels influence engineered T-cell differentiation lineage, as low Bach2 overexpression retained more functional progenitor exhausted T cells and exhibited improved therapeutic efficacy. Finally, in human CART19-28ζ cells, BACH2 overexpression enhanced cytotoxicity and tumor control following chronic cancer stimulation.Controllable SB mutagenesis using DiSBey mice provides a novel platform for functional screening of genes that improve T-cell phenotypes important for their use as therapies. Our findings highlight a dose-dependent role of BACH2 in enhancing the function of engineered T cells under conditions of chronic antigenic stimulation.© Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined how to improve engineered immune cells called T cells that are used to fight cancer by identifying genes that help these cells survive and function better when exposed to constant tumor signals. They created special mice with a controllable genetic system that randomly inserted DNA sequences into T cell genes, causing both increased and decreased activity of different genes, and then exposed these modified cells to repeated stimulation over eighteen days to mimic what happens in the body during chronic cancer. The screens identified thirty-eight genes that were repeatedly targeted by these DNA insertions, with a gene called BACH2 standing out as particularly important for preventing T cells from becoming exhausted and worn out during prolonged exposure to cancer signals. When researchers increased BACH2 levels in engineered cancer-fighting cells, the cells showed better ability to kill tumors and maintain their function, with the benefit depending on the exact amount of BACH2 present. These findings suggest that controlling BACH2 expression could be a promising way to improve engineered T cell therapies for cancer patients, though further research will be needed to determine the optimal levels and safety of this approach.

llm_summary: Background:  The American Society of Breast Surgeons holds an annual meeting where researchers and doctors submit abstracts, which are short summaries of their research findings, to be considered for presentation. Selecting which abstracts to include in the meeting program is a time-consuming process that requires expert reviewers to read and evaluate many submissions, but large language models, which are artificial intelligence systems trained to understand and process text, can help speed up this selection process.

title: Real-World Treatment Patterns in Advanced Cutaneous Melanoma in the USA.
abstract: Melanoma has an excellent prognosis when detected at a localized stage, but when patients present with regional or distant metastases, 5-year survival decreases to approximately 76% and 35%, respectively. Although recent advances in systemic therapies have improved outcomes for patients with advanced melanoma, these treatments are often not curative, and many patients ultimately develop disease progression requiring subsequent lines of therapy.This study aimed to characterize real-world treatment patterns among patients in the USA with advanced cutaneous melanoma who transitioned from first-line (1L) to second-line (2L) systemic therapy.This retrospective, observational study used administrative claims data from a large US managed care database. Adult patients with metastatic melanoma who initiated 1L systemic therapy between January 2023 and December 2025 and subsequently received 2L therapy were included. Claims-based algorithms identified treatment regimens by line of therapy. Sankey diagrams illustrate treatment transitions overall and by BRAF V600 mutation status.Of 1772 patients who met study criteria, 680 (38.4%) were classified as presumed BRAF V600-mutated (BRAFmut) on the basis of treatment exposure, and 1092 (61.6%) were classified as presumed BRAF wild-type (BRAFwt). Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based regimens were the most common first-line (1L) therapies (78.5%), while BRAF + MEK inhibitors accounted for 14.4%. In second-line (2L) therapy, sequencing patterns were diverse, with no dominant 2L pathway observed. BRAF + MEK inhibitors were the most frequently used 2L therapy (27.5%). In patients with BRAFmut, targeted therapy predominated in 2L (71.8%), whereas ICI-based regimens remained dominant in patients with BRAFwt (84.9%). 1L therapy was significantly associated with 2L treatment selection (p < 0.001). Treatment distributions differed across index years for both 1L (p = 0.001) and 2L (p = 0.005) therapies. Over time, use of PD-1 monotherapy decreased, while use of nivolumab plus ipilimumab increased; use of BRAF + MEK therapy remained stable.Although treatment practices for advanced melanoma continue to evolve in response to emerging clinical evidence, substantial uncertainty remains regarding optimal treatment sequencing after 1L progression. These findings highlight the need for prospective sequencing studies and more effective therapeutic options following disease progression.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Melanoma is a serious type of skin cancer that becomes much harder to treat once it spreads to other parts of the body, with survival rates dropping significantly when the disease reaches distant areas. Researchers examined real-world treatment patterns by analyzing insurance claims data from nearly 1,800 patients in the United States who had advanced melanoma and received two different rounds of cancer treatment. The study found that most patients received immune-boosting drugs as their first treatment, but when those stopped working, doctors switched to different therapies based on whether the patient's cancer had a specific genetic mutation called BRAF V600. Patients whose cancers had the BRAF mutation were more likely to receive targeted drugs designed to attack that mutation in their second round of treatment, while those without the mutation continued with immune-boosting drugs. The researchers concluded that while treatment approaches for advanced melanoma are changing over time, there is still no clear best strategy for what to do when the first treatment fails, highlighting the need for better studies and new treatment options.

title: Respiratory rate and minute ventilation independently modulate cardiovascular and autonomic responses in healthy adults.
abstract: Respiration influences autonomic and cardiovascular function, yet the independent contributions of respiratory rate (RR) and minute ventilation (MV) remain unclear. We investigated how RR and MV independently and interactively affect cardiovascular and autonomic responses using a 2 × 2 controlled-breathing design in 19 healthy adults (24.6 ± 1.2 years): spontaneous RR versus slow RR (6 breaths/min), combined with MV at 100% versus 180% of resting baseline. We recorded heart rate (HR), stroke volume (SV), cardiac output (CO), and heart rate variability (SDNN). Elevating MV to 180% significantly increased HR (5-8%) and CO (6-12%) across both respiratory rates (p < 0.01), whereas changing RR alone at constant MV produced no significant cardiovascular effects. Temporal analysis revealed a mechanistically biphasic CO response: the early rise (minutes 1-2) was driven by increasing SV while HR remained stable, whereas the sustained later elevation was driven by progressive HR increases as SV declined. Slow RR increased HRV by 75-86% (p < 0.01), indicating increased overall heart rate variability, which may reflect enhanced autonomic flexibility. Notably, combining slow RR with high MV produced concurrent increases in both HR and HRV, diverging from the typical inverse HR-HRV relationship and suggesting sympathetic-parasympathetic co-activation. These findings demonstrate a clear bifurcation in cardiorespiratory control, identifying minute ventilation as the primary driver of short-term systemic cardiovascular modulation. In contrast, respiratory rate remains the dominant determinant of cardiac autonomic regulation (HRV).© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Researchers examined how breathing patterns affect heart function and the nervous system's ability to regulate the heart, since previous studies showed these systems are connected but the exact mechanisms were unclear. The study involved nineteen healthy young adults who performed controlled breathing exercises at different rates and depths while researchers measured their heart rate, heart strength, and heart rate variability, which is the natural variation in time between heartbeats. The main finding was that breathing more air per minute increased heart rate and how much blood the heart pumped throughout the body, while breathing slowly without changing air volume increased heart rate variability, meaning the heart showed more flexibility in its rhythm. These results suggest that the amount of air you breathe controls immediate changes in heart pumping power, while the speed of your breathing controls how well your nervous system can adjust your heart's rhythm. Future research should explore whether these breathing techniques could help people manage heart health or stress, and whether the findings apply to people with heart or breathing conditions.

title: Butyrate epigenetically licenses sustained epithelial-T cell crosstalk for intestinal immune tolerance.
abstract: Intestinal epithelial cells (IEC) are the primary cell type in direct contact with stimuli from the luminal microbiota, playing a critical role in host-microbe interactions. However, how IECs communicate with underlying immune cells to maintain homeostasis remains poorly understood. In addition, the mechanisms by which IECs sense microbiota-derived stimuli to initiate this crosstalk are not yet fully understood. Here, we demonstrate that oral administration of the gut microbiota metabolite butyrate induces sustained IL-10 production in CD4⁺ T cells, conferring long-lasting protection against intestinal inflammation even after treatment withdrawal. This persistent immunoregulatory effect is also observed in germ-free mice, indicating the establishment of a butyrate-conditioned intestinal environment. By metabolomic profiling, we identify N1-acetylspermidine as a metabolite contributing to the IL-10-inducing activity of butyrate-treated IEC-conditioned medium. Mechanistically, butyrate induces sustained transcriptional and epigenetic activation of the acetylpolyamine biosynthetic enzyme Sat1 in IECs, which catalyzes the acetylation of spermidine to generate N1-acetylspermidine, and this activation persists after butyrate withdrawal. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism by which butyrate sensing establishes persistent crosstalk between IECs and T cells, thereby maintaining intestinal immune tolerance through epigenetic regulation and reprogramming of epithelial metabolism.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined how the intestines maintain a healthy balance between beneficial bacteria and the immune system, which is important because problems with this balance can lead to inflammatory bowel diseases. The team studied how butyrate, a substance produced when gut bacteria break down fiber, helps intestinal cells communicate with immune cells called T cells to prevent harmful inflammation. They found that when mice received butyrate treatment, their T cells produced more of a protective substance called IL-10, and this protective effect lasted long after the treatment stopped, even in mice without any bacteria in their guts. The researchers discovered that butyrate works by triggering intestinal cells to produce a specific molecule called N1-acetylspermidine, which signals T cells to become more tolerant and less likely to cause inflammation. These findings suggest that butyrate could potentially be used as a treatment to help people with inflammatory bowel disease maintain intestinal health by strengthening the communication between gut cells and the immune system.

title: Medical strategies of cardiovascular protection to reduce cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity: where do we stand?
abstract: Cancer therapy has dramatically changed over the past many decades, not only in efficacy but also complexity, with targeted therapeutics that have novel mechanisms of action. As a direct result of these remarkable treatments that have extended the lives of many patients, the increased recognition of cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction as well as the broader description of cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) has become obvious. The discipline of cardio-oncology has accepted the challenge to provide excellent cardiovascular (CV) protection for our patients being treated for cancer in order to achieve the best overall outcomes. The successful application of optimal CV protection by cardio-oncology needs to incorporate basic principles to realise these improved overall outcomes. Critical paradigm principles include: (1) using effective CV therapy; (2) targeting the likely mechanisms of action responsible for CTR-CVT; and (3) documenting cancers and cancer therapies associated with high CTR-CVT. Such a CV protection paradigm is likely to have the biggest impact and confirm an improved overall outcome. In addition, it is important to emphasise that knowing those cancers with high CTR-CVT risk requires careful comparative study of CV endpoints during exploratory cancer trials. Furthermore, astute clinical observations of specific CTR-CVT should be routinely reported to allow the development of strategies that minimise the negative impact of CTR-CVT. Lastly, coordinated efforts that allow realistic goals of cancer treatment while minimising the impact of CTR-CVT are the end goal in order to eliminate CV disease as a barrier to effective cancer treatment.© Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2026. llm_summary: Modern cancer treatments have become much more effective at saving lives, but they can also damage the heart and blood vessels as a side effect, which doctors now recognize as an important health problem that needs attention. A medical field called cardio-oncology has developed to help protect the hearts of cancer patients while they receive treatment, using specific strategies based on how different cancer drugs work and which cancers carry the highest risk of heart damage. The researchers suggest that successful heart protection requires three main steps: using proven heart medicines, targeting the specific ways cancer drugs harm the heart, and identifying which cancer types and treatments pose the greatest danger to patients' cardiovascular health. To make real progress, doctors need to carefully track heart health during cancer treatment trials, report problems they observe, and work together to balance the goal of treating cancer effectively with the goal of preventing heart damage. By taking these coordinated steps, doctors can prevent cardiovascular disease from becoming a barrier that stops cancer patients from receiving the best possible treatment.

title: Novel BCG Combination or Modified BCG Regimens in BCG-Naïve High-risk Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: Despite Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) remaining the standard of care for high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (HR-NMIBC), novel combination strategies are being actively investigated. Comparative evidence on the efficacy and tolerability of these regimens in BCG-naïve patients remains limited. The objective of this study was to synthesize and compare the efficacy and safety of treatments for BCG-naïve HR-NMIBC evaluated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs).A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science was performed through October 20, 2025, following a registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420251079219). Eligible studies were phase III RCTs enrolling adults with BCG-naïve HR-NMIBC that reported recurrence-free survival (RFS), event-free survival (EFS), disease-free survival (DFS), and common terminology criteria for adverse events (CTCAE)-graded AEs. Two independent reviewers extracted data following PRISMA guidelines. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses and a frequentist network meta-analysis (NMA) were performed. Primary outcomes were tumor recurrences, with secondary outcomes including EFS and DFS, AEs, and subgroup analyses.Five phase III RCTs (n = 3486) met inclusion criteria. Pooled analyses showed 1-yr and 2-yr EFS/DFS for combination therapy of 87% (95% CI 85-89) and 82% (95% CI 79-85) versus 84% (95% CI 82-87) and 78% (95% CI 75-81) with BCG (induction + maintenance [I + M]). In trials with centrally-adjudicated high-grade recurrence, ICI + BCG (I + M) reduced HG-recurrence (RR 0.63; 95% CI 0.41-0.98). Including ALBAN attenuated the effect (RR 0.75; 95% CI 0.50-1.12). Subgroup analyses favored ICI + BCG (I + M) in CIS and T1 disease (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.50-0.92). Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 25% of combination-treated patients versus 6% with BCG alone.Interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in treatment regimens, diagnostic definitions, and incomplete reporting of key prognostic factors, including variant histology, lymphovascular invasion, programmed cell death ligand 1 status, and transurethral resection of bladder tumor quality, contributing to between-study variability.The modest, heterogeneity-sensitive recurrence benefit of adding systemic ICI to BCG (I + M), set against a marked increase in toxicity and no demonstrated survival gain, does not justify routine systemic intensification in unselected BCG-naïve HR-NMIBC. Its use should instead be individualized to higher-risk subgroups pending biomarker-driven selection and mature survival data.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). Published by Elsevier B.V. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether adding new immunotherapy drugs to the standard bladder cancer treatment called BCG could help patients with high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, which is cancer that has not spread to the muscle layer of the bladder. The team reviewed five major clinical trials involving over 3,400 patients to compare how well different treatment combinations worked and how many side effects patients experienced. The results showed that combining immunotherapy drugs with BCG provided only a modest improvement in preventing cancer from coming back, with slightly better outcomes at one and two years compared to BCG alone, but this benefit was not consistent across all studies. However, patients who received the combination treatment experienced significantly more severe side effects, with about one in four patients having serious complications compared to only one in twenty-five patients receiving BCG alone. The researchers concluded that adding immunotherapy to standard BCG treatment should not be given to all patients routinely because the small benefit does not outweigh the increased risk of harm, and instead doctors should carefully select which patients might benefit based on individual risk factors and future research on genetic markers.

title: Evaluation of Spin Bias in Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Comparing Bankart Repair with Remplissage Versus the Latarjet Procedure.
abstract: Anterior shoulder instability is common in young, active patients and, when managed surgically, is typically treated with either Bankart repair with remplissage or a bony procedure such as Latarjet. Both procedures have demonstrated favorable clinical outcomes, but differences in recurrent instability, complications, functional outcomes, and return-to-sport rates continue to be debated. In the setting of ongoing clinical equipoise and heterogeneous evidence, systematic reviews and meta-analyses may help guide treatment decisions. The aim of this study was to assess the prevalence of spin bias, defined as misrepresentation or overinterpretation of study findings, in the abstracts of systematic reviews comparing these procedures, and its potential influence on clinical decision-making.A systematic review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses comparing arthroscopic Bankart repair with remplissage to the Latarjet procedure for anterior shoulder instability was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and the Cochrane Handbook. MEDLINE, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Database of systematic reviews were searched from inception to October 29, 2025. Eligible studies were published in English and reported ≥1 clinical outcome. Abstracts were assessed independently in duplicate for 15 domains of spin while the methodological quality of included studies was evaluated using AMSTAR-2. Descriptive statistics were calculated, and exploratory comparisons were performed for studies with versus without the most common spin types.Thirteen systematic reviews were included, seven of which incorporated meta-analyses, with a median of 16 primary studies and 778 shoulders per review. Spin was identified in 12 of 13 abstracts (92.3%), most related to misleading reporting (51.2%) and misleading interpretation (41.5%). Spin Types 5 (claims of benefit despite high risk of bias) and 12 (claims of equivalence despite non-significant results with wide confidence intervals) were most frequent (each 46.2%). No significant associations were identified between the presence of Type 5 or Type 12 spin and study characteristics. AMSTAR-2 assessments revealed ten systematic reviews with "critically low" and three with "low" methodological quality, primarily due to failure to report funding sources, assess the impact of risk of bias, and justify included study designs.Spin is highly prevalent in abstracts of systematic reviews and meta-analyses comparing Bankart repair with remplissage to the Latarjet procedure. Most included systematic reviews were rated as low or critically low quality by AMSTAR-2, with abstract conclusions frequently overstating benefit or equivalence despite limited evidence. Clinicians should interpret these findings with caution when using systematic reviews to guide management of anterior shoulder instability.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether systematic reviews comparing two surgical procedures for shoulder instability were presenting their findings fairly and accurately to doctors and patients. The team looked at thirteen published systematic reviews, which are summaries of multiple research studies on the same topic, and checked their abstracts (the brief summaries at the beginning) for signs of spin, meaning misleading or exaggerated claims about what the evidence actually showed. They found that twelve out of thirteen reviews contained some form of spin, with most reviews making claims that one treatment was better or equal to another even though the actual evidence did not clearly support these conclusions. The reviews themselves were also found to have serious quality problems, with ten rated as critically low quality because they failed to report important information like who funded the research and whether they properly checked for bias in the studies they reviewed. Doctors should be cautious when using these systematic reviews to decide how to treat patients with shoulder instability and should look for more reliable evidence before making treatment decisions.

title: The Vascular Contribution to Dementia. World Stroke Organisation Scientific Statement.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and cerebrovascular pathology are the two most common causes of dementia, frequently co-occurring in older people. Community-based neuropathology studies indicate that vascular disease accounts for approximately one third of the population attributable risk of dementia, controlling for other pathologies (including AD). The proportion with vascular disease as co-pathology is likely to be higher (50-70%).The most common vascular substrate is cerebral small vessel disease, which includes small artery fibrosis (arteriolosclerosis), vascular amyloid deposits (cerebral amyloid angiopathy) and monogenic forms of small vessel disease, the commonest being Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL). Post-stroke cognitive impairment following both ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage also contribute. In this World Stroke Organisation (WSO) scientific statement we assembled a multi-disciplinary international group of experts to review the vascular contribution to dementia, encompassing both vascular and neurodegenerative dementia. This statement has been reviewed and approved by the WSO executive.We summarize the epidemiology, neuropathology, cognitive profile, clinical impact and management of vascular disease in dementia, and discuss the recent VasCog-2-WSO diagnostic criteria. We consider the substantial overlap with clinical stroke and with AD dementia. We catalogue transcriptomic and proteomic studies that have revealed novel candidate molecules (COL4A1/4A2, HTRA1, TRIM47, FOXF2) as possible treatment targets. We appraise imaging-based biomarkers relevant to vascular disease, and potential biochemical markers (VEGF-A, PLGF, IL-6, MMP9, CTSB). We highlight the potential for vascular interventions to treat not only vascular dementia, but also the vascular component of neurodegenerative dementia. We review recent clinical trials targeting multiple pathways, including nitric oxide signalling, high blood pressure, the GABAergic system, angiogenic activity, microglial inhibition, PDE3 and PDE5 inhibition, as well as dietary supplementation with omega-3-fatty acid, s-equol and vitamin E. Finally, we consider upcoming opportunities and challenges relevant to vascular disease in dementia.

llm_summary: Dementia, or loss of memory and thinking skills, is often caused by two main problems in the brain: Alzheimer's disease and damage to blood vessels, which frequently happen together in older people. A group of international experts reviewed all available scientific evidence about how blood vessel disease contributes to dementia, including studies of brain tissue after death and modern brain imaging scans. They found that blood vessel problems, especially damage to tiny blood vessels in the brain called cerebral small vessel disease, account for about one third of dementia cases on their own and appear alongside other brain diseases in half to seventy percent of dementia patients. The experts identified several new molecules and blood markers that could potentially become targets for future medicines, and they reviewed recent clinical trials testing various treatments ranging from blood pressure medications to dietary supplements like omega-3 fatty acids. This scientific statement highlights that treating blood vessel disease in the brain could help prevent or slow dementia in many people, though researchers still need to conduct more studies to determine which treatments work best and how to identify patients most likely to benefit.

llm_summary: Background:  Mitral valve disease occurs when the valve between the heart's left chambers doesn't work properly, either leaking blood backward or not opening fully, and doctors have traditionally focused on measuring how severe the problem is using imaging tests. Artificial intelligence is now being used to go beyond simply quantifying the disease to help doctors understand the underlying biological mechanisms and reasons why the valve fails in the first place.

title: Spatial Configuration of Pancreatic Cancer Is Associated with Disease Recurrence after Neoadjuvant Therapy and Curative-Intent Resection.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) frequently recurs after neoadjuvant therapy (NT) and curative-intent resection. Although major pathologic response predicts favorable outcomes, most patients achieve only minor response with heterogeneous recurrence risk. We asked whether the spatial organization of residual PDAC encodes clinically relevant biology beyond residual tumor burden.In a retrospective cohort of 203 resected PDAC patients treated with NT and restricted to minor pathologic response, routine H&E whole-slide images were segmented into cancer and stroma using an AI-enabled pipeline. Spatial composition (patch density, edge density) and configuration (compactness/complexity, intermixing) were quantified and tested associations with disease-free survival (DFS) using multivariable models adjusted for standard clinicopathologic factors.Shorter DFS was associated with a fragmented, interface-rich tumor-stroma ecology featuring higher edge density and diversity and reduced homotypic aggregation, independent of clinicopathologic variables. Two spatial risk models were independently prognostic: (i) cancer mean shape index plus stromal shape-index variability (adjusted HR 1.71; P=0.003) and (ii) mean stromal patch area plus edge density (adjusted HR 2.19; P=0.002). Both models stratified outcomes where pathologic response grading and residual cancer area did not. High-risk configurations were further associated with reduced intratumoral tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) density and infiltration ratio, with relative TIL accumulation at the cancer periphery and within the stroma, consistent with an immune-excluded phenotype.Residual cancer-stroma topology quantified from standard H&E slides yields independent prognostic signals after NT in PDAC, provides a cellular immune correlate for spatial risk, and motivates prospective validation and spatially informed adjuvant strategies.

llm_summary: Pancreatic cancer often comes back after patients receive chemotherapy and surgery, even when doctors remove all visible tumors, so researchers wanted to understand why some patients do better than others. Scientists studied 203 pancreatic cancer patients who had received chemotherapy before surgery and examined their tumor tissue samples under a microscope, using artificial intelligence to map out how cancer cells and supporting tissue were arranged in a spatial pattern. They found that tumors with a fragmented, scattered appearance with more boundaries between cancer and healthy tissue were linked to cancer returning sooner, and this pattern was a better predictor of outcomes than traditional measures like how much tumor remained. The researchers discovered that these high-risk spatial patterns were connected to fewer immune cells fighting the cancer inside the tumor, with immune cells instead gathering around the edges rather than throughout the tumor itself. These findings suggest that analyzing the physical organization of tumors from standard tissue samples could help doctors identify which patients need more aggressive follow-up treatment and could guide new strategies to improve survival rates.

title: Mayo Test Drive Español: A model of digital cognitive test adaptation.
abstract: Objective: Test adaptations for Spanish are typically 1:1 translations of traditional paper-and-pencil tests that prioritize the fidelity of the original measure and have not undergone cross-cultural adaptation. Mayo Test Development through Rapid Iteration, Validation, and Expansion-Español (Mayo Test Drive-Español) is an adaptation of digital cognitive tests (Stricker Learning Span, Symbols Test) for and by heterogeneous Spanish speaking populations via a mixed methods approach. Method: Participants who spoke Spanish as a first and/or primary language, living in or outside of the United States, were recruited for the Mayo Test Drive-Español registry to complete surveys assessing linguistic background, familiarity with cognitive testing, cognitive diagnoses, and technological accessibility. A subsample completed additional questionnaires and virtual focus groups including cognitive interviewing and direct feedback on test instructions/stimuli. Iterative adaptations and alternative sets of stimuli/instructions were presented to subsequent focus groups and underwent team review. Saturation was determined by team consensus. Professional transcriptions of focus groups were analyzed qualitatively. Results: A subsample of Mayo Test Drive-Español registry participants (n = 85) were enrolled into 10 focus groups (n = 38, 1-7 per group). 8 iterative revisions of test stimuli (including 54/92 words) and 9 iterative revisions of instructions were made based on focus group feedback, team meetings, and quality control procedures. Transcribed sessions were analyzed for themes related to the platform, paradigms/construct, instructions, and content. Conclusions: Mayo Test Drive-Español demonstrates the importance of early input from stakeholders (professionals, patients, community members) from various regions to improve the adaptation of cognitive measures for different languages and contexts.  .

llm_summary: Researchers examined how to adapt digital cognitive tests, which are computer-based tools that measure thinking and memory skills, for Spanish-speaking people from different backgrounds and regions. The team created a process where Spanish speakers themselves helped shape the tests by providing feedback through surveys, focus groups, and one-on-one interviews about whether the test instructions and content made sense to them. Based on what participants told them, the researchers made eight rounds of changes to the test words and nine rounds of changes to the instructions, ultimately modifying more than half of the original words used in the tests. The study shows that when you involve patients, doctors, and community members from various places in the process of adapting tests for different languages, you create better tools that actually work for the people who will use them. This approach of getting real feedback from the people who speak the language is more effective than simply translating tests word-for-word from English to Spanish without considering cultural differences and regional variations.

title: Modifiable Risk Factors and Attributable Ischemic Heart Disease Mortality in US States, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract: Ischemic heart disease (IHD), the leading cause of death in the US, is predominantly due to modifiable risk factors. Estimates of IHD mortality attributable to risk factors provide evidence for health policy decision-making.To estimate the burden of IHD death attributable to risk factors in the US from 1990-2023.The Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 (GBD 2023) used vital records and a broad set of epidemiologic data to estimate IHD death rates, risk factor exposure, and relative risk curves for risk-outcome pairs for 1990-2023 for the general population. Data analysis was performed from October 2024 to December 2025.Twelve metabolic, behavioral, and environmental risk factors.The primary outcomes were IHD death rates per 100 000 persons, counts, and attributable risks from 1990-2023 by age, sex, and US state. Estimates include 95% uncertainty intervals (UI). IHD death rates were estimated using ensemble modeling methods. Risk exposures were estimated using bayesian meta-regression methods. Relative risks were estimated following the Burden of Proof framework.In 2023, there were 473 000 IHD deaths (95% UI, 414 000-510 000) in the US, a decrease of 58.7% (95% UI, 56.8%-61.0%) in age-standardized rate since 1990. Between 2010 and 2023, there was a 19.0% decrease (95% UI, 15.0%-22.9%) for males and a 24.5% decrease (95% UI, 20.3%-29.7%) for females in IHD death rates. High systolic blood pressure (SBP), dietary risks, and high low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) were the leading risk factors for IHD deaths in 2023, accounting for 47.2% (95% UI, 36.4%-57.0%), 38.6% (95% UI, 17.2%-56.8%), and 28.5% (95% UI, 19.3%-39.6%) of IHD deaths, respectively. Increased exposure to several risk factors substantially increased their attributable burden for IHD deaths in 2023, with high fasting plasma glucose (FPG) increasing 38.8% (95% UI, 11.5%-81.1%) and high body mass index (BMI) increasing 54.5% (95% UI, 41.8%-66.3%) since 1990. Smoking and particulate matter pollution had the greatest decrease in attributable IHD mortality since 1990, at 33.3% (95% UI, 23.6%-41.7%) and 74.9% (95% UI, 46.7%-88.8%), respectively.Per the results of this systematic analysis of GBD 2023, a total of 88.7% (95% UI, 83.4%-92.5%) of IHD deaths were attributable to modifiable risk factors in the US in 2023, with high SBP, dietary risks, and high LDL-C being the greatest contributors. High BMI and high FPG showed the largest attribution increases, while exposure to other risks did not increase significantly for the population.
