llm_summary: Heart disease caused by blocked arteries, known as ischemic heart disease, remains the leading cause of death in the United States, yet most deaths from this condition could be prevented by controlling modifiable risk factors like high blood pressure, poor diet, and high cholesterol. Researchers analyzed death records and health data collected over more than thirty years from 1990 to 2023 to determine which specific risk factors were responsible for the most heart disease deaths across different states, ages, and sexes in America. In 2023, nearly 473,000 Americans died from ischemic heart disease, but the good news is that the death rate has dropped by almost 59 percent since 1990, with particularly steep declines between 2010 and 2023 for both men and women. The study found that high blood pressure, unhealthy diets, and elevated cholesterol levels were responsible for nearly half of all ischemic heart disease deaths, while weight gain and high blood sugar levels showed the largest increases in their contribution to deaths since 1990. These findings suggest that nearly 89 percent of heart disease deaths in America could be prevented through lifestyle changes and medical management of these controll.

title: Development and Validation of a Simplified Martin-Hopkins LDL-C Equation Using Machine Learning.
abstract: Although the Martin-Hopkins equation is widely validated and used to estimate low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) for clinical care, a simplified equation could streamline implementation and enable broader adoption.To develop a simplified machine learning-based alternative to the Martin-Hopkins equation using multivariate adaptive regression splines (LDL-C-MH-MARS) and compare its performance with the Friedewald (LDL-C-F), Sampson-National Institutes of Health (LDL-C-S), Modified Sampson (LDL-C-MS), and Martin-Hopkins (LDL-C-MH) equations.The Very Large Database of Lipids is a cross-sectional database of clinical lipid measurements from a population-representative convenience sample of adult and pediatric patients. Lipid measurements were performed by Vertical Auto Profile ultracentrifugation between October 1, 2015, and June 30, 2019. The study included patients with complete lipid panel data who were randomly assigned to a training set and a test set. External validation against preparative ultracentrifugation-based LDL-C measurements was performed in reference laboratory datasets from the Mayo Clinic (broad LDL-C concentrations) and the Further Cardiovascular Outcomes Research With Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type 9 (PCSK9) Inhibition in Subjects with Elevated Risk (FOURIER) trial (observations from patients with low LDL-C concentrations while taking evolocumab). Study data were analyzed from January to October 2025.LDL-C-F, LDL-C-S, LDL-C-MS, LDL-C-MH, and LDL-C-MH-MARS equations.Accuracy of estimated vs ultracentrifugation-measured LDL-C concentration based on bias, root mean square error (RMSE), and concordance by guideline-based categories.The study included 4 939 528 patients (mean [SD] age, 56 [16] years; 2 635 486 female [53%]) with complete lipid panel data who were randomly assigned to a training set (n = 3 292 889) and a test set (n = 1 646 639). LDL-C-MH-MARS equation demonstrated a very low median (IQR) bias of -0.1 (-2.1 to 1.8) mg/dL (to convert to millimoles per liter, multiply by 0.0259), comparable with LDL-C-MH. The median (IQR) difference between the MARS and original Martin-Hopkins equations (ie, LDL-C-MH-MARS - LDL-C-MH) was -0.5 (-1.2 to 0) mg/dL, further suggesting comparability between the 2 methods. The RMSE was smallest for LDL-C-MH-MARS (4.7 mg/dL) and LDL-C-MH (4.9 mg/dL), followed by LDL-C-S (5.8 mg/dL), LDL-C-MS (6.0 mg/dL), and LDL-C-F (7.2 mg/dL). The proportion of patients correctly classified according to clinical categories was nearly identical for LDL-C-MH-MARS (89.7%) and LDL-C-MH (89.6%) but lower for LDL-C-S (86.3%), LDL-C-MS (84.7%), and LDL-C-F (83.1%). The LDL-C-MH-MARS, LDL-C-MH, LDL-C-MS, LDL-C-S, and LDL-C-F equations underestimated LDL-C concentration in 16%, 17%, 28%, 39%, and 60%, respectively, when classifying LDL-C less than 70 mg/dL in patients with triglyceride concentrations of 200 to 399 mg/dL (to convert to millimoles per liter, multiply by 0.0113). The patterns of results were similar in external validation datasets, with the LDL-C-MH-MARS and LDL-C-MH equations demonstrating the highest accuracy.Study results suggest that the new machine learning-based LDL-C equation provided results comparable with those of the original Martin-Hopkins method while simplifying implementation to a single equation.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a new machine learning method could simplify the way doctors estimate cholesterol levels in the blood, specifically a type called LDL cholesterol that contributes to heart disease risk. The study involved nearly five million patients whose cholesterol measurements were analyzed to develop and test a simplified equation using a computer learning technique, then compared it against four existing methods that doctors currently use. The new simplified equation performed just as well as the original complex method it was based on, with very small errors and correctly classifying patients into appropriate cholesterol risk categories nearly ninety percent of the time. This new approach could make it easier for hospitals and clinics to calculate accurate cholesterol estimates since it requires less complicated math while maintaining the same level of accuracy as more complex formulas. The findings suggest that this simplified machine learning method could be adopted more widely in clinical practice to help doctors better manage their patients' heart disease risk through more accurate cholesterol assessment.

abstract: We describe a case of a child with macrolide-resistant Mycobacterium abscessus who initially had clinical improvement on a dual β-lactam regimen but continued to have positive cultures. Suitable phages active against the bacterial strain were identified, administered both systemically and directly to the ear, and were associated with microbiological remission.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: A child suffered from a serious ear bone infection caused by a bacteria called Mycobacterium abscessus that had become resistant to common antibiotic medicines. Doctors first tried treating the infection with strong antibiotics called beta-lactams, which helped at first, but the bacteria kept growing back and showing up in tests. The medical team identified special viruses called bacteriophages, which are tiny organisms that naturally attack and kill bacteria, and gave them to the patient both through the bloodstream and directly into the infected ear. After receiving the bacteriophage treatment, the patient's infection finally cleared up and the bacteria stopped appearing in medical tests. This case shows that bacteriophage therapy, which uses viruses to fight drug-resistant bacterial infections, may offer hope for patients whose infections do not respond to traditional antibiotics.

title: Risk factors associated with cardiovascular hospital admissions and all-cause mortality in cancer patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are highly effective cancer therapies. However, they are associated with considerable adverse cardiovascular (CV) outcomes. We investigated the risk factors for CV hospitalisations and all-cause mortality in oncology patients receiving ICIs.A retrospective cohort study of adult patients administered ICIs between 1st January 2010 and 1st January 2020 in New South Wales, Australia. Electronic medical records were accessed to obtain demographic and clinical data. Univariate analysis included Chi-squared test for categorical variables and Student's t-test for continuous variables. Binary logistic regression was used for multivariate analysis. Mortality was analysed using Cox regression including (i) time-dependent Cox models with CV admission as a time-varying covariate and (ii) a 1-year landmark sensitivity analysis.Out of 1,080 patients receiving ICIs during the study period, 340 patients (31.5%) had at least one CV hospital admission, and 763 patients (70.6%) had died by the end of the follow-up period. On multivariable analysis, prior history of heart failure and/or cardiomyopathy (p < 0.001), arrhythmia (p < 0.001) and ischaemic heart disease (p < 0.001) were independently associated with an increased risk of CV hospital admission by approximately fourfold, while CV hospitalisation during follow-up (p < 0.001) was independently associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality. In a time-dependent Cox model (n = 928; excluding CV admissions with missing admission timing), CV admission was associated with higher subsequent mortality (HR 3.29 [95% CI 2.70-4.02]; p < 0.001). In a 1-year landmark sensitivity analysis among patients alive at 365 days (n = 533), CV admission within 1 year was associated with higher subsequent mortality (HR 2.36 [95% CI 1.61-3.45]; p < 0.001).In cancer patients treated with ICIs, pre-existing CV risk factors significantly increase the risk of CV hospitalisations and all-cause mortality. Appropriate CV risk monitoring and management should be considered for people with cancer receiving ICI therapy.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Immune checkpoint inhibitors are powerful cancer drugs that help the body fight tumors, but they can cause serious heart problems as a side effect. Researchers looked at over one thousand cancer patients in Australia who received these drugs between 2010 and 2020, tracking their hospital visits and deaths to understand which patients faced the highest risk. They found that patients who already had heart conditions like heart failure, irregular heartbeats, or blocked arteries were about four times more likely to be hospitalized for heart problems while taking these cancer drugs. Importantly, patients who did end up in the hospital for heart issues during their cancer treatment had significantly higher chances of dying from any cause compared to those who did not have heart hospitalizations. The study suggests that doctors should carefully monitor and manage heart health in cancer patients receiving these drugs, especially those who already have existing heart conditions.

title: Dyssynergic defecation in adolescents with constipation: Anorectal manometry findings.
abstract: To describe and compare anorectal manometry findings in constipated adolescents with and without dyssynergic defecation (DD).We retrospectively reviewed adolescents ≤18 years who underwent anorectal manometry (ARM) and/or balloon expulsion testing (BET) between 2015 and 2022. Patients with prior pelvic floor therapy, inflammatory bowel disease, or colon surgery were excluded. DD was defined by abnormal ARM (paradoxical anal contraction or inadequate anal relaxation ≤20% during simulated evacuation) and/or abnormal BET (>60 s). Manometric parameters were compared between patients with and without DD and between those with abnormal versus normal BET. Diagnostic performance of rectoanal pressure gradient cutoffs were assessed.A total of 170 adolescents were included; 69 (40.6%) met criteria for DD. Median age was 17 years (interquartile range [IQR] 16-18), and 80.7% were female. Gastrointestinal symptoms did not differ between groups. Patients with DD demonstrated significantly more negative rectoanal pressure gradients compared with those without DD (median [IQR]: -49.0 mmHg [-73.9 to -31.4] vs. -25.2 mmHg [-40.2 to -9.8]; p < 0.001). Rectal sensory thresholds did not differ significantly between groups. A rectoanal pressure gradient cutoff of -45 mmHg demonstrated the best balance of sensitivity (58%) and specificity (86%) for identifying DD. Depression was more prevalent among adolescents with DD (p = 0.007).Rectoanal pressure gradient is a useful manometric parameter for identifying DD in constipated adolescents, particularly when BET is unavailable. Psychological factors such as depression may be more prevalent in this population.© 2026 European Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition and North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a group of adolescents with constipation to understand a condition called dyssynergic defecation, which happens when the muscles around the rectum and anus don't work together properly during bowel movements. The study looked back at medical records from 2015 to 2022 for 170 teenagers who had special tests called anorectal manometry, which measures the pressure and muscle function in the lower bowel area. They found that teenagers with dyssynergic defecation had significantly more negative pressure differences between the rectum and anus compared to those without the condition, and depression was more common in the group with dyssynergic defecation. A specific pressure measurement called the rectoanal pressure gradient, set at negative 45 millimeters of mercury, was found to be useful for identifying which teenagers had this muscle coordination problem. These findings suggest that doctors can use this pressure measurement to help diagnose dyssynergic defecation when other tests are not available, and they should also pay attention to mental health issues like depression in teenagers with constipation problems.

title: Consensus on Biomarker Utility for ACTH-Dependent Cushing's Syndrome: A Pituitary Society Modified Delphi Panel.
abstract: Biochemical test results are central to clinical decision-making for the diagnosis and management of Cushing's syndrome (CS). With emerging research and increasing availability of different tests, updated consensus on the utility of these biomarkers is warranted.To establish an updated consensus on the role of biomarkers in the diagnosis and monitoring of adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent CS, address novel therapeutic approaches, and identify areas for future research.A modified two-round Delphi panel was conducted. Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement/disagreement for Likert-scale statements or ≥70% selection of the same option for single-choice questions.Participants represented a range of international expertise.Forty-one participants took part in the Delphi panel, with no attrition between rounds (one non-clinician was not required to complete the second round). An eight-member Steering Committee guided statement development.Of statements designed to reach consensus, 45% (14/31) and 44% (11/25) statements reached consensus in Rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Notably, most panelists reported the use of late-night salivary cortisol for diagnosis of mild CS and for monitoring following pituitary surgery or medical or radiation therapy. Most panelists responded that block-and-replace therapies can be considered in patients with cyclical or severe CS, and consensus was reached that restoration of circadian rhythm is a treatment goal for patients with CS.Areas of alignment among experts on the diagnosis and monitoring of CS are presented. The findings from this study are intended to support clinicians in their clinical decision-making and highlight priority areas for future research.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Doctors need clear guidance on which blood tests and other measurements work best for diagnosing and monitoring Cushing's syndrome, a serious condition where the body produces too much of a stress hormone called cortisol. A group of international experts used a structured voting process called a modified Delphi panel, where participants answered questions in two rounds to reach agreement on the most useful biomarkers, which are measurable signs of disease found in blood or saliva. The experts reached consensus on several important points, including that late-night saliva cortisol tests are helpful for diagnosing mild cases and monitoring patients after surgery or treatment, and that restoring the body's natural daily rhythm of cortisol is an important treatment goal. These findings provide doctors with clearer recommendations for choosing the right tests and treatments when caring for patients with this condition. The study also identifies areas where more research is needed to improve how doctors diagnose and manage Cushing's syndrome in the future.

title: Metabolomic analyses of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, muscle cramps, and TJ-68 treatment.
abstract: Most patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a fatal motor neuron disease, experience painful muscle cramps. Our recent pilot trial of the Japanese Kampo medicine TJ-68 suggested its efficacy in improving muscle cramps in patients with ALS.This study analyzed plasma metabolomic changes to identify the underlying mechanisms of muscle cramps in ALS and the effects of TJ-68.Plasma was obtained from 11 participants with ALS in the repeated crossover trial at five time points (baseline, two placebo phases, and two TJ-68 phases). Metabolites were analyzed using mass spectrometry. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to identify metabolite changes associated with muscle cramps, determine the effects of TJ-68 on metabolites, and predict which participants would respond to TJ-68.Higher glutamine/glutamate, arginine, and leucine levels were associated with more severe muscle cramps. TJ-68 treatment increased tryptophan and aconitate levels but reduced serotonin and acetylcarnitine levels. Long-chain acylcarnitine levels were correlated with muscle cramp severity, and their levels tended to decrease with treatment. Uric acid, β-aminoisobutyric acid, α-aminoadipic acid, and acetylcholine emerged as predictors of the efficacy of TJ-68.This study identified the metabolite profile of muscle cramps in ALS and the changes in metabolite levels after TJ-68 treatment. Several baseline metabolites were associated with the prediction of the response to muscle cramps following TJ-68 treatment. Uric acid might be particularly useful because of its easy measurement in standard assays. Our study affirms the value of metabolomic technology for future pharmacotherapy and studies in ALS.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined a Japanese herbal medicine called TJ-68 to understand how it might help reduce painful muscle cramps that affect most patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, a serious disease that damages nerve cells controlling muscles. The study involved eleven patients with this disease who participated in a crossover trial, meaning they received both the herbal medicine and a placebo at different times, while researchers measured chemical substances in their blood using specialized equipment. The researchers found that certain chemicals in the blood, including amino acids like glutamine and arginine, were linked to more severe muscle cramps, while the herbal medicine changed levels of other chemicals such as tryptophan and reduced harmful substances like acetylcarnitine. The study identified specific baseline chemicals, particularly uric acid which is easy to measure in standard blood tests, that could predict which patients would benefit most from TJ-68 treatment. These findings suggest that measuring blood chemicals could help doctors personalize treatment for muscle cramps in patients with this disease and guide the development of new therapies in the future.

title: Placement of Triangular Titanium Implants Suprajacent to Pelvic Fixation Screws Reduces Pelvic Fixation Failure in Multilevel Spinal Fusion: Results of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine whether placement of triangular titanium implants (TTI) suprajacent to S2-alar-iliac (S2AI) pelvic fixation screws during multilevel spinal fusion surgery for adult spine deformity reduces pelvic fixation failures.This prospective, multicenter, international, partially blinded randomized clinical trial included 222 patients scheduled for multilevel spinal fusion surgery with S2AI-based pelvic fixation. In the S2AI+TTI group, the mean age was 64.9 years, 54.1% were female, 3.7% were Hispanic, 5.5% were African American, and 1.8% were Asian. In the S2AI-alone group, the mean age was 64.8 years, 58.4% were female, 3.5% were Hispanic, 7.1% were African American, and 0.9% were Asian. Subjects were randomized to pelvic fixation using S2AI screws alone versus S2AI+TTI. Scheduled follow-up included a 24-month full-spine radiograph and a high-resolution computed tomography (CT) scan, which was independently interpreted.The primary composite radiographic end point (S2AI screw breakage, lucency, or pullout, or posterior spinal rod breakage distal to S1) occurred less frequently in the S2AI+TTI group than in the S2AI-alone group (11.0% versus 20.4%, p = 0.0415). Except for rod-screw dissociation and rod fracture distal to S1, all components of the primary composite end point occurred less frequently in the S2AI+TTI group. TTI placement did not affect sagittal or coronal spinal alignment parameters. The rate of rod fracture throughout the spinal construct was slightly higher in the S2AI+TTI group (9.2% versus 5.3%) but the difference was not significant (p = 0.197).Placement of TTI suprajacent to S2AI screws reduced the rate of pelvic fixation failure in patients undergoing multilevel spinal fusion with pelvic fixation.Therapeutic Level I. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether adding small triangular titanium implants could improve the success of spinal fusion surgery, which is a procedure that joins bones in the spine together to treat severe spine problems in adults. The study involved 222 patients who were randomly assigned to receive either standard pelvic fixation screws alone or the same screws combined with the triangular titanium implants placed above them. After two years of follow-up with imaging scans, patients who received the additional titanium implants had significantly fewer problems like screw breakage, loosening, or pulling out compared to those who received screws alone. This finding suggests that adding these small titanium pieces above the pelvic fixation screws can help prevent the hardware from failing and improve the long-term success of spinal fusion surgery. While the results are promising, doctors should continue monitoring patients over time to confirm these benefits hold up and to ensure the implants do not cause other unexpected problems.

title: Breast Cancer Follow-Up and Surveillance After Primary Treatment: ASCO Guideline Update.
abstract: To offer clinicians recommendations concerning breast cancer follow-up and surveillance after primary treatment.ASCO convened an Expert Panel to develop recommendations based on a systematic review and a formal consensus process.One randomized controlled trial (RCT) was identified and formed the evidentiary basis for the surveillance mammography guideline recommendation. No RCTs were identified that evaluated different follow-up approaches by risk of relapse in patients treated for early-stage breast cancer. Given the dearth of evidence identified in the systematic review of the literature, formal modified Delphi consensus-based recommendations were generated.The guideline offers recommendations on the role of a risk-based approach to the frequency and intensity of follow-up among patients with breast cancer in the adjuvant setting. Regular history, physical examination, and mammography are recommended for breast cancer follow-up. Either virtual or in-person visits can be offered. Certain patients at high risk of cancer recurrence warrant closer surveillance, such as those patients with locally advanced disease or residual disease following neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Recommendations on the use of blood-based biomarkers and supplemental imaging are provided. Guideline recommendations will be updated once additional evidence-based tools become available to better individualize surveillance.Additional information is available at www.ascopubs.org/topics/asco-guidelines/breast-cancer.

llm_summary: The American Society of Clinical Oncology created new guidelines to help doctors know how to monitor breast cancer patients after their initial treatment is complete. Experts reviewed existing research studies and used a consensus process where specialists voted on recommendations to develop practical guidance for follow-up care. The guidelines recommend that patients receive regular physical exams, mammograms (breast imaging scans), and check-ins with their doctors, which can happen either in person or through virtual visits. Patients who have more aggressive cancers or who still have cancer remaining after chemotherapy need more frequent and intensive monitoring than those with lower-risk disease. The experts acknowledged that more research is needed in the future to create better tools for personalizing surveillance plans based on each patient's individual risk of cancer returning.

title: The Impact of Preference Signaling on Orthopedic Surgery Residency Interviews.
abstract: This study examines whether the effectiveness of preference signaling in obtaining interview offers for orthopedic surgery residency varies by program type and size.We conducted a retrospective cohort study of orthopedic surgery applicants in 2024 using the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) Residency Explorer Tool. The primary outcome was the "interview offer rate," defined as the number of interviews given to applicants who signaled the program divided by the number of signals sent. Programs were analyzed by type (academic or community) and size (small = ≤5 residents, medium = 6-8, large = ≥ 9). Data were evaluated via Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn post hoc tests.This study was performed at Duke University Medical School in Durham, North Carolina. There was no clinical care provided.We incorporated data from all MD, DO, IMG, and non-IMG applicants invited to interview at orthopedic surgery residency programs in 2024. Inclusion criteria were residency programs in the AAMC database which reported the rates of interviews offered to applicants who did and did not send a preference signal (120 programs total).Of 210 programs, 90 were excluded due to incomplete data, leaving 120 (57.1%). Across all institutions, applicants who signaled a program were significantly more likely to receive an interview offer (median 22% versus 1%, p < 0.001). For applicants who sent a signal, there was no significant difference in interview offer rate by program type, size, or type and size combined. There were also no significant differences across these metrics for applicants who did not signal a program.Interview rates for signals were consistent across program types and sizes, suggesting similar effects wherever signals are sent. All programs were unlikely to interview applicants who did not signal, highlighting the importance of careful signal selection.Copyright © 2026 Association of Program Directors in Surgery. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether signaling preference for a specific orthopedic surgery residency program, which is a way for medical school graduates to indicate their interest, actually helps applicants get interview offers, and whether this effect differs depending on the program's type and size. They studied data from 120 orthopedic surgery residency programs across the United States in 2024, comparing interview offer rates between applicants who sent a preference signal and those who did not. The results showed that applicants who signaled a program were dramatically more likely to receive an interview offer, with a median rate of 22 percent compared to just 1 percent for those who did not signal. Importantly, the benefit of signaling was consistent across all types of programs, whether they were academic or community-based and whether they were small, medium, or large in size. These findings suggest that applicants should carefully choose which programs to signal their interest to, since preference signaling appears to be an effective strategy across all residency programs.

title: The role of Vagus nerve stimulation in epilepsy with eyelid myoclonia - A case series.
abstract: To study the effectiveness of vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) in patients with epilepsy with eyelid myoclonia (EEM, previously known as Jeavons Syndrome).EEM is an epilepsy syndrome characterized by eyelid myoclonia, eyelid closure-induced generalized EEG paroxysms or seizures, and photosensitivity. Many patients have drug-resistant epilepsy; however, the effectiveness of VNS in this epilepsy syndrome has not been well studied.This is a single institution retrospective observational study of patients with EEM. Among a database of 134 patients with EEM, we identified those treated with VNS. Epilepsy history, VNS parameters, and response to VNS were abstracted.We identified 12 patients who were treated with VNS (50% female). The median age of epilepsy onset was 5 (range 4-14) years; age of VNS implantation was 16 (range 6-33) years, and median duration of VNS treatment was 13.5 (range 0-24) years. Four patients (33.3%) were responders reporting greater than 50% improvement in seizure frequency. All four patients (33.3%) showed response with generalized tonic-clonic seizures, myoclonic seizures, and three patients (25%) reported response with eyelid myoclonia and absence seizures. One patient had the VNS explanted due to lack of efficacy and one had it turned off for enrollment in a clinical trial. The median maximum tolerated output current settings for our cohort were 1.75 mA (IQR 1.38-1.94; range 0.75-2.25) with an OFF time of 1.8 min (IQR 1.1-3, range 0.2-3) and median duty cycle of 24% (IQR 16-29; range 12-58).From this small case series of patients with EEM, four (33.3%) were responders to VNS, with improvement noted in multiple seizure types. llm_summary: Epilepsy with eyelid myoclonia is a rare seizure disorder where patients experience involuntary eye twitching and seizures triggered by closing their eyes or exposure to light, and many people with this condition do not respond well to standard seizure medications. Researchers conducted a review of medical records from a single hospital to examine whether vagus nerve stimulation, a treatment that involves surgically implanting a device to send electrical pulses to a nerve in the neck to reduce seizures, could help patients with this specific type of epilepsy. Among twelve patients who received this implanted device, four patients (about one-third) experienced significant improvement with more than fifty percent fewer seizures, and these improvements were seen across different seizure types including eye twitching, muscle jerks, and loss of consciousness episodes. The results suggest that vagus nerve stimulation may be a helpful treatment option for people with epilepsy with eyelid myoclonia who have not benefited from traditional seizure medications. However, because this study included only a small number of patients from one hospital, larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and determine which patients are most likely to benefit from this treatment.

title: Pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome.
abstract: Despite the continued absence of a definitive biomarker for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), research over the last three decades has identified a wide range of underlying pathophysiological abnormalities. Peripheral mechanisms include gastrointestinal infection, changes in the gut microbiome, visceral hypersensitivity, increased intestinal permeability, low-grade mucosal inflammation and altered immune function, abnormal gastrointestinal motility, and the role of serotonin, bile acid metabolism, and carbohydrate metabolism. Central mechanisms include psychological health and altered central pain processing. These central and peripheral mechanisms can act in an integrated way to cause IBS symptoms, via the gut-brain axis, supporting the concept of IBS as a disorder of gut-brain interaction. Some mechanisms can be quantified using validated tests and questionnaires, including abnormal bile acid metabolism, accelerated colonic transit, and psychological comorbidity. However, more work is needed to translate most mechanisms into reliable tests able to identify specific targets for treatment. This Review discusses the current understanding of the pathophysiology of IBS in terms of peripheral, central, and integrated mechanisms.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. llm_summary: Irritable bowel syndrome, a common digestive disorder that causes stomach pain and irregular bowel movements, has puzzled doctors for decades because there is no single test that can definitively diagnose it. Researchers reviewed three decades of scientific studies to understand the many different physical and mental factors that contribute to this condition, which involves problems in how the gut and brain communicate with each other. They found that irritable bowel syndrome involves numerous mechanisms including changes in gut bacteria, increased sensitivity to pain in the digestive tract, inflammation in the intestines, abnormal muscle contractions, and psychological issues like stress and anxiety. While some of these underlying causes can now be measured using existing tests and questionnaires, most mechanisms still cannot be reliably identified in individual patients to guide specific treatments. Future research needs to develop better diagnostic tools that can pinpoint which specific factors are causing symptoms in each person so that doctors can offer more targeted and effective treatments.

This condition presents numerous clinical challenges for doctors because it requires careful management of infection, fluid imbalances, and potential surgical intervention to improve patient survival rates.

title: Dexamethasone is Associated with a Dose-Dependent Reduction in Venous Thromboembolic Complications following Total Knee and Hip Arthroplasty.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) following total knee (TKA) and hip (THA) may be mediated by postoperative inflammatory dysregulation. Emerging literature has suggested that perioperative dexamethasone may reduce the risk of VTE by mitigating inflammation-driven thrombogenesis. The present study sought to compare postoperative VTE complications across patients receiving varying perioperative dexamethasone doses.Using a national healthcare database that captures approximately 25% of inpatient procedures in the United States, we identified adult patients undergoing primary TKA and THA between 2016 and 2023. Patients who received dexamethasone on the day of surgery were identified and stratified into either a no dexamethasone, low-dose (less than eight milligrams [mg]), medium-dose (eight to 12 mg), or high-dose (greater than 16 mg) cohort. Outcomes were compared between the cohorts utilizing mixed-effects logistic regression. The primary outcome was the 90-day adjusted odds of VTE complications.Among TKA patients (n = 946,019), 393,971 (41.7%) did not receive dexamethasone, 161,287 (17.1%) received low-dose, 310,595 (32.8%) received medium-dose, and 80,166 (8.5%) received high-dose. Among THA patients (n = 537,684), 239,671 (44.6%) did not receive dexamethasone, 80,166 (14.9%) received low-dose, 151,875 (28.3%) received medium-dose, and 66,482 (12.4%) received high-dose. Within the TKA cohort, all dosing groups had significantly lower adjusted odds of VTE compared to the unexposed patients (low dose - adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 0.93, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.87 to 0.99, P = 0.020; medium dose - aOR: 0.84, 95% CI: 0.80 to 0.89, P < 0.001; high dose - aOR: 0.79, 95% CI: 0.72 to 0.88, P < 0.001) when compared to those who did not receive dexamethasone. For THA patients, the adjusted odds of VTE were significantly lower in just the medium (aOR: 0.85, 95% CI: 0.77 to 0.94, P = 0.001) and high dose (aOR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.64 to 0.94, P = 0.009) groups.Patients who received higher doses of dexamethasone experienced lower rates of VTE complications. Arthroplasty surgeons should consider higher doses of dexamethasone as a perioperative adjunct to standard VTE chemoprophylaxis regimens.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a common steroid medication called dexamethasone could reduce dangerous blood clots that sometimes develop after knee and hip replacement surgery, since these clots may be caused by inflammation in the body after surgery. The study looked at nearly one and a half million patients who had knee or hip replacements between 2016 and 2023, dividing them into groups based on whether they received no dexamethasone, a low dose, a medium dose, or a high dose of the medication on the day of surgery. Patients who received higher doses of dexamethasone had significantly lower rates of blood clots within 90 days after surgery, with the benefit being strongest in those who received the highest doses. These findings suggest that surgeons should consider giving patients higher doses of dexamethasone along with standard blood clot prevention treatments to help reduce this serious complication after joint replacement surgery. Future research should confirm these results and determine the safest and most effective dexamethasone dose to use in routine surgical practice.

title: Pseudotumor-Related Compression Neuropathies Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
abstract: Pseudotumor-related compression neuropathies following total hip arthroplasty (THA) represent a severe phenotype of adverse local tissue reaction. While historically attributed to metal-on-metal (MoM) bearings, other constructs such as dual-modular necks and taper corrosion with cobalt-chrome femoral heads have been implicated as well. Furthermore, inflammatory responses to polyethylene wear debris and non-foreign body sources can similarly stimulate pseudotumor formation, resulting in symptomatic nerve compression. This study aimed to characterize the etiology, clinical presentation, and surgical outcomes of patients who have pseudotumor-induced neuropathies.A retrospective review identified 83 patients who had a pseudotumor or local mass effect of 9,042 revision THA performed between 1997 and 2024. There were 24 patients (25 hips) who had a confirmed pseudotumor-related compression neuropathy. Implant characteristics, serum biomarkers, neurologic deficits, and clinical outcomes following surgical intervention were studied.Taper corrosion (n = 11), MoM articular wear (n = 4), and dual-modular neck corrosion (n = 4) were the predominant pseudotumor etiologies. Seronegative pseudotumors were observed in a subset of patients who presented with normal serum metal ions and inflammatory markers, despite massive soft-tissue lesions. Presenting neurologic deficits were complete in six cases and partial in 19 (motor: n = 15, sensory: n = 4), involving the femoral (n = 8), gluteal (n = 7), sciatic (n = 6), and peroneal (n = 4) nerves. Following revision THA and neurolysis, motor recovery was variable, with complete sciatic or peroneal division neuropathy resulting in persistent foot drop in four of five cases. Postoperative dislocation requiring revision surgery was seen in five cases.Pseudotumor-related neuropathy is a distinct complication observed across various implant designs and modular interfaces. Normal serum ion levels do not exclude the diagnosis. While surgical decompression is effective for pain relief, motor recovery is poorly predictable, carrying a guarded prognosis.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a serious complication that can occur after hip replacement surgery, where abnormal tissue growths called pseudotumors can form and press on nerves, causing pain and weakness. The study looked back at medical records from 1997 to 2024 and identified 24 patients out of 9,042 hip revision surgeries who developed nerve compression from these pseudotumors, studying what caused them and how patients responded to treatment. The researchers found that the pseudotumors came from different sources, including worn metal-on-metal implants, corroded metal connections between implant parts, and wear debris from plastic components, though some patients had massive tissue growths despite having normal blood tests for metal levels. After surgery to remove the pseudotumors and relieve pressure on the nerves, patients experienced good pain relief, but recovery of muscle strength and function was unpredictable and often incomplete, with some patients left with permanent foot drop or inability to move their feet properly. This research shows that pseudotumor-related nerve compression can happen with various hip implant designs and that normal blood test results do not rule out the condition, meaning doctors need to stay alert for this com.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Prostatic Urethral Lift for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Men with a History of Prostate Radiation.
abstract: To assess the efficacy of the prostatic urethral lift (PUL) procedure for treating lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in men with a history of prostate irradiation.A retrospective review was performed on patients who underwent PUL following radiation therapy between November 2019 and November 2025. Preoperative and postoperative patient-reported symptom scores, uroflowmetry, post-void residual (PVR), catheter utilization, and need for lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) medications were compared to assess the efficacy of the procedure in this cohort.A total of 41 patients were included in the analysis. The proportion of patients requiring catheterization declined from 51.2% preoperatively to 23.1% at one year postoperatively (p=0.002). The mean International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) improved from 17.8 preoperatively to 12.9 at one-year follow-up (p=0.028). The mean IPSS Quality of Life score improved from 4.5 preoperatively to 2.7 at one-year follow-up (p<0.001). PVR decreased from a mean of 215.9 mL preoperatively to 126.0 mL at one year (p=0.093). The procedure did not significantly lower the need for LUTS medications (p=0.867).The PUL procedure may offer durable symptomatic benefit and improved urinary function in carefully selected patients with a history of prostate irradiation.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a minimally invasive procedure called a prostatic urethral lift, which widens the urethra (the tube that carries urine) without removing prostate tissue, could help men who had previous radiation therapy for prostate cancer and were experiencing urinary problems. The study looked back at records from 41 men who received this procedure between 2019 and 2025, comparing their symptoms and urinary function before and one year after treatment. The results showed meaningful improvements, including a drop in the percentage of patients needing catheters (tubes to drain urine) from about half to roughly one quarter, and significant reductions in symptom severity scores that measure how much urinary problems affect daily life. However, the procedure did not significantly reduce the need for medications that help with urinary symptoms, and the amount of urine left in the bladder after urination decreased but not by a statistically significant amount. These findings suggest that the prostatic urethral lift may be a helpful option for carefully selected men dealing with urinary problems after prostate radiation, though more research would be needed to fully understand its long-term benefits and limitations.

title: Transurethral incision with transverse mucosal realignment for the treatment of bladder neck contractures after benign prostate surgery; mid-term outcomes.
abstract: To describe mid-term anatomic and functional outcomes of a novel endoscopic treatment, transurethral incision with transverse mucosal realignment (TUITMR), for bladder neck contracture (BNC) following benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) surgery.We retrospectively reviewed a prospectively maintained registry of men undergoing TUITMR for BNC following BPH surgery between November 2021 and July 2025. Primary outcomes were anatomic success (cystoscopic patency) and freedom from reintervention. Secondary outcomes included functional success, symptom scores (IPSS), post-void residual (PVR), continence, and complications.Ninety-two patients were analyzed with median follow-up of 15.9 months (IQR 8.8-22.4). Primary anatomic success was achieved in 93.5% of patients. Freedom from reintervention after a single procedure was 83.7%. Among patients requiring retreatment, repeat TUITMR resulted in high salvage rates, yielding overall clinical success of 93.5% and final anatomic success of 96.7% after up to two procedures. No patients had de novo incontinence. Complications occurred in 12% of patients, predominantly minor urinary tract infections, with rare need for secondary intervention.TUITMR achieves high anatomic and durable clinical success for BNC following BPH surgery, with excellent salvage potential after retreatment and low morbidity.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Bladder neck contractures, which are narrowing of the opening between the bladder and urethra, can develop after surgery to treat enlarged prostate glands and cause serious urinary problems that need additional treatment. Researchers reviewed medical records of ninety-two men who received a new minimally invasive procedure called transurethral incision with transverse mucosal realignment, which uses a camera inserted through the urethra to carefully cut and reposition tissue to widen the narrowed area. The procedure successfully restored normal opening width in over ninety-three percent of patients, and eighty-four percent of patients did not need another procedure during the follow-up period of about sixteen months. When some patients did need retreatment, repeating the same procedure worked well in most cases, with nearly all patients eventually achieving a successful outcome without developing new problems with urine leakage. This new technique appears to be a safe and effective option for treating this complication of prostate surgery, though longer-term studies will help confirm how well these results hold up over many years.

title: Surgeon Perceptions on Fertility Counseling and Preservation in Children with Cancer: A Multicenter Survey of North American Hospitals.
abstract: Treatment of pediatric cancers often requires gonadotoxic therapies, making fertility preservation (FP) an essential component of comprehensive oncologic care. However, surgeon exposure to oncofertility care varies. This study evaluated pediatric surgeon knowledge, comfort, and perceptions regarding FP counseling and care.A cross-sectional survey was administered to lead surgeon investigators from 52 sites across North America participating in the Pediatric Surgical Oncology Research Collaborative (PSORC) to evaluate surgeon perceptions on FP. Surgeon knowledge and comfort levels providing FP services to patients with cancer diagnoses were ascertained.Ninety-three percent of invited PSORC surgeons completed the survey. Most respondents desired further educational opportunities in pediatric oncofertility (92%) and supported incorporation of FP training into fellowship education (83%). Among surgeons without a dedicated FP program, 96% were interested in establishing one, and 43% reported active program development. A minority (10.4%) of respondents reported no fertility preservation counseling at all at their institutions. Surgeons at institutions with dedicated FP programs were significantly more comfortable performing FP procedures (p=0.003) and risk stratifying patients (p=0.042). They were also more knowledgeable about FP options (p=0.003), outcomes of ovarian tissue cryopreservation (OTC) and testicular tissue cryopreservation (TTC) for fertility and hormone restoration (p=0.005), and options for future hormone and fertility restoration (p=0.002).Significant opportunities exist to expand surgeon education, institutional resources, and multidisciplinary FP infrastructure. Respondents were highly motivated to increase educational opportunities and resources to improve fertility care for pediatric oncology patients.Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: Cancer treatments in children can damage the organs that produce eggs and sperm, so doctors need to talk with young patients about ways to preserve their ability to have children in the future. Researchers surveyed pediatric surgeons from 52 hospitals across North America to understand how much they knew about fertility preservation options and how comfortable they felt discussing these options with their patients. Most surgeons wanted more training in this area, and those who worked at hospitals with special fertility preservation programs felt much more confident and knowledgeable than those without such programs. The study found that nearly all surgeons without a dedicated fertility program were interested in starting one, showing strong motivation to improve care for young cancer patients. These results suggest that hospitals should invest in creating fertility preservation programs and training surgeons in this important area so that more children with cancer can receive counseling about protecting their future ability to have families.

title: Impact of Inspiratory Muscle Training on Inspiratory Muscle Metaboreflex in Patients with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: High inspiratory muscle work elicits respiratory muscle metaboreflex activation, contributing to increases in mean arterial pressure (MAP) and decreases in leg blood flow in adults at rest. Patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) have exaggerated cardiovascular responses with inspiratory muscle metaboreflex activation. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effect of inspiratory muscle training (IMT) on respiratory muscle metaboreflex-mediated cardiovascular responses in patients with HFpEF. METHODS: 13 patients with HFpEF (6M/7F; 69±9 years; 33±5kg/m2) underwent evaluation of cardiovascular responses to inspiratory resistive breathing tasks (IRBT) at 60% maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP) pre- and post-IMT. Beat-by-beat blood pressure and heart rate were measured using finger plethysmography. Vastus lateralis blood flow index (BFI) was measured using near infrared spectroscopy and indocyanine green dye. Vastus lateralis vascular resistance index was calculated. IMT consisted of 30 repetitions/day, 7 days/week for 8 weeks at 40% MIP. RESULTS: MIP increased from 71±21 to 95±25cmH2O following IMT (p<0.01). Following 8 weeks of IMT, the increases in MAP (Pre-IMT: 15±6 vs. Post-IMT: 9±6mmHg; p<0.01) and heart rate (Pre-IMT: 9±6 vs. Post-IMT: 6±5 beats/min, p=0.03) during the 60% IRBT were attenuated compared to pre-IMT. The % increase in vastus lateralis vascular resistance index during the 60% IRBT was smaller post-IMT than pre-IMT (Pre-IMT: 87±53 vs. Post-IMT: 47±34%, p<0.01). The % decrease in vastus lateralis BFI during the 60% IRBT was attenuated post-IMT than pre-IMT (Pre-IMT: -33±14 vs. Post-IMT: -23±12%; p<0.01). CONCLUSION: IMT attenuates the inspiratory muscle metaboreflex-mediated cardiovascular responses in patients with HFpEF.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether training the muscles used for breathing could help patients with heart failure and a normal pumping heart, who often experience excessive blood pressure increases and reduced leg blood flow when breathing against resistance. The study involved thirteen patients who performed breathing exercises against resistance at forty percent of their maximum breathing strength for eight weeks, doing thirty repetitions daily. After the training period, patients showed significant improvements, including stronger breathing muscles and reduced blood pressure spikes during difficult breathing tasks, dropping from a fifteen millimeter increase to just nine millimeters. The leg blood flow restrictions that occurred during the breathing resistance tests were also less severe after training, suggesting that the breathing muscle training reduced the exaggerated cardiovascular responses these patients typically experience. These findings suggest that inspiratory muscle training could be a helpful treatment approach for heart failure patients with preserved ejection fraction to reduce their abnormal cardiovascular reactions during physical stress.

title: Machine learning evaluation of clinical, social and behavioural factors influencing progression from pre-diabetes to type 2 diabetes: a retrospective cohort study in southeast Michigan.
abstract: We aimed to use machine learning (ML) models to investigate the impact of clinical, social and behavioural factors on 1-year progression from pre-diabetes to type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM).A retrospective cohort study.A large health system including eight sites in southeast Michigan.Adults with haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) between 5.7% and 6.4% for two consecutive years between 1 January 2008 and 31 December 2023, and no prior history of type 2 DM or metformin use.New-onset type 2 DM (HbA1c ≥6.5%) in 1 year.Among 11 809 individuals, 815 (6.9%) progressed to type 2 DM within 1 year. CatBoost demonstrated the best performance (average area under the curve 0.78). Prior-year HbA1c was the most influential covariate (SHapley Additive exPlanations 1.02). Traditional metabolic factors (high-density lipoprotein, body mass index (BMI), white blood cell, age, gender, triglycerides) also contributed. Lastly, while inclusion of social and behavioural determinants of health (SBDH) did not significantly improve the overall model performance, depression emerged as the prominent SBDH covariate. Depression was a stronger predictor of diabetes progression in individuals with higher baseline BMI and lower baseline HbA1c.Inclusion of social and behavioural covariates provided no incremental value for prediction of diabetes progression from pre-diabetes. However, machine learning revealed that depression may play a role in progression to type 2 DM.© Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2026. Re-use permitted under CC BY-NC. No commercial re-use. llm_summary: Researchers examined what factors influence whether people with pre-diabetes, a condition where blood sugar levels are higher than normal but not yet diabetic, progress to type 2 diabetes within one year. They studied over eleven thousand adults from southeast Michigan between 2008 and 2023, using computer programs called machine learning models to analyze which factors best predicted who would develop diabetes. Among the participants, about seven percent developed type 2 diabetes within a year, and the computer models found that the most important predictor was a person's previous year's blood sugar level, followed by traditional health factors like cholesterol, weight, and age. While the researchers also looked at social and behavioral factors like depression and life circumstances, these did not significantly improve the computer's ability to predict diabetes progression overall. However, the study did reveal that depression appeared to be particularly important for predicting diabetes in people who were overweight and had lower baseline blood sugar levels, suggesting that mental health may play a role in diabetes development that deserves further investigation.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Portable Low- and Ultra-Low-Field MRI for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Portable low-field and ultra-low-field MRI enables bedside imaging, but its diagnostic performance for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) detection remains uncertain.To evaluate the diagnostic performance of portable MRI for AIS detection.Four databases were searched on February 2, 2026.Eligible studies enrolled adults with suspected or confirmed AIS undergoing portable MRI. Nine studies comprising 474 patients with AIS were included.In studies with an appropriate reference standard, pooled sensitivity and specificity were synthesized using a bivariate random-effects model, and a hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic curve was generated. Across all eligible AIS cohorts, the pooled lesion detection rate was estimated using a generalized linear mixed-effects model with random effects.In six comparative studies, the pooled sensitivity for AIS detection was 73.3% (95% CI, 65.4-80.0), corresponding to approximately one in four confirmed infarcts being missed, with missed lesions generally small or sub-centimetric. Pooled specificity was 79.3% (95% CI, 69.1-86.8), and the area under the curve was 0.818. The pooled AIS lesion detection rate was 87.65% (95% CI, 75.7-94.2).There was substantial between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 74.2%). This estimate was interpreted as secondary and descriptive because it included case-only confirmed AIS cohorts.Portable low/ultra-low-field MRI showed moderate diagnostic performance for AIS detection in comparative studies and may serve as a bedside adjunct where conventional MRI is constrained. However, given the false-negative risk, portable MRI should not be relied upon as a stand-alone rule-out test for AIS when clinical suspicion persists.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether portable magnetic resonance imaging machines, which are smaller and can be brought to a patient's bedside, could accurately detect acute ischemic stroke, which is a type of stroke caused by a blood clot blocking blood flow to the brain. The team reviewed nine studies involving 474 patients with confirmed strokes and analyzed how well these portable machines performed compared to standard hospital imaging equipment. The portable machines correctly identified about 73 out of every 100 confirmed strokes but missed roughly one in four cases, typically smaller lesions that were less than one centimeter in size, while they correctly ruled out stroke in about 79 out of every 100 cases where no stroke was present. These results suggest that portable machines could be useful as an additional tool when standard imaging is not available, but they should not be used alone to rule out a stroke when doctors still suspect one based on a patient's symptoms. Future research should focus on improving the technology and determining the best situations where portable machines can safely supplement traditional stroke imaging.

title: Cardioneural and accessory atrioventricular pathway ablation for vagally mediated atrial fibrillation in PRKAG2 syndrome.
abstract: Cardioneural ablation (CNA) is an emerging strategy for vagally mediated arrhythmias, but its role in patients with underlying conduction system disease remains undefined. Here, a young patient with PRKAG2-mediated cardiomyopathy presented with refractory paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) despite prior accessory atrioventricular pathway (AP) ablation and antiarrhythmic therapy. Episodes of AF were triggered consistently by cold milk ingestion, and dual-chamber pacemaker interrogation revealed a high atrial pacing burden due to sinus pauses, suggesting a vagally mediated mechanism superimposed on underlying conduction disease. Extracardiac vagal stimulation during electrophysiology study unmasked residual AP conduction and resulted in sinus pause and AV block. These findings confirmed vagal tone as the dominant arrhythmia modulator and prompted repeat AP ablation and CNA. At follow-up, CNA eliminated vagally mediated sinus pauses, reducing atrial and ventricular pacing burden to 0%, with only low-burden asymptomatic AF persisting.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: A young patient with a genetic heart condition called PRKAG2 syndrome experienced repeated irregular heartbeats in the upper chambers of the heart, which doctors call atrial fibrillation, even after previous surgery to remove an extra electrical pathway in the heart and treatment with heart rhythm medications. The doctors discovered that the patient's irregular heartbeats were triggered by drinking cold milk and were caused by an overactive vagus nerve, which is a major nerve that controls heart function, combined with an underlying problem with the heart's electrical system. The medical team performed a new procedure called cardioneural ablation, which involves using heat or cold to disable parts of the vagus nerve that were causing the irregular heartbeats, along with repeating the previous surgery to remove the extra electrical pathway. After the combined procedures, the patient no longer experienced the vagus nerve-related pauses in heartbeat and no longer needed the pacemaker to pace the heart as much, though some mild irregular heartbeats continued to occur without causing symptoms. This case suggests that cardioneural ablation may be a helpful treatment option for patients with genetic heart conditions who have vagus nerve-related irregular heartbeats that do not respond to.

title: A Prospective, Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) of the da Vinci SP® Surgical System versus Open Surgery in Nipple-Sparing Mastectomy (NSM) Procedures for Patients with Breast Cancer.
abstract: This prospective randomized trial evaluated the safety and effectiveness of robotic-assisted nipple-sparing mastectomy (rNSM) using the da Vinci Single Port (SP)® compared with open NSM in women with early stage breast cancer.This Food and Drug Administration (FDA) investigational device exemption (IDE)-approved, two-arm, multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) randomized eligible women (clinical Tis-T2, N0) 1:1 to rNSM or open NSM with immediate implant-based reconstruction. Operations were performed at 14 US sites by 23 surgeons. Primary endpoints included conversion to open surgery, adverse events at 42 days, and positive surgical margin (PSM) rates. Secondary outcomes included operative time, estimated blood loss, nipple-areolar complex (NAC) and skin flap viability, final pathology, and patient-reported outcomes (BREAST-Q).Overall, 74 patients completed surgery, totaling 65 rNSM (38 therapeutic, 27 prophylactic) and 66 open NSM (38 therapeutic, 28 prophylactic). Operative time was longer for rNSM (141.6 versus 83.9 min) with no conversions to open surgery. Serious adverse events (SAEs) occurred in three rNSM and eight open NSM patients, with no device-related SAEs reported. NAC preservation at 42 days was 100% for rNSM and 98.5% for open NSM. PSM rates were identical (six patients each). Higher BREAST-Q scores favored rNSM in multiple domains.These results demonstrate that da Vinci SP® rNSM is feasible and has a safety profile comparable to open NSM for early stage breast cancer, with similar margin status and postoperative complications. Although SAEs and patient-reported outcomes were more favorable with rNSM, these differences were not statistically significant. rNSM was associated with longer operative times, which may in part reflect early experience with the technique.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a new robotic surgical system could safely remove breast tissue while preserving the nipple in women with early stage breast cancer, comparing it to traditional open surgery. The study involved 74 women across 14 hospitals in the United States who were randomly assigned to receive either robotic-assisted surgery or conventional open surgery, with both groups receiving immediate breast reconstruction using implants. The robotic surgery took longer to complete, averaging about 142 minutes compared to 84 minutes for open surgery, but no patients needed to be converted to open surgery and serious complications were actually fewer in the robotic group. Both surgical approaches preserved the nipple equally well, achieved the same rates of clear surgical margins (meaning cancer was completely removed), and patients who had robotic surgery reported higher satisfaction scores in multiple areas. These results suggest that robotic-assisted nipple-sparing mastectomy is a safe and effective option for treating early stage breast cancer, though the longer operating time may improve as surgeons gain more experience with the new technology.

title: Socioeconomic status and informal preference signaling among medical school applicants.
abstract: Medical school applicants engage in informal preference signaling by submitting letters of intent (which include a commitment to accept an admission offer) and letters of interest (which include no such commitment). Commitments are unenforceable and are based on an honor system. Applicants submit letters to medical schools before receiving financial aid offers, potentially disadvantaging low socioeconomic status (SES) applicants. This study describes postinterview communication patterns and analyzes associations among applicant demographics, letter submission rates, and admissions outcomes. It tests the hypothesis that low SES is negatively associated with letter of intent submission.The authors collected postinterview communications from all interviewees at the Mayo Clinic Alix School of Medicine during 3 admissions cycles (2021-2023). Authors developed and validated codebook definitions for the 2 letter types. SES was defined using the Association of American Medical Colleges education-occupation indicator. Letter submission rates were compared using mixed-effects logistic regression.Of 1,313 applicants, 1,109 submitted 1 letter or more. The sample included 257 (19.6%) low-SES and 1,056 (80.4%) non-low-SES applicants. Coders showed excellent interrater reliability (Gwet AC1 range, 0.89-0.995). Low-SES applicants submitted letters of intent with similar frequency to higher-SES applicants (33.9% [87/257] vs 33.5% [354/1,056]; odds ratio, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.76-1.37; P = .88) and submitted letters of interest at similar frequency (55.6% [143/257] vs 59.5% [628/1,056]; odds ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.65-1.13; P = .27). Among 116 applicants who wrote letters of intent and were offered admission, 20 (17.2%) declined the admission offer.There was no difference in letter of intent submission based on SES, and letter of intent submission was positively associated with matriculation. Among letter of intent writers who were offered admission, 1 in 6 declined. Undergraduate medical education may wish to consider a formalized preference signaling system to promote an honest and transparent application process.© The Author(s) 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether medical school applicants from lower-income backgrounds were less likely to submit letters of intent, which are formal commitments to accept an admission offer if accepted, because they submit these letters before learning about financial aid packages. The study collected data on postinterview communications from 1,313 applicants across three years at one medical school, comparing submission rates between applicants from lower-income families and those from higher-income families using statistical analysis. The results showed that low-income applicants submitted letters of intent at nearly identical rates to higher-income applicants, with about one-third of each group submitting these commitment letters. Among applicants who wrote letters of intent and received admission offers, one in six applicants declined the offer despite their earlier commitment, suggesting that these informal honor-system promises are not always kept. The researchers recommend that medical schools consider creating a more formal and transparent preference signaling system to ensure fairness and honesty throughout the application process.

title: Safety and efficacy of preoperative embolization in the treatment of brain arteriovenous malformations with perinidal aneurysms and single draining vein: a multicenter study with propensity score-weighting.
abstract: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) with perinidal aneurysms and single draining vein are associated with an elevated risk of rupture and increased procedural complexity. The role of preoperative embolization in this high-risk anatomical subset remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of microsurgery with preoperative embolization, compared with microsurgery alone in patients with such AVMs.We conducted a multicenter retrospective analysis of an AVM registry from the MISTA (Multicenter International Study for Treatment of Brain AVMs) consortium and included AVMs with perinidal aneurysms and a single draining vein. Baseline characteristics, angiographic outcomes, functional outcomes, and complication rates were compared. Propensity score weighting (PSW) using the covariate balancing method was applied to adjust for baseline differences.Out of a total of 1919 patients, 65 met the inclusion criteria; 45 patients underwent preoperative embolization followed by microsurgery, and 20 underwent microsurgery alone. After adjustment, complete obliteration rates were similar between groups (OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.04 to 16.33, P=0.92), as were rates of functional independence at discharge and follow-up. Overall complication, symptomatic complication, and mortality rates did not differ significantly between groups. However, permanent complications were significantly lower in patients with preoperative embolization (OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.004 to 0.84, P=0.03).In patients with AVMs featuring perinidal aneurysms and single draining vein, preoperative embolization followed by microsurgery was associated with fewer permanent complications and no increase in adverse outcomes compared with microsurgery alone. However, given the small number of events, this finding should be interpreted cautiously.© Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2026. No commercial re-use. See rights and permissions. llm_summary: Brain arteriovenous malformations, which are abnormal tangles of blood vessels in the brain, are particularly dangerous when they have small aneurysms near their edges and only one vein draining blood away from them. Researchers from multiple medical centers examined whether adding a procedure called embolization, which involves blocking blood vessels before surgery, would improve outcomes compared to surgery alone in patients with this high-risk type of malformation. The study included 65 patients total, with 45 receiving embolization followed by surgery and 20 receiving surgery without embolization beforehand. The results showed that both treatment approaches were equally effective at completely removing the malformations and restoring normal function, but patients who had embolization first experienced significantly fewer permanent complications from their treatment. Although this finding suggests that preoperative embolization may be beneficial for this challenging group of patients, the researchers cautioned that the small number of patients studied means these results should be confirmed with larger future studies before changing standard treatment practices.

title: The Promise and Peril of Alzheimer Disease Prevention.
abstract: Interventions to delay or prevent Alzheimer disease dementia hold the promise of sizable personal and public benefit. The nomenclature, research designs, and interpretation of results for studies assessing prevention outcomes, however, are inconsistent and would benefit from greater consensus about the necessary requirements for specific intervention claims. Moreover, the public space includes substantial media attention, direct-to-consumer diagnostics, and marketing of unproven interventions for brain health and dementia prevention. This article outlines these issues in hopes of catalyzing further consensus building and alerting professional and regulatory agencies to these topics.

llm_summary: Preventing Alzheimer disease, a brain condition that causes memory loss and confusion, could help millions of people avoid serious health problems and reduce the burden on families and society. Researchers examined how scientists currently study and talk about prevention efforts, finding that different studies use different methods and language, which makes it hard to compare results fairly. The authors discovered that there is no clear agreement about what counts as real prevention versus what is just marketing hype, and they noted that many unproven brain health products are being sold directly to consumers through advertisements and online tests. The study highlights the need for doctors, scientists, and government agencies to work together to create clear standards for what prevention claims are actually supported by solid evidence. Without better rules and clearer communication, people may waste money on treatments that do not work while missing out on interventions that could genuinely help them.

title: PSC's itch is worth scratching: Pruritus can be more than a symptom.
abstract: No abstract available.
authors: Yigit Yazarkan

authors_display: Yigit Yazarkan
llm_summary: Background:  Primary sclerosing cholangitis, or PSC, is a rare liver disease where the bile ducts become inflamed and scarred over time, making it harder for the liver to function properly. Itching, or pruritus, is a common symptom that patients with PSC experience, but this article suggests that itching may be more significant than previously thought and could warrant greater clinical attention and treatment focus.

title: Sex Differences in Exercise Capacity and Outcomes Following Outpatient Cardiac Rehabilitation.
abstract: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) leads to increased exercise capacity (VO2peak) and risk reduction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Women exhibit blunted VO2peak improvements following CR. The purpose was to examine sex differences in the clinical predictors of VO2peak improvement and odds of MACEs following CR.From 1999 to 2017, all consecutive patients undergoing cardiopulmonary exercise testing before and after CR were included. Sex differences in peak exercise metrics in response to CR were compared. Multiple logistic regression models were fit to assess clinical predictors of VO2peak improvement (defined as >0% from pre-CR) and MACEs following CR for men and women.A total of 513 men and 158 women were included. Men had greater increases in VO2peak than women following CR (P=0.001). For men, independent predictors of VO2peak improvement following CR included higher CR session attendance (odds ratio [OR], 1.04 [95% CI, 1.02-1.06]), peripheral artery disease (OR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.25-0.86]), and pre-CR VO2peak (OR, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.97-0.99]) (all, P<0.02). Independent predictors of lower odds of MACEs following CR in men included higher number of CR sessions (OR, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.95-0.99]), pre-CR VO2peak (OR, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.97-0.99]), surgical CR indication (OR, 0.34 [95% CI, 0.18-0.68]), and no history of peripheral artery disease (OR, 2.94 [95% CI, 1.60-5.38]) (all, P<0.02). For women, the selected clinical characteristics were not statistically significant independent predictors of VO2peak improvement or odds of MACEs (except for diabetes) following CR.These findings suggest that clinical predictors of VO2peak improvement and odds of MACEs following CR are sex specific.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether men and women respond differently to cardiac rehabilitation, which is a supervised exercise program that helps heart patients recover and improve their fitness levels. The study followed 513 men and 158 women from 1999 to 2017 who completed exercise tests before and after participating in cardiac rehabilitation programs, measuring their oxygen uptake capacity and tracking whether they experienced serious heart problems afterward. Men showed greater improvements in their exercise capacity than women after completing the rehabilitation program, and the factors that predicted success were different between the sexes. For men, attending more rehabilitation sessions and having a higher fitness level before starting the program were linked to better outcomes and fewer heart problems, but these same factors did not reliably predict results for women. These findings suggest that doctors may need to develop different rehabilitation approaches for men and women rather than using a one-size-fits-all treatment plan.

title: Endotypes of Vascular Health Predict Transplantation-Free Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract: The current classification of pulmonary hypertension (PH), based largely on expert opinion, has limitations in prognostication and guiding therapies. We hypothesize that novel PH clusters that predict survival will reveal mechanistic phenotypes associated with biomarkers of vascular health across all PH groups.We first identify novel PH clinical clusters by performing unsupervised clustering analysis on the CC-PH (Cleveland Clinic PH) registry (N=1529). We develop classification models to predict the new PH clusters and then apply them to the multicenter PVDOMICS (Pulmonary Vascular Diseases Phenomics) cohort (N=853) for validation. We compare transplantation-free survival across the new PH clusters. We quantify metabolites of the arginine-nitric oxide pathway and D-dimer levels and calculate global arginine bioavailability (arginine/[ornithine+citrulline]) to assess endothelial function and activation in the new clusters and link these biomarkers to clinical outcomes.Clustering analysis identify 3 clear clusters in CC-PH that are validated in PVDOMICS and outperform conventional classifications in predicting transplantation-free survival. The phenotype associated with the worst survival is characterized by reduced lung diffusion capacity, decreased arginine bioavailability and nitrate levels, and elevated D-dimer levels, consistent with loss of pulmonary microcirculation and endothelial dysfunction.We identify new informative PH phenotypes associated with mortality and defined by biomarkers of endothelial function and activation. Loss of endothelial health and pronounced pulmonary vascular rarefication contribute more substantially to mortality across the spectrum of PH than right heart function.
