llm_summary: Researchers examined how the body's resting metabolic rate, which is the amount of energy your body burns at rest, relates to heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, a condition where the heart cannot pump blood efficiently even though its pumping chambers appear normal in size. The study involved 472 patients with this heart condition who underwent exercise testing while doctors measured their actual resting metabolic rate using a special breathing technique and compared it to what would be expected based on their body size and composition. Patients whose bodies burned more energy at rest than expected were older, more likely to be women, less likely to be overweight, and showed signs that their hearts were working harder to meet their body's energy demands even while sitting still. However, these same patients with higher-than-expected metabolic rates showed a concerning problem during exercise: their hearts could not increase their pumping power adequately and their blood vessels did not relax enough, meaning their cardiovascular system lacked the reserve capacity needed for physical activity. Over nearly five years of follow-up, patients with higher-than-expected metabolic rates had more than two and a half times greater risk of dying from heart-related causes or being hospitalized for worsening.

title: Trypanosoma cruzi Retinitis Following Donor-Derived Chagas Disease After Heart Transplantation.
abstract: Donor-derived Trypanosoma cruzi infection is a recognized complication of solid organ transplantation, but ocular involvement has never been reported. We described a case of necrotizing retinitis due to T. cruzi in a heart transplant recipient. A 62-year-old man developed unexpected donor-derived Chagas disease three months post-transplant and completed a 12-week course of nifurtimox with near-complete clearance of parasitemia. Thirty-eight days after nifurtimox discontinuation, he presented with progressive unilateral vision loss and clinical findings consistent with acute retinal necrosis. Vitreous biopsy with pan-pathogen PCR was negative for viral etiologies but confirmed T. cruzi. Despite systemic benznidazole therapy and clearance of blood parasitemia, intraocular disease progressed, ultimately attempting a salvage adjunctive intravitreal therapy with voriconazole. Ocular inflammation improved, but vision remained limited to light perception. This case underscores the need for continued clinical vigilance for late complications of Chagas disease in transplant recipients. Universal screening for donors with T. cruzi should be considered in future practice, pending the identification of the most appropriate assay, improved accessibility to such assays, and logistical challenges faced by individual organ procurement organizations.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: A parasite called Trypanosoma cruzi causes a disease known as Chagas disease, which can spread through organ transplants from infected donors, though eye involvement had never been documented before this case. Doctors treated a 62-year-old heart transplant patient who developed donor-derived Chagas disease three months after surgery and initially seemed to recover after taking antibiotics for twelve weeks. Thirty-eight days after stopping the antibiotics, the patient developed sudden vision loss in one eye caused by a serious infection of the retina, which is the light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye. Despite additional antibiotic treatment and a procedure to inject medicine directly into the eye, the infection continued to damage the eye tissue, leaving the patient with only the ability to see light. This case shows that doctors need to watch more carefully for late complications of Chagas disease in transplant patients and suggests that screening all organ donors for this parasite should be considered as standard practice in the future.

title: The Society of Thoracic Surgeons / World Society for Pediatric and Congenital Heart Surgery / European Congenital Heart Surgeons Association 2026 Expert Consensus Document on Timing, Indications, and Options for Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Children with Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
abstract: Contemporary surgical and medical management has enabled excellent long-term survival and quality of life for children following repair of tetralogy of Fallot. However, most patients are left with residual pulmonary regurgitation that requires long-term surveillance and eventual pulmonary valve replacement to prevent right ventricular failure. Guidelines have been developed regarding the indications for and timing of pulmonary valve replacement in adults, but such do not exist for children. This expert consensus document aimed to address those gaps by supporting clinical decision-making regarding the surgical and transcatheter management of chronic pulmonary regurgitation in children with repaired tetralogy of Fallot.The Society of Thoracic Surgeons Workforce on Evidence Based Surgery assembled a multidisciplinary expert panel composed of congenital surgeons and cardiologists. A focused literature review was performed, and expert consensus statements were developed using a Modified Delphi process and clustered under two key topics: (1) pediatric-specific considerations and (2) surgical versus transcatheter techniques.Consensus was reached for 13 recommendations. The recommendation statements reflect contemporary expert opinion on the timing and decision-making for pulmonary valve replacement in children.While decision-making regarding the management of chronic pulmonary regurgitation after repair of tetralogy of Fallot in children is complex, this document provides guidance for congenital heart teams to optimize management based on a synthesis of contemporary evidence.Copyright © 2026. llm_summary: Children who have surgery to repair a heart condition called tetralogy of Fallot often develop a leaky pulmonary valve, which is the valve that controls blood flow from the heart to the lungs, and this leakage can eventually lead to heart failure if not treated. A team of heart surgeons and cardiologists from major medical organizations around the world reviewed medical research and used a structured voting process to develop expert recommendations about when and how to replace the pulmonary valve in children with this condition. The experts reached agreement on thirteen recommendations that provide guidance on the timing of valve replacement and whether to use traditional surgery or newer catheter-based techniques, which involve threading a device through blood vessels rather than opening the chest. These recommendations will help heart teams make better decisions about caring for children with this common heart problem by combining the latest medical evidence with expert knowledge. While managing this condition remains complicated and requires careful monitoring of each child, this new guidance document gives doctors a clear framework to help them provide the best possible care and improve long-term outcomes for these young patients.

llm_summary: Background:  Polymyalgia rheumatica is a condition that causes muscle pain and stiffness, typically affecting older adults over the age of 50, and it can significantly impact a person's ability to perform daily activities like getting dressed or climbing stairs. Early recognition and proper management of this inflammatory condition are important because it can be effectively treated with medication, and identifying it quickly helps prevent complications and improves quality of life for patients.

title: Self-Reported Geriatric Impairments and Treatment Toxicity in Older Patients with Multiple Myeloma-A Single Center Prospective Study.
abstract: Frailty influences treatment tolerance and outcomes in older patients with multiple myeloma (MM), yet existing frailty tools capture limited geriatric domains and are incompletely studied in the context of contemporary therapies. We prospectively evaluated patient-reported comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) domains, frailty, and their associations with treatment toxicity and patient-reported outcomes(PROs) in older adults with MM.In this single-center prospective study, patients ≥60 years with newly-diagnosed or relapsed/refractory MM initiating a new therapy completed electronic CGA and PRO questionnaires at baseline and 4 months. Outcomes included clinician- and patient-reported treatment toxicity, treatment adaptations, healthcare utilization, and health-related quality of life (HRQOL). A cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) was derived from CGA and HRQOL domains.Among 90 patients (mean age:72 years), geriatric impairments were common, particularly physical function domains. High-grade non-hematological toxicities were significantly associated with older age, comorbidities, patient-reported functional limitations, and anxiety. The toxicity rates on PROCTACE were higher than CTCAE, highlighting a discordance between physician-reported and patient-experienced treatment toxicity. Frailty was present in 22% and was associated with worse baseline HRQOL and increased high-grade non-hematological toxicity, but not treatment adaptations or healthcare utilization. Average CGA and HRQOL scores remained stable over 4 months, though individual trajectories varied.Patient-reported geriatric impairments are prevalent in older adults with MM and strongly associated with non-hematological toxicities even in the contemporary treatment era. Reliance on physician assessed CTCAE alone fails to fully capture the symptom burden experienced by patients. Changes in geriatric domains during treatment emphasize the need for longitudinal assessment.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Hematology.

llm_summary: Older patients with multiple myeloma, a blood cancer affecting bone marrow, often experience physical weakness and other age-related health problems that can make cancer treatment harder to tolerate. Researchers at a single medical center asked ninety patients aged sixty and older with newly diagnosed or returning multiple myeloma to complete detailed health questionnaires at the start of treatment and again four months later, tracking both what doctors observed and what patients actually experienced. The study found that physical limitations, anxiety, older age, and existing health conditions were strongly linked to serious side effects from treatment, and that patients reported much worse symptoms than doctors documented in their medical records. These findings suggest that doctors need to pay closer attention to what patients tell them about their treatment side effects rather than relying only on standard medical assessments, since patient reports revealed significantly more suffering than clinical records showed. Future care for older cancer patients should include regular check-ins about how patients are managing physically and emotionally during treatment, rather than just measuring changes in the cancer itself.

title: Predictors of post-transplant measurable residual disease negativity and impact on clinical outcomes in multiple myeloma.
abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) is a powerful prognostic tool in multiple myeloma, but predictors of achieving MRD negativity after autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) are not well defined. We studied 814 patients who achieved at least a very good partial response after ASCT between January 2016 and January 2023 and underwent MRD assessment by next-generation flow cytometry (median sensitivity 2.4x10-6). Overall, 48% (n=387) achieved MRD negativity post-ASCT. The presence of t(11;14) (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.4-3.2; p<0.01) and pre-transplant response less than complete remission (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.2-3.7; p<0.01) independently predicted MRD positivity. MRD-positive patients had inferior progression-free survival (PFS) (HR 1.99, 95% CI 1.53-2.58; p<0.001) and overall survival (OS) (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.10-2.28; p=0.009). Despite lower MRD-negative rate, 5-year PFS was similar among t(11;14) MRD-positive (58%) and MRD-negative (63%); p=0.12. The adverse prognostic effect of high-risk cytogenetics (HRCA) on 5-year PFS appears partially mitigated in MRD-negative patients, 5-year PFS was 73% in those without ≥2 HRCA compared with 55% in those with ≥2 HRCA (HR 1.9, 95% CI 1.2-3.3; p=0.01). In the MRD-positive cohort, 5-year PFS was 53% in patients without ≥2 HRCA versus 17% in those with ≥2 HRCA (HR 2.4, 95% CI 1.6-3.6; p<0.01). Additionally, higher residual clonal plasma cell burden within MRD-positive disease was associated with inferior PFS (HR 2.4, 95% CI 1.2-6.9; p=0.002). This study highlights that presence of t(11;14) independently predicts MRD positivity post-ASCT, although it does not significantly impact prognosis in this subgroup.Copyright © 2026 American Society of Hematology.

llm_summary: Researchers examined what factors help predict whether multiple myeloma patients achieve a disease-free state after a stem cell transplant, since knowing this information helps doctors understand how well patients will do long-term. The study looked at 814 patients who had received transplants between 2016 and 2023 and tested their blood using advanced laboratory methods to detect any remaining cancer cells, finding that only 48 percent of patients had no detectable disease after the procedure. The researchers discovered that patients with a specific genetic change called t(11;14) and those who had not reached complete remission before transplant were more likely to still have detectable cancer cells afterward, and these patients with remaining disease had worse outcomes including shorter survival times. Interestingly, patients with the t(11;14) genetic change who did achieve a disease-free state had similar long-term survival rates as those without this change, suggesting that reaching a disease-free state after transplant may overcome some of the negative effects of this particular genetic mutation. These findings suggest that doctors should pay special attention to monitoring patients with certain genetic markers and incomplete responses before transplant, since achieving a disease-free state appears to be an important goal.

title: Azithromycin versus doxycycline in hospitalised adult patients with community-acquired pneumonia treated with beta-lactams: protocol for a pragmatic randomised clinical trial.
abstract: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is common and remains the leading infectious cause of death worldwide. Antibiotics remain the mainstay of treatment, but organisms are often not identified, necessitating empirical treatment. Current treatment guidelines recommend combination therapy with beta-lactams and macrolides or monotherapy with fluoroquinolones for non-severe CAP. However, rising antibiotic resistance and safety concerns have led to increased doxycycline use, despite limited evidence supporting its efficacy. Our goal is to conduct a pragmatic, open-label, randomised clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of azithromycin with that of doxycycline in combination with beta-lactam therapy in adult patients hospitalised for CAP.Patients presenting to the emergency department or directly referred to the hospital with a clinical presentation concerning for CAP and need for hospitalisation are eligible. We plan to enrol 1120 adults hospitalised at six hospitals across four states, including rural, suburban and urban settings and academic and community hospitals. Randomisation will be 1:1 using an electronic health record (EHR)-embedded screening and randomisation tool triggered by the treating clinician's orders for azithromycin or doxycycline. Outcomes will be ascertained pragmatically via EHR-based data retrieval and will not require additional study visits. Our primary outcome is days alive and out of the hospital through day 28. Secondary outcomes include oxygen-free days; a composite of a need for advanced respiratory support or in-hospital mortality with analyses of each component separately; an ordinal measure of clinical deterioration defined by a prespecified severity scale; and 60-day and 180-day mortality. Safety outcomes are the incidence of Clostridioides difficile infection and QT prolongation. Analyses will follow an intention-to-treat framework, with per-protocol analyses for sensitivity. The primary endpoint will be compared between groups using a stratified van Elteren test, with supportive analyses using proportional odds regression and analysis of covariance adjusted for key covariates.The Mayo Clinic Institutional Review Board reviewed and approved this protocol with a waiver of written consent, requiring verbal consent to be obtained by the clinician initiating the antibiotics (IRB# 24-0 06 503). llm_summary: Community-acquired pneumonia, which is a lung infection people catch in everyday life rather than in hospitals, remains a leading cause of death worldwide and is typically treated with antibiotics, though doctors often must guess which antibiotics to use before identifying the specific germ causing the infection. Researchers are conducting a large practical trial at six hospitals across four states to compare whether azithromycin, a common antibiotic from the macrolide family, or doxycycline, an older antibiotic, works better when combined with beta-lactam antibiotics (a different class of antibiotics) in hospitalized adults with pneumonia. The study will enroll 1,120 adult patients and track their recovery over 28 days by measuring how many days they spend alive and out of the hospital, along with other measures like how many days they can breathe without extra oxygen and whether they need advanced breathing support or die. The findings from this trial could help doctors choose the safest and most effective antibiotic combination for treating pneumonia in hospitalized patients, especially as antibiotic resistance becomes a growing concern worldwide. The study uses electronic health records to collect information automatically without requiring patients to make extra visits, making.

title: Systemic and local chronic inflammation and hormone disposition promote a tumor-permissive environment for breast cancer in older women.
abstract: Estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer is the most common subtype of breast cancer and is an age-related disease. How systemic and tumor microenvironment hormone signaling intersects with chronic inflammation and how this shapes aging-associated tumor biology remain incompletely understood. Here, using an aged rat model of ER+ tumors, we identify age-associated differences in tumor development and immune features. In parallel, analysis of samples from patients with ER+/HER2- breast cancer and age-matched controls demonstrated estrone-predominant systemic estrogen patterns and increased tumor HSD17B7 expression in older patients, consistent with enhanced local estrone-to-estradiol conversion. In patient-derived organoids from older women, pharmacologic inhibition of HSD17B7 reduced estrogen conversion and proliferation-associated transcriptional programs. Tumors from older patients also exhibited chemokine enrichment, including CCL2, associated with immunosuppressive macrophage features. Targeting both estrogen signaling and chemokine pathways attenuated macrophage polarization ex vivo. These findings support a model linking age-associated hormonal and inflammatory changes to features of a tumor-permissive microenvironment in ER+ breast cancer.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, which is the most common type of breast cancer and becomes more frequent as women age, develops in an environment shaped by both hormonal changes and chronic inflammation, but scientists have not fully understood how these factors work together in older women. Researchers used aged rats with tumors similar to human breast cancer and analyzed tissue samples from older patients with this cancer type to understand the differences between younger and older women. They discovered that older patients had higher levels of a specific enzyme called HSD17B7 in their tumors that converts one form of estrogen into another, along with increased inflammatory signals that suppress the immune system's ability to fight cancer. When the researchers blocked this enzyme in laboratory-grown tumor cells from older women or targeted both estrogen and inflammatory pathways together, they were able to slow cancer cell growth and reduce the tumor-promoting immune cells. These findings suggest that treating older women with estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer may require addressing both hormone signaling and inflammation simultaneously to create a less favorable environment for tumors to grow.

title: Enhancing missense variant classification in predicted intrinsically disordered regions.
abstract: Classifying disease-causing missense variants in intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) remains a significant challenge, with over 25% of known deleterious variants occurring in these regions. Existing in silico missense variant predictors that predict variant classification generally perform better in ordered regions of the protein, limiting their effectiveness. To address this, we developed a machine learning methodology that integrates global IDR conformation (gIDRc) features from ALBATROSS, phase separation (PS) features from BioPython, and 1024-dimensional protein embeddings from ProtTransBertBFD generated for both wild-type (WT) and mutant IDR sequences. IDR boundaries were defined using the AlphaFold-RSA predictions, which identifies disordered regions based on AlphaFold2 pLDDT scores and relative solvent accessibility. Using ClinVar variant classifications as ground truth, AlphaMissense, EVE, and ESM1b were the highest scoring unsupervised in silico missense predictors for IDR variants. Our baseline model, using only IDR-specific features achieved competitive performance on the hold-out test set with a PR-AUC of 0.817. Critically, when these IDR features were combined with these methods we saw significant overall improvement. The AlphaMissense-Enhanced model increased its PR-AUC from 0.807 to 0.919. Similarly, ESM1b-Enhanced improved PR-AUC from 0.679 to 0.845 and EVE increased from 0.591 to 0.910. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our enhancements for classifying missense variants in IDRs and highlight its ability to complement existing in silico missense predictors.Copyright: © 2026 Gnanaolivu, Hart. llm_summary: Researchers examined a significant problem in genetic medicine: identifying harmful genetic mutations in flexible, unstructured regions of proteins, where over one quarter of known disease-causing mutations occur. The team developed a machine learning system, which is a computer program that learns patterns from data, that combined information about protein structure, phase separation properties, and protein sequences to better classify these mutations. Their enhanced system dramatically improved predictions when combined with existing mutation-prediction tools, boosting accuracy scores from as low as 59 percent to as high as 92 percent. These improvements suggest that the new approach could help doctors and researchers more accurately identify which genetic mutations cause disease, potentially leading to better genetic testing and diagnosis. The findings demonstrate that adding specialized knowledge about flexible protein regions to existing prediction tools can significantly enhance their ability to spot harmful mutations.

title: What Is the Role of Endothelial Cells in Cerebral Blood Flow Dysregulation in Small Vessel Disease?
abstract: Endothelial cells are a critical component of the neurovascular unit (NVU). They express ion channels and receptors that sense multiple signals, including shear stress and increased extracellular potassium (K+) resulting from neuronal activity. They release several mediators that regulate cerebral blood flow and promote vasodilation, particularly nitric oxide, thereby contributing to neurovascular coupling (functional hyperemia). Endothelial cells are connected through tight junctions and are crucial for the formation and maintenance of the blood-brain barrier. They are particularly susceptible to senescence, and their dysfunction has a key role in NVU dysregulation in cerebral small vessel disease.

llm_summary: Endothelial cells, which are the thin layer of cells that line blood vessels in the brain, play a crucial role in controlling blood flow and maintaining the protective barrier that separates the brain from harmful substances in the bloodstream. These cells are equipped with special sensors that detect signals from nerve activity and physical forces from blood moving through vessels, allowing them to respond by releasing chemicals like nitric oxide that help blood vessels relax and increase blood flow to active brain regions. The tight connections between endothelial cells form the blood-brain barrier, a critical protective structure that these cells must constantly maintain to keep the brain safe and functioning properly. When endothelial cells become damaged or age prematurely, they lose their ability to regulate blood flow correctly, which contributes to a condition called cerebral small vessel disease where tiny blood vessels in the brain stop working as they should. Understanding how endothelial cell dysfunction causes problems with blood flow regulation is important for developing new treatments for small vessel disease and other conditions that affect the brain's blood supply.

title: Locally Recurrent Rectal Cancer in the Molecular Era: A Scoping Review of Biomarkers of Oncologic Outcome following Salvage Surgery.
abstract: Radical salvage surgery offers the only chance of cure for patients with locally recurrent rectal cancer (LRRC), yet up to 50% develop disease recurrence after surgery. Identification of those at highest risk of disease recurrence may improve selection for surgery and intensification of neoadjuvant treatment. This scoping review aimed to identify molecular determinants of oncologic outcomes following surgery for LRRC.This study was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews. MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Scopus databases were searched for articles published between 2005 and 2025 that reported associations between blood, tissue, or other molecular factors and postoperative oncologic outcomes (recurrence and survival) in patients undergoing treatment for LRRC.The search identified 2799 articles, of which 17 were included. Sample size varied from 21 to 213 patients. Locoregional recurrence rates after surgery ranged from 15% to 52% (various timepoints between 3 and 5 years), while 5-year overall survival ranged from 22% to 53%. Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) was associated with shorter overall survival in 11 studies, and poorer relapse-free survival in 1 study. Elevated serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9) was associated with shorter overall survival and disease-specific survival in two studies. No studies evaluating contemporary biomarkers (mutational profile, microsatellite instability, or circulating-tumour DNA) were identified.Evidence evaluating molecular biomarkers in LRRC is limited and has focused on traditional serum biomarkers such as CEA and CA19-9. Contemporary colorectal cancer biomarkers including mutational profile and ctDNA are yet to be studied in this population.© 2026. The Author(s).

llm_summary: Locally recurrent rectal cancer, which means cancer that comes back in the same area after initial treatment, is a serious condition where surgery offers the only real chance of cure, yet about half of patients experience the cancer returning again after the operation. Researchers reviewed seventeen studies published between 2005 and 2025 that looked for biological markers, or measurable signs in blood and tissue samples, that could predict which patients would do better or worse after salvage surgery for this type of cancer. The studies found that a traditional blood marker called carcinoembryonic antigen, or CEA, was linked to shorter survival times in most cases, while another marker called CA19-9 showed similar results in a couple of studies. The major limitation of this research is that none of the studies examined modern biomarkers like genetic mutations or circulating tumor DNA, which are pieces of cancer DNA floating in the bloodstream that could provide much better predictions about patient outcomes. Future research should focus on testing these newer, more advanced biomarkers in patients with locally recurrent rectal cancer to help doctors better identify which patients are at highest risk and might benefit from more aggressive treatment before surgery.

title: Hepatic Safety of Ketamine and Esketamine for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Real-World Cohort Study.
abstract: Ketamine and esketamine are increasingly used for treatment-resistant depression (TRD), yet their hepatic safety profile with repeated or long-term use remains poorly characterized. Chronic recreational ketamine abuse has been linked to cholestasis and cholangiopathy, raising concern that therapeutic use may carry similar risks. No systematic data exist on liver enzyme trajectories or biliary injury at subanesthetic doses used for depression.This historical cohort study included adults with TRD receiving IV ketamine or intranasal (IN) esketamine at the Mayo Clinic Ketamine Clinic (2017 to 2024). Patients were eligible if they had at least one liver enzyme value (AST, ALT, ALP, or bilirubin) within 12 months before through 3 months after treatment. Longitudinal enzyme trajectories were modeled using generalized linear-mixed models with a Gamma distribution. Clinically significant elevation was defined as ≥2× the upper limit of normal (ULN). Wilcoxon signed-rank tests compared pretreatment and post-treatment paired values.Of 104 enrolled patients, 74 had liver enzyme data available; 51 had post-initiation data. Median age was 51.5 years; 72% were female. Most (78.4%) received IV ketamine. No clinically meaningful changes in enzyme trajectories were observed. Three patients (5.9%) had elevations ≥2× ULN, all attributable to alcohol use, myalgias, or pre-existing hepatic steatosis rather than (es)ketamine.Subanesthetic IV ketamine (0.5 mg/kg) and FDA-approved IN esketamine doses were not associated with clinically significant liver enzyme elevations in this real-world TRD cohort. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether ketamine and esketamine, which are increasingly used to treat severe depression that does not respond to other medications, might damage the liver during repeated use, since heavy recreational use of ketamine has been linked to liver problems. The study looked at 51 patients with treatment-resistant depression who received either intravenous ketamine injections or nasal spray esketamine at a clinic between 2017 and 2024, tracking their liver enzyme levels before and after treatment to see if there were any harmful changes. The results showed that none of the patients experienced clinically meaningful liver damage from the medications, and only three patients had elevated liver enzymes, which were caused by other factors like alcohol use or existing liver conditions rather than the ketamine or esketamine itself. These findings suggest that the doses of ketamine and esketamine used to treat depression appear to be safe for the liver and do not require doctors to routinely monitor liver function in patients without symptoms. However, the researchers note that larger and longer-term studies are still needed to fully confirm that these medications are safe for the liver over extended periods of use.

title: Psychological symptoms during perimenopause: a global perspective.
abstract: Psychological health changes are known to occur during perimenopause, but the extent to which these differ from premenopause remains unclear. This study aimed to assess psychological symptoms during perimenopause compared with premenopause and evaluate differences by country.Flo app users aged 35 years or above not taking hormonal contraception or hormone therapy were included. The psychological domain of the Menopause Rating Scale (range 0-16) and symptoms within this domain of depressive mood, irritability, anxiety, and exhaustion (range 0-4 each) were evaluated. Participants in perimenopause were compared with those in premenopause (self-reported not in perimenopause or postmenopause).A total of 7,975 women were included, with 2,353 in perimenopause (mean age 45 years [SD±4.5]) and 5,622 in premenopause (39 y [SD±4.0]). Psychological Menopause Rating Scale scores in the perimenopause group were significantly higher (7.3 [SD±3.56]) than in the premenopause group (4.8 [SD±3.56]; P<0.001). The individual symptoms of depressive mood, irritability, anxiety, and exhaustion were also higher in the perimenopause group (P<0.001, for all respectively), with the largest difference being exhaustion. These findings remained after adjusting for known confounders, including an existing diagnosis of anxiety or depression. Geographic analysis included 20 countries across 6 continents, with significant differences identified between countries for the overall psychological symptom domain score and all individual symptoms.Significantly greater psychological symptom burden was identified in the perimenopause group compared with the premenopause group, with the greatest difference noted for the individual symptom of exhaustion. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether women going through perimenopause, which is the transition period leading up to menopause when hormone levels become unstable, experience more psychological symptoms like depression, irritability, anxiety, and exhaustion compared to women still in their regular reproductive years. The study included nearly eight thousand women from twenty countries across six continents who used a health tracking app and were not taking hormonal birth control or hormone therapy, and researchers measured their psychological symptoms using a standardized rating scale. Women in perimenopause reported significantly higher levels of all four psychological symptoms compared to women in premenopause, with exhaustion showing the largest difference between the two groups, and these results held true even after accounting for other factors like whether women already had diagnosed anxiety or depression. The findings suggest that perimenopause brings a real and measurable increase in psychological symptom burden that goes beyond what women experience in their earlier reproductive years, which could help healthcare providers better recognize and support women during this life transition. The study also found that the severity of these psychological symptoms varied considerably depending on which country women lived in, suggesting that cultural, environmental, or healthcare system differences may play a role in how women experience perimenopause.

title: Weight loss interventions and sexual function in midlife women: the emerging role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists.
abstract: Sexual health is a multidimensional aspect of women's well-being. It is particularly vulnerable during midlife, when the physiological and psychosocial changes of the menopause transition intersect with the growing burden of obesity. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have emerged as highly effective pharmacologic treatments for obesity, yet their effects on female sexual function remain largely uncharacterized. This review aims to discuss the interplay among obesity, midlife, obesity treatments, and female sexual health, with a focused synthesis of available evidence on GLP-1-based therapies and sexual outcomes in women.This narrative review synthesizes preclinical studies, case reports, observational data, and clinical trials identified through PubMed searches from inception through March 2026, examining female sexual function in the context of obesity, the menopause transition, obesity treatments, and GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy.Obesity impairs female sexual function through hormonal, vascular, and psychosocial mechanisms. Accordingly, lifestyle interventions and bariatric surgery have demonstrated meaningful improvements in sexual function. In contrast, GLP-1 receptor agonists, despite conferring substantial weight loss and favorable metabolic effects, may paradoxically suppress sexual desire and arousal through central neuroendocrine mechanisms, including the modulation of dopaminergic reward and serotonergic signaling. While emerging case reports and preclinical data support this concern, systematic clinical evidence remains limited, highlighting the need for prospective studies with longitudinal sexual function endpoints. In this context, clinicians should proactively assess sexual function before and during GLP-1 therapy using validated instruments and integrate sexual health into comprehensive obesity care for midlife women.Copyright © 2026 by The Menopause Society.

llm_summary: Sexual health becomes particularly challenging for women in midlife when obesity and menopause changes happen at the same time, making this an important health issue to understand. Researchers reviewed scientific studies, case reports, and clinical trials to examine how weight loss treatments, especially a newer drug class called glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (medications that help people lose weight by affecting hunger signals in the brain), affect sexual function in midlife women. The review found that obesity itself damages sexual function through hormonal imbalances, blood vessel problems, and emotional stress, while traditional weight loss methods like lifestyle changes and weight loss surgery do improve sexual health. However, the newer weight loss medications, despite helping people lose significant amounts of weight and improving metabolism, may actually reduce sexual desire and arousal by changing brain chemistry related to pleasure and mood. Doctors should talk with midlife women about their sexual health before and during treatment with these weight loss medications and should include sexual wellness as part of overall obesity care, while more research is needed to fully understand these effects.

title: Shared Decision making aids in palliative care: A systematic review & meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Shared Decision Making in palliative care encompassing patient-clinician collaboration has shown potential for improved patient outcomes. However, the impact of decision aids intended to support palliative care decision making discussions across clinical care settings remains uncertain.To assess the impact of shared of decision aids on decision making, clinical outcomes, and quality of life for patients with palliative care needs and their caregivers.Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, reported according to PRISMA, with overall evidence quality assessed using GRADE.Ovid MEDLINE (all segments), EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and Scopus, from inception through September 20, 2024, without restrictions on publication date, sample size, or language. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials that included adult patients with palliative care needs or their caregivers, using any form of decision aids. Outcomes encompassed decision-related, clinical, and quality of life measures.Sixteen randomized controlled trials were included. Participant ages ranged from 44 to 85 years. Predominant decision aids were videos or printed materials addressing goals of care and treatment options, with aims that included improving understanding of prognosis and supporting values clarification. Decision aids significantly improved decision-related knowledge (SMD: 0.40, 95% CI: 0.14-0.67, p = 0.003) and lowered preference for cardiopulmonary resuscitation (OR: 0.28, 95% CI: 0.20-0.40, p < 0.001). They showed no significant impact on decisional conflict, satisfaction, or regret.Evidence regarding the effectiveness of decision aids in palliative care decision making is limited and of low overall quality, with observed improvements primarily in patient knowledge and changes in stated treatment preferences rather than established improvements in decision quality or values-concordant care. Future research should prioritize integration into comprehensive shared decision making frameworks, cultural adaptations, and larger-scale studies to enhance patient-centered outcomes.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether decision aids, which are tools like videos or printed materials that help patients and doctors talk through medical choices together, could improve how people make decisions about end-of-life care. The team reviewed sixteen randomized controlled trials, which are studies where some patients received decision aids while others did not, to see if these tools actually helped patients understand their options better and feel more satisfied with their choices. The decision aids did help patients understand their medical situation more clearly and led fewer people to choose cardiopulmonary resuscitation, which is the emergency procedure doctors perform when someone's heart stops, but the tools did not reduce patients' worry about making the right choice or improve their overall satisfaction. The researchers found that while these decision aids show some promise, the overall quality of evidence supporting their use is still low, meaning we need more and better studies to truly know if they help patients make choices that match their personal values and beliefs. Future research should focus on testing these tools in larger groups of patients, adapting them for different cultures and communities, and combining them with comprehensive conversations between patients and doctors to create real improvements in patient-centered care.

title: Hearing in noise and cognitive status in older adults: Biomarker associations and bidirectional survival analyses.
abstract: BackgroundHearing impairment (HI) has been identified as a potentially modifiable risk factor for dementia, yet its relationship with Alzheimer's disease (AD) neuropathology and the temporal directionality remain unclear, particularly in late life.ObjectiveTo examine cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between HI, clinical cognitive status, and AD biomarkers in community-dwelling older adults.MethodsWe included 474 DRIVES Project participants (mean age 73.5 ± 5.2 years). Hearing was assessed using the NIH Toolbox Words-in-Noise (WIN) test. Clinical cognitive status was assessed using Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR). AD biomarkers included cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) Aβ42/Aβ40, t-tau/Aβ42, and p-tau/Aβ42 ratios and amyloid PET imaging. Multivariable linear, logistic, Cox proportional hazards, and Fine-Gray competing-risk models were used.ResultsHI was more prevalent among participants with mild cognitive impairment (MCI; defined as CDR = 0.5) than cognitively normal individuals (50% versus 24%, p < 0.001), and MCI status was independently associated with worse baseline WIN thresholds (β = 1.55 dB SNR; 95% CI 0.72-2.37). HI was not cross-sectionally associated with CSF amyloid or tau ratios or amyloid PET positivity. Longitudinally, baseline MCI was associated with a higher risk of incident HI (Cox HR = 2.63, 95% CI 1.48-4.67; Fine-Gray sHR = 2.79, 95% CI 1.06-7.40), whereas baseline HI was not associated with subsequent CDR progression.ConclusionsIn older adults, HI was associated with MCI but not core AD biomarkers or future CDR progression, suggesting that late-life HI may reflect cognitive vulnerability or broader brain aging rather than independently driving AD pathology.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether hearing loss in older adults is connected to Alzheimer's disease and cognitive decline, since previous studies suggested hearing problems might increase dementia risk. The study followed 474 community-dwelling older adults with an average age of 73 years, measuring their hearing ability using a speech-in-noise test and checking their cognitive status and brain biomarkers, which are biological signs of disease found in spinal fluid and brain imaging. The results showed that people with mild cognitive impairment were more likely to have hearing loss than those with normal thinking abilities, but hearing loss was not directly linked to the biological markers of Alzheimer's disease in the brain. Interestingly, people who started the study with mild cognitive impairment were more likely to develop hearing loss over time, but those with hearing loss at the beginning did not show faster cognitive decline later. These findings suggest that late-life hearing loss may be a sign of general brain aging or cognitive vulnerability rather than a direct cause of Alzheimer's disease development.

title: Hidden risk in normal myocardial perfusion scans: AI-detected proximal coronary calcium on CT attenuation maps improves prognosis.
abstract: Spatial distribution of coronary artery calcium (CAC) may provide additional prognostic value in patients undergoing SPECT and PET myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI). We aimed to automatically identify CAC in proximal segments from attenuation correction CT (CTAC) scans using artificial intelligence (AI) and to evaluate prognostic significance in two large international multicenter registries.From hybrid MPI/CT imaging (N = 43,099) across 15 sites, we included 4,552 most relevant patients with (1) no prior coronary artery disease; (2) AI-derived mild CAC scores (1-99); and (3) normal perfusion (stress total perfusion deficit < 5%). The independent associations between AI-identified proximal CAC and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality (ACM) were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression, likelihood ratio test (LRT), and continuous net reclassification index (NRI).Among the patients with mild CAC and normal perfusion (mean age 65 ± 12 years, 51% male), 1,730 (38%) had proximal CAC. Over 3.6 (inter-quartile interval 2.1, 5.2) years follow-up, 599 (13%) and 444 (10%) patients had MACE or ACM, respectively. Proximal CAC was associated with an increased risk of MACE (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.24, 95% CI 1.03-1.48, P = 0.02) and ACM (adjusted HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.01-1.53, P = 0.04) after the adjustment of CAC score and density, clinical risk factors, and perfusion deficit. Proximal CAC improved the risk stratification of MACE (LRT P = 0.02; NRI 12%) and ACM (LRT P = 0.04; NRI 12%).In patients with mild CAC and normal myocardial perfusion, AI-based proximal CAC detection identified a subgroup at increased risk of adverse outcomes. Automated identification of proximal CAC may provide incremental prognostic information beyond perfusion findings and CAC scoring and could improve risk stratification in patients who might otherwise be considered low risk.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether the location of calcium buildup in heart arteries could help predict which patients might have heart problems in the future, even when their heart scans appear normal. The study used artificial intelligence to automatically detect calcium deposits in the main sections of coronary arteries from CT scans taken on over 4,500 patients with mild calcium buildup and normal heart perfusion scans across 15 medical centers worldwide. Among these patients, those with calcium deposits in the proximal or main portions of their arteries had a higher risk of major heart events and death over the following years compared to those without calcium in these key locations. The findings suggest that identifying where calcium is located in the arteries provides important additional information beyond standard calcium scoring and perfusion imaging, potentially helping doctors identify patients who need closer monitoring or more aggressive treatment. This artificial intelligence approach could improve how doctors assess heart disease risk in patients who might otherwise be considered low-risk based on their normal perfusion scans alone.

title: Multi-center Phase 1 study of Triapine in Combination with [177Lu]Lutetium-Dotatate in Patients with Well-Differentiated Neuroendocrine Tumors (ETCTN 10388).
abstract: Next generation of Theranostics studies are looking at novel combinations with radiation sensitizers to enhance PRRT's efficacy. Here, we present safety and efficacy data from a multi-center phase 1 study of a [¹⁷⁷Lu]lutetium-dotatate -triapine combination in patients with GEP-NETs.The study consisted of two phases (dose escalation and expansion) administering the recommended phase 2 doses (RP2D) for the two agents. All patients received 200 mCi of [¹⁷⁷Lu]lutetium-dotatate on day 1 of four 8-week cycles, in combination with oral triapine administered at assigned dose levels (100 mg, 150 mg or 200mg) from days 1 to 14 of each cycle.A total of 31 (A: 15 ; B: 16 ) patients received treatment. Nine patients experienced dose-limiting toxicities; Grade 3 anemia (n=1), Grade 5 cardiac arrest (n=1), and Grade 4 neutropenia (n=7). Based on the overall safety and pharmacokinetics data, a [¹⁷⁷Lu]lutetium-dotatate (200 mCi) plus triapine (150 mg) dose was selected as the RP2D for the expansion phase. Grade ≥3 treatment related adverse events were observed in 77% patients: anemia (23%), nausea and vomiting (3% ), lymphopenia ( 58%), neutropenia ( 35%) and leukopenia ( 39%). The majority of cytopenias were transient and resolved within two weeks. Among the 28 evaluable patients, the objective response rate (ORR) was 21.4% and the median progression-free survival (mPFS) has not been reached (median follow-up period: 23.7 months).The combination of [¹⁷⁷Lu]lutetium-dotatate (200 mCi) and oral triapine (150 mg D1-14) was well tolerated and demonstrated preliminary activity in patients with well-differentiated GEP-NETs. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new treatment approach for neuroendocrine tumors, which are rare cancers that grow slowly in hormone-producing cells throughout the body, by combining a radioactive therapy with a drug designed to make cancer cells more sensitive to radiation. The study involved 31 patients who received four treatment cycles over eight weeks, with each cycle including a radioactive injection on day one followed by an oral medication taken for two weeks. The treatment caused significant side effects in most patients, particularly low blood cell counts that were usually temporary and resolved within two weeks, though one patient experienced a serious heart-related event. Among the 28 patients who could be evaluated for treatment response, about one in five showed tumor shrinkage, and the average time before cancer returned or worsened had not yet been reached even after nearly two years of follow-up. The combination of the radioactive therapy at a dose of 200 millicuries with the oral medication at 150 milligrams appeared to be tolerable and showed promise for treating patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors, though further testing in larger patient groups is needed to confirm these early results.

title: Continuation of direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin during critical illness: bleeding and clinical outcomes in a multicenter ICU cohort.
abstract: A growing proportion of patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) receive chronic oral anticoagulation with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) or warfarin. The comparative safety of continuing DOACs versus warfarin during critical illness remains uncertain. We evaluated bleeding and clinical outcomes among ICU patients who continued the same oral anticoagulant during the early ICU course. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult ICU admissions across Mayo Clinic sites from 2012 to 2023. Eligible patients were taking a DOAC or warfarin at ICU admission and continued the same anticoagulant during the first three ICU calendar days. The primary outcome was major bleeding during the index hospitalization. Secondary outcomes included ICU and hospital mortality, ICU- and hospital-free days, bleeding subtypes, and need for procedural interventions. Among 6,258 eligible ICU admissions, 2,410 patients continued the same oral anticoagulant during the first three ICU calendar days, including 1,074 continuing DOAC therapy and 1,336 continuing warfarin therapy. In the multivariable analysis, there was no statistically significant difference in major bleeding events, (aOR 1.34, 95% CI 0.89-2.02; p = 0.161) between the DOACs and warfarin groups, respectively. Gastrointestinal bleeding (GI) was more frequent among patients continuing warfarin and remained significant after adjustment (adjusted OR 3.90, 95% CI 1.91-7.94; p < 0.001). Hospital mortality was lower with warfarin use than DOACs (5.6% vs 11.6%; p < 0.001; aOR 0.47, 95% CI 0.33-0.68). Among ICU patients selected to continue their baseline oral anticoagulant, continued DOAC therapy was not associated with higher adjusted odds of major bleeding and was associated with lower GI bleeding events than warfarin, but this bleeding advantage did not translate into lower mortality. This discordance suggests that the mortality in this population is driven largely by illness severity, comorbidity, unmeasured confounding and other non-bleeding related pathways.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether patients in intensive care units who were already taking blood-thinning medications should continue taking the same type they used at home, comparing two common options called direct oral anticoagulants and warfarin. The study looked back at medical records from over six thousand intensive care patients across Mayo Clinic hospitals between 2012 and 2023, focusing on about twenty-four hundred patients who continued their original blood thinner during their first three days in the unit. The results showed that continuing direct oral anticoagulants did not cause more major bleeding than warfarin, and patients on warfarin actually experienced more stomach and intestinal bleeding, yet surprisingly those on warfarin had lower death rates during their hospital stay. This unexpected finding suggests that the deaths in these critically ill patients were likely caused by how severe their illness was and other health problems rather than by bleeding complications from the blood thinners. Future research should explore why the bleeding advantage of direct oral anticoagulants did not lead to better survival rates and help doctors make better decisions about managing blood thinners in very sick patients.

Enzymatic assays, which are laboratory tests that use special proteins called enzymes to measure creatinine, can sometimes give false or misleading results when certain medications like acetaminophen are present in a patient's blood.

title: A Retrospective Analysis of Itraconazole and Hydroxy-Itraconazole Serum Concentrations Correlation to Clinical Outcomes of Histoplasmosis Treatment.
abstract: Itraconazole is the preferred antifungal agent for mild to moderate histoplasmosis and step-down therapy following amphotericin B treatment. Although hydroxy-itraconazole, a major metabolite of itraconazole, displays antifungal activity comparable with that of the parent compound, its role in therapeutic drug monitoring targets for histoplasmosis remains uncertain.The objective was to compare clinical outcomes and adverse events using itraconazole parent-compound concentrations alone versus combined itraconazole and hydroxy-itraconazole concentrations in patients treated for histoplasmosis. This retrospective cohort study included adults with probable or proven histoplasmosis who received itraconazole and had at least 1 documented serum concentration. The primary outcome was clinical response across 3 groups: (1) parent (itraconazole parent-compound concentration >1.0 mcg/mL), (2) combined (parent-compound concentration <1.0 mcg/mL with combined itraconazole plus hydroxy-itraconazole >1.0 mcg/mL), and (3) subtherapeutic (failure to reach either threshold). Treatment response and adverse events were analyzed using the Fisher exact test.Among 108 patients (parent, n = 40; combined, n = 40; subtherapeutic, n = 28), response rates differed across groups (parent (95%); combined (90%); subtherapeutic (67.9%); P = 0.006). There was no difference between the parent and combined groups. Adverse events did not differ, although drug discontinuation occurred more frequently in the subtherapeutic group (parent (5%); combined (20%); subtherapeutic (25%); P = 0.04).Patients who failed to achieve either an itraconazole concentration >1 mcg/mL or a combined itraconazole plus hydroxy-itraconazole concentration >1 mcg/mL had lower response rates. Similar outcomes among patients achieving the itraconazole target alone and those achieving the combined target suggest that hydroxy-itraconazole concentrations may contribute to therapeutic drug monitoring targets in histoplasmosis.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. llm_summary: Itraconazole is a common antifungal medication used to treat histoplasmosis, a serious fungal infection, but doctors have been uncertain whether they should monitor just the main drug in the bloodstream or also track its byproduct called hydroxy-itraconazole. Researchers reviewed medical records of 108 patients who received itraconazole treatment for histoplasmosis and had their blood drug levels measured to see which monitoring approach worked best. Patients who had adequate levels of itraconazole alone had a 95 percent success rate, while those with adequate combined levels of both the drug and its byproduct had a 90 percent success rate, and those with insufficient levels of either had only a 68 percent success rate. The similar outcomes between the two adequate-level groups suggest that doctors may be able to count the byproduct hydroxy-itraconazole toward their treatment targets, which could help more patients achieve therapeutic benefit. This finding could change how doctors monitor itraconazole therapy in the future, though more research may be needed to confirm these results in larger patient populations.

title: Comparison of eGFR based on Serum Cystatin C or Creatinine in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
abstract: Total kidney volume (TKV), a prognostic biomarker in ADPKD, is used to stratify high risk individuals. eGFR measures may carry significant error in ADPKD compared to measured GFR(mGFR). This retrospective study investigates the association between height adjusted TKV (htTKV) and eGFR derived from race-free CKD-EPI equations utilizing creatinine and cystatin C.eGFR was calculated using 3 race-free CKD-EPI formulas: creatinine-based (CKD-EPI creatinine), cystatin C (CKD-EPI cys), and creatinine-cystatin C (CKD-EPI creatinine-cystatin C) equations on 697 Mayo Clinic ADPKD patients. Correlations between eGFR and TKV measures were estimated and stratified by MIC class risk groups and CKD. Linear regression models were computed to predict ln(htTKV) from the 3 eGFR data sets. The eGFR measures were compared to iothalamate-based mGFR in a subset of patients (n=50).A correlation between eGFR measures and htTKV (Pearson correlation r of -0.53 to -0.54), varied by MIC stratification. Pearson correlation was -0.47 to -0.48 for MIC 1A and 1B, -0.67 to -0.71 for MIC 1C, and -0.67 to -0.68 for MIC 1D and 1E. All equations were significantly associated with htTKV levels, with similar adjusted beta values (95% CI) of -0.15 (-0.17 to -0.13), -0.14 (-0.16 to -0.12), -0.15 (-0.16 to -0.13), for CKD-EPI creatinine, CKD-EPI cystatin C, and CKD-EPI creatinine-cystatin C, respectively. Compared to mGFR, the CKD-EPI creatinine-cystatin C equation was the least biased (mean -0.86 (95% CI: -3.09 to 1.37)) versus CKD-EPI creatinine (2.31 (-0.73 to 5.34)) or CKD-EPI cystatin C (-3.54 (-5.86 to -1.21)), and most precise, with 1-P30 of 16% (95% CI 7.2% to 29.1%), compared to 18% (8.6% to 31.4%) for CKD-EPI creatinine, or 20% (10.0% to 33.7%) for CKD-EPI cystatin C.A moderate correlation between eGFR and htTKV associated with MIC stratification. Associations between htTKV and all 3 CKD-EPI equations were similar. llm_summary: Researchers examined how well different blood tests measure kidney function in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, a genetic condition where cysts grow in the kidneys and gradually damage them. The study looked at nearly 700 patients from Mayo Clinic and compared three different equations that estimate kidney function using either creatinine (a waste product in blood), cystatin C (another protein in blood), or a combination of both. All three blood test methods showed similar moderate connections to kidney size measurements, which doctors use to predict how quickly the disease will progress, though the strength of these connections varied depending on how advanced the disease was in each patient. When compared to a more accurate gold-standard kidney function test, the combination equation using both creatinine and cystatin C proved to be the most reliable and least likely to give misleading results. These findings suggest that using both blood markers together may be a better approach for monitoring kidney function in patients with this inherited kidney disease.

title: Harnessing the Biologic Power of Bacteriophages to Improve the Treatment of Periprosthetic Joint Infection: Barriers and Future Directions.
abstract: ➢ Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains the most common cause of failure after total joint arthroplasty, with current standard therapies associated with failure rates between 10% and 30%.➢ The 2025 International Consensus Meeting in Istanbul, Türkiye, highlighted the potential benefits of bacteriophage (phage) therapy in managing PJI.➢ One of the barriers to integrating phage therapy into standard clinical PJI care is the knowledge gap between preclinical research and clinical practice.➢ This Expert Review summarizes the key therapeutic advantages of using phages as an adjuvant therapeutic platform for PJI. It also highlights the current challenges that are continuing to limit the integration of phages into standard PJI care.Copyright © 2026 by The Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery, Incorporated.

llm_summary: Infections that develop around artificial joints after replacement surgery remain a major problem, causing about 10 to 30 percent of surgeries to fail even with current treatments. Researchers and doctors gathered at an international meeting in Istanbul to discuss using bacteriophages, which are tiny viruses that attack bacteria, as a new way to fight these stubborn joint infections. This expert review examines the potential benefits of using phage therapy alongside other treatments for periprosthetic joint infections, while also identifying the main obstacles preventing doctors from using this approach in regular patient care. The biggest challenge is that laboratory research on phages shows promise, but doctors and hospitals do not yet have enough real-world evidence and practical knowledge to confidently use this treatment in hospitals and clinics. Moving forward, researchers need to bridge the gap between what works in the lab and what can actually help patients in everyday medical practice.

title: Lisocabtagene maraleucel combined with ibrutinib in R/R CLL or SLL: primary results from TRANSCEND CLL 004.
abstract: Patients in the liso-cel plus ibrutinib cohort of the phase 1/2, open-label TRANSCEND CLL 004 study had relapsed/refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) and received liso-cel (50×106 [dose level (DL)1] or 100×106 [DL2] chimeric antigen receptor-positive T cells) with concurrent ibrutinib from enrollment through 90 days after liso-cel infusion or longer per investigator discretion. Primary end point was complete response/remission (CR)/CR with incomplete marrow recovery (CRi) by investigator assessment. Among 56 patients who received ibrutinib plus liso-cel (DL1, n=5; DL2, n=51), median (range) age was 64.5 years (44‒77), 98% had high-risk cytogenetics, 55% had progression on Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor and venetoclax failure, and median (range) number of prior therapies was 5 (1‒13). Median (range) follow-up was 24.8 months (3.1‒51.8). At DL2, CR/CRi rate was 45% (95% confidence interval [CI], 31‒60) and overall response rate was 86% (95% CI, 74‒94). Median (95% CI) duration of response was not reached (NR; 28.7‒NR) for patients with CR/CRi and 41.4 months (23.3‒NR) for all responders. Median (95% CI) progression-free survival was 31.4 months (20.1‒NR). In DL1+DL2, most common grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAE) were neutropenia (52%) and anemia (41%). Cytokine release syndrome was reported in 80% of patients (grade 3, 4%; no grade 4/5), and neurological events in 41% (grade 3/4, 11%; no grade 5). Ibrutinib-related TEAEs were reported in 68% of patients (grade 3/4, 43%; no grade 5). Liso-cel plus ibrutinib demonstrated notable efficacy in patients with relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL with predictable and manageable safety. llm_summary: Researchers examined a combination treatment approach for patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia, a blood cancer that had stopped responding to standard therapies, because existing treatments were no longer working for many of these patients. The study tested whether combining two drugs—lisocabtagene maraleucel, which is a type of immune cell therapy that teaches a patient's own white blood cells to fight cancer, and ibrutinib, a targeted cancer drug—could help 56 heavily treated patients achieve remission or significant improvement. The results showed that 45 percent of patients experienced complete remission or near-complete remission, while 86 percent of patients responded positively to the treatment, with many maintaining their response for years. The main side effects included low white blood cell counts and anemia, along with manageable immune reactions, meaning this combination appeared to work well without causing uncontrollable harm. These findings suggest that combining these two drugs could offer hope to patients with hard-to-treat blood cancers, though doctors will need to continue monitoring long-term outcomes and comparing this approach to other available options.

title: Guidelines for Pediatric Radiotherapy Simulation: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group Radiation Oncology Discipline.
abstract: Pediatric radiation therapy presents unique challenges compared to adult treatments, including those of immobilization, potential need for sedation, and the critical importance of accurate, reproducible positioning. Additionally, heightened attention to imaging doses is necessary to minimize long-term toxicity in survivors. Many of these challenges must be addressed during the process of simulation. This report provides guidelines for pediatric radiotherapy simulation from the Children's Oncology Group. These guidelines cover all anatomic sites and include recommendations for photon and proton therapies, as well as specialized procedures such as stereotactic body radiation therapy, brachytherapy, and total body irradiation. These guidelines are presented as recommendations rather than prescriptive standards as the practice will vary depending on patient age, diagnosis, clinical judgment, and institutional resources.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Treating cancer with radiation in children is more complicated than treating adults because children need special positioning devices to stay still, may require sedation or sleep medicine, and must be positioned exactly the same way each time for accuracy. The Children's Oncology Group, which is a large network of cancer doctors and hospitals, created a set of guidelines to help doctors prepare children for radiation therapy in the safest and most effective way possible. These guidelines cover all parts of the body and include recommendations for different types of radiation treatment, including standard radiation, proton therapy which uses different particles, and specialized procedures like stereotactic body radiation therapy which targets tumors very precisely. The guidelines also emphasize keeping imaging doses as low as possible because children who survive cancer need to avoid unnecessary radiation exposure that could cause health problems later in life. These recommendations are flexible rather than strict rules because the best approach depends on each child's age, type of cancer, what the doctor thinks is best, and what equipment and resources each hospital has available.

title: Lesion-Level Association Between Artificial Intelligence-Derived Coronary Calcium Volume and Plaque Vulnerability.
abstract: Extensively calcified lesions are typically at low risk for lesion-level acute events, which may be related to less vulnerable plaques.This study sought to evaluate the lesion-level association between total calcification volume and plaque vulnerability.Data were derived from the prospective, observational PECTUS-obs study, in which patients with myocardial infarction underwent intracoronary optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging of all fractional flow reserve-negative nonculprit lesions. OCT images were analyzed by a core laboratory for plaque vulnerability features (lipid-rich plaque, thin-cap fibroatheroma, layered plaque, macrophage accumulation, microvessel, and cholesterol crystal) and by a validated artificial intelligence algorithm (OCT-AID) for automated volumetric calcium quantification. Total calcium volume was indexed for lesion length and stratified by quartiles (Q1-Q4), from lowest to highest.Among 488 lesions from 414 patients, calcium plaques were identified in 470 (96.3%) lesions. The lesion-level median indexed total calcium volume ranged from 0.004 mm3/mm (IQR: 0.001-0.011) in Q1 to 0.83 mm3/mm (IQR: 0.63-1.18) in Q4. The lower quartiles demonstrated the highest prevalence of lipid-rich plaques, macrophage accumulation, and microvessels. Thin-cap fibroatheroma and layered plaques accumulated predominantly in the middle quartiles (Q2-Q3). Cholesterol crystals showed no significant differences between quartiles. Overall, Q1-Q3 lesions demonstrated a greater mean number of plaque vulnerability features than Q4 lesions (P < 0.001 for all).Most severely calcified nonculprit lesions demonstrate a significantly lower prevalence of plaque vulnerability features as compared to less calcified, more lipid-rich lesions, which may contribute to the lower lesion-level acute event rate observed in heavily calcified lesions.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether heavily calcified plaques in coronary arteries, which are the blood vessels that supply the heart, are actually safer and less likely to cause heart attacks compared to less calcified plaques. The study analyzed images from 488 coronary lesions, which are areas of plaque buildup, taken from 414 heart attack patients using a special imaging technique called optical coherence tomography combined with artificial intelligence software to measure calcium volume. The results showed that lesions with the highest amount of calcium had significantly fewer dangerous features like lipid-rich plaques, macrophage accumulation, and microvessels, while lesions with lower calcium levels showed more of these risky characteristics. This finding helps explain why heavily calcified lesions appear to cause fewer acute heart events, suggesting that extensive calcium buildup may actually stabilize plaques and make them less likely to rupture and trigger a heart attack. These results could help doctors better assess which coronary lesions pose the greatest risk to patients and guide treatment decisions in the future.

title: Safety of Ketorolac in Primary Total Hip Arthroplasties: An Analysis of over 7,000 Cases.
abstract: Ketorolac is commonly utilized perioperatively in primary total hip arthroplasty (THA), either intravenously (IV) or via periarticular infiltration analgesia (PAI). While effective for pain control, concerns remain regarding its potential to cause acute kidney injury (AKI), particularly in patients who have chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study evaluated the association between perioperative ketorolac administration and postoperative AKI, stratified by baseline renal function and administration route.We retrospectively analyzed 7,211 inpatient THAs performed between 2011 and 2021. An AKI was defined according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Multivariable logistic regressions evaluated the association between perioperative ketorolac administration and in-hospital AKI, adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates. Subgroup analyses were conducted for patients who had (15%) and did not have (85%) preexisting CKD. Ketorolac was administered perioperatively in 35% of cases (25% periarticular infiltration analgesia, 7% intravenously, and 3% both) with a median cumulative dose of 30 mg (range, 15 to 90 mg). The mean age was 66 years, mean body mass index (BMI) 31 and 51% were women.An AKI occurred in 3.4% of cases. Ketorolac use was not associated with increased AKI risk (odds ratio (OR) 0.8; P = 0.08), regardless of administration route (all OR less than 1; all P > 0.05). Chronic kidney disease was an independent risk factor for the development of AKI (OR 4.1; P < 0.001). In patients who did not have CKD, ketorolac use was associated with a decreased risk of AKI (OR 0.6; P = 0.03) and not associated with an increased or decreased risk in those who have CKD (OR 1.1; P = 0.80). Additional independent risk factors for AKI included intraoperative transfusion (OR 4.4; P < 0.001), new-onset atrial fibrillation (OR 3; P < 0.001), history of hypertension (OR 2.2; P < 0.001), men (OR 1.4; P = 0.047), and elevated BMI (OR 1.04 per unit increase, P < 0.001).Perioperative ketorolac use does not elevate the postoperative AKI risk, regardless of administration route. Risk factors for AKI include preexisting CKD, men, elevated BMI, need for intraoperative transfusion, and history of hypertension.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether ketorolac, a common pain-relieving medication given during hip replacement surgery, might damage the kidneys, especially in patients who already have kidney problems. The study looked back at records from over seven thousand hip replacement surgeries performed between 2011 and 2021 to see how many patients developed acute kidney injury, which is a sudden loss of kidney function, and whether ketorolac use was connected to this problem. The results showed that ketorolac did not increase the risk of kidney injury after surgery, whether the medication was injected directly into the surgical area or given through an IV, and surprisingly, patients without existing kidney disease who received ketorolac actually had a lower risk of kidney problems. The findings suggest that doctors can safely use ketorolac for pain control after hip replacement surgery without worrying about it harming the kidneys, even though other factors like needing a blood transfusion during surgery, being male, having high blood pressure, or already having kidney disease do increase the risk of kidney injury. Future research should continue monitoring ketorolac use in different patient groups to confirm these results and help doctors make the best decisions about pain management after surgery.

title: Artificial intelligence in antimicrobial stewardship: prediction, clinical applications, and implementation challenges.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) continues to threaten modern infectious diseases practice. Antimicrobial stewardship programs (ASPs) remain central to optimizing antimicrobial use, yet stewardship has become increasingly challenging because of rising clinical complexity, expanding data sources, and persistent workforce and analytic constraints. Artificial intelligence (AI) may strengthen stewardship by integrating clinical, microbiologic, and contextual data to support more timely and individualized decision-making.To review current applications of AI in antimicrobial stewardship, with emphasis on resistance prediction and risk stratification, empiric therapy selection, diagnostic stewardship, antimicrobial optimization, and implementation challenges in clinical practice.Relevant studies evaluating AI and machine learning approaches for AMR prediction, diagnostic stewardship, antimicrobial optimization, and clinical implementation were reviewed.AI-based models have been developed to predict AMR and identify patients at risk for multidrug-resistant infections using electronic health record data. These approaches may support empiric therapy selection and patient-level risk stratification, although important methodological limitations remain, including heterogeneous prediction targets, data leakage, and limited external validation. AI applications also extend to diagnostic stewardship, including optimization of blood culture use, rationalization of molecular diagnostics, and support for interpretation of microbiologic results. In the therapeutic phase, AI may support de-escalation, intravenous-to-oral conversion, duration-of-therapy reassessment, and prioritization of stewardship review, aligning clinical decisions with antimicrobial stewardship goals. However, successful implementation depends not only on model performance but also on effective integration into clinical workflows, interpretability, governance, and clinician uptake.AI has the potential to enhance antimicrobial stewardship by enabling more precise, scalable, and workflow-integrated decision support. Future work should prioritize prospective and multicenter evaluation, careful implementation in routine care, and governance frameworks that address safety, transparency, equity, and clinician oversight. AI should be viewed as a tool to augment ASP expertise rather than replace clinical judgment.Copyright © 2026 European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases. llm_summary: Antimicrobial resistance, which occurs when bacteria and other germs become immune to the drugs designed to kill them, is a growing problem that makes treating infections harder and more dangerous. Researchers reviewed studies that tested whether artificial intelligence, a computer technology that learns from data patterns, could help doctors make better decisions about which antibiotics to prescribe and when to use them. The review found that artificial intelligence models can predict which patients are likely to have drug-resistant infections and can help doctors choose the right antibiotic treatment faster, as well as assist in deciding when to stop antibiotics or switch from injections to pills. However, the researchers noted that these artificial intelligence tools have important weaknesses, including that they were tested in different ways across studies, they sometimes used information that shouldn't have been included in their predictions, and they were rarely tested in multiple hospitals to confirm they work everywhere. The researchers concluded that artificial intelligence works best when it is designed to fit smoothly into how doctors actually work in hospitals, remains transparent and explainable to the doctors using it, and is always viewed as a helpful tool that supports doctor judgment rather than replaces the expertise of medical professionals.
