title: Sex Differences in Access-site and Clinical Outcomes Following Transradial Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Transradial access (TRA) for percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is associated with lower rates of bleeding and vascular complications than transfemoral access. However, it remains uncertain whether radial (including distal) access fully mitigates these established sex-based disparities in PCI outcomes. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate sex-specific procedural, access-site, and clinical outcomes following radial and distal radial PCI. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched from inception through October 2025 for randomized controlled trials and observational studies reporting PCI outcomes stratified by sex in patients undergoing radial or distal radial access. Outcomes were categorized as procedural, access-site safety, and clinical endpoints. Pooled mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Study quality was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Nine studies comprising 214,638 patients (52,486 women and 162,152 men) were included. Compared with men, women had higher rates of access-site crossover (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.58-2.22) and slightly lower procedural success (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97-0.99), despite shorter procedure duration (MD -3.62 minutes, 95% CI -7.21 to -0.04). Women experienced significantly higher rates of access-site bleeding (RR 1.84, 95% CI 1.23-2.75), hematoma (RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.00-2.91), and radial artery spasm (RR 3.40, 95% CI 1.30-8.87), while radial artery perforation did not differ by sex. Clinically, women had higher cardiovascular mortality (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.14-2.69) and major bleeding (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.24-1.84), but unexpectedly lower target vessel revascularization (RR 0.59, 95% CI 0.36-0.95). Rates of all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and major adverse cardiac events were similar between sexes. In conclusion, women undergoing PCI via radial or distal radial access experienced higher rates of access-site complications, major bleeding, and cardiovascular mortality than men, whereas ischemic outcomes were generally similar between sexes. These findings suggest that sex-related differences may persist despite the widespread use of radial access. However, the contribution of vascular access itself to these differences remains uncertain, as other clinical and procedural factors may also influence outcomes.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether using the radial artery in the wrist for heart procedures, which is known to cause fewer bleeding problems than using the groin artery, might reduce the health differences between men and women undergoing these interventions. The team reviewed nine studies involving over 214,000 patients, with about one quarter being women, and compared how often men and women experienced complications and other health outcomes during and after the procedures. Women had significantly higher rates of problems at the access site, including bleeding and artery spasms, were more likely to need to switch to a different access point, and experienced more major bleeding and heart-related deaths compared to men. Despite these complications, women and men had similar rates of heart attacks, strokes, and other serious cardiac events, though women unexpectedly needed fewer repeat procedures on the treated blood vessel. The findings suggest that even though using the wrist artery is generally safer than using the groin, sex-based differences in outcomes still exist and may be influenced by factors beyond just the choice of access site.

title: Beyond initial weight loss: procedure-specific predictors of weight recurrence after metabolic and bariatric surgery.
abstract: Weight recurrence (WR) after metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) remains a significant long-term challenge, yet the preoperative factors that predispose patients to WR may differ across procedures. This study aimed to compare preoperative predictors of WR following sleeve gastrectomy (SG), Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB), and duodenal switch (DS).This is a retrospective review of patients undergoing primary SG, RYGB, or DS between 2008 and 2022, with at least 36 months follow-up and achievement of an optimal clinical response ≥ 20% of total weight loss (TWL). Baseline demographic and clinical variables were collected including age, sex, race, preoperative body mass index (BMI), smoking history, and preoperative comorbidities. Postoperative weight measurements were used to calculate TWL and WR outcomes. Statistical analyses included chi-square testing, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and multivariable Cox regression models.A total of 2207 qualified patients (80% female, mean age 47.8 ± 11.9 years, mean BMI 46.0 ± 8.2 kg/m2) were followed over a median of five years (interquartile range (IQR) 4-5). In this cohort, 1253 (56.8%) patients experienced WR > 20%; 60.4%, 57.4%, and 33.3% of whom underwent SG, RYGB and DS, respectively (p < 0.001). Notably, WR > 50% in SG, RYGB and DS was 24.3%, 15% and 5.1%. On multivariable analysis for WR > 20% in the RYGB subgroup, older age and a history of smoking were associated with a decreased risk of WR, whereas White race was associated with an increased risk. In SG and DS subgroups, no significant predictors of WR were identified.Clinically significant WR occurred in more than half of SG and RYGB patients but was less frequent after DS. Preoperative predictors had limited value and varied by procedure, reinforcing procedure selection as a key modifiable factor in predicting WR risk.© 2026. llm_summary: Weight gain after weight loss surgery remains a major problem for many patients, making it important to understand which patients are most likely to regain weight so doctors can better prepare them. Researchers studied over two thousand patients who had one of three common weight loss surgery types—sleeve gastrectomy, gastric bypass, or duodenal switch—and followed them for about five years to see who gained weight back. More than half of the patients who had sleeve gastrectomy or gastric bypass surgery regained more than twenty percent of their lost weight, while only about one-third of those who had duodenal switch surgery experienced this level of weight regain. When doctors looked at patient information collected before surgery, they found that factors like age, race, and smoking history only predicted weight regain in the gastric bypass group, and even then the predictions were weak. These findings suggest that the type of surgery a patient chooses is more important than their personal characteristics in determining whether they will regain weight, and doctors should focus on selecting the right procedure for each patient rather than relying on preoperative factors to predict outcomes.

title: Contralateral Prophylactic Mastectomy in Women with Unilateral Breast Cancer by Age, Race, and Tumor Subtype.
abstract: Contralateral prophylactic mastectomy (CPM) is discouraged in average risk women with unilateral breast cancer (UBC) per national consensus guidelines. CPM rates among different UBC populations are unknown. Our aim was to determine CPM rates by age, race, and tumor subtype.Women with stage I-III UBC undergoing therapeutic mastectomy were identified from SEER18 cancer registries from 2010 to 2021 to compare the no CPM group and CPM group.Of 240,613 women, 31.3% underwent CPM. Non-Hispanic white (NHW) women were more likely to undergo CPM compared with non-Hispanic black (NHB), Hispanic white, and Asian women (34.7% vs. 27.6%, 27.5%, and 20.2% respectively; p < 0.0001). CPM rates increased 8.2%, from 25.4 to 33.6%, with the greatest increase in NHB (16.7%) and the smallest in Asian women (6.3%) (p < 0.0001). On multivariable analysis (MVA), factors associated with CPM were age 18-39 years (OR 3.39), white race (OR 2.46), ER-HER2- subtype (OR 1.29), and stage I disease (OR 1.43) (all p < 0.0001). MVA considering race, age, and receptor subtype, CPM rates were highest in: NHWs age 18-49 years with triple negative breast cancer (TNBC), followed by NHWs 18-49 years with ER+ cancer, and NHBs age 18-49 years with TNBC. NHBs age 18-49 years with TNBC had the greatest increase in CPM rates (24%).CPM rates in women with UBC who undergo therapeutic mastectomy continue to increase. CPM was most frequent in young NHW women with TNBC. Young NHBs with TNBC had the greatest rate of increase. Further research is needed to identify factors motivating CPM, especially in average risk women with UBC.© 2026. Society of Surgical Oncology.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether women with cancer in one breast were having surgery to remove their healthy other breast as a preventive measure, even though major medical guidelines discourage this procedure for women at average risk. The study looked at data from over 240,000 women diagnosed with early to mid-stage breast cancer between 2010 and 2021 to understand how often this preventive surgery happened and which groups of women chose it most. They found that about one in three women had this preventive surgery, with white women choosing it more often than Black, Hispanic, or Asian women, and the rate of this surgery increased significantly over the time period studied. Young white women with a particularly aggressive type of breast cancer called triple negative breast cancer had the highest rates of preventive surgery, while young Black women with the same cancer type showed the biggest increase in choosing this procedure over time. The researchers concluded that more studies are needed to understand why women are choosing this preventive surgery, especially since it is not recommended for women at average risk of developing cancer in their healthy breast.

title: Senotypes define the diverse landscape of senescent cells.
abstract: Cellular senescence was initially defined in vitro as a stable cell-cycle arrest that occurs after repeated replication, but it is now recognized as a heterogeneous state shaped by cell type, species, senescence-inducing stress, tissue microenvironment and time. To organize this complexity, we propose the term 'senotype' to classify senescent cells by their inputs, molecular features and functional effects. We outline a practical framework incorporating: (1) cell identity and context; (2) inducing mechanism; (3) temporal stage; (4) multimodal molecular and structural features; and (5) physiological or pathological functions. Experimentally defined senotypes can serve as references for interpreting tissue-derived senotypes, where parameters may be incomplete. Senotypes should be anchored in combinations of core hallmarks (that is, durable cell-cycle arrest, altered secretory profiles, macromolecular or organelle damage, disrupted homeostasis) rather than single markers. Advances in single-cell, spatial, proteomic and computational methods enable rigorous senotype characterization, improving consistency and accelerating development of targeted senotherapeutics.© 2026. llm_summary: Researchers have long understood that cells can stop dividing and enter a dormant state called senescence, but they recently discovered that this dormant state is far more complex and varied than previously thought, depending on the cell type, what triggered the dormancy, and the surrounding environment. To better organize and understand this complexity, the scientists introduced a new classification system called "senotypes" that categorizes senescent cells based on their origins, molecular features, and effects on the body. The framework they created considers five key factors: what type of cell it is and where it exists, what caused it to become senescent, how long it has been in that state, what molecular changes have occurred, and whether it helps or harms the body. Rather than relying on single markers or signs to identify senescent cells, the researchers emphasized that scientists should look for combinations of core characteristics such as permanent cell-cycle arrest, changes in how cells communicate with their surroundings, damage to cellular structures, and loss of normal cellular balance. These advances in understanding senotypes could help scientists develop more targeted and effective treatments to address the harmful effects of senescent cells in aging and disease.

title: Pediatric Trauma Education in the United States: A Nationwide Clinician Needs Assessment.
abstract: Standardized training and education are priorities for improving system-level quality and outcomes for pediatric trauma patients. The objective of this study is to identify common educational needs of pediatric trauma clinicians in the United States and the gaps in currently available education courses, to inform future curriculum development.An anonymous, IRB-approved, 30-item cross-sectional survey was developed and distributed to pediatric trauma clinicians via e-mail. Demographic and quantitative data were analyzed with descriptive statistics. Open-ended responses were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis.Two hundred four surveys were analyzed. Respondents were faculty physicians (40.7%), nurses (23.5%), trauma program managers (18.6%), advanced practice providers (11.3%), EMS (4.4%), and trainee physicians (1.5%) representing thirty-seven states. 70% worked at a pediatric trauma center. 65% had taken the ATLS course, but only 50% felt that the course prepared them to care for pediatric trauma patients. 97% had taken PALS, but only 45% felt the course prepared them for pediatric trauma care. Respondents ranked comfort with specific pediatric trauma skills. Confidence was lowest for chest tube placement (mean=5.7/10) and dosing intubation medications (6.1/10). Confidence was highest for tourniquet placement (8.2/10) and assigning a GCS to a school-aged child or teen (8.1/10). Qualitative themes included: (1) Neither ATLS nor PALS provide comprehensive pediatric trauma education; (2) Comfort with pediatric trauma comes from experience rather than course completion; (3) There is a desire for additional pediatric-specific education, and (4) Multiple specific topics were identified as educational needs.ATLS and PALS alone do not meet the need for comprehensive pediatric trauma education in the United States. Experience is most helpful for proficiency, putting low-volume centers at a disadvantage. Pediatric-specific trauma education is desired, including simulation-based courses and app-based reference materials. llm_summary: Researchers examined what training gaps exist for doctors, nurses, and other healthcare workers who treat injured children across the United States because better education could improve care and outcomes for these young patients. They sent an anonymous survey to two hundred four pediatric trauma clinicians from thirty-seven states asking about their training, comfort level with specific medical skills, and what educational needs they felt were missing. The study found that while most clinicians had taken standard trauma courses like ATLS and PALS, only about half felt these courses actually prepared them well for caring for injured children, and they reported low confidence in critical skills like placing chest tubes and calculating medication doses for intubation. The researchers discovered that clinicians felt most confident in skills they had practiced many times and that experience on the job was more helpful than course completion alone, which puts hospitals with fewer injured children at a disadvantage. The findings suggest that pediatric-specific trauma education programs, including hands-on simulation training and digital reference tools, are needed to fill gaps in current training and ensure all clinicians can confidently care for injured children.

title: Successful treatment of nonunion after high tibial osteotomy using combined Extracorporeal Magnetotransduction Therapy (EMTT) and Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy (ESWT): a case report.
abstract: This study applies pulsed electromagnetic fields, with Extracorporeal Magnetotransduction Therapy (EMTT) delivering high-intensity magnetic pulses at approximately 80 mT for therapeutic bone stimulation. High tibial osteotomy (HTO) is a commonly performed joint-preserving procedure for patients with unilateral knee osteoarthritis and malalignment of the mechanical axis. One potential complication after HTO is impaired bone healing at the osteotomy site, which can lead to nonunion. The standard treatment for nonunion typically involves surgical revision with autologous bone grafting, a method that carries the risk of increased morbidity and healthcare burden. In recent years, Extracorporeal Magnetotransduction Therapy (EMTT) and Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy (ESWT) have gained attention as emerging non-invasive treatment modalities in bone regeneration and fracture healing. This case report describes a 51-year-old male with nonunion following medial open-wedge HTO, presenting with pain and limited mobility. He received five sessions of combined EMTT and ESWT. Four weeks later, imaging confirmed complete bone healing. The patient recovered fully without complications or need for revision surgery. This case demonstrates the potential of EMTT and ESWT as non-invasive treatment options for managing nonunion following osteotomy. Further prospective studies are needed to assess their clinical efficacy and support their integration into standard treatment protocols.

llm_summary: High tibial osteotomy is a common surgical procedure that helps people with knee arthritis by realigning their leg bones, but sometimes the bone fails to heal properly at the surgery site, which normally requires another surgery with bone grafts that can cause additional problems. Researchers tested whether two non-invasive treatments using magnetic pulses and shock waves could help heal this type of bone healing failure in a 51-year-old man who had experienced this complication. The patient received five sessions combining extracorporeal magnetotransduction therapy, which uses high-intensity magnetic pulses to stimulate bone healing, and extracorporeal shock wave therapy, which uses sound waves to encourage bone repair. Within four weeks of treatment, imaging scans showed that the bone had completely healed, and the patient recovered fully without needing the traditional revision surgery that would have involved more invasive procedures. While this single case shows promising results for using these non-invasive treatments instead of surgery, doctors need to conduct larger studies with more patients to confirm whether these therapies should become standard treatment options for this type of bone healing problem.

title: Outcomes of Pediatric Non-Rhabdomyosarcoma Soft-Tissue Sarcomas of the Extremities.
abstract: Non-rhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcomas (NRSTS) account for less than 4% of pediatric cancers. Treatment and outcomes have been described in adults, but pediatric data are lacking. The purpose of this study is to review our institution's outcomes of extremity NRSTS in pediatric patients.Ninety-eight (56 male: 42 female) pediatric patients with NRSTS of the extremity at our institution were reviewed. Mean age at diagnosis was 11 ± 5 years, and mean follow-up was 12 ± 10 years. The most common diagnosis was synovial sarcoma (27%), and 60% were high-grade.Treatment included surgical resection in all patients, with 33% receiving radiation and 37% receiving systemic therapy. 20-year local recurrence- (LRFS) and metastatic disease-free survival (MDFS) were 91% and 91%, respectively, with 92% disease specific survival (DSS). High grade tumors were associated with lower LRFS (p = 0.02) and DSS (p = 0.03). Tumor size < 5 cm demonstrated improved MDFS (p = 0.03), and stage 3 tumors showed worse MDFS (p < 0.01).Treatment of pediatric NRSTS was variable, with large, deep, high-grade tumors more likely to receive neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatments. Multidisciplinary treatment was associated with high rates of local control and durable survival. This study provides an extended follow-up of pediatric patients to identify late complications.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Soft tissue sarcomas that are not rhabdomyosarcoma, which is a rare type of cancer muscle tumor, make up less than four percent of childhood cancers, yet doctors have limited information about how children with these tumors do after treatment. Researchers reviewed ninety-eight children with these tumors in their arms or legs, tracking their health for an average of twelve years to understand which treatments worked best and what happened to patients over time. The most common type was synovial sarcoma, and all patients had surgery to remove the tumor, while about one-third also received radiation therapy and more than one-third received chemotherapy or other cancer-fighting drugs. After twenty years, about nine out of ten children were free from cancer returning to the same spot, nine out of ten were free from cancer spreading to other parts of the body, and ninety-two percent survived their disease. Larger tumors and tumors that were more aggressive under the microscope had worse outcomes, suggesting that doctors should treat these cases more intensively and follow children closely for many years to catch any late problems that might develop.

title: Twenty-Five-Year Follow-Up of Quantified Mitral Regurgitation.
abstract: Current guidelines recommend consideration of surgical treatment for asymptomatic patients with severe mitral valve regurgitation, but the long-term prognosis and optimal treatment of those with moderate mitral regurgitation (MR) remain uncertain.To evaluate the long-term prognostic value of baseline MR severity and the association of surgery with survival outcomes in asymptomatic patients.This was a prospective cohort study with extended follow-up among 449 asymptomatic patients with holosystolic degenerative MR enrolled between January 1991 and November 2000 and followed up with through May 2025 (median [IQR] follow-up, 26 [14-29] years; maximum, 34 years) at a single tertiary referral center (the Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota).Baseline MR severity quantified by effective regurgitant orifice area (ERO). Patients were monitored under medical therapy and, when applicable, after subsequent surgical correction.All-cause mortality, assessed according to baseline ERO using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors.Among the 449 patients included, the mean (SD) age was 64 (14) years, and 278 participants (62%) were male. At baseline, 127 patients (28%) had ERO <20 mm2, 128 (28%) had ERO 20-39 mm2, and 194 (43%) had ERO ≥40 mm2. During follow-up, 254 patients (57%) underwent mitral valve surgery. Ten-year cumulative incidence of surgery was 18% for ERO <20 mm2, 64% for 20-39 mm2, and 88% for ≥40 mm2. Survival of medically treated patients declined progressively with increasing ERO category (5-year rate: 88% [<20 mm2], 72% [20-39 mm2], and 55% [≥40 mm2]; P = .01), and multivariable analysis confirmed the incremental risk of higher ERO on a continuous scale (adjusted hazard ratio per IQR increase, 2.53; 95% CI, 1.30-4.93; P = .01). When extending the analysis through subsequent surgical follow-up, the survival difference between patients who did vs did not undergo operation widened with ERO (χ23 = 8.4; interaction P = .04), starting at values above 30 mm2.In this 25-year follow-up cohort study, increasing ERO was associated with an increase in risk of mortality under medical therapy. Patients with upper-moderate MR (ERO 30-39 mm2) at baseline demonstrated a significant association between surgical treatment and improved long-term survival.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether the severity of mitral valve leakage, which is when blood flows backward through a heart valve, affects how long patients live and whether surgery helps them survive longer. The study followed 449 patients with heart valve problems for up to 34 years, measuring the size of the leakage opening in their hearts and tracking whether they had surgery or received only medical treatment. Patients with larger leakage openings had worse survival rates when treated with medicine alone, with five-year survival dropping from 88 percent in those with small leaks to just 55 percent in those with large leaks. The most important finding was that patients with moderate-to-large leaks between 30 and 39 square millimeters lived significantly longer if they had surgery compared to those who only took medicine. These results suggest that doctors should consider recommending heart surgery earlier for patients with moderate mitral valve leakage rather than waiting to see if their condition gets worse.

title: Global Burden of Elevated LDL-C: Findings From the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract: Elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is a modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, the leading cause of premature death worldwide. Assessing the LDL-C-related burden is critical for guiding prevention and treatment strategies.To estimate the global, regional, and national burden of ischemic heart disease and ischemic stroke attributable to elevated LDL-C (relative to 35-54 mg/dL) from 1990 to 2023 and to quantify the contributions of population growth, aging, risk-deleted burden, and exposure changes to burden trends.This comparative risk assessment, part of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, estimated population-level LDL-C exposure and associated health loss in 204 countries and territories. Mean LDL-C levels were estimated using spatiotemporal gaussian process regression based on 806 studies across 161 countries. Relative risks were derived from meta-analyses of 38 randomized clinical trials. Population-attributable fractions for deaths and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were estimated by age and sex for adults aged 25 years or older from 1990 to 2023, with 95% uncertainty intervals.Population-level LDL-C concentrations.Population-attributable fractions, counts, and rates (all ages and age standardized per 100 000) of LDL-C-attributable deaths and DALYs from ischemic heart disease and ischemic stroke, with uncertainty intervals.In 2023, elevated LDL-C accounted for 3.6 million deaths (95% uncertainty interval, 2.2-5.4 million; 6.0% of global mortality) and 90.7 million DALYs (95% uncertainty interval, 58.9-123.3 million; 3.2% of DALYs). Although global all-ages rates remained stable, age-standardized death and DALY rates decreased by 45.6% and 39.5%, respectively, since 1990. In 2023, age-standardized LDL-C-attributable DALY rates were highest in Eastern Europe and lowest in high-income Asia-Pacific. One-third of the global LDL-C burden occurred in India and China. Population growth and aging drove the increasing burden, with notable regional disparities in LDL-C exposure and risk-deleted DALY rates shifting toward middle-sociodemographic settings.Despite declining age-standardized rates, the absolute LDL-C burden has increased since 1990 due to demographic changes and has shifted toward middle-sociodemographic countries. Measurement and surveillance gaps persist. Strengthened prevention, diagnosis, and treatment access strategies are essential to mitigate the health burden of LDL-C.

llm_summary: High cholesterol, specifically a type called low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), is a major risk factor for heart attacks and strokes, which are the leading causes of death worldwide, making it important to understand how much illness and death it causes globally. Researchers analyzed data from over 800 studies across 161 countries to measure cholesterol levels in populations and combined this with information from 38 clinical trials to estimate how many deaths and cases of disability resulted from elevated cholesterol between 1990 and 2023. In 2023, elevated cholesterol caused approximately 3. 6 million deaths and 90. 7 million years of life lost to illness or disability, accounting for about 6 percent of all deaths globally, though the age-adjusted rates have actually improved by roughly 45 percent since 1990.

title: End-Organ Damage Associated With Primary Hyperparathyroidism.
abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) is common and contributes to skeletal and kidney end-organ damage. Although parathyroidectomy can mitigate these complications, many patients are managed with observation, and real-world data on the population-based frequency and timing of end-organ damage under usual care are limited.To evaluate the frequency and timing of end-organ damage associated with PHPT.This cohort study included a population-based cohort identified from national electronic health record (EHR) and claims data (2010-2023) with follow-up through 2023. Participants were adults with a new biochemical diagnosis of PHPT. Data analysis was performed from August 2025 to April 2026.A new biochemical diagnosis of PHPT was defined as an elevated PTH (>65 pg/mL) within 1 month after a second elevated calcium level (serum calcium >10.2 mg/dL or ionized calcium >1.3 mmol/L or >5.3 mg/dL).PHPT-associated end-organ damage (osteoporosis, atraumatic fractures, kidney stones, stage 3 or worse chronic kidney disease) at or after PHPT diagnosis using EHR or claim codes and laboratory data, in addition to the frequency and timing of parathyroidectomy.A total of 43 399 patients with PHPT were identified (mean [SD] age, 67.9 [12.5] years; 33 854 [78%] female and 9545 [22%] male), of whom 22 279 (51.3%) had end-organ damage at diagnosis. Among 21 120 patients without end-organ damage at diagnosis, 6762 (32.0%) progressed to end-organ damage after a median (IQR) 516 (166-1125) days. Only 4442 patients (19.9%) with end-organ damage at diagnosis were treated with parathyroidectomy. Among those who progressed to end-organ damage, 1348 (19.9%) underwent subsequent parathyroidectomy, which occurred a median (IQR) 154 (41-439) days later.In this national cohort of adults with a biochemical diagnosis of PHPT, 67% had PHPT-associated end-organ damage at diagnosis or on follow-up. Despite this, parathyroidectomy was uncommon. These findings may inform strategies to optimize utilization of parathyroidectomy and mitigate PHPT-associated morbidity.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a common condition called primary hyperparathyroidism, where the parathyroid glands produce too much hormone and can damage bones and kidneys over time. The study looked at nearly 43,400 patients diagnosed with this condition between 2010 and 2023, tracking whether they developed serious complications like weak bones, fractures, kidney stones, or kidney disease. The results showed that two-thirds of patients had some type of organ damage either at the time of diagnosis or during follow-up, yet only about one in five patients received surgery to remove the problematic parathyroid glands. Among patients who did not have damage at first but developed it later, surgery was performed in less than one in five cases, and it typically happened several months after the damage appeared. These findings suggest that many patients with this condition are not receiving surgery even when they develop serious complications, which points to a need for better strategies to help doctors decide when surgery would benefit their patients.

title: Cardiovascular Health Across the Life Course for Individuals With Breast Cancer: A Review.
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common cancer diagnosed in women. Therapies for breast cancer are evolving rapidly, and several are associated with cardiovascular adverse effects, can exacerbate cardiovascular risk factors, or can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease.Advances in screening and treatment have led to earlier diagnosis and improved disease-free survival. For long-term survivors of breast cancer, cardiovascular adverse effects can pose a greater threat to overall long-term health than the cancer itself. Additionally, the increasing incidence of breast cancer in younger, premenopausal women has created a distinct demographic with unique medical needs.Cardiology practitioners need to remain updated on rapidly evolving breast cancer therapies to care for this growing, unique patient population. The field of cardio-oncology has evolved to address the cardiovascular needs of patients and survivors.

llm_summary: Breast cancer is the most common cancer affecting women, and while new treatments have improved survival rates, many of these therapies can harm the heart or worsen existing heart disease risk factors. For women who survive breast cancer long-term, heart problems can actually become a bigger health threat than the cancer itself, especially since more younger women are now being diagnosed with the disease. Doctors who specialize in heart health need to stay informed about the latest breast cancer treatments so they can properly care for this growing group of patients and watch for heart-related side effects. A new medical field called cardio-oncology has developed specifically to address the heart health needs of cancer patients and survivors by combining expertise from both heart doctors and cancer specialists. Understanding how breast cancer therapies affect the heart across a woman's entire life is essential for improving long-term health outcomes and preventing serious complications in this vulnerable population.

title: Dysregulated Iron Metabolism In Remodeling of Aging Asthmatic Human Airways.
abstract: Iron is essential for cellular function, and lung cells are no exception. Previous studies have demonstrated an association between increased level of iron in the lung and aging and age-related lung diseases including pulmonary fibrosis and asthma in the elderly (AIE). However, the mechanisms underlying the accumulation of iron with aging or AIE, or the cell types involved, remain understudied. In the context of asthma, airway smooth muscle is a key cell type contributing to contractility as well as airway remodeling (proliferation, fibrosis). In this study we characterized iron level and regulation in human (hASM) from young (<45 yr), old (≥65 yr) and AIE (≥65 yr) male/female patients, and investigated the contribution of iron overload in hASM to airway remodeling. Cells were treated with ferric ammonium citrate (FAC) (100 μM; 72h) or iron chelator deferoxamine (DFO) (100 µM; 72h). Basal levels of intracellular ferrous iron (Fe2+) were determined using the fluorescent dye FerroOrange. Cell lysates were analyzed for iron accumulation, antioxidant, lipid peroxidation, and extracellular matrix (ECM) markers, and cell proliferation was assessed. We found that iron accumulates with aging, but surprisingly decreases with AIE. hASM from AIE patients showed activated antioxidant pathways and lipid peroxidation, while FAC-exposure impaired iron metabolism and enhanced ECM deposition. Iron depletion mitigated the antioxidant response, lipid peroxidation, cell proliferation, ECM production. These findings suggest that iron metabolism in hASM contributes to cell hyperplasia and ECM, while in aging and particularly AIE, counter-regulatory changes in iron metabolism and antioxidant pathways occur, overall promoting airway remodeling.

llm_summary: Iron is an essential mineral that helps cells function properly, and previous research has shown that iron builds up in the lungs as people age and develop age-related diseases like asthma in elderly patients. Researchers studied airway smooth muscle cells, which are the muscles surrounding airways that control breathing and can thicken during asthma, from young patients under 45 years old and older patients over 65 years old, including those with elderly asthma, to understand how iron levels change and affect these cells. The study found that iron accumulated in cells from aging patients but surprisingly decreased in cells from elderly asthma patients, and when researchers added extra iron to cells, it worsened the buildup of scar tissue and increased cell growth. When researchers removed iron from the cells using a chelating agent, which is a chemical that binds to and removes iron, they reduced cell overgrowth, scar tissue production, and the activation of protective cellular pathways. These findings suggest that iron metabolism plays an important role in airway remodeling during aging and elderly asthma, opening new possibilities for understanding how iron management might help prevent or slow the progression of asthma in older adults.

title: Pragmatic Assessment of VA-ECMO Decannulation Readiness After Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
abstract: Readiness for venoarterial-extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) decannulation after extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains poorly defined.The objective of the study was to identify bedside clinical variables associated with successful decannulation in OHCA patients treated with ECPR.Consecutive OHCA patients treated under the Minnesota Resuscitation Consortium ECPR protocol from December 2015 to March 2023 were analyzed. Hemodynamic, vasoactive medication, echocardiographic, and mechanical circulatory support variables were compared between successful and failed decannulation. Feature importance analysis was conducted using Bayesian additive regression trees and multivariable logistic regression.Among 390 OHCA ECPR patients, 125 underwent VA-ECMO decannulation; 110 (88%) were successful. Failed decannulations were less likely to have been witnessed arrests (73% vs 100%; P = 0.04) and had lower rates of bystander CPR (36.4% vs 68.6%; P = 0.05). On weaning readiness assessment, left ventricular ejection fraction at lowest VA-ECMO flow (OR: 0.96; 95% CI: 0.92-0.99; P = 0.024), arterial pulsatility (OR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.90-0.99; P = 0.027), Vasoactive inotrope score (OR: 1.16; 95%-CI: 1.04-1.32; P = 0.013) and days on VA-ECMO support (OR: 1.40; 95%-CI: 1.13-1.79; P = 0.003) were significantly associated with decannulation success. A Bayesian additive regression trees model incorporating left ventricular ejection fraction, pulsatility, vasoactive-inotrope score, predecannulation VA-ECMO flow, and concomitant intra-aortic balloon pump support predicted success with an area under the curve of 0.91.Our study identifies several pragmatic variables, noninvasive and accessible at the bedside that are predictive of successful decannulation among OHCA patients undergoing ECPR. Prospective validation of a composite decannulation prediction score incorporating these variables is warranted to aid decision-making.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers examined how to determine when patients who suffered out-of-hospital cardiac arrests and were kept alive using a heart-lung machine called VA-ECMO could safely have that machine removed. The study looked at 125 patients from December 2015 to March 2023 who were treated with this machine after their hearts stopped beating, comparing those who successfully came off the machine with those who did not. The researchers found that successful patients tended to have had witnessed arrests where bystanders performed CPR, and they identified five key measurements taken at the bedside that predicted success, including how well the heart was pumping, how steady the heartbeat was, how many medications were needed to support the heart, and how long the patient had been on the machine. A computer model using these five measurements could predict whether a patient would successfully come off the machine with high accuracy, suggesting these simple bedside tests could help doctors make better decisions about when to remove the device. The researchers say that testing this prediction tool in future studies could help doctors more confidently decide when patients are ready to be disconnected from the heart-lung machine.

title: Feasibility of Laryngoscopy & Videostroboscopy Education Modules: Knowledge and Confidence Outcomes.
abstract: To evaluate the effectiveness of a comprehensive, web-based educational module on laryngoscopy and videostroboscopy in improving knowledge and confidence scores among otolaryngology-head and neck surgery residents and related medical trainees.Eighteen otolaryngology residents, medical students, and speech-language pathology trainees completed a web-based educational module on laryngoscopy and videostroboscopy, as well as premodule and postmodule knowledge assessments and confidence ratings. Participants also rated postmodule satisfaction and provided qualitative feedback.Statistically significant improvements (P < 0.001) with large effect sizes were observed in knowledge assessment scores and confidence ratings for both laryngoscopy and videostroboscopy. Satisfaction with the module was high, with 100% of participants reporting they were either fairly or completely satisfied. Qualitative feedback highlighted the module's clarity, flexibility, and usefulness, particularly for early-stage learners.This web-based module effectively improved learner knowledge and confidence regarding laryngoscopy and videostroboscopy. The findings support its use as a flexible, accessible educational tool for otolaryngology trainees and learners in related fields.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Doctors who treat voice and throat problems need good training to perform laryngoscopy and videostroboscopy, which are procedures that let them see inside the voice box to check for problems. Researchers tested whether a web-based educational module, or online learning program, could help eighteen medical trainees including otolaryngology residents, medical students, and speech-language pathology students learn these procedures better. After completing the online module along with knowledge tests before and after, participants showed significant improvements in both what they knew about the procedures and how confident they felt performing them. All of the participants reported being satisfied with the online module, and many noted that it was clear, easy to access at their own pace, and especially helpful for people just starting to learn these skills. These results suggest that web-based educational modules like this one could be a valuable tool for training doctors and other medical professionals in laryngoscopy and videostroboscopy procedures.

title: Differential Endothelial and Smooth Muscle Cell Proliferation on Metallic Substrates Used in Flow Diversion and Coil Embolization of Intracranial Aneurysms.
abstract: Endovascular treatment of intracranial aneurysms (IA) relies on flow diversion and coil embolization. The metallic substrates used in these devices directly contact endothelial cells (ECs) and smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and influence healing. Because controlled comparisons of vascular response across clinically used metals are limited, this study evaluated whether commonly used bare-metal substrates differentially affect EC and SMC proliferation.Flat coupons of nitinol, nitinol with a light thermal oxide (LTO) coating, 316LVM (stainless steel), 35NLT (cobalt-nickel-chromium), platinum, and cobalt were prepared. Human aortic ECs and SMCs were cultured on each surface. EC proliferation was assessed at 24, 48, and 72 hours, and SMC proliferation at 5, 7, and 10 days using a fluorometric live-dead viability assay and immunofluorescence microscopy. Group differences were analyzed by analysis of variance.EC proliferation varied markedly by material and time. Nitinol, nitinol+LTO, 35NLT, and 316LVM supported robust endothelial growth (all p < 0.001), unlike platinum and cobalt. Immunofluorescence showed dense coverage on nitinol/stainless steel but sparse on platinum/cobalt. SMCs attached to most substrates except cobalt with limited, nonprogressive proliferation, indicating restrained neointimal expansion.EC proliferation differed across bare-metal substrates under static in vitro conditions, whereas SMC proliferation was comparatively limited. Nitinol, nitinol+LTO, 35NLT, and 316LVM supported greater EC proliferation than platinum and cobalt. These findings identify material-dependent vascular cell responses that warrant confirmation in flow-based, blood-contacting, device-level models before clinical extrapolation.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how different metal materials used in devices that treat brain aneurysms (bulges in blood vessels in the brain) affect the growth of two types of cells that line and surround blood vessels. The team tested six different metals commonly used in these medical devices by growing human blood vessel cells on flat samples of each metal and measuring how well the cells multiplied over several days and weeks. They found that four metals—nitinol, nitinol with a special coating, stainless steel, and cobalt-nickel-chromium—supported strong growth of the inner lining cells, while platinum and cobalt did not, and all metals showed limited growth of the muscle cells that surround blood vessels. These results suggest that the choice of metal material in brain aneurysm devices could influence how well the body's own cells heal around the device after it is placed. The researchers noted that these findings came from laboratory tests in still conditions and that more testing is needed using flowing blood and actual devices before doctors can apply these results to patient care.

title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy and Neurocognitive Outcomes in Medically Managed Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have been shown to reduce invasive interventions and improve symptom control in idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH). However, their impact on neurocognitive outcomes remains unknown.We used the TriNetX US Collaborative Network to conduct a propensity score-matched study of adults with a first IIH diagnosis from January 2016 to December 2025. The GLP-1RA cohort-initiated therapy within 1 month before to 3 months after diagnosis. Patients with CSF diversion, venous sinus stenting, or pre-existing cognitive or fatigue diagnoses were excluded. Matching balanced demographics, cardiometabolic comorbidities, IIH-directed pharmacotherapy, BMI, and HbA1c. Cognitive decline, dementia composite, fatigue, inpatient admission, and emergency department visits were assessed at 1, 3, and 5 years using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses.After matching, 3,652 patients were retained in each cohort. At 5 years, GLP-1RA use was associated with lower event probabilities for cognitive decline, 4.69% versus 7.99%, HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.38-0.69; cognitive decline or dementia, 4.88% versus 8.17%, HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.39-0.69; and fatigue, 11.79% versus 14.88%, HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.59-0.87. Event probabilities were also lower for inpatient admission, 39.24% versus 41.70%, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.64-0.77; and emergency department visits, 29.55% versus 37.82%, HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.62-0.76.In medically managed adults with IIH, GLP-1RA therapy was associated with lower risks of incident cognitive decline, cognitive decline or dementia, fatigue, inpatient admission, and emergency department visits. These findings suggest GLP-1RAs improve neurocognitive outcomes and quality of life in IIH.© 2026 by American Journal of Neuroradiology.

llm_summary: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension is a serious condition where pressure builds up inside the skull without a clear cause, and it can affect thinking and memory, so researchers wanted to see if a diabetes medication called glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist could help protect the brain. The researchers compared two groups of patients with this condition—one group that took the medication within a few months of diagnosis and another group that did not—making sure both groups were similar in age, weight, and other health factors to make a fair comparison. After five years, patients who took the medication had significantly lower rates of thinking problems and memory loss, with only about 4. 7 percent experiencing cognitive decline compared to 8 percent in the group without the medication. The medication also reduced other problems like fatigue, hospital admissions, and emergency room visits, suggesting it may improve both brain health and overall quality of life for people with this condition.

title: De-escalation trials in multiple myeloma: past, present and future.
abstract: De-escalation of therapy constitutes a new phase in the development of therapeutic approaches for patients with multiple myeloma (MM) and is aimed at maintaining durable disease control while reducing the toxicity and burden associated with prolonged treatment. Given that increasingly effective agents, including immunotherapies, are now used earlier in the course of MM, we must assess not only how much therapy is needed to enable a clinical response but also how much is required to sustain it. In this Review, we synthesize emerging evidence supporting multiple de-escalation strategies, including dose and schedule modification, withdrawal of individual agents from multidrug regimens, fixed-duration approaches with treatment-free intervals, minimal residual disease-adapted strategies, omission of autologous stem cell transplantation and single infusion of chimeric antigen receptor T cells. We highlight how contemporary trials are beginning to define the patient populations and treatment components most amenable to de-escalation while exposing ongoing uncertainties and challenges, including those relating to monitoring strategies, re-treatment criteria and feasibility. Finally, we discuss methodological and implementation challenges including end point selection, clinical trial design, integration of correlative translational research, funding models and the involvement of key stakeholders required to translate de-escalation approaches from concept to a clinical trial and, eventually, routine clinical practice.© 2026. llm_summary: Multiple myeloma is a serious blood cancer that requires ongoing treatment, but doctors are now testing whether patients can receive less intensive therapy while still keeping their disease under control and reducing harmful side effects. Researchers reviewed emerging evidence from clinical trials testing various de-escalation strategies, which means reducing the amount or intensity of cancer treatment, including lowering drug doses, stopping certain drugs while continuing others, taking breaks from treatment, and using newer approaches like special immune cells called chimeric antigen receptor T cells that only need to be given once. The review found that several de-escalation approaches show promise for maintaining disease control while decreasing the burden and toxicity patients experience, and that trials are beginning to identify which patients and treatment combinations work best for this reduced-intensity approach. However, significant challenges remain in determining how to monitor patients after treatment reduction, when to restart treatment if the cancer returns, and how to design clinical trials that properly test these new strategies. Moving forward, researchers and healthcare systems will need to work together to establish clear guidelines, select appropriate measures of success, and integrate new scientific discoveries to make de-escalation approaches a standard part of multiple myeloma care.

title: Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.
abstract: Senescent cells promote tissue dysfunction in part through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)1. Cytosolic mitochondrial nucleic acids activate innate immune signalling to initiate this inflammatory programme2,3. Here we show that mitochondrial metabolism provides a second layer of control that enables execution of the inflammatory programme. In senescent cells, the mitochondrial pyruvate-citrate-acetyl-CoA axis is upregulated, increasing the availability of acetyl-CoA to support histone acetylation at SASP genes. Whereas mitochondrial DNA-driven signalling activates inflammatory transcription factors, acetyl-CoA availability is required for robust transcription of SASP genes. Accordingly, enhancing acetyl-CoA levels promotes SASP gene expression, whereas inhibition of SLC25A1, the mitochondrial citrate exporter, reduces histone acetylation at SASP loci, limiting activity of this programme. In vivo, inhibition of SLC25A1 reduces chromatin accessibility at SASP loci, dampens inflammation and improves healthspan in aged mice. Together, these findings identify a mitochondrial metabolic checkpoint that enables the epigenetic execution of innate immune signalling, revealing a mechanism that selectively controls the inflammatory output of senescent cells.© 2026. llm_summary: Senescent cells, which are aging cells that stop dividing, release harmful substances that damage tissues and contribute to age-related diseases, a process scientists call the senescence-associated secretory phenotype or SASP. Researchers discovered that senescent cells use a specific metabolic pathway involving mitochondria, the energy-producing structures inside cells, to produce a molecule called acetyl-CoA that fuels the production of inflammatory proteins. The team found that while damaged genetic material from mitochondria initially triggers the inflammatory response, the availability of acetyl-CoA is what actually allows cells to produce large amounts of these harmful inflammatory proteins. When scientists blocked the protein responsible for exporting citrate from mitochondria in aging mice, they reduced inflammation and improved the animals' overall health and lifespan. These findings suggest that targeting this metabolic checkpoint could be a new way to reduce harmful inflammation in aging and age-related diseases without completely shutting down the immune system.

title: Stuck in traffic: CART cells targeting the tumor microenvironment in hematological malignancies, current advances and future perspectives.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CART) therapy has revolutionized the treatment of B cell hematological malignancies, and has lead to several FDA-approved CART products beginning in 2017. However, while CART cell therapy has improved outcomes and survival, many patients eventually relapse after treatment. Research into the reasons for patient relapse following CART cell therapy has identified multiple mechanisms of resistance. These primarily include antigen loss, poor CART cell expansion or exhaustion, and tumor- or tumor-microenvironment (TME)-mediated immunosuppression of CART cells. While methods to study and engineer CART cells to circumvent antigenic loss or to prevent exhaustion are being investigated, the development of standalone or combination CART cell therapies that target both cancer cells and immunosuppressive components of the TME are less studied. In this review, we focus on the impact of the TME on CART cell efficacy in hematological malignancies and discuss promising basic and clinical approaches that may enable CART cells to overcome TME-mediated dysfunction.© 2026. llm_summary: Chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy, which is a treatment that trains a patient's own immune cells to fight cancer, has become a major breakthrough for treating blood cancers and has earned approval from the FDA starting in 2017. Although this therapy has helped many patients survive longer, researchers have noticed that some patients eventually experience cancer returning after treatment, which led scientists to investigate why the therapy sometimes fails. The main reasons for treatment failure include cancer cells hiding from the immune system, the engineered T cells becoming weak or exhausted, and the tumor creating an environment that suppresses the immune system's ability to fight back. This review focuses on how the tumor's surrounding environment interferes with the effectiveness of these engineered T cells in blood cancers and explores new approaches that might help the immune cells overcome this interference. Future treatments that target both the cancer cells and the immunosuppressive components of the tumor environment, either alone or in combination with other therapies, may help more patients benefit from this promising cancer treatment.

title: Meta-Analysis of Genome-Wide Association Studies of Doxorubicin-Induced Arrhythmia Identifies MMP16 and KCTD15 as Risk Loci.
abstract: Anthracyclines are a widely used and effective class of chemotherapy. However, a major limitation for their use is cardiotoxicity, manifesting as systolic dysfunction, congestive heart failure, and arrhythmias. The objective of this study was to identify genes and genetic risk variants for doxorubicin-induced arrhythmia.We performed genome-wide association studies and meta-analysis across 2 independent nonoverlapping, genetically homogenous data sets from the Molecular Epidemiology Resource (cases N=77, controls N=1184) and Tapestry (cases N=13, controls N=172). Doxorubicin-related arrhythmia was the primary cardiac outcome, followed by investigation of a broader phenotype of cardiac events. Effects of doxorubicin on top-associated genes were assessed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction on RNA extracted from human cardiomyocytes following treatment with doxorubicin and by echocardiography in a zebrafish model of doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy.In the meta-analysis, rs12151014 at the KCTD15 locus was associated with doxorubicin-related arrhythmia at the genome-wide significance (minor allele frequency in Molecular Epidemiology Resource cases 0.195 versus 0.069 in controls; Tapestry cases 0.192 versus 0.079 in controls) P=9.01×10-9; odds ratio, 3.61. MMP16 rs1094199 was associated with the broader phenotype of arrhythmia and heart failure (minor allele frequency in Molecular Epidemiology Resource cases 0.079 versus 0.019 in controls; Tapestry cases 0.038 versus 0.015) P=1.98×10-8; odds ratio=6.15. In human cardiomyocytes, MMP16 and KCTD15 gene expression was significantly downregulated by doxorubicin, and in a zebrafish MMP16 knockout was protective of doxorubicin-induced decline in left ventricular ejection fraction.Genetic variants at KCTD15 and MMP16 are associated with doxorubicin-related arrhythmia and cardiac events. MMP16 is a potential cardioprotective therapeutic target.

llm_summary: Doxorubicin is a powerful cancer-fighting drug that saves many lives, but it can damage the heart and cause dangerous irregular heartbeats in some patients, which limits how much doctors can safely use it. Researchers combined genetic information from two separate groups of cancer patients to search for specific DNA variations that might make certain people more likely to develop heart rhythm problems from this drug. They discovered that two genetic variants, one in a gene called KCTD15 and another in a gene called MMP16, were strongly linked to patients who experienced irregular heartbeats after receiving doxorubicin treatment. When the researchers tested these genes in human heart cells treated with doxorubicin and in zebrafish with damaged hearts, they found that the MMP16 gene appeared to protect the heart from injury. These findings suggest that doctors might one day use genetic testing to predict which patients are at high risk for heart problems from this cancer drug, and that MMP16 could be a target for developing new medicines to protect the heart during chemotherapy.

title: Women's Experiences With Telemedicine: Predictors of Satisfaction in Ambulatory Care.
abstract: Telemedicine use has expanded rapidly across ambulatory care. Satisfaction with telemedicine services has been associated with social determinants of health (SDOH) such as socioeconomic status, ethnicity, and employment status. However, little is known about gender-specific patterns in patient experience. This study examined how demographic and SDOH are associated with telehealth satisfaction among women.A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using data from female patients who completed standardized post-telehealth surveys within the Mayo Clinic Health Care System between March 2020 and December 15, 2023. Logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between patient satisfaction and the following demographics and SDOH: age, race, ethnicity, marital status, Elixhauser score, mental health diagnosis, stress risk, financial risk, transportation risk, food insecurity risk, primary language, and physical activity risk.Among 51,512 female patients, higher age was associated with less satisfaction with "ease of scheduling appointment" and "ease of contacting clinic," but was associated with significantly higher satisfaction for other measures, including "care practitioners' efforts to include" and "recommending healthcare office." A high Elixhauser score was associated with lower satisfaction with "how well the audio and video connections worked."A higher Elixhauser score and older age emerged as key factors associated with telehealth satisfaction among women. Targeted efforts to support patients with complex health needs and those requiring enhanced care coordination may improve satisfaction and equity in ambulatory telemedicine.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. llm_summary: Researchers examined how women's satisfaction with telemedicine, or doctor visits conducted remotely through video and phone, is affected by factors like age, health status, and social circumstances such as income level and access to transportation. The study looked at survey responses from over 51,000 women who used telemedicine services at Mayo Clinic between 2020 and 2023, using statistical analysis to identify which patient characteristics predicted satisfaction with their remote care experience. The results showed that older women were less satisfied with scheduling and contacting their clinics but were actually more satisfied with how their doctors included them in care decisions, while women with more serious health conditions reported problems with audio and video connection quality. The findings suggest that healthcare systems should focus on improving technology and scheduling systems for older patients and provide extra support for women managing multiple complex health conditions to make telemedicine work better for everyone. Future efforts to improve telemedicine should address these specific needs so that all women, regardless of age or health status, have equally positive experiences with remote healthcare.

title: Single-electrode simultaneous detection of tonic dopamine and serotonin in vivo using an interleaved cyclic square wave voltammetry approach.
abstract: Tonic levels of DA and 5-HT serve as master regulators of motivational behavior and affective stability, yet their simultaneous quantification in vivo has remained a significant technical challenge. Here, we present an interleaved scanning strategy that alternates between Multiple Cyclic Square Wave Voltammetry (MCSWV) and N-shaped Multiple Cyclic Square Wave Voltammetry (N-MCSWV) waveforms on a single carbon fiber microelectrode, enabling the concurrent measurement of absolute basal concentrations of both neurotransmitters. Systematic optimization of repetition time and holding potential confirmed that the interleaved approach fully preserves the sensitivity and selectivity of each individual waveform. A two-step mathematical deconvolution algorithm, exploiting the inherent 5-HT selectivity of N-MCSWV, was established to precisely isolate the DA contribution from the composite MCSWV signal. In vitro validation demonstrated excellent linearity and selectivity against key metabolic interferents, including DOPAC and 5-HIAA. Pharmacological challenges in the NAc of anesthetized rats further confirmed the in vivo efficacy of the platform: escitalopram selectively elevated tonic 5-HT to 171.1% of baseline while leaving DA unchanged, whereas pargyline concurrently increased both tonic DA (120.4%) and 5-HT (116.1%). These findings demonstrate that interleaved scanning is a robust, high-resolution tool for simultaneously monitoring complex monoaminergic interactions, offering a powerful platform for advancing our understanding of the neurochemical basis of reward and emotional regulation.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a longstanding challenge in neuroscience: measuring two important brain chemicals called dopamine and serotonin at the same time, since these chemicals control mood, motivation, and emotional stability. They developed a new technique using a single tiny electrode that switches between two different electrical scanning methods to detect both neurotransmitters simultaneously in the brains of living rats. The method worked by using a special mathematical process to separate the signals from each chemical, and tests showed it could accurately measure dopamine and serotonin without being confused by other similar chemicals in the brain. When they gave rats different drugs that affect these neurotransmitters, the electrode successfully tracked how each chemical changed independently, proving the technique could reveal how dopamine and serotonin interact in real brain tissue. This breakthrough offers scientists a powerful new tool to better understand how these brain chemicals work together to control behavior and emotions, which could eventually help develop better treatments for mood and motivation disorders.

title: DNR Status and Hospital Mortality Measures Postmyocardial Infarction: Differentiating Preventable From Unpreventable Deaths in CMS Data.
abstract: Publicly reported 30-day acute myocardial infarction (AMI) mortality rates are widely used to benchmark hospital performance. However, these measures may lack validity when they include deaths among patients with do-not-resuscitate (DNR) orders or those receiving palliative care-groups for whom mortality may be expected and goal-concordant.We analyzed the national 100% Medicare Inpatient Standard Analytic File and Medicare Beneficiary Summary file to assess 30-day AMI mortality rates stratified by DNR status (absent, present-on-admission, and postadmission) and palliative care involvement. We then conducted a retrospective chart review of all 30-day AMI mortalities at a single academic medical center (2019-2025), applying Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events and a Palliative Performance Scale scores to identify unpreventable deaths, which we defined as a Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events >190.5 or Palliative Performance Scale ≤40%. Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events is a risk-stratification tool using clinical and laboratory variables whereas the Palliative Performance Scale is a bedside functional status and palliative care assessment quantifying patient's self-care ability.Across n=467 259 total AMI encounters, mean (SD) age was 75.1 (10.5), and the population was 44% female. Thirty-day mortality was 10.4% (39 112/376 062) among patients without DNRs, 43.1% (26 181/60 719) in those with present-on-admission DNR, and 72.1% (21 984/30 478) in those with postadmission DNR. Among 9.2% (43 090/467 259) of encounters with palliative care, there was a 76.9% mortality rate (33 151/43 090). Hazard ratios for mortality were 5.25 (95% CI, 5.17-5.33) for present-on-admission DNR and 10.73 (95% CI, 10.55-10.91) for postadmission DNR as compared with encounters without DNRs. Among n=24 AMI mortalities at our institution, 71% (17/24) had DNRs, and 33% (8/24) met the unpreventable death criteria.The validity of 30-day AMI mortality metrics may be undermined by their inclusion of high-acuity, end-of-life patients, which may disincentivize hospitals from delivering appropriate, patient-centered care. Removal of DNR or palliative cases from performance measures should be explored to better identify opportunities for reducing preventable deaths.

abstract: The purpose of this Guideline is to provide a framework for the treatment and follow-up of patients with a history of kidney stones in order to reduce the likelihood of recurrent disease. The summary presented herein represents Part II of the two-part series dedicated to Medical Management of Kidney Stones. Please refer to Part I for additional information on this topic.The systematic review utilized in the creation of this Guideline is based on research conducted by the Research Triangle Institute (RTI) International-University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill Evidence-based Practice Center (EPC) under contract to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) and funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute® (PCORI®). llm_summary: Kidney stones are a common problem that often comes back in people who have had them before, so doctors need clear guidance on how to prevent recurrence and manage patients over time. This guideline was created by reviewing thirty scientific studies about the best ways to prevent kidney stones through diet changes and medications, as well as how often patients should have imaging tests to check for new stones. The expert panel developed recommendations for identifying which patients are most likely to get kidney stones again and determining which of those patients should receive preventive treatment based on their individual risk level. The guideline provides doctors with evidence-based advice on when to start dietary changes and medications, helping them treat motivated patients who want to reduce their chances of developing more kidney stones. These recommendations aim to give healthcare providers a clear framework for managing kidney stone patients effectively while considering both the scientific evidence available and the practical needs of individual patients.

title: Clinical reasoning research priorities for advancing diagnostic safety: researcher and patient perspectives.
abstract: This study used both researcher and patient perspectives to identify high-priority research questions related to clinical reasoning.This study integrates findings from two previously published research prioritization exercises aimed at advancing the science of diagnostic safety, focusing on questions relevant to clinical reasoning. In Study 1 (April 2019), 97 researchers submitted 177 unique research questions that could be useful "to reduce patient harm in the diagnosis process". In Study 2 (November 2019), 41 patients/caregivers/advocates submitted 84 unique research questions on the same topic. In an in-person meeting, a subset of these participants identified 81 of these questions as high-priority (51 from Study 1; 30 from Study 2). For the current study, five investigators identified questions that focused on clinical reasoning, first independently and then by consensus. They then categorized the clinical reasoning questions into inductively identified themes.Twenty-nine of the 81 high-priority research questions addressed clinical reasoning and were categorized into 5 themes: understanding clinical reasoning and cognition (12 questions), decision support/technology (6 questions), team-based decision making (5 questions), how to learn from cases/scenarios (3 questions), and patient engagement (3 questions). Questions addressed a range of basic/foundational science and clinical applications, and involved individuals, teams, and/or systems.Identification of high-priority clinical reasoning research questions can help medical educators, clinicians, researchers, and funders catalyze research and discovery of interventions to improve clinical reasoning and ultimately improve patient outcomes.© 2026 Walter de Gruyter GmbH, Berlin/Boston.

The study combined input from two groups: ninety-seven medical researchers who submitted research questions about diagnosis safety, and forty-one patients, family members, and patient advocates who also shared their concerns about the same topic. From all the questions submitted, the researchers identified twenty-nine high-priority questions focused on clinical reasoning, which is the thinking process doctors use to figure out what is wrong with a patient, and organized them into five main categories including understanding how doctors think, using technology to help with decisions, teamwork in medical settings, learning from past cases, and involving patients in the decision-making process. These findings can help medical schools, hospitals, researchers, and organizations that fund research decide which areas to focus on to improve how doctors think through diagnoses and ultimately help patients get better care. The study shows that both doctors and patients agree on important research directions, suggesting that future work should combine expert knowledge with patient experiences to create better diagnostic tools and training.

title: Microbial Diversity in Odontogenic Sinusitis: Next-Generation Sequencing Versus Culture.
abstract: BackgroundOdontogenic sinusitis (ODS) is a common cause of unilateral infectious maxillary sinusitis but is frequently underdiagnosed due to nonspecific symptoms, subtle dental findings on imaging, and limitations of traditional bacterial cultures-particularly for anaerobic organisms. Next-generation DNA sequencing (NGS) may enhance detection of odontogenic bacteria.ObjectiveThis study compared bacterial detection between standard cultures versus NGS in patients with confirmed ODS.MethodsTwenty consecutive adults with confirmed ODS were enrolled. Maxillary sinus purulence was collected endoscopically and submitted for routine aerobic and anaerobic bacterial cultures and for NGS-based microbial profiling using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Detected organisms were categorized by aerotolerance and ODS relationship, and likely nasal colonizers were excluded from analyses. Alpha diversity, beta diversity, and compositional differences between methods were analyzed statistically.ResultsNGS detected significantly more bacterial species per specimen than culture (mean 4.9 vs 2.7; P = .0015). Compared to cultures, NGS identified more anaerobic bacteria (4.2 vs 0.9; P = .00004) and more ODS-related species (4.4 vs 1.0; P = .0001), while detection of aerobic species was similar between methods. Cultures also often yielded nonspeciated results, whereas NGS consistently revealed polymicrobial communities dominated by oral anaerobes. Microbial composition differed significantly between detection methods.ConclusionIn confirmed ODS, NGS detected significantly more anaerobic and ODS-related species than culture from the same specimens. These findings suggest that culture alone may underestimate odontogenic contributions to purulent sinusitis. Future studies should explore he utility of NGS as an adjunctive tool to facilitate diagnosis and treatment in the setting of possible ODS.

llm_summary: Odontogenic sinusitis, which is a sinus infection caused by dental problems, is often missed by doctors because symptoms are unclear and traditional bacterial tests fail to detect many of the organisms involved, especially those that grow without oxygen. Researchers studied twenty patients with confirmed tooth-related sinus infections by collecting fluid from their sinuses and testing it using two methods: standard bacterial cultures, which grow bacteria in labs, and next-generation sequencing, which is a DNA technology that identifies all bacteria present in a sample. The DNA sequencing method found significantly more bacterial species in each sample compared to traditional cultures, particularly detecting many more oxygen-avoiding bacteria and bacteria known to cause tooth-related sinus infections. These results suggest that standard culture tests alone may be missing important information about the true causes of these infections, which could lead to incomplete diagnosis and treatment. Future research should investigate whether using DNA sequencing alongside traditional tests could help doctors better diagnose and treat patients with suspected tooth-related sinus infections.

title: Factors Associated with Improved Survival for Stage I and II Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Utilizing the National Cancer Database.
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a leading cause of cancer related death in the United States. While Stage I and II PDAC represent the most treatable and potentially curative stages, most patients do not survive past 5 years of treatment. We sought to understand factors associated with long term survival in early-stage PDAC to improve outcomes and reduce disparities.The National Cancer Database (NCDB) was queried for Stage I and II PDAC patients treated between 2012 and 2021. Patients were only included if they had a documented survival information. Comparisons between patients alive or deceased at 1, 3 and 5 years were evaluated using Wilcoxon, Chi-square, and Cochran-Armitage trend tests where appropriate. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model (MVA) was used to evaluate factors associated with overall survival (OS).We analyzed 43,398 patients with Stage I (n = 21,938) and Stage II (n = 21,460) PDAC. One-, three-, and five-year survival rates were 75.2%, 30.3%, and 12.8% for Stage I, and 68.6%, 23.4%, and 10.5% for Stage II, respectively. Across both stages, improved survival was significantly associated with younger age, lower Charlson-Deyo comorbidity score, Asian race, private insurance, higher income and education levels, and tumor location in the pancreatic body or tail (all p < 0.0001). Higher tumor grade, Black race, Medicaid or uninsured status, and treatment at community-level facilities were associated with significantly worse outcomes. Multivariable analysis confirmed these variables as independent predictors of one-, three-, and five-year survival. Despite early-stage diagnosis, marked disparities in long-term survival persisted based on race, insurance, and socioeconomic status.Long-term survival for Stage I and II PDAC remains limited, despite diagnosis at an early and potentially curative stage. This highlights the need to not only focus on screening mechanisms for early diagnosis, but to address disparities and expand access to high-quality care that limit long term survival in this cohort. These results support ongoing investment in early detection, equitable treatment delivery, and research into tailored therapeutic strategies.© 2026.
