llm_summary: Researchers examined whether wearable sleep tracking devices, like smartwatches that monitor sleep patterns, actually measure sleep quality the same way that patients report it themselves or the way doctors measure it in sleep labs. The team searched medical databases for studies comparing wearable devices with validated methods of assessing sleep quality, meaning trusted tools that doctors use to evaluate how well someone sleeps, and found five studies involving over two thousand people. The results showed that wearable devices had poor to moderate agreement with what patients reported about their sleep, explaining only a small portion of the variation in sleep quality, and the devices performed especially poorly in people with insomnia and older adults compared to good sleepers. The findings suggest that wearable sleep trackers should be used as helpful tools alongside traditional sleep assessments rather than replacing them, since the current technology has significant limitations and tends to overestimate some measurements while underestimating others. Healthcare providers and patients should understand that while wearable devices can provide useful information about sleep patterns, they cannot fully capture the true picture of sleep quality that comes from validated medical assessments and patient experiences.

title: Beyond ion channel dysfunction: Integration of the transcriptome and proteome from patient-specific re-engineered cardiac cells, and population-level QT genome-wide association study reveals broad cellular dysfunction.
abstract: Congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS) is a cardiac channelopathy with increased risk of cardiac-triggered syncope/seizures, sudden cardiac arrest, and sudden cardiac death.This study aimed to describe the transcriptomic and proteomic profiles in patient-derived inducible pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte (iPSC-CM) models of the 3 canonical genotypes of congenital LQTS: LQT1, LQT2, and LQT3 and integrate these omics-level findings with each other and with population/clinical level QT-genome-wide association study (GWAS) data.LQT1, LQT2, LQT3 and respective isogenic control iPSC-CMs were cultured, and RNA and protein samples were collected. RNA sequencing and mass spectrometry-enabled proteomic analysis was performed. PrediXcan analysis was performed using QT GWAS summary statistics and transcriptome expression data. Differential gene and protein expression and ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) was performed comparing each LQT genotype with its respective isogenic control.1645 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified; 13 were altered in all 3 LQTS genotypes. IPA analysis of DEGs revealed 301 altered pathways; 47 were altered in all LQTS genotypes. Proteomic analysis identified 2561 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs); 30 were altered in all 3 genotypes. IPA analysis of DEPs identified 646 altered pathways. 306 genes/proteins were identified as significantly altered in both the transcriptome and proteome; pathway analysis of these 301 genes identified 201 altered pathways. 7 pathways were altered in all 3 LQTS genotypes in both the transcriptome and proteome. Integration of the population-level PrediXcan results and the cardiomyocyte-derived omics results identified multiple shared pathways.Multi-omics analysis of LQTS and integration of omics results with QT GWAS data reveals that primary LQTS-causative ion channel defects precipitate secondary alterations in a wide range of cellular pathways. Our findings suggest more broad molecular level changes throughout the cell. This study lays the foundation for further exploration of broad cellular changes resulting from ion channel disturbances and how they contribute to disease mechanism.Copyright © 2026 Heart Rhythm Society. llm_summary: Congenital long QT syndrome is a heart condition where people have an increased risk of fainting, seizures, and sudden cardiac death because their heart cells have problems with ion channels, which are tiny openings that control electrical activity in the heart. Researchers studied heart cells created from patient stem cells with three different types of this genetic condition and compared them to normal control cells, using advanced techniques to measure which genes were turned on or off and which proteins were present in each type of cell. The analysis revealed that while the primary problem in each type involved a specific ion channel, the genetic defects actually triggered widespread changes throughout the cells, affecting over 1,600 genes and 2,500 proteins, with many of these changes being shared across all three types of the condition. When the researchers combined their findings with large population studies of genetic variations linked to heart rhythm problems, they discovered that the same cellular pathways were affected at both the individual patient level and the population level. These results suggest that understanding long QT syndrome requires looking beyond just the broken ion channels to recognize how the initial genetic defect causes damage across many different cellular systems, which could lead to better treatments in the future.

title: Extracorporeal Life Support Use During Severe Anaphylaxis: A Systematic Review and Pooled Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
abstract: Severe anaphylaxis is a rare but life-threatening condition that may require extracorporeal life support (ECLS). A systematic review was conducted to evaluate the outcomes of patients receiving ECLS for severe anaphylaxis.A medical librarian searched six databases (2000-present) for studies reporting ECLS use in severe anaphylaxis, without language or design restrictions. Outcomes included survival, neurologic recovery, and ECLS-related complications. Data extraction was performed in duplicate, risk of bias was assessed using Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions-I and Joanna Briggs Institute tools, and event rates were estimated using Bayesian mixed-effects logistic regression. The certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation guidelines.Patients hospitalized due to anaphylactic shock.The use of ECLS in patients suffering severe anaphylaxis.A total of 50 studies describing 78 patients were included. Most underwent venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (72%), 53% underwent cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and medications were the most common trigger (60.2%). The pooled survival rate was 85.9% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 77.0-92.9), with favorable neurologic outcomes in 86.3% (95% CI: 77.5-93.8) of survivors and a complication rate of 11.0% (95% CI: 2.4-21.9). The risk of bias was high, and the certainty of the evidence was low.ECLS may provide meaningful survival and neurologic benefits in severe anaphylaxis, though complications are frequent and evidence remains limited. Larger studies are needed to better define its role in anaphylaxis management.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Severe anaphylaxis, a dangerous allergic reaction that can cause shock and organ failure, sometimes requires a special medical machine called extracorporeal life support that takes over the work of the heart and lungs when the body cannot do it alone. Researchers searched medical databases from 2000 to the present and gathered information from 50 studies involving 78 patients who received this life-support treatment during severe anaphylaxis, tracking whether patients survived, recovered brain function, and experienced complications from the treatment. The results showed that about 86 out of every 100 patients survived, and among those who lived, about 86 out of every 100 had good brain function afterward, though about 11 out of every 100 patients experienced problems related to the life-support machine itself. These findings suggest that using extracorporeal life support during severe anaphylaxis may help save lives and protect the brain, but doctors need to be aware that the treatment can cause its own complications. The researchers noted that the quality of evidence from existing studies is low and larger, better-designed studies are needed to understand exactly when and how this life-support treatment should be used for anaph.

title: Differences in intensive care outcomes between older adults with and without dementia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) admissions among older adults with dementia have more than doubled in the past two decades, now representing over 15% of ICU admissions. This population is particularly vulnerable to functional decline and complications following critical illness. This study systematically reviewed evidence on ICU utilization and outcomes among older adults with dementia compared with those without dementia.We conducted a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of cohort studies (2003-2023) identified in MEDLINE, EMBASE, SCOPUS, and Web of Science. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated.Fifteen studies from six countries including 1,738,285 patients (173,107 with dementia) met inclusion criteria. Adjusted analyses showed no difference in ICU mortality (OR 1.05,95%CI 1.00-1.11;n = 1). However, dementia was associated with higher 30-day (OR 1.54,95%CI 1.47-1.62;n = 1) and 12-month mortality (OR 1.95,95%CI 1.88-2.02;n = 1). Patients with dementia also had lower odds of receiving mechanical ventilation (OR 0.69,95%CI 0.60-0.80;n = 3) and higher odds of developing delirium (OR 4.80, 95%CI 1.81-12.72;n = 1).Older adults with dementia admitted to ICUs experience similar ICU mortality but higher long-term mortality, more delirium, and lower odds of mechanical ventilation. These findings highlight the need for prospective studies to guide patient-centered ICU care in this population.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how older adults with dementia fare when admitted to intensive care units, or ICUs, because these admissions have more than doubled over the past twenty years and now make up over fifteen percent of all ICU patients. The team reviewed fifteen studies from six different countries involving more than one and a half million patients, of which about 173,000 had dementia, to compare how these two groups of older adults responded to critical illness. The results showed that while older adults with dementia had similar death rates while in the ICU itself, they were significantly more likely to die within thirty days and twelve months after leaving the hospital, and they also developed more cases of delirium, which is a state of severe confusion. Additionally, patients with dementia were less likely to receive mechanical ventilation, which is a machine that helps people breathe when they cannot do so on their own. The researchers concluded that older adults with dementia need better-designed care plans in intensive care units and called for more detailed studies to understand how to best treat this vulnerable population.

title: Neuraxial anesthesia for surgical pregnancy termination in patients with severe pulmonary hypertension: a case series (2019-2025).
abstract: Current literature on the anesthetic management for surgical pregnancy termination in patients with pulmonary hypertension is limited to patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension using epidural or opioid-only spinal techniques. We report three cases of severe pulmonary hypertension with different etiologies undergoing surgical pregnancy termination using low-dose spinal anesthesia from 2019 to 2025. Two cases were performed in the cardiac surgery operating room with invasive blood pressure monitoring and postoperative cardiac care unit observation; one was managed in the labor and delivery operating room with standard monitoring and general floor observation. All patients were discharged on postoperative day one. This case series suggests that low-dose spinal anesthesia may be a reasonable option for surgical pregnancy termination in select patients with severe pulmonary hypertension, highlighting the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in a Level IV Maternal Care center and an anesthetic plan tailored to the pulmonary hypertension etiology and associated comorbidities.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. llm_summary: Patients with severe pulmonary hypertension, a serious condition where blood pressure in the lungs becomes dangerously high, face significant risks during surgery, especially when undergoing pregnancy termination procedures. Researchers documented three cases from 2019 to 2025 where patients with severe pulmonary hypertension received low-dose spinal anesthesia, which is numbing medication injected into the fluid around the spinal cord, for surgical pregnancy termination. All three patients tolerated the procedure well, with two receiving care in a specialized cardiac operating room with extra monitoring equipment and one receiving care in a standard labor and delivery operating room, and all were healthy enough to go home the next day. These cases suggest that carefully planned low-dose spinal anesthesia may be a safe option for pregnant patients with severe pulmonary hypertension who need surgery, as long as doctors from multiple specialties work together and customize the anesthesia plan based on each patient's specific type of lung disease and other health conditions. The findings are limited because this is only a small group of three patients, so larger studies are needed to confirm whether this approach works safely for more patients with this serious condition.

llm_summary: Background:  Bipolar II disorder is a mental health condition characterized by episodes of depression and periods of elevated mood that are less severe than those seen in bipolar I disorder. The current name of this condition may be misleading because it suggests a straightforward relationship to bipolar I disorder, when in fact the two conditions have distinct characteristics, symptom patterns, and treatment needs that warrant clearer differentiation.

title: Machine and deep learning in REM sleep behavior disorder: a scoping review and analysis of reporting quality.
abstract: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a parasomnia, and its isolated form is of particular interest, as it is an early phase alpha-synucleinopathy. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models offer potential for automated detection, prediction of phenoconversion, and phenotyping. This scoping review identified 75 studies applying ML/DL in RBD and evaluated their methodological and reporting quality using the APPRAISE-AI tool. Most studies (73.3%) focused on RBD detection and mainly used polysomnographic data for this, while 16% addressed prediction of phenoconversion, with imaging data being the most employed modality. Sample sizes were generally small (most studies including only 20-100 individuals). According to APPRAISE-AI scores, 80% of studies had moderate overall methodological and reporting quality. Common deficiencies included lack of transparency in data and code sharing (23.3%), and poor reporting of hyperparameter tuning (17.1%), bias assessment (26.9%), and error analysis (0.66%). Data leakage was observed in 32% of studies. These issues hinder clinical translation and prevent incremental progress between research groups. Without transparent reporting and shared resources, replication and model comparisons become nearly impossible. Future work should adopt open science principles and rigorous validation to advance AI-based tools in sleep medicine.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd.. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how artificial intelligence and machine learning, which are computer systems that learn from data to make predictions, could help detect and understand a sleep disorder called REM sleep behavior disorder, which causes people to act out their dreams and is linked to serious brain diseases. The team reviewed seventy-five studies that used these computer-based approaches and checked the quality of how the research was conducted and reported using a standard evaluation tool. Most studies focused on automatically detecting the sleep disorder using sleep monitoring data, while fewer studies tried to predict whether patients would develop related neurological conditions, though many of these studies had small numbers of participants and lacked important details about their methods. The researchers found that while most studies had acceptable quality overall, they often failed to share their data and computer code with other scientists, did not clearly explain how they adjusted their computer models, and did not properly check for errors or bias in their results. To move these artificial intelligence tools from research into actual patient care, future studies must follow open science practices by sharing their data and methods transparently so that other researchers can verify the results and build upon them.

title: The association of metabolic and bariatric surgery and postabdominoplasty complications: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Previous studies reported that the rate of complications after abdominoplasty is higher in patients with a history of metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS). The current study aims to compare the rate of complications after abdominoplasty in patients with and without a history of MBS and their risk factors in patients with a history of MBS. A systematic search was conducted to identify observational studies that compare postoperative complication rates after abdominoplasty in patients with and without a history of MBS up to 15 April 2025. Pooled odds ratios were computed to compare complication rates between groups, and additional analyses evaluated complication rates and risk factors among MBS. A total of 26 retrospective studies and one prospective study, involving 6328 patients with a history of MBS, were included in the current study. There were no significant differences in the rate of wound dehiscence, surgical site infection, skin necrosis, fat necrosis, deep venous thrombosis, and reoperation after abdominoplasty in patients with and without a history of MBS. In meta-regression analysis, lower body mass index at the time of abdominoplasty is associated with a higher risk of wound dehiscence. Although body contouring surgery after MBS was associated with a higher risk of seroma and hematoma compared to non-MBS cases, the rate of other complications was not significantly different.Copyright © 2026 American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether people who have had weight loss surgery followed by belly tightening surgery experience more complications than those who only have belly tightening surgery. They reviewed 27 studies involving over 6,300 patients who had weight loss surgery and then belly tightening surgery, comparing their complication rates to patients who only had belly tightening surgery. The study found that most serious complications like wound separation, infection, skin death, and blood clots occurred at similar rates in both groups, though patients with prior weight loss surgery did have higher rates of fluid buildup and bleeding around the surgical site. Importantly, patients who had lower body weight at the time of their belly tightening surgery faced a higher risk of wound separation, which doctors should monitor carefully. These findings suggest that having previous weight loss surgery does not significantly increase most complications after belly tightening surgery, though surgeons should remain vigilant about fluid and bleeding complications in this patient population.

title: Diagnostic utility of artificial intelligence in musculoskeletal physical therapy: A comparison with physical therapists.
abstract: Although generative artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise in healthcare, its diagnostic performance relative to physical therapists (PTs) in musculoskeletal conditions remains largely unknown. Limited research has examined how generative AI diagnostic reasoning compares to PTs.Generative AI's diagnostic performance in musculoskeletal cases was examined by assessing case accuracy (correct final diagnosis), efficiency (when the correct diagnosis was selected), and funneling behavior (progressive narrowing of diagnoses), compared to PTs of varying expertise.Cross-sectional comparative case-based study evaluating generative AI diagnostic ability.Generative AI models (ChatGPT [GPT-4/GPT-4 Turbo] and Gemini [Pro Model and 2.0 Flash]) were evaluated using five standardized musculoskeletal clinical cases presented in a sequential, clue-based format. AI responses were scored for accuracy, efficiency, and funneling behavior. Each AI model completed five clinical cases in 15 independent trials. AI performance was compared with previously published responses from 1201 PTs across experience levels who completed the same cases.AI responses achieved the highest overall accuracy rates (20.0-83.3%) compared with specialist PTs (19.7-79.6%) and non-specialists (7.6-60.4%) (p < 0.001), with generally higher efficiency. However, specialist PTs outperformed AI in both accuracy and efficiency in 2 of 5 cases, specifically for the lumbar spine and hip (p < 0.001). Specialist PTs also demonstrated greater funneling behavior (up to 50.0%) than generative AI (up to 13.3%; p < 0.001).Generative AI demonstrated case-dependent agreement with expert-derived diagnoses in standardized musculoskeletal cases, including higher case accuracy and comparable efficiency to specialists. However, the constrained case design limits generalizability and does not reflect open-ended clinical reasoning.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether artificial intelligence systems like ChatGPT and Gemini could diagnose musculoskeletal conditions, which are problems affecting bones, muscles, and joints, as well as human physical therapists could. The study had the AI systems work through five real patient cases presented one clue at a time, just like human physical therapists had done before, and then compared how often each got the diagnosis right, how quickly they figured it out, and whether they narrowed down their guesses in a logical way. The artificial intelligence systems were generally more accurate than non-specialist physical therapists and performed about as well as specialist physical therapists overall, though specialist physical therapists actually did better on cases involving the lower back and hip. However, the specialist physical therapists showed better logical reasoning by progressively narrowing down their diagnosis options, while the AI systems did not demonstrate this same careful thinking process. The researchers noted that because the cases were presented in a limited, structured way that does not match how real clinical situations unfold, more research is needed to determine whether these findings would hold true in actual patient care settings.

title: Prognostic Value of the Hemodynamic Gain Index in Patients With Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Hemodynamic gain index (HGI) is a novel, simple parameter calculated from resting and peak systolic blood pressure and heart rate (HR) during exercise, however, its prognostic value in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is unknown. We investigate the prognostic value of alternative nonmetabolic exercise testing parameters in a contemporary HCM cohort. HGI was calculated from systolic blood pressure at rest and peak /HR data from consecutive HCM patients who underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing for symptom evaluation. Multivariable Cox regression analysis was performed with the primary outcome of all-cause mortality and/or heart transplantation. Logistic regression models were used for HGI to predict the need for future myectomy or alcohol septal ablation. In our cohort of 905 patients with HCM, HGI correlated well with circulatory power (CP, r = 0.71, p <0.001) and peak VO2 (r = 0.64, p <0.001). HGI (Area Under Curve (AUC) 0.87, 95% CI 0.81-0.92) demonstrated comparable accuracies to CP (AUC 0.88, 95% CI 0.83-0.92) and peak VO2 (AUC 0.81, 95% CI 0.75-0.87) in predicting transplant-free survival. Higher HGI was independently associated with a lower risk of primary endpoint (adjusted HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.15-0.42, p <0.001), all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.31,95% CI 0.17-0.56, p <0.001), and was associated with lower risk for future myectomy or alcohol septal ablation (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.67-0.91, p = 0.002). HGI may serve as an independent predictor for adverse outcomes in patients with HCM with comparable prognostic value to peak VO2 and CP. In addition, HGI may identify those who would likely need myectomy or alcohol septal ablation, independent of pVO2 evaluation.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a simple new measurement called the hemodynamic gain index, which uses blood pressure and heart rate data collected during exercise tests, to see if it could predict which patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (a condition where the heart muscle becomes abnormally thick) would have worse health outcomes. The study included 905 patients with this heart condition who underwent exercise testing, and doctors used statistical analysis to determine whether the hemodynamic gain index could predict death, the need for a heart transplant, or the need for surgical procedures to improve blood flow. The hemodynamic gain index performed just as well as two other established exercise measurements at predicting which patients would survive longer without needing a transplant, and patients with higher hemodynamic gain index values had significantly lower risks of death and needing future heart surgery. This simple measurement could help doctors identify which hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients are at highest risk for serious complications and might need more aggressive treatment or closer monitoring. Future research should confirm these findings in other patient groups and determine whether using the hemodynamic gain index in routine clinical practice actually improves patient outcomes and treatment decisions.

title: Portal Vein Stent Placement in a Pancreatic Cancer Cohort: Outcomes and Predictors of Portal Stent Occlusion.
abstract: To determine the patency of portal vein stents in patients with pancreatic cancer, identify risk factors for stent occlusion, and determine whether anticoagulation improves stent patency.Patients with pancreatic cancer who had a portal vein stent placed between March 2018 and December 2023 were identified. A total of 182 subjects were included in this study. Procedural details, medical history, and follow-up imaging and outcomes were extracted. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize baseline demographics. Stent patency rates were calculated. Univariate and multivariate analyses were performed on a variety of factors as they relate to stent patency. Adverse events were evaluated.Stent patency was 76.4% at a median follow-up of 12.2 months. Anticoagulation was not found to be associated with stent patency. Odds of stent failure was higher in patients with periportal inflammation (odds ratio [OR], 2.84; 95% CI, 1.37-5.88; P = .005), preintervention portal vein occlusion (OR, 2.97; 95% CI, 1.39-6.33; P = .005), and persistent robust collaterals after stent placement (OR, 3.85; 95% CI, 1.07-13.85; P = .039).This study found stent patency of 76.4% at 1 year in patients with pancreatic cancer. Anticoagulation did not improve stent patency. The presence of periportal inflammation, preintervention portal vein occlusion, and robust collaterals after stent placement had higher odds of stent occlusion.Copyright © 2026 SIR. llm_summary: Researchers examined how well stents, which are small metal tubes used to keep blood vessels open, work in patients with pancreatic cancer whose portal veins (the major blood vessel carrying blood to the liver) have become blocked or narrowed. The study looked at 182 patients who received portal vein stents between 2018 and 2023, tracking whether the stents stayed open over time and identifying factors that might cause them to fail. The results showed that about 76 percent of the stents remained open and working after one year of follow-up, and surprisingly, blood-thinning medications did not help keep the stents patent (open and functioning). Patients were more likely to experience stent failure if they had inflammation around the portal vein, had a completely blocked portal vein before the stent was placed, or developed extra blood vessels that bypassed the stent after placement. These findings suggest that doctors should pay special attention to patients with these risk factors and may need to develop new strategies to improve stent durability in pancreatic cancer patients.

title: SIRPα Cleavage Is Associated with Inflammatory Response, Corticosteroid Nonresponse, and Worse Prognosis in Clinical and Preclinical Models of Alcohol-Associated Hepatitis.
abstract: Severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (sAH) has been associated with a high 30-day mortality rate. Corticosteroids are used in patients with sAH with limitations. There are no biomarkers measured upon hospitalization that predict responsiveness to corticosteroids. The role of signal regulatory protein (SIRP)-α, a receptor that regulates inflammation, has not been studied in patients with AH. In prospective test and validation cohorts of sAH patients treated with corticosteroids, plasma cytokines and SIRPα levels were measured. Studies in Sirpa-/- mice and in vitro studies were performed to characterize the impact of Sirpa-/- and cleavage. Plasma SIRPα levels were elevated at baseline in corticosteroid nonresponders (CS-NR) versus responders (CS-R) in both cohorts. Plasma SIRPα levels were elevated with disease severity and mortality. In CS-NR patients, proinflammatory cytokines were increased. In mice, Sirpα cleavage was induced by ethanol and lipopolysaccharide and associated with A disintegrin and metalloproteinase domain-containing protein (Adam)-10 activity and cytokine release. Adam10 inhibition reduced Sirpα cleavage and cytokine release. In an experimental model of alcohol-associated liver disease, Sirpa-/- mice developed exacerbated liver injury and inflammation. Based on these findings, plasma SIRPα is a potential biomarker for responsiveness to corticosteroids and prognosis. Sirpa-/- mice developed a hyperinflammatory phenotype similar to SIRPα cleavage in humans. Future clinical studies are necessary to validate plasma SIRPα as a biomarker to guide the use of corticosteroids in patients with sAH.Copyright © 2026 American Society for Investigative Pathology. llm_summary: Severe alcohol-related liver disease causes high death rates within 30 days of hospitalization, and doctors currently use steroid medications to treat it even though some patients do not respond to this treatment. Researchers studied a protein called SIRPα, which helps control inflammation in the body, by measuring its levels in blood samples from patients with severe alcohol-related hepatitis and comparing those who improved with steroids to those who did not. They found that patients who did not respond to steroid treatment had much higher levels of SIRPα in their blood, along with increased inflammatory markers, and that this protein was broken down more in sicker patients through a process involving another protein called Adam-10. In laboratory studies with mice, blocking or removing the SIRPα protein made inflammation worse, suggesting that the breakdown of this protein is harmful and contributes to poor outcomes. These findings suggest that measuring SIRPα levels in a patient's blood when they arrive at the hospital could help doctors predict whether steroids will work and identify patients at higher risk, though more research in actual patients is needed to confirm this approach.

title: "They don't care": The implications of systemic racism on Black women's help-seeking during the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: Black women in the United States experience disproportionately high rates of intimate partner violence (IPV) and persistent barriers to care. Guided by decolonial frameworks, this study examines how systemic racism shaped Black women's help-seeking during the COVID-19 pandemic.This qualitative inquiry is part of a mixed-methods R01 study conducted in the Upper Midwest. Between 2021 and 2023, we conducted semi-structured interviews with 28 urban Black women who experienced IPV during the pandemic. Participants were recruited through community agencies using purposive and snowball sampling. Interviews examined help-seeking, system interactions, and perceptions of safety. Data were thematically analyzed using an interpretive approach informed by Black feminist thought.Three interrelated themes shaped help-seeking: (1) mistrust rooted in racialized harm; (2) mistrust reinforced through harmful interactions with institutions; and (3) conditions that supported trust. Help-seeking was shaped by individual histories, community context, and perceived safety.Systemic racism shapes Black women's help-seeking following IPV. Public health responses must address structural drivers of mistrust, strengthen culturally responsive and trauma-informed care, and center lived experiences to advance trust, cultural safety, and accountability in policy and practice.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. llm_summary: Black women in the United States face higher rates of intimate partner violence, which is physical or emotional abuse by a romantic partner, and struggle to get help due to systemic racism and distrust of institutions. Researchers interviewed twenty-eight Black women from the Upper Midwest between 2021 and 2023 who had experienced intimate partner violence during the COVID-19 pandemic to understand how racism affected their willingness to seek help. The study found that Black women's decisions to ask for help were shaped by three main factors: deep mistrust based on past experiences of racial harm, mistrust that grew worse through negative interactions with hospitals and police, and specific conditions that helped them feel safe enough to trust others. The findings show that public health systems need to address the root causes of why Black women distrust institutions, provide culturally responsive care that respects their backgrounds and experiences, and listen to what Black women themselves say about their needs. These results highlight that healthcare and support systems must work to rebuild trust and accountability with Black communities if they want to help women experiencing abuse.

title: Safety of biopsy in phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma: an international, multicentre, retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Biopsy of phaeochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGLs) is discouraged due to the perceived risk of catecholamine-related complications. However, a systematic review showed that this recommendation is primarily supported by case reports. We aimed to assess the safety of percutaneous biopsy in patients with PPGLs.This international, multicentre, retrospective study included patients of any age with PPGLs referred to participating centres who had had percutaneous core-needle biopsy or fine-needle aspiration. Biopsies of head and neck paragangliomas were excluded. Participating centres completed standardised data-collection forms. The primary outcome was biopsy-related mortality rate for all patients who had biopsies performed at participating centres, given that biopsies done elsewhere that had fatal outcomes would be unlikely to be referred. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of serious catecholamine-related and non-catecholamine-related complications among all included patients.Between Sep 1, 1993, and May 31, 2025, 222 patients (110 [50%] female, 112 [50%] male) underwent 234 biopsies in 19 hospitals across 11 countries. 139 (67%) of 207 patients had elevated epinephrine or norepinephrine (or metabolites) and 27 (12%) of 232 biopsies were preceded by the administration of α-adrenoceptor blockade. One (mortality rate 0·9% [95% CI 0·0-5·1]) of 106 biopsies led to death due to biopsy-related infection. Serious catecholamine-related complications occurred after four (1·7% [0·5-4·3]) of 233 biopsies and included tachyarrhythmia, hypertensive crisis, and cardiogenic shock. No serious catecholamine-related complications occurred in patients without catecholamine excess (n=59), receiving fine-needle aspiration (n=46), or after biopsy of metastatic lesions (n=114). Serious non-catecholamine-related complications occurred after ten (4·3% [2·1-7·8]) of 233 biopsies, mainly bleeding and infection.Percutaneous biopsy of PPGLs was associated with a low mortality rate. Serious complication rates were also low, most of which were not catecholamine-related. These findings challenge current recommendations that biopsy should be avoided in suspected or confirmed PPGLs, and instead support a personalised, risk-benefit-based approach to the procedure.Cancerfonden.For the Chinese and French translations of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Doctors have traditionally avoided taking tissue samples from tumors called phaeochromocytomas and paragangliomas because these tumors produce dangerous chemicals called catecholamines that can cause serious heart problems during a biopsy. Researchers from hospitals across eleven countries collected information on 222 patients who had undergone 234 biopsies, or tissue samplings, to see whether this procedure was actually as risky as doctors believed. The study found that only one patient died from a biopsy-related infection, serious heart-related complications occurred in just four cases, and most complications were not related to the tumor's chemicals at all. These results suggest that taking a tissue sample from these tumors is much safer than previously thought, especially when doctors carefully assess each patient's individual risk factors before performing the procedure. The findings challenge the current medical advice to avoid biopsies in these patients and instead support a more flexible approach where doctors weigh the benefits and risks for each person individually.

title: Clinical evaluation of deep learning accelerated 3D magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography at 1.5 T and 3 T.
abstract: Routine clinical 3D magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) is typically performed either as lower resolution breath-hold (BH) acquisition or higher resolution triggered navigator breathing (NAV) acquisition with a longer acquisition time, potentially limiting clinically applicability. Our aim was to evaluate the clinical feasibility of MRCP obtained using a new deep learning acceleration approach, Sonic DLTM 3D (SDL), as compared to the standard 3D MRCP..Sixty-four and 32 patients underwent 1.5 T and 3 T MRCP scans, respectively. The standard 3D MRCP was obtained using a BH and NAV. Two SDL MRCP acquisitions for each magnetic field were performed with BH and scan times of 11-17 s, utilizing the SDL based acquisition and reconstruction technique. Three radiologists visually evaluated all MRCP datasets for 4 different features: overall image quality, image noise, image sharpness and artifacts. Differences were compared using the Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed rank and chi-squared tests.At both field strengths (1.5 T and 3 T) the proportion of overall image quality scores of 3 or higher (good, very good and excellent) and proportion of cases with reduced artifacts were better (p < 0.05) for both SDL MRCP acquisitions compared to the standard with NAV or BH. However, SDL MRCP was not superior to the standard MRCP technique for all evaluated feature categories and scoring varied between readers.SDL MRCP demonstrated improved image quality consistency and scan time, however, variations between radiologists in quality scores were present, underlying the need for future development and validation.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier B.V. llm_summary: Researchers examined a new faster imaging method for scanning the pancreas and bile ducts, which are tubes that carry digestive fluids, because standard scans either take a long time or produce lower quality images. The study involved ninety-six patients who received traditional pancreas and bile duct scans as well as new deep learning accelerated scans, which use artificial intelligence to speed up the imaging process, at two different magnetic field strengths used in hospital machines. The new deep learning method produced better overall image quality with fewer visual problems compared to standard scans, and it completed the imaging in just eleven to seventeen seconds instead of the longer times required by traditional methods. However, the new technique did not perform better than standard methods in every single category that doctors evaluated, and different radiologists sometimes disagreed about how good the images were. The researchers concluded that while the new deep learning approach shows promise for faster and more consistent imaging, more work is needed to make sure all doctors interpret the images the same way and to fully validate this technology before it becomes routine in hospitals.

title: Implementing remote patient monitoring in lung transplant care: A real-world evaluation.
abstract: Lung transplant recipients require close post-transplant surveillance, which imposes substantial travel and resource burdens. Remote patient monitoring (RPM), which uses home-based transmission of patient symptoms and physiologic data, has demonstrated benefit in other populations; however, data in lung transplantation remains limited.We conducted a single-center observational study of lung transplant recipients enrolled in a 12-month RPM program at Mayo Clinic Rochester. Patients used home devices to transmit symptoms, vital signs, and spirometry. Prespecified abnormal values generated alerts that were reviewed and escalated as appropriate. Primary outcomes included adherence, early discontinuation, and the impact of escalations on management.One hundred and sixteen patients were enrolled. By December 2025, 47 (40.5%) completed the program, 15 (12.9%) discontinued participation, and 54 (46.6%) remained monitored. The median distance from the transplant center was 234 miles (IQR 99-385). Four hundred and seventy escalation alerts were generated, most commonly due to declines in FEV₁ (58.3%). Most escalations (72.8%) were managed with continued monitoring, while 27.2% prompted changes in care, including expedited clinic visits, diagnostic testing, medication adjustments, or emergency evaluation. Among 64 admissions with transmitted data, 31 (48.4%) were preceded by an RPM escalation in the prior 7 days.RPM is feasible and acceptable for post-transplant surveillance and can identify meaningful changes in health status and may be particularly useful with geographically dispersed patients. Nearly half of admissions with transmitted data were preceded by an escalation, but a substantial proportion were not, highlighting opportunities to optimize adherence and alerting thresholds.© 2026 The Author(s).

llm_summary: Lung transplant patients normally need frequent visits to their transplant center for monitoring, which creates a heavy burden of travel and costs, especially for those living far away. Researchers at Mayo Clinic tested whether patients could use home devices to send their symptoms, vital signs, and breathing test results to their medical team instead of traveling for in-person visits. Over one hundred patients participated in the year-long program, and the system generated alerts when concerning changes were detected, with nearly three-quarters of these alerts managed through continued monitoring and about one-quarter leading to actual changes in treatment like expedited clinic visits or medication adjustments. The study found that remote monitoring is practical and acceptable for patients, and nearly half of hospital admissions were preceded by an alert from the home monitoring system in the week before admission. While the results show promise for helping geographically distant patients stay connected to their care team, the researchers noted that some hospital admissions still occurred without prior alerts, suggesting there is room to improve how the system identifies problems and how well patients use it.

title: Decreasing Administrative Effort Related to Non-Approval of Image-guidED Procedures Using Large Language Models - The DENIED-AI Pilot Study.
abstract: To evaluate whether large language models (LLMs) can generate accurate, clinically valid, and usable letters to appeal insurance denials for radiology procedures.This pilot study generated insurance appeal letters for a simulated clinical scenario. Four LLMs (Claude 3.5, Nova Pro, Llama-3.1-70B, ChatGPT-4o) were used with zero-shot, few-shot, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) techniques. Four board-certified interventional radiologists, blinded to model and technique, scored letters for content (accuracy, personalization, references), grammar and structure (readability, tone, persuasiveness), and usability (estimated editing time, usefulness as a template). References were verified for accuracy, and outputs were carefully examined for hallucinations. Statistical analyses included ANOVA, Chi-square, and Fleiss' Kappa for interrater reliability.Mean content and grammar scores were 3.9 ± 0.95 and 4.3 ± 0.9 (out of 5), with no significant differences by model or technique (p >.05). Reviewer agreement was poor (Fleiss' Kappa -0.18 for content, -0.085 for grammar). Hallucinations were flagged by reviewers in 16/48 assessments, significantly more often with the online model (ChatGPT-4o: 58% vs offline 25%; p =.03). Of 44 references, 80% from the offline models were fabricated compared with 29% from ChatGPT-4o (p <.001). Estimated editing time was less than 10 min in 71% of responses, and the reviewers felt the letters would be useful as templates in 73% of cases.LLM-generated appeal letters for insurance denials were generally well received, with high usability and adequate quality. However, fabricated references and hallucinations remain prevalent, necessitating careful human review before clinical use.Copyright © 2026 The Association of University Radiologists. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether artificial intelligence language models could help doctors write appeal letters to insurance companies when imaging procedures are denied coverage, which is a time-consuming administrative task that takes away from patient care. The study tested four different artificial intelligence systems using various techniques to generate these appeal letters for a realistic medical scenario, and then had four specialist doctors review the letters for accuracy, writing quality, and usefulness. The letters received decent scores overall with good grammar and structure, and doctors thought most of them could be useful as starting templates that would need less than ten minutes of editing. However, the artificial intelligence systems had serious problems with making up fake medical references and including false information, with offline systems fabricating references eighty percent of the time compared to the online system at twenty-nine percent. While artificial intelligence shows promise for reducing the administrative burden of insurance appeals, doctors must carefully review and correct any made-up information before using these letters in real clinical practice.

title: Upper Airway Cough Syndrome.
abstract: Upper airway cough syndrome (UACS), formerly known as postnasal drip syndrome, is one of the most common causes of chronic cough. It encompasses a spectrum of upper airway disorders, including allergic rhinitis, nonallergic rhinitis, and chronic rhinosinusitis which stimulate cough through mucosal inflammation and upper airway hypersensitivity. This article reviews the pathophysiology, diagnostic evaluation, and management of UACS from an otolaryngologic perspective. The lack of a clear diagnostic test requires clinical differentiation from other causes of chronic cough. Evidence-based treatment strategies aim to resolve cough through targeted control of airway inflammation and mucus production.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Upper airway cough syndrome, which used to be called postnasal drip syndrome, is one of the most common reasons why people develop a long-lasting cough that won't go away. This condition happens when the upper airways, which are the passages in your nose and throat, become inflamed and overly sensitive due to allergies, sinus infections, or other irritation that causes mucus to drip and trigger coughing. The authors reviewed how doctors can understand what causes this problem, how they can figure out if a patient has it, and what treatments work best to help patients feel better. Because there is no single clear test that doctors can use to diagnose upper airway cough syndrome, they have to carefully examine patients and rule out other possible causes of chronic cough before confirming the diagnosis. The most effective treatment approach focuses on reducing inflammation in the airways and controlling the amount of mucus being produced, which helps stop the cough at its source.

title: Cardiac Biomarkers as Potential Indicators of Neuroimaging Brain Changes in Children and Young Adults with Psychiatric Disorders: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Cardiac biomarkers are recognized as potential indicators for brain function, emotion regulation, and psychiatric risk. While research in adults has suggested associations between cardiac variables of autonomic function and neural changes, little is known about these relationships in children and young adults with psychiatric conditions. This systematic review aimed to examine the evidence linking cardiac biomarkers with structural, functional, and connectivity-based brain changes in this population.A systematic review was conducted in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Multiple databases were searched for studies examining associations between any cardiac biomarker and neuroimaging findings in individuals under 21 years old with psychiatric diagnoses. After screening and full-text review, 11 eligible studies were included.The included studies investigating a range of psychiatric conditions and cardiac biomarkers were associated with brain changes across three domains: structure, connectivity, and neural responses. Associations were most consistent between higher vagal tone and structural and functional integrity of emotion-regulating regions such as the prefrontal cortex, amygdala, and insula. However, findings were heterogeneous and potentially moderated by symptom severity or environmental stressors.This review supports the potential of cardiac biomarkers, particularly high-frequency heart rate variability and root mean square of the successive differences, as proxies of brain changes in youth with psychiatric disorders. While promising, current evidence is too limited and variable for clinical applications. Future research should prioritize large-scale, longitudinal studies using harmonized protocols and wearable technologies to validate these indices as translational tools in child and adolescent psychiatry.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether measurements of heart function could help predict changes in the brain of children and young adults with mental health conditions, since the heart and brain are known to be connected through the nervous system. The team searched scientific databases for studies that looked at the relationship between heart-based measurements, such as heart rate variability or how much the heart rate changes from beat to beat, and brain imaging results in people under age twenty-one with psychiatric diagnoses. The eleven studies they found showed that stronger heart function, particularly higher vagal tone or better control of the heart through the vagus nerve, was most consistently linked to healthier structure and activity in brain regions responsible for managing emotions like the prefrontal cortex and amygdala. While these findings suggest that heart measurements could someday serve as simple tools to track brain health in young people with mental illness, the current evidence is too limited and inconsistent to use in clinical practice right now. The researchers recommend that future studies use larger groups of participants, follow them over longer periods of time, and use standardized methods along with wearable heart monitors to better understand whether heart measurements can reliably predict brain changes in children and teenagers with psychiatric conditions.

title: High-grade cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma: A clinicopathologic analysis of six patients and a review of the literature.
abstract: Cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma was formally considered a subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma due to its architecture and nuclear features. The genomic landscape and immunophenotype of cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma are distinct from papillary thyroid carcinoma. Given this constellation of findings, questions were raised regarding its histogenesis and the 5th edition of the WHO endocrine and neuroendocrine tumors placed cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma in the thyroid tumors of uncertain histogenesis category. This distinction excludes cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma from the high-grade follicular cell-derived non-anaplastic thyroid carcinoma. Thus, we sought to investigate if the criteria for differentiated high-grade thyroid carcinoma would be applicable to cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma tumor category. Herein, we report six patients with high-grade cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma and review of the literature for additional patients. There are at least 10 probable high-grade cribriform morular thyroid carcinomas in the English literature. The study population included 5 females and 1 male aged 19-48 years (median 34.5 years). Two patients had documented syndromes Familial adenomatous polyposis and Gardner syndrome. One patient presented with distant metastatic disease while four patients recurred with distant metastatic disease. Three patients had pathogenic alterations involving the APC gene and one patient had a pathogenic CTNNB1 alteration. Two cases had pathogenic alterations in genes associated with aggressive thyroid carcinoma: TERT and PIK3CA. In this limited series only one patient died of disease. Even so, three were alive with disease at distant metastatic sites. Whether this is a consistent finding in this tumor category remains to be addressed as more patient series are published.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma is a rare type of thyroid cancer that was previously grouped with papillary thyroid cancer but is now recognized as a distinct disease with different genetic characteristics and uncertain origins. Researchers examined six patients with high-grade cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma, which means the cancer cells appeared aggressive under the microscope, and reviewed similar cases reported in medical literature to better understand this tumor type. The study found that patients ranged in age from nineteen to forty-eight years old, with some having genetic syndromes like familial adenomatous polyposis that increase cancer risk, and several patients had genetic mutations in genes called APC, CTNNB1, TERT, and PIK3CA that are associated with aggressive cancers. Although only one patient in this small group died from the disease, three others were still alive but living with cancer that had spread to distant parts of their body, suggesting this tumor type may have unpredictable outcomes. More research with larger groups of patients is needed to determine whether high-grade cribriform morular thyroid carcinoma consistently behaves in a particular way and to develop better treatment strategies.

title: Association of Diet, Supplements, and Physical Activity With Risk of Incident Spondyloarthritis.
abstract: Dietary, supplement, and activity exposures have only been studied in spondyloarthritis (SpA) with retrospective studies. We aimed to determine the association of diet, supplements, and physical activity with incident SpA.We performed a case-control study in the Mayo Clinic Biobank from 2009 through 2015, matching criteria-confirmed incident SpA cases to controls 1:5 on age, sex, recruitment year, and location. Questionnaires assessed 16 dietary, 29 supplement, and leisure-time/work activity exposures. Logistic regression models calculated adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% CIs of SpA for each exposure, adjusting for covariates. Sensitivity analyses were conducted within HLA-B27-positive patients, and those with baseline questionnaires completed 5+ years before index.We identified 73 cases of incident SpA matched with 365 controls (mean age: 60, 70% females). No dietary or activity exposures were associated with SpA overall. However, among HLA-B27-positive individuals, non-diet soft drink consumption was associated with increased risk of SpA (aOR: 4.82, 95% CI: 1.29-18.1), whereas caffeinated coffee was associated with decreased risk (aOR: 0.20, 95% CI: 0.04-0.89). Zinc was associated with increased risk of SpA (aOR: 4.16, 95% CI: 1.19-14.6), as were B vitamins in the HLA-B27-positive subgroup (aOR: 4.21, 95% CI: 1.04-17.1). In the 5-year sensitivity analysis, low leisure-time physical activity plus high work physical activity was associated with increased risk of SpA (relative excess risk due to interaction: 0.50, 95% CI: 0.03-0.98).Due to small sample size and multiple comparisons, the risk factors we identified (non-diet soft drinks, B vitamins, and zinc) should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant further investigation.Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether eating certain foods, taking supplements, and physical activity levels might affect the risk of developing spondyloarthritis, which is a type of inflammatory joint disease. They compared 73 people who had recently developed this condition with 365 people who had not, asking them detailed questions about their diet, supplements, and exercise habits over several years. In people who carried a specific genetic marker called HLA-B27, drinking non-diet soft drinks and taking zinc or B vitamin supplements were linked to higher risk of developing the disease, while drinking caffeinated coffee was linked to lower risk. The researchers also found that people who did little exercise in their free time but had physically demanding jobs faced increased risk of developing spondyloarthritis. Because the study included a relatively small number of patients and tested many different exposures, the researchers emphasized that these findings are preliminary and need to be confirmed with larger studies before doctors can make specific recommendations about diet and supplements for preventing this disease.

title: Association of SGLT2 inhibitors with suicidality, all-cause mortality, and hospitalization in bipolar disorder: A cohort study of 1.23 million adults.
abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) have demonstrated promising neuropsychiatric properties in animal research.We aimed to examine whether SGLT2i exposure is associated with reduced incidence of suicidality, all-cause mortality, and hospitalization in bipolar disorder (BD).This cohort study utilized the TriNetX network (2008-2025) to identify 1,230,821 adults with BD, including 36,092 SGLT2i users and 1,194,729 non-users. The outcomes were incident suicidality, all-cause mortality, and hospitalization over 5-years of follow-up. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, with additional 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) for survival analysis conducted to control for confounding. Subgroup analyses stratified results by sex, race/ethnicity, concurrent mood stabilizer use, and somatic comorbidities.SGLT2i exposure was associated with significantly reduced risk of suicidality (aHR 0.75, 95% CI 0.71-0.79), all-cause mortality (aHR 0.55, 95% CI 0.52-0.57), and hospitalization (aHR 0.71, 95% CI 0.69-0.72). Protective associations remained consistent across subgroups, including patients receiving lithium, lamotrigine, or valproate. After PSM (31,001 matched pairs), five-year outcomes favored SGLT2i users: suicidality-free survival 94.51% versus 93.56%, overall survival 88.99% versus 79.57%, and hospitalization-free survival 72.39% versus 66.72% (all p < 0.001).In this large cohort of over 1.23 million adults with BD, SGLT2i therapy was associated with substantially lower risks of suicidality, hospitalization, and all-cause mortality, with consistent benefits across demographic and clinical subgroups. These novel findings suggest SGLT2is may represent a promising therapeutic strategy to improve psychiatric and survival outcomes in BD. Prospective RCTs are warranted to evaluate long-term safety and efficacy.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a type of diabetes medication called SGLT2 inhibitors might help people with bipolar disorder, a serious mental health condition that causes extreme mood swings. People who took SGLT2 inhibitors had significantly lower rates of suicidal thoughts and behaviors, death from any cause, and hospital stays compared to those who did not take the medication.

title: Competency-Based Simulation Training for Procedural Skills: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: We conducted a systematic review of competency-based simulation education for medical procedural skills, encompassing a diverse range of healthcare domains and professions. Meta-analysis showed competency-based simulation is more effective than noncompetency-based simulation for skill outcomes (large effect). Outcomes are favorable, but small, for behaviors in practice and patient effects. Specific instructional design features examining different simulators and different types and sources of feedback were common themes identified among studies though no instructional design features were found to have significant impact on skill acquisition. This review also identified significant gaps in research including a lack of standardized terminology and reporting methods as well as a limited number of studies assessing the impact on behaviors in practice and patient effects. This study contributes to the ongoing evidence to support competency-based simulation training and highlights the need for further research to enhance the efficacy and efficiency of training of healthcare professionals.Copyright © 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined whether training healthcare workers with specific skill targets using practice simulators works better than training without clear goals. They reviewed many studies across different medical fields and combined the results to see what worked best, finding that competency-based simulation, which means practicing until you meet specific skill standards, was much more effective than regular simulation practice for teaching procedural skills like surgery or medical procedures. While the training showed strong results for teaching the actual skills, the benefits were smaller when looking at whether doctors and nurses actually changed how they worked in real hospitals or whether patients got better care. The researchers found that studies often used different types of practice equipment and feedback methods, but none of these specific design choices made a clear difference in how well people learned the skills. The study highlights that competency-based simulation training is a promising approach for healthcare education, but more research is needed with better standardized methods to understand how to make the training even more effective and to measure whether it truly improves patient care.

title: Computer-aided polyp detection multicenter international randomized controlled study with a focus on community clinics: Geriatric Assessment-Driven Intervention clinical trial.
abstract: Computer-aided polyp detection (CADe) systems can enhance polyp detection, although their performance has largely been evaluated at academic rather than community practices. This randomized controlled trial evaluated the impact of the DEtection of Elusive Polyps-2 (DEEP2) CADe system on colonoscopy quality metrics.Participants undergoing routine colonoscopies were randomized to a control arm, standard-of-care high-definition white-light endoscopy (HD-WLE), or an intervention arm, HD-WLE with real-time DEEP2 system assistance. Coprimary end points: adenomas per colonoscopy (APC; superiority evaluation at a 0.025 level of significance), and percent positive agreement (PPA, defined [per regulatory request] as the proportion of histologically confirmed clinically significant excised lesions relative to total lesions; noninferiority evaluation with a lower 95% CI threshold of -10%). Secondary end points included adenoma detection rate (ADR), polyp detection rate, polyps per colonoscopy, false positive rate, and false alarm rate.This study enrolled 1407 participants, most in community clinics (n = 1208, 85.9%). Use of the DEEP2 system resulted in significantly higher APC (0.74 vs 0.60; difference, 0.14; P = .0002). The PPA difference was -0.06 (95% CI, -0.15 to 0.03; P = .09). There was a numerical, but not statistically significant, ADR improvement (42.9% vs 38.9%; P = .031). A post hoc analysis revealed significant benefit in APC and ADR with the DEEP2 system only within community clinics.These results support the incorporation of CADe devices into colonoscopy practice for improving efficacy and quality over standard-of-care, particularly in community practices.Copyright © 2026 American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a computer system designed to help doctors spot polyps during colonoscopies could improve detection rates, especially in community clinics rather than large academic hospitals. The study randomly assigned over 1,400 patients undergoing routine colonoscopies to either receive standard care or standard care plus real-time assistance from the computer detection system called DEEP2. Patients who received help from the DEEP2 system had significantly more polyps detected per colonoscopy compared to those who received standard care alone, and the computer system performed well without producing excessive false alarms. The benefits were particularly strong in community clinics, where most of the study participants received their care, suggesting that computer-aided detection tools could be especially valuable in smaller medical practices. These findings support doctors adopting computer detection systems during colonoscopies to catch more polyps and improve the quality of cancer screening, particularly in community healthcare settings.

title: Current Indications and Outcomes of Arthroscopic Treatment for Radial-Sided Wrist Injuries.
abstract: Wrist arthroscopy has become an essential tool for treating intraarticular pathologies, with advancements in techniques and instruments expanding its indications over the past few decades. It is the benchmark for diagnosing intraarticular ligament pathologies, such as scapholunate ligament and triangular fibrocartilage complex injuries. In addition, it can be used an adjunct in the management of intraarticular fractures, particularly distal radius and scaphoid fractures. The objective of this article is to outline the role of arthroscopy in the management of common radial-sided wrist disorders and evaluate the surgical outcomes.Copyright © 2025 by the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons.

llm_summary: Wrist arthroscopy, which is a minimally invasive surgical technique that allows doctors to see inside the wrist joint using a small camera, has become an important tool for treating various wrist injuries over the past several decades. This review article examines how arthroscopy is currently used to diagnose and treat common injuries on the thumb side of the wrist, including damage to ligaments (the tissues that connect bones) and fractures of the radius bone and scaphoid bone in the wrist. The authors found that arthroscopy is particularly valuable for identifying injuries to the scapholunate ligament and the triangular fibrocartilage complex, which are two important structures that stabilize the wrist, and it can also help surgeons manage fractures inside the wrist joint. This minimally invasive approach offers patients potential benefits such as smaller incisions, less tissue damage, and faster recovery compared to traditional open surgery. The article provides surgeons with a comprehensive overview of when and how to use arthroscopy for radial-sided wrist problems and summarizes the outcomes patients can expect from these procedures.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Treatment Outcomes in Patients With Incomplete Microscopic Colitis: Consideration for Expanding the Definition of Microscopic Colitis.
abstract: Incomplete microscopic colitis (MCi) is inadequately characterized and does not meet the histologic criteria for microscopic colitis (MC). The clinical features, treatment outcomes, and rates of recurrence are not well-known. The objective of this study was to assess these features.Adults with chronic watery diarrhea diagnosed with MCi on histology (2010-2023) at Mayo Clinic were identified. Response at 12 ± 4 weeks after treatment initiation was defined as: complete (resolution of diarrhea), partial (≥50% improvement), nonresponse (<50% improvement), or intolerance (withdrawal due to adverse effects). Logistic and Cox regression were used to identify predictors of nonresponse and risk of recurrence.A total of 204 patients were identified (median age, 62 years [range, 22-90 years]; 66.2% women) with median follow-up of 3.1 years (range, 0.4-13.3) years. Most (80.4%) were on drugs commonly implicated in MC; 6.8% had improvement after discontinuation of associated culprit medications alone. Patients were treated with the following: 37.3% loperamide, 28.4% budesonide, 18.6% bismuth subsalicylate, 7.4% bile acid sequestrant, and 1.5% other medications. Clinical outcomes were: 72.6% complete response, 22.1% partial response, 3.4% nonresponse, and 1.9.% intolerance. There were no differences in outcomes between MCi subtypes (P = .11). Fecal incontinence was the only predictor of nonresponse. After discontinuation of therapy, 35.8% had recurrence, and 13.7% developed MC.In one of the largest cohorts of MCi, the majority were on drugs implicated in MC and almost three-fourths had a complete response to therapy including budesonide. Given the commonalities with MC, the histologic definition should potentially be expanded to include these patients.Copyright © 2025 American Gastroenterological Association Institute. llm_summary: Researchers examined a condition called incomplete microscopic colitis, which causes chronic watery diarrhea but does not fully meet the standard medical definition of microscopic colitis, a disease where the colon becomes inflamed in ways only visible under a microscope. The study looked at 204 patients with this incomplete form of the disease treated at Mayo Clinic between 2010 and 2023, tracking their symptoms and how well different medications worked to stop their diarrhea. About three-quarters of the patients had complete relief from their diarrhea symptoms after treatment, with most receiving either loperamide (an anti-diarrheal medication), budesonide (a steroid that reduces inflammation), or bismuth subsalicylate, and about one-third of patients experienced a return of symptoms after stopping treatment. The findings suggest that incomplete microscopic colitis behaves very similarly to the standard form of the disease and responds well to the same treatments, which could mean doctors should consider expanding the official definition to include these patients. The researchers recommend that the medical community reconsider how this condition is classified so that more patients with similar symptoms and treatment responses can be properly recognized and treated.

title: Venoactive drugs for venous origin chronic pelvic pain in women: A systematic review.
abstract: BackgroundThis review evaluates the current evidence for the role of venoactive drugs (VADs) for venous origin chronic pelvic pain (VO-CPP) and provide insights to inform the design of an ideal randomized controlled trial (RCT) for future research.MethodsA search was performed in the following databases: Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and Scopus. Studies retrieved were screened for eligibility using Covidence software following PRISMA reviews' methodology. The quality of RCTs and cross-over RCTs was assessed using the Cochrane review tools.Studies were reviewed by 3 physicians, with discrepancies resolved by consensus. A narrative review of the studies was conducted to identify and synthesize clinical outcomes and safety profile of VADs.ResultsEleven studies (n = 748) were identified: 3 RCTs and 8 open-label prospective studies. Most participants were reproductive-age women with confirmed VO-CPP, diagnosed via imaging or laparoscopy. Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction (MPFF) was the most studied VAD.Pain assessment with VAS scores was the primary endpoint in all studies, with significant benefit in patients consistently demonstrated. Other endpoints included Pelvic Venous Clinical Severity Score (PVCSS) and Pelvic Varicose Vein Questionnaire (PVVQ), with improved symptoms and quality of life. Quantitative outcomes were also reported (reduced pelvic vein diameter; better venous hemodynamics). MPFF was safe, with few adverse events reported. Three RCTs had methodological limitations, with two judged high-risk for bias.ConclusionsWhile many identified studies appear to be of low quality, the consistent beneficial effect on VO-CPP scores and the safety profile observed across all reviewed studies suggest that flavonoids have a positive role in the conservative management of pelvic venous disease (PeVD). Future well-designed RCTs are needed to confirm these findings. In the meantime, flavonoids should be considered a therapeutic option for symptomatic patients with PeVD who are not qualified for, not wishing, or are awaiting intervention.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether venoactive drugs, which are medications designed to improve blood flow in veins, could help women with chronic pelvic pain caused by problems with veins in the pelvic area. The team searched medical databases for all published studies on this topic and reviewed eleven studies involving 748 women, including three rigorous randomized controlled trials where patients were randomly assigned to receive either the medication or a placebo. The studies showed that a flavonoid-based medication called Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction consistently reduced pain scores and improved quality of life in women with this condition, and the medication was safe with very few side effects reported. While the researchers noted that many of the studies had some quality issues and limitations, the fact that pain relief was seen across all the studies suggests that flavonoid medications could be a helpful treatment option for women with pelvic vein disease who cannot have surgery or are waiting for other treatments. The researchers recommend that larger, better-designed studies be conducted in the future to confirm these findings before flavonoids become a standard treatment recommendation.

title: Long-term considerations following living liver donation-Guidelines from the 2025 ILTS-iLDLT consensus conference on living liver donor safety.
abstract: Living liver donation is a critical component for addressing organ shortage and improving outcomes for patients with end-stage liver disease. As the prevalence of living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) increases worldwide, understanding and optimizing long-term donor health is paramount. The 2025 International Liver Transplantation Society and International Living Donor Liver Transplantation Society (ILTS-iLDLT) Consensus Conference convened experts in the field of liver transplantation to establish evidence-based guidelines focused on the long-term medical, psychological, and social considerations following living liver donation. The aim of this working group was to integrate current evidence and expert consensus on donor follow-up protocols, risk assessment, and management strategies to promote long-term donor health, quality of life, and living liver donor programs globally to safeguard the welfare of this unique population.Copyright © 2025 American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases.
